(1) Course page: a summary line (ready, approved, to write, course open or closed), the topics in course order as numbered steps (`Teacher::CourseReview#steps`), each with the title, the kind in words, the skills as D-218 references, one badge (Da scrivere, Gli agenti ci lavorano, Pronto per te, Approvato, Aperto allo studente; "Approvato, c'è una versione nuova" for a newer pending revision), one line of what is missing (the reasons of `Course::TopicStage` in Italian), the counts (lesson, exercises, findings to decide), the progress of the students (the official student once the course is released, the trial students before; never mixed; `Teacher::PracticeProgress`) and the one primary button "Rivedi e approva" on ready topics. The filter "Solo quelli pronti per te" is a link (`?only=ready`). The release block follows the path: what opening needs, each condition done or not, the line that trial students see drafts. The student has no display name in the configuration (`BANCO_STUDENT_USERS` maps logins to keys), so the page says "lo studente"; the progress lines use the picker's label. (2) Topic page: four steps with a progress bar (a sticky `<progress>` and four anchors): the lesson as the student sees it (the same classes, section names and renderer, `renderMarkup` with lists v2) beside the lesson review (all eight points, the recomputed values); the exercises, one card each in level order, four instances drawn by the student's own templates and switched off (`items/frozen_slot.js`, shared with "Tutte le domande", from `Teacher::StoredPresentation`), then collapsed hints, messages for the typical errors, worked solution, review and blind solve, "Prova questo esercizio come S" (the item play page, which now goes back to the topic), "Rimanda l'esercizio"; the findings, the `teacher/tests/_finding` partial of D-222 (opinions, "Segui il parere", minors folded) and the lesson review's own findings; the approval, the checklist of the gate with ticks and plain reasons, the button closed with its reason, "Rimanda all'autore" with its codes, and after approving the next ready topic or "Nessun altro argomento da approvare". (3) Seen records: `teacher_read_lesson {topic_revision_id}` ("Ho letto la lezione") and `teacher_saw_exercise {topic_revision_id, item_revision_id}` (a card seen by the button or when half of it has been on screen), posted to `POST /teacher/topic-revisions/:id/seen` (`Teacher::SeenController`, `Teacher::TopicSeen`): app events like `teacher_viewed_topic`, never decisions; a guest, the student's computer and a topic revision that is not the latest write nothing. The gate does not read them: the existing mechanism (`teacher_viewed_topic` and `confirm_seen`) is untouched. The page uses them only to mark steps done and to keep "Approva" closed until the lesson is read and every exercise seen; the form still posts `confirm_seen` as before, and the server accepts it with or without these records. A step is done when: the lesson is read; every exercise is seen; no blocker or major finding of an item is undecided or a fix request, and the lesson was not sent back; the topic revision is approved. (4) A guest reads both pages: no buttons, no forms, no records. Phones: the steps stack, the review sits below the lesson, the progress bar stays at the top of the screen.
- **Why:** the old topic page was about 9400 px long and showed the approval at the top before anything was read; the course page gave a stage word without saying what was missing, what to do or how the student was doing.
- **Cost:** one app event per exercise seen; the page does the same work as before plus the stored presentations of the four samples of each exercise.
- **Status:** implemented
- **Amendment (review fixes, same day):** the lesson body is one partial (`lessons/_body`) drawn by the student's page and by the topic page; each exercise card opens one sample and folds the other three; the progress bar has "Vai ad Approva"; the course page names the student by the login mapped in `BANCO_STUDENT_USERS` ("allo studente" when the map is unset), never a configured name; counts use I18n plurals; "Guarda" became "Vedi" with a state hint.
## D-242 · 2026-10-09 · operator request: the teacher's home is a dashboard that follows the ledger

- **Design ref:** C-04 (the teacher's first page), D-217 (roles and student list), D-215, D-223+
- **Design said:** the home lists the subjects with what waits in each; every detail page is reached and left by clicking back and forth.
- **We do:** Operator, 2026-10-09: "Ci sono troppi click avanti e indietro: una pagina principale, pagine in nuovi tab, autoaggiornamento." (1) `/teacher` is "Cruscotto": "Da fare adesso" (`Teacher::Dashboard#todos`, most blocking first: findings with "di cui M con un parere chiaro" and a link to "Segui il parere", graphs, tests ready, tests blocked with one reason, course topics, corrections, release) over one row per subject (graph, test, course, students with the D-217 list). It reads `Teacher::Home` and the existing read models; no rule is duplicated. (2) Links from the dashboard to a detail page open in a new tab (`target=_blank rel=noopener`); "Apri in nuove schede" switches it off and is remembered in localStorage. (3) `GET /teacher/dashboard/state` returns `{digest, at}`, the digest computed from the ledger watermarks (`Teacher::DashboardDigest`, count and max id of the tables, the heartbeat of the minutes excluded); `GET /teacher/dashboard/fragment` returns the body. Teacher and guest only, `no-store`. (4) One Stimulus controller polls every 20 s while the tab is visible (60 s after 10 unchanged polls, at once on visibilitychange and on a `BroadcastChannel("banco")` message), replaces the body keeping scroll and focus, marks changed rows "aggiornato ora" for 10 s, announces the change in an aria-live region and has an "Aggiorna" button. A teacher page that comes back with a success flash posts the BroadcastChannel message. (5) Guests see the same page without forms. Student pages are untouched.
- **Why:** the teacher works across 11 subjects and kept going back to the home to see what changed.
- **Cost:** one cheap digest query per open dashboard every 20 s; a fragment render when something changed.
- **Status:** implemented

## D-243 · 2026-10-09 · operator request: a persistent menu for the teacher

- **Design ref:** D-242, D-217
- **Design said:** a small nav with the home and the corrections.
- **We do:** Operator, 2026-10-09: "stessa cosa per il teacher aggiungiamo un menu". Every teacher page (the layout `teacher`) has a menu: Cruscotto, Materie (a panel of the subjects with Grafo, Test, Tutte le domande, Corso, Resoconto; opens with Enter or Space, closes with Esc, a click or a tab outside, no hover), Rilievi (`/teacher/findings`: the dashboard's findings lines, same tab), Correzioni, Studenti (`/teacher/students`: report and practice links per student and subject), Prova come S (teacher only), Esci (`BANCO_LOGOUT_URL`). The current section has `aria-current`. Pages of a subject have a breadcrumb ("Cruscotto › Italiano › Test › skill") and a "Cambia materia" switcher to the same page of another subject (a skill, topic or question page goes to its parent page). Menu links open in the same tab; the new-tab rule is only for links inside the dashboard. The preview pages keep the student layout. `TeacherMenuHelper`, `menu_controller.js`.
- **Why:** the teacher moved between pages by going back to the home.
- **Cost:** none beyond the extra pages.
- **Status:** implemented

## D-244 · 2026-10-09 · operator request: rich lessons (cards, diagrams, checks in the page), the two releases, the E7 mapping of the prototypes, the answers F1 to F3; R0 formats

- **Design ref:** D-224..D-226 (lesson/1), D-234, D-236, D-241; firm rules 1 to 6; the design pages 01-contenuti and 03-app-studente (high readability)
- **Design said:** a lesson is one column of eight sections, about 500 words, then eight exercises and their solutions. Nothing to do until "Prova tu".
- **We do:** operator, 2026-10-09: a lesson is split into several short cards, one idea each, with a visual, icons, colour that means something, a summary and a schema, and exercises presented at their best; the student may go as deep as they want; anything a web page can do is allowed. Shape: three layers, cheapest first: (1) lesson/2 cards of typed blocks, (2) the diagram DSL `banco.diagram/1`, (3) free pages (agent code in a sandboxed frame, release 2). **Two releases.** Release 1 (rich lessons) is layers 1 and 2 with the release-1 subset of the block and diagram lists, the render check, the teacher's preview, the print of the summary and schema, and the math pilot; release 1.1 adds the 3D hero, the balance laboratory, "Ascolta", the `ordering` and `tiles` checks, `reveal`, `image`, print with solutions, `bar_model` and `fraction_bar`; release 2 is free pages. **The operator's answers of 2026-10-09:** F1 (free pages) yes, after release 1, with firm rule 3 amended in its own D entry written and merged before any of the free-page work; F2 wait for the lesson/2 math pilot before approving the wave-1 topics; F3 keep a thin positional progress bar inside lessons (no percentage, no time), adopted in release 1 (the bar of A10: "Scheda 3 di 11" with a segmented line; it counts cards, nothing else). **The prototypes** (`research/banco-lezione-prototipo-equazioni-2026-10.html`, `...-soggetto-predicato-2026-10.html`) are mapped element by element in the spec's E7: cards, parts, the lesson map, procedures, cases, legend, step-tagged and diagram-linked examples, mistake cards, the try pager with checks answered in the page (by our graders, never counting), the cover with a hero and goals, colour roles with icon carriers. **Not adopted:** the prototypes' own formula renderer (KaTeX stays, set upright in the body font by CSS), the font Atkinson Hyperlegible Next (app-wide, its own entry), custom 24 px icons (Lucide equivalents), negative terms drawn as balloons, answers checked in the browser, anything from a CDN. **R0** (this entry and D-245 to D-251) delivers the formats, the contract, the palette and icons, the rules and codes, the briefs and the fixtures: `config/banco/schemas/{lesson,diagram,lesson_review}.json`, `config/banco/{lesson_palette,icons}.yml`, `public/vendor/lucide@1.54.0/`, `bin/build-icons`, the `lesson2` block of `config/banco/validation_rules.yml` (rules version 8), 27 error codes (registry version 19), `contract/commands.json` (`lesson open --schema 2`, the new codes on `lesson submit` and `lesson-review submit`), `briefs/{lesson,lesson-v1,lesson-review}.md`, and `test/fixtures/{lesson2,diagrams}` with the markup cases in `test/fixtures/markup/v2.json`. The parser, checks, renderer, events and render check are tracks R1 to R4, built against these.
- **Why:** the 500-word column of lesson/1 is correct and discouraging for a student who is not at ease with reading; the operator liked both prototypes. Layers 1 and 2 keep the guarantee of firm rule 3: agents write data, our templates draw it with `textContent` and DOM APIs.
- **Cost:** the authoring cost rises (about twice lesson/1 for the author and the reviewer, measured on the pilot; the ceilings of D-245 are the brake, and are lowered before the other five lessons if the pilot exceeds 2.5 times). Two schemas, a palette, a DSL and a render check to maintain.
- **Status:** decided
- **Back-port:** none. Free pages (release 2) and release 1.1 get their own entries when they are built; D-247 of the spec (firm rule 3 amended) is not one of these numbers: it is written when F1 is acted on.

## D-245 · 2026-10-09 · banco.lesson/2: cards of typed blocks next to lesson/1 (lesson.md, body, rules version 8, accept_schema1, the splitter and what the spec left open)

- **Design ref:** D-224, D-225, D-234; spec A1 to A5, A9, A12
- **Design said:** `banco.lesson/1`: front matter, eight sections, `finals_it`, parsed body of strings.
- **We do:** `schema: banco.lesson/2` selects the new parser (`Lessons::Parser` dispatches on it, R1); lesson/1 stays as is while `lesson.accept_schema1` is true (rules file; its flip is D-251). **Source:** front matter as lesson/1 plus `goals_it` (1 to 3, each starting with a bold verb), `why_it` (the old "Perché ti serve", on the cover), `hero` (one diagram, optional), `book_it` (optional; the fixed line is ours); no `finals_it`. Body: optional parts (`# `), cards (`## Titolo {ROLE [extra] [icon=] [id=] [tone=]}`) of blocks: paragraphs and lists are `text`, everything else a `::: TYPE` directive (`:::: more` is the only nesting). Release 1 blocks: `text callout math procedure cases legend example mistake check more summary schema diagram table try`; blocks of release 1.1 and 2 are `E-LESSON-BLOCK` "not available yet". **Body JSON** (`config/banco/schemas/lesson.json`, `$defs.body2`, `schema_version` 2): cards with `n`, `id` (the slug or `cN`), `role`, `level` core or extra, `title_it`, `icon`, `tone?`, `part?`, blocks with `n` and `line`; `words {core, extra}`; `pages` empty in release 1. Budgets and ceilings are the `lesson2:` block of `validation_rules.yml`; **rules version 8** (no existing number changes). **Where the spec was closed or corrected in R0:** (1) the schema dispatches on `schema` with `if/then` (not `oneOf`: a bad body gives the errors of its own version, not "matches none of two"), and the root is closed by `unevaluatedProperties`; the diagram schema is referenced by `urn:banco:schema:diagram` (`Banco::Schemas` resolves it; `NAMES` gains `diagram`; `name_for` maps both lesson formats to `lesson`). (2) A `{` or `}` in a card title outside `$...$` is `E-LESSON-CARD`: the regex of the spec would accept it, but the tag must be the only brace group of the line, and the A1 list of bad fixtures asks for the case; braces inside `$...$` are accepted (`good/heading-braces-in-math.md`). (3) A table is at most 4 columns everywhere (A3 said 5 for a schema table, A4 4 for the block: one rule). (4) A step blank is one of `choice number fraction normalized_text`; a `try` exercise has `check` or `checks`, not both, and `solution_it` or `solution_steps`, not both; `final_it` stays optional (`W-LESSON-FINAL-MISSING`). (5) `check` and `blank` bodies reuse the practice components' fields (`any_answer` for the answer of a matching or span_select error). (6) YAML 1.1 turns the key `on` and the values `yes no on off` into booleans: the DSL field `on` of a cartesian point is `on_lines`, and the brief says to quote `"sì"` and `"no"`. (7) `lesson_review.json` accepts 8 or 11 checklist points (the exact count by the revision's schema is `E-REVIEW-CHECKLIST` in Ruby, R1) and a finding names `section` (lesson/1) or `card` with an optional `block` (lesson/2, 0 is the cover); `recomputed.where` gains `check`. (8) `lesson open --schema 2` is a flag of the existing command: the server answers the converted draft of the latest lesson/1 revision (`Lessons::Convert1to2`, R1). (9) Brief names may hold digits (`lesson-v1`): `Brief::NAME` and the route constraint. **Briefs:** `lesson` is rewritten as version 2; version 1 is `lesson-v1` while `accept_schema1` is true; `lesson-review` version 2 holds both checklists. **Fixtures** (`test/fixtures/lesson2`): `base.md`, `demo.md` (math, 10 core and 2 extra cards), `demo-italian.md`, 77 bad files with `manifest.json` (one code each, with the line; the render codes are R4's), `good/` splitter cases, `context.json` (the invented course), `numbers.json`, `whitelist.json`; `test/fixtures/content/lesson/{good,bad}/lesson2-*.json` and `front_matter/*lesson2*` for the schema; the markup cases for roles and links are in `test/fixtures/markup/v2.json` with `"options": {"roles": true}` and are skipped by the lesson/1 tests until R1 and R2 run them.
- **Why:** one idea per card, a visual on every idea and short checks need a typed structure the machine can check; the splitter and the YAML rules close the ways an agent's file silently turns into something else.
- **Cost:** a second parser and set of checks (R1), and `lesson.accept_schema1` to flip at the end.
- **Status:** decided (formats, contract, rules, briefs and fixtures in R0; the code in R1 to R4)
- **Back-port:** none.

## D-246 · 2026-10-09 · lesson colour roles, carriers and icons: lesson_palette.yml, icons.yml, the vendored Lucide subset, the contrast and colour-vision rules

- **Design ref:** spec A5, A6, C1, E2 (spikes S5, S6); the design's rule of 7:1 text contrast
- **Design said:** nothing: lessons had no colour or icons.
- **We do:** `config/banco/lesson_palette.yml` (version 1): a `common` group (`highlight correct wrong muted`) and a palette per subject (math: `unknown known left right coefficient`; italian: `predicate subject complement object time cause purpose agent`), each role with a label, a **carrier** (`glyph`: the text already says it; `position`: the place says it, a background tint; `icon`: colour plus the role's icon before the span, explained by the legend; `tint`: the highlighter; `band`: the card's header), colours for `cream` (also print) and `dark`, a marker `shape` (box, weight, circle, square, triangle, diamond, ring, star: one per role) and, for icon roles, the question it answers. No underline style is used and right and wrong use no green and no red (ink with a check or a lightbulb). `step_tags` holds the verbs of procedures and example steps with their Italian label and icon. `config/banco/icons.yml` maps our names to Lucide 1.54.0 (ISC): `structural` (agents may use; the role defaults), `ui` (our templates only) and a list per subject (at most 30); an agent names our icons only (`E-LESSON-ICON`). The files used are vendored under `public/vendor/lucide@1.54.0/` with `LICENSE` and `SHA256SUMS`, and `bin/build-icons` makes `banco-sprite.svg` (74 icons, about 22 KB) from the list; `bin/build-icons --check` (in `test/lib/lesson_icons_test.rb` and CI) fails when the committed sprite or sums differ. Icons are drawn with `<svg><use href="/vendor/lucide@1.54.0/banco-sprite.svg#NAME">`, `aria-hidden`, `stroke: currentColor`. `bin/build-palette` and the generated `lesson_roles.css` are R2. **Checked by `test/lib/lesson_palette_test.rb`** (not by agents): at most 8 roles per subject beyond `common`; every role's text colour 7:1 on `--bg` and `--surface` of cream and dark (and on white, with the cream colours, for the light theme); marks 3:1; the ink 7:1 on every tint; roles that share a diagram distinguishable under protanopia, deuteranopia and tritanopia (Machado 2009, severity 1, CIEDE2000). **Where the spec was adjusted:** (1) the colour-vision distance is 12 between two roles that rely on colour alone (math: the smallest pair is 12.4 in dark, 15.0 in cream) and **6** for a pair that includes an icon role: with eight italian roles, recognisable hues and 3:1 against both grounds, the best reachable was 6.6; the icon, the printed label and the shape tell those roles apart too. (2) "Tints 3:1 against the ground" cannot hold for a highlighter or a position tint (a tint is a pale background): what is checked is the ink at 7:1 on every tint, and no role is carried by a tint alone (a position role is also a glyph or a label in the legend). (3) `correct` and `wrong` are in the palette as ink with an icon so the feedback has one source. **Spikes** (throwaway, in Chrome headless 151): S5, the sprite through `<use href>` under the app's CSP (`default-src 'self'`, same origin) draws all icons (28 px at 20 px text: 1.4 em), no CSP violation. S6, a container query on the lesson column re-lays out at 600 px (one column at 420, three at 1000), and CDP `Emulation.setEmulatedMedia {features: [{name: "forced-colors", value: "active"}]}` through `page.command` (not `browser.command`) turns `@media (forced-colors: active)` on in Ferrum; it changes the media feature only, it does not remap colours, so R2's forced-colors check is on the rules (borders, icons, labels that remain), not on the system colours.
- **Why:** colour that means something is the operator's request; the carriers keep the meaning when colour is not seen (colour blindness, forced colours, print).
- **Cost:** a vendored set of 74 files and a generated sprite and stylesheet to keep in step; the colour maths test is code to maintain.
- **Status:** decided
- **Back-port:** none.

## D-247 · 2026-10-09 · the diagram DSL banco.diagram/1: types of release 1, the state overlay, solution fields, exact numbers, the balance's scope, the vectors

- **Design ref:** spec A7, A8, E3; firm rule 3 (agents write data, our code draws)
- **Design said:** nothing; lessons had no pictures.
- **We do:** `config/banco/schemas/diagram.json`, dispatched on `type`, each type closed (`additionalProperties: false`). **Release 1 types:** `equation_parts number_line balance area_model cartesian sentence` (diagrams) and `concept_map flow table` (schemas, in the summary card); `bar_model` and `fraction_bar` are 1.1, `timeline tense_timeline venn map` later, `circuit molecule tiles solid3d` reserved. Every diagram has `alt_it` (5 to 50 words), `caption_it?`, `size`, `states?`. **State rule:** a state overlays the top level, shallowly; `op_it`, `groups`, `next_label_it` exist only in states; `alt_it`, `caption_it`, `size` and the solution fields are top level only (`x-banco-state-keys` and `x-banco-state-only-keys` per type); the merge is done once, in Ruby, before the checks and before serving. **Solution fields** carry `x-banco-solution: true` (release 1: `balance.x_value`); the server serves a computed `tilt` per state and the value only with `show_value`; `whitelist.json` and its test list them. **Numbers** are exact strings (integer, decimal with comma, fraction `a/b` with `b > 0`, `-inf`/`+inf` only in number line intervals), parsed by `Lessons::Num` (Ruby, Rational) and `lesson/num.js` (BigInt) against `test/fixtures/lesson2/numbers.json`; the schema pattern accepts exactly what the file accepts; no float is used in any check. **The balance's scope** is natural terms and a positive solution: with `states` every effective state is level at `x_value`, `groups: n` needs both plates divisible by n, `try` has at most 12 values and holds the solution, `x_value` is omitted exactly when both plates hold the same number of boxes; negative terms, zero or negative solutions and subtraction have no honest picture and the brief sends the author to a number line, an example or a flow. **Where the spec was adjusted:** (1) `left`/`right` of a balance and `text_it`/`parts` of a sentence may be given only in the states, as the spec's own A1 example does (the schema requires them at the top level or in every state). (2) The `cartesian` point field `on` is `on_lines` (YAML 1.1 reads `on:` as `true`, see D-245). (3) The grammar of `cartesian.eq` is fixed: `y = mx + q`, `x = k` or `ax + by = c`, with `m q k a b c` exact numbers (a coefficient of 1 may be left out: `y = x + 1`, `x + y = 7`). (4) `equation_parts.brackets` index whole parts of the list, `from` at most `to`. **Vectors** (`test/fixtures/diagrams/vectors.json`, 106): data, the subject of its roles, the schema verdict and, for what the schema accepts, the semantic verdict of `Lessons::Diagrams` (R1: `E-LESSON-DIAGRAM`, `E-LESSON-ALT`, `E-LESSON-ROLE`, `E-LESSON-MAP`, `E-LESSON-ICON` with the JSON pointer); R2's `layout` must return `{error}` without throwing for every vector Ruby refuses and a Scene for the others, at widths 320 to 1280 and text sizes 18 to 26. `test/content/diagram_vectors_test.rb` runs the schema column now.
- **Why:** about 90% of the visual needs of the first lessons are these nine shapes; agents write data and cannot draw something the data does not support (a balance cannot be unlevel in a chain of equivalences).
- **Cost:** each new type is a schema, a Ruby check, a browser module and vectors (a D entry each).
- **Status:** decided
- **Back-port:** none.

## D-248 · 2026-10-09 · lesson checks: the StudentBody whitelist, the shuffle, graded by the server, lesson_events, student_questions.card; lesson checks never count

- **Design ref:** spec A2, A9, A11; firm rules 1, 3 and 4; D-235 (`Grading::Closed`), `Diagnosis::Rekey`
- **Design said:** lessons had no questions; practice items are graded by `Grading`, answers never in the page.
- **We do (R0 fixes the interfaces; R1 and R3 build them):** (1) **StudentBody whitelist.** `Lessons::StudentBody.for(revision, seed:)` copies only the fields named in `test/fixtures/lesson2/whitelist.json` (served and dropped, per block type and check component; a test fails until every declared field of a schema is in one of the two columns); never served: `answer`, `accept`, `errors`, `explain_it`, `final_it`, `solution_it`, `solution_steps`, the `do_it` of a blank step and of the steps after it, the `result_it` of an example with a blank, a diagram's solution fields. The page embeds the projection as `<script type="application/json" id="lesson-body">`. A property test (R1, 300 runs) puts unique sentinels in the answer-side fields of random bodies and asserts none reaches the projection. (2) **Shuffle.** Choice options (and in 1.1 ordering and matching) go through `Diagnosis::Rekey` with the seed `lesson|STUDENT|REVISION|CARD|BLOCK` (`preview` for the teacher's box); the check endpoint recomputes it and grades with the `id_map`. (3) **Grading** is the server's: `POST /topics/:topic/lesson/checks/:card/:block[/:step]` (and `.../ex/:n[/:part]`) with `{response, try, client_event_id}` answers `{verdict, message_it, explain_it?, try, steps?}`; `Lessons::Checks.grade` maps to `Grading::Closed` or compares sets (`span_select`); retries are free, the explanation comes after the second wrong answer; `response` is at most 200 characters and filtered from the logs. (4) **`lesson_events`**: a new append-only table with triggers (R3), one nullable column `card` on `student_questions` (no rebuild). (5) **A lesson check never writes to the practice ledger, never enters `Practice::Fold` and never counts for a skill state**; a later decision may change it (a new rules version). (6) No model in the student's path: the feedback is a fixed word ("Sì.", "Non ancora.") and the author's own messages.
- **Why:** one notion of correct (decimal comma, accents, normalisation) shared with practice, the answers stay out of the page, the teacher sees what was answered. The prototypes check in the browser and say so in their notes.
- **Cost:** a round trip per check (100 to 300 ms, "Controllo..." on the button); one table and one column.
- **Status:** decided
- **Back-port:** none.

## D-249 · 2026-10-09 · render check of a lesson/2 revision in the server's Chrome, screenshots, purge, the gate reason

- **Design ref:** spec A12 (2, 3), C2; D-223 (Chrome validation of items); firm rule 3 (our code only)
- **Design said:** a lesson was text; nothing drew it before the teacher.
- **We do (R4 builds it; R0 fixes the numbers in `lesson2.render` and the codes):** after a stored lesson/2 revision (not on a dry run) `RenderLessonRevisionJob` renders every card in the harness's render host at 390 x 844 and 1280 x 800 in cream and 1280 in dark (extra cards at 390 in cream), `more` open and every state shown, and reports an exception or a KaTeX error (`E-LESSON-RENDER`), horizontal overflow (`E-LESSON-OVERFLOW`), two label boxes overlapping or a diagram layout that returns an error (`E-DIAGRAM-LAYOUT`), any text under the student's size, never under 18 px (`E-DIAGRAM-SMALL-TEXT`); all four are **errors** because they depend on the author's data. Screenshots are WebP quality 80, stored by content (`storage/lesson_shots/<sha256>.webp`), the result is a row of `lesson_renders` (append-only); a budget of 90 s per revision and 5 s per card-viewport; `bin/purge-lesson-shots` deletes files of unpinned, superseded, older than 30 days renders (the rows stay). `banco lesson status REV` shows the result, `banco lesson shots REV --dir D` downloads the shots. `Approval::TopicGate` gains the mechanical reason "the lesson revision has a render without errors" (lesson/2 only).
- **Why:** an unreadable card shows only when drawn; the author and the reviewer must see it before the teacher does.
- **Cost:** about 35 shots (2.5 MB) per revision, a job of up to 90 s below item validation in priority.
- **Status:** decided
- **Back-port:** none.

## D-250 · 2026-10-09 · lesson review for lesson/2 (11 points, findings by card) and the teacher's preview of the lesson as the student sees it

- **Design ref:** spec A13, A14; D-230, D-233 (4)
- **Design said:** a lesson review has 8 points and findings by section.
- **We do:** `banco.lesson_review/1` keeps its shape; for a lesson/2 revision the checklist has exactly 11 points (numbers; solutions and check answers; rules; mistakes; examples with their reveal order; scope; readability by card; prova tu; **visuals**: every diagram says what the text says and no picture draws something false; **cards**: one idea each, the order builds up; free pages, `na` in release 1), a finding names `card` and optionally `block`, the quote is still an exact substring of `lesson.md`; `Review::LessonChecklist.for(revision)` gives the points by the revision's schema and a wrong count is `E-REVIEW-CHECKLIST` (R1). `lesson-review open` adds the render result and the URLs of the screenshots; the brief tells the reviewer to look at every card at 390 px. The teacher's topic page shows the lesson/2 as the student sees it in a preview box (R2) with the removed answer fields through a teacher-only JSON endpoint (R3). No new decision kind: the approval is `approve_topic`.
- **Why:** the reviewer's work doubles with the visuals; a card review keeps findings attached to what the student sees.
- **Cost:** about twice the reviewer's time of lesson/1, measured on the pilot.
- **Status:** decided
- **Back-port:** none.

## D-251 · 2026-10-09 · migration of the six wave-1 lessons to lesson/2; the later flip of lesson.accept_schema1

- **Design ref:** spec A15, A16, D3; operator answer F2 (wait for the math pilot)
- **Design said:** the six wave-1 lessons are lesson/1 revisions, reviewed and approved.
- **We do:** the math pilot is rewritten as lesson/2 first (author Opus, reviewer of another family, screenshots to the operator), starting from `banco lesson open KEY --schema 2` (a converted draft: the content is rewritten into cards, with a visual on every idea); the operator's go on the pilot's look is the gate for the other five. Wave-1 topics are not approved before it (F2). lesson/1 revisions already stored keep their schema and render with the old page. `lesson.accept_schema1` stays true until the six lessons are lesson/2; flipping it to false (then a lesson/1 submit is `E-LESSON-SCHEMA`) is its own commit with its own entry.
- **Why:** the pilot tests the format on the hardest lesson before the cost is paid five more times.
- **Cost:** a rewrite of six lessons and their reviews.
- **Status:** decided
- **Back-port:** none.

## D-252 · 2026-10-10 · rich lessons R1: the Ruby side of lesson/2 (parser, blocks, diagram checks, StudentBody, Checks, converter, review intake) and what the build closed or corrected

- **Design ref:** D-244..D-251; spec A1 to A9, A12, A13, A15.1, E1 row R1
- **Design said:** R0 fixed the formats and the fixtures; R1 builds the parser and the checks against them.
- **We do:** `Lessons::Parser2` (a line-by-line, fence-aware splitter: a `# ` or `## ` line counts only at depth 0, a `:::` block is closed by `:::`, `:::: more` by `::::`, a blank line is required around every fence, a `:::` opening inside an unclosed block reports that block at its opening line), `Lessons::Directives` (the opening line, YAML with no aliases and a raw scan that refuses a double-quoted value holding a backslash, `math` as one formula or `lines:`, `summary` as a list), `Lessons::Blocks` (types, prose, visuals, checks, the walk over a body, per-type checks in `Blocks::{Check,Example,Try,Simple}` and the `Blocks::Context` that resolves a finding to the line of the field in the block's YAML), `Lessons::Diagrams` (the state overlay `merge_states`, `effective_states`, `solution_fields` from the schema, and one module per type with the checks of the vectors), `Lessons::Num` (exact numbers, `numbers.json`), `Lessons::Palette`, `Lessons::Icons`, markup v2 with `roles: true` (role spans, `scheda:` and `argomento:` links, the formula allowlist and `\role{name}{tex}`), `Validation::Lesson2Checks` (budgets, readability per paragraph, roles, links, icons, diagrams, inline checks, counts; `Validation::LessonChecks.call` dispatches on `schema:` and answers `E-LESSON-SCHEMA` for a lesson/1 file when `lesson.accept_schema1` is false), `Lessons::StudentBody` (the whitelist; Rekey seeds `lesson|STUDENT|REVISION|CARD|BLOCK`, plus `|stepN` for a blank, `|exN` and `|exN|K` for an exercise check; balance `tilt` computed per state, `x_value` only with `show_value`; the states of an example's diagram are cut like its steps), `Lessons::Checks.grade(check, response, id_map, subject:)` (the shared `Grading::Closed`, span_select as a set; a verdict is `right`, `wrong` or `invalid`, with the hint of the matched `errors[]` entry), `Lessons::Convert1to2` and `lesson open KEY --schema 2` (the server answers the converted draft of a lesson/1; a lesson/2 as it is), `Validation::TopicChecks` (`W-TOPIC-INSTANCE-IN-LESSON` reads example problems, check prompts, try texts and the equation a balance draws), `Review::LessonChecklist.for` and `LessonIntake` (11 points for lesson/2, findings by card and block, a recomputed entry for every try exercise with a final or a check). `LessonRevision#exercise(n)` reads an exercise in either format and `POST /topics/:topic/lesson/exercises/:n/solution` answers `{n, solution_it}` or, for tagged `solution_steps`, `{n, steps}` (the final is never sent apart). The body JSON keeps `line` on cards and blocks. The lesson API refuses a lesson/2 only above 4 times the size limit (413); between 96 KB and that it is `E-LESSON-SIZE`.
- **Where the spec was closed or corrected:** (1) **The balance cannot be tilted with a declared solution.** The vectors (`balance-not-level`) say that `x_value` must be the solution of the drawn plates even without states, so a balance is tilted only when both plates hold the same number of boxes; the pilot's card 5 ("a tilted balance, 3 taken from one plate only") cannot be drawn in release 1 as written. It is a choice-check card over a level balance's states, or waits for `balance_lab` (1.1); the lead should have R7 settle it. (2) **Vector fixed:** the Cartesian vector `cartesian-vertical-and-fractional-slope` wrote a line as `1/2x - 1,5`; a line is `y = 1/2x - 1,5` (the three forms of A7). (3) **Fixtures fixed:** `demo-italian.md` had an idea card whose only block was a `cases` without a diagram, which A3 says is not a visual: one case now carries a sentence diagram (and the same in `bad/card-roles.md`); `bad/visuals-thirteen.md` counted an example as a visual (4 + 8 = 12), it now adds nine diagrams (4 + 9 = 13); `good/heading-inside-yaml.md` stays good for the splitter but its `solution_it` holds a `## ` line, which the strict markup refuses (`E-LESSON-MARKUP`), and the test says so. (4) **Lines:** a finding about a field of a YAML block reports the line of that field (the manifest of R0 mostly meant this); a text block reports the line of the paragraph; a count on a summary reports its last point; `block-check-in-more` is line 46, the fence. (5) **E-LESSON-BOLD** is the share of bold words in the running text (the `text` and `callout` blocks), not in the whole file: the goals are bold by rule and the checks are not prose. (6) **Visual ceiling:** diagrams, schemas and procedures count, a `cases` and an `example` count each diagram they hold, a `more` block's diagrams count as extra, an example without a diagram is not a visual (so the pilot's 11 + 1 fit 12). (7) **Counts with a code of their own** (the points of a summary, the blocks of a card) are left to Ruby: the copy of a body the schema judges is trimmed or padded to fit (`Parser2.for_schema`), so the code is `E-LESSON-SUMMARY` or `E-CARD-BLOCKS`, never `E-SCHEMA`. (8) **A `number` check takes an integer or a decimal with comma**; a fraction answer belongs to the `fraction` component (the number box does not read `7/2`). (9) `try`, `mistake` and `summary` blocks belong only in cards of their role. (10) **The converter writes no goals** (the old lesson has none): the draft fails the front matter schema until the author adds them, then exactly `E-CARD-NO-VISUAL`, `E-LESSON-CHECKS` and `E-LESSON-MAP`; what it cannot map without loss (a step with no "Perché:", a mistake with no ✗ and ✓) stays as text in its card. (11) `W-CHECK-ANSWER-IN-PROMPT` is for `number`, `fraction` and `normalized_text`: a choice lists its options and a span_select shows its sentence. (12) A role name in a formula is `[a-z]+(-[a-z]+)*` and the commands `\htmlClass \htmlId \htmlStyle \htmlData \href \url \includegraphics \def \gdef \edef \xdef \newcommand \renewcommand \providecommand \let \futurelet \global \class \cssId \raw \include \input` are refused in Ruby (the browser parser refuses them too, R2). (13) `Validation::Context` gains `topic:` (the topics of the subject's latest course map) for `argomento:` links. (14) **Not done here, on purpose:** the student's and the teacher's pages still read `body.sections` (`lessons/show`, `teacher/topics/show`): a topic that pins a lesson/2 revision needs R2's `show2` and R3's preview before it is used; `StudentBody` is the whole contract of what the page may be told.
- **Why:** these are the places where the spec text, the fixtures and the vectors disagreed; the vectors and the codes are the contract, so the prose or the data was fixed, never a code.
- **Cost:** a parse of a lesson is a few milliseconds; the converter keeps all the old text.
- **Status:** decided
- **Back-port:** none.

## D-253 · 2026-10-10 · lesson/2 renderer (R2): the page, the cards, the diagram layouts, the thin positional bar, the interface choices the spec left open

- **Design ref:** spec A4, A5, A6, A7, A9, A10, A14, C2, E1 row R2, E3 (R2), F3 (operator answer: keep a thin positional progress bar inside lessons, no percentage, no time).
- **Design said:** a browser renderer under `app/javascript/lesson/`, `lesson2_controller.js`, `lessons/show2.html.erb`, `lesson.css`, the palette and icon build scripts, preferences, safe mode, the teacher's box.
- **We do:** `lesson/render.js` draws the cover, one card at a time (or all in one column, chunked by an IntersectionObserver), the lesson map (side panel from 1100 px, dialog below), the bottom bar, the settings dialog, print and "Stampa riassunto e schema", the `card_seen` batch after 3 seconds, resume from the server. The thin bar is one segment per core card, the current one marked, aria-hidden: position only (F3). Blocks: `lesson/blocks/*` (text, callout, math chains, procedure, cases, legend, example with reveal and blank, mistake cards, check, more, summary, schema, diagram, table, try pager). Diagrams: `lesson/diagrams/*`, each `layout(data, {width, fontPx, measure, subject, state, tryValue}) -> Scene | {error}` and `describe(data)`, never throwing; `draw.js` makes SVG (classes only) plus an HTML label layer, the controls (Avanti, the balance's number stepper, tapping a part of a sentence) and the "Descrizione"; parts with the same id move between states (FLIP, a swap under reduced motion). The shape of every diagram is checked with the same schema as Ruby: `bin/build-diagram-schema` compiles `config/banco/schemas/diagram.json` into `lesson/diagram_schema.js` (a small reader in `lesson/schema.js`), and the semantic rules are mirrored per type; all 106 shared vectors run both ways, plus a mangling test (layout never throws). `bin/build-palette` makes `lesson_roles.css` (custom properties on the theme element, so a theme switched on a box wins over the page) and `lesson/palette.js` (labels, carriers, icons, shapes, step tags, icon lists, no colours); `bin/build-icons` was R0's. Text: `markup_parser.js` takes `{roles: true}` (role spans, `scheda:`/`argomento:` links, refuses `\htmlClass` and friends and a bad `\role`); `lesson/text.js` draws them, KaTeX with the one macro `\role` and a trust function that allows only `\htmlClass` with a `role-` class; icon roles get their icon inside formulas too. The KaTeX look (upright, body font) is CSS. `BANCO_LESSON2_ENABLED` (`Banco::Lesson2.enabled?`, default on, in `banco health` as `lesson2.enabled`) puts the page in safe mode: the long column, no diagrams (alt text and description), no checks, no reveal, mistakes open. Preferences keep `lesson_view` and `reduce_motion` apart from theme and size (`Diagnosis::Preferences.lesson`, `for` is unchanged); `POST /diagnosis/preferences` answers JSON to the lesson page. The teacher's box (`lesson2_preview_controller.js`, `teacher/topics/_lesson2_box`) is the same renderer in a box of 390, 768 or 1280 px with theme and size switches; "Modalità docente" opens every `more` and shows answers from `full.json`.
- **Interfaces chosen where the spec was silent (R1 and R3 must meet them):** (1) `Lessons::StudentBody.for(revision, seed:)` is the only way the page gets a body, with the student's key as `seed` ("preview" in the box); there is no fallback to the stored body. (2) The served diagram: states already merged; `balance` has a computed `tilt` per state and at the top level, 1 when the left pan is heavier, -1 right, 0 level, and no `x_value` (unless `show_value`); the page accepts `tilt` only where `x_value` is absent or `show_value` is set, so an agent-declared tilt stays refused. (3) A state's `next_label_it` names the button that leaves that state. (4) Check endpoint `POST /topics/:topic/lesson/checks/:card/:block[/:step]` and `.../:card/:block/ex/:n[/:part]` with `{response, try, client_event_id}`; `response` is the item template's raw text (number text, `{"n","d"}` JSON for a fraction, the option id for a choice, normalized text), `{"left_id":"right_id"}` JSON for matching and the sorted JSON array of span ids for span_select; the reply is `{verdict, message_it, explain_it?, try, steps?, result_it?}` where `steps` is the blank step and every step after it, with `do_it` (one blank per example is assumed). (5) The solution POST (`.../lesson/exercises/:n/solution`) may answer `solution_it` or `solution_steps` plus `final_it`. (6) Events: `POST /topics/:topic/lesson/events` with `{events: [{kind: "card_seen", card, client_event_id}]}`. (7) "Non ho capito" sends `card` too (the existing control, now with a `card` value). (8) The page asks `Lessons::Progress.for(student, revision)` (`{card:, seen: []}`) for resume and seen marks when that class exists (R3). (9) The teacher's box posts checks to `/teacher/lesson-revisions/:id/checks/...` and exercises to `/teacher/lesson-revisions/:id/exercises/:n/solution`, and reads `/teacher/lesson-revisions/:id/full.json` (the author form, cards by `n`); until R3 the box shows "Le risposte non sono disponibili ora." when that is 404.
- **Why:** the browser's side is fixed by the contract, the prototypes' look comes from CSS and small data-driven components, and nothing about an answer is in the page.
- **Cost / known gaps:** axe-core is not vendored (the spec's test-only library), so the system tests check keys, focus, labels, sizes and overflow but not axe; the manual DSA pass (Orca, VoiceOver, forced colours on a Windows machine) is the pilot's acceptance. `importmap-rails` maps `index.js` to its directory name, so the diagram registry is `lesson/diagrams/registry.js`. Print relayouts the diagrams on the `print` media change; the one-A4-page fit of the summary schema is measured by R4's render check.
- **Status:** decided
- **Back-port:** none.

## D-254 · 2026-10-10 · lesson events, check endpoint, questions by card, the teacher's full body (R3) and what the build closed or corrected

- **Design ref:** D-244, D-246; spec A9, A10, A11, A14, E1 row R3, E3 (R3).
- **Design said:** `lesson_events` with every kind in the CHECK; `student_questions.card`; the check endpoint with `steps` for blanks; the events batch; Oggi resume by card; the teacher's progress line and questions by card; `full.json` with guards; `filter_parameters`.
- **We do:** migration `20261010100001` (table, partial unique index on `(student_id, client_event_id)`, append-only triggers; `ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN card`, the triggers of `student_questions` stay). `LessonEventsController` (`POST /topics/:topic/lesson/events`: batch of 1 to 20, today only `card_seen`, the whole batch refused when one event is wrong, idempotent on `client_event_id`, one `card_seen` per card per 10 minutes kept, the others accepted and dropped). `LessonChecksController` (`.../lesson/checks/:card/:block[/:step]` and `.../ex/:n[/:part]`) over `Lessons::CheckAnswer`: finds the check in the stored body, recomputes the student's `Rekey` seed, grades with `Lessons::Checks`, records `check_answered` (payload `component, response, verdict, code, try` plus `step|ex|part`; `grader_version`). `Lessons::Progress` (`for`, `summary`, `resume_card`) is the only reader of `lesson_events`. `Teacher::LessonRevisionsController`: `GET /teacher/lesson-revisions/:id/full.json` (the stored body), and the box's `POST .../checks/...` (seed "preview", records nothing) and `POST .../exercises/:n/solution`. `QuestionsController` takes `card` (must exist in the revision, section becomes the card's role). `filter_parameters` gains `response`.
- **Choices where the spec was silent or wrong:** (1) The try number is the server's (rows already recorded for that check and locator, plus one), not the browser's; the explanation and the rest of a faded example come at the second wrong answer or a right one. An `invalid` answer (unreadable, longer than 200 characters) is not a try and is not stored. A repeated `client_event_id` answers the same try again and writes nothing; reusing an id on another check is a 422. (2) Step and part in the URL are 1-based (as the renderer sends them); the shuffle seed uses the 0-based `seed_for_step`/`seed_for_exercise` of `StudentBody`. (3) The blank's reply `steps` runs from the blank to the next blank (that blank served as `StudentBody` serves a first one, answer withheld), `result_it` only when no blank is left; the reply also carries `states`, the drawing's merged states from the blank on, which the renderer does not use yet (its figure keeps the states cut before the blank): a follow-up for R2. (4) The box's check and solution POSTs are teacher only: every write of the teacher's area is refused to a guest (`guest_read_only_test`), so a guest sees the box but cannot try its checks; `full.json` is for the teacher and a guest, 403 with no body on the student's computer (`banco_device`) and for any student identity, 404 on the API listener, `no-store`. `full.json` serves a lesson/1 body too (the teacher's page already shows it). (5) The teacher's line "controlli giusti al primo tentativo 5 su 7": 7 is the checks answered at least once (a check = card, block, step, exercise, part), 5 those whose first answer was right; "ultima apertura" is the time of the last lesson event; the line is absent for a lesson/1. (6) "Riprendi" on Oggi opens `/topics/KEY/lesson#scheda-N` when the last `card_seen` of the pinned revision is later than the last practice serve of the topic's skills, else the topic page as before. (7) Questions by card are labelled "Scheda N «titolo»" (position among core cards) or "Approfondimento N «titolo»" (position among extra cards).
- **Isolation:** no file under `app/models/{practice,diagnosis,teacher,course,approval}` or `lib/{diagnosis,practice}` names `lesson_events` or `LessonEvent` (a test scans them); `Practice::Fold` states and the teacher's practice progress are equal before and after twenty answered checks (a test). Checks never write to the practice ledger.
- **Why:** one notion of correct for lesson checks and practice, the answers stay on the server, the teacher sees what was answered, and the lesson ledger needs no table rebuild when 1.1 and 2 add writers.
- **Cost / known gaps:** the student's `response` (up to 200 characters) is stored in `payload_json` and shown to the teacher only; a guest does not see it on the practice page (as the questions). Tries are counted per revision, so a new lesson revision starts again. `more_opened`, `steps_shown`, `lesson_printed` and the `page_*` kinds have no writer yet.
- **Status:** decided
- **Back-port:** none.

## D-255 · 2026-10-10 · render check of a lesson/2 revision (R4): the render host, the runner, lesson_renders, shots and their purge, the gate reason, the teacher line

- **Design ref:** spec A12 (2, 3), A13, A14 (render result), C2, E1 row R4, E3 (R4); D-249 is the design this builds; firm rule 3 (our code only).
- **Design said:** `RenderLessonRevisionJob` after a stored lesson/2 revision, a render host on the harness listener, `Validation::LessonRenderRunner` with overflow, overlapping labels and text too small as errors, `lesson_renders`, WebP shots by content and a purge script, `LessonShotsController` and the API, `banco lesson shots`, a gate reason, one line on the teacher's topic page.
- **We do:** (1) **Host.** `GET /h/:token/lesson-render.html?theme=cream|dark` on the harness listener (`HarnessController#lesson`, token kind `lrev`, a new kind of `Validation::Harness`). The page is `app/views/harness/lesson_render.html.erb`: the student's CSS, the student importmap, KaTeX and the entry `lesson/render_host.js`, with the student's projection of the revision (`Lessons::StudentBody`, seed "preview") and the texts as two JSON blocks. Its CSP allows no connection (`connect-src 'none'`, `default-src 'none'`), scripts only from `'self'` and the page's two inline scripts by hash (computed per page from the rendered HTML), no cookie, `no-store`; the harness listener serves `/assets` and `/vendor` like every listener (the Rack static middleware answers before the routes). (2) **The page's API** (`window.bancoLessonRender`): `ready` (renderAll in the scroll view, then the cards view) and `inspect(n)`, which goes to card n, steps every figure of the card through its states (`api.figures()` is new in `render.js`, as is `config.expand`: every "more" open, every mistake turned, every example step shown, as in safe mode), and reports findings. `render.js` also takes `mode: "render"`. (3) **Findings, all errors:** `E-LESSON-RENDER` (an exception or an unhandled rejection, a `.katex-error`, the lesson not drawing, a card not drawn, a timeout), `E-LESSON-OVERFLOW` (the page wider than the window, or any element of the card, `.l2-card` and the case boxes that clip included, that is wider inside than its box by more than 3 px: a card's own `overflow: hidden` hides such a thing from the eye, not from `scrollWidth`; label boxes excluded), `E-DIAGRAM-LAYOUT` (a figure whose `layout` answered an error, two labels whose text boxes overlap by more than 2 px, a label drawn outside its figure), `E-DIAGRAM-SMALL-TEXT` (a label or SVG text with a computed size under `lesson2.render.min_text_px`). (4) **Runner.** Viewports from `lesson2.render` (`core_viewports`, `extra_viewports`): one fresh Chrome context and page per viewport and theme, the window set by `Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride`; per viewport the cover (looked at, not shot), then the core cards and, at the viewports listed for them, the extra cards (390 cream only). Motion is off in the host (`reduceMotion`), so a shot never catches a fade. The shot is the whole page as the student has it (card, bars, map), taken with the window made as tall as the page (at most 9000 px), so the fixed bar sits under the card as when the student has scrolled to the end; Chrome's `Page.captureScreenshot` as WebP quality 80. A budget of 90 s per revision and 5 s per card-viewport (a card that does not answer: `E-LESSON-RENDER` "timeout", the page is loaded again for the next card); infrastructure trouble (Chrome gone, the host not defining `bancoLessonRender`) is raised, never a verdict. (5) **Print.** "Stampa riassunto e schema" must fit one A4 page (A10 asks for it in the render check): once, at the first viewport, under print media, with `data-print="summary"`, Chrome prints the page to a PDF (A4, 0.4 in margins) and the pages are counted; more than one is `E-LESSON-RENDER` on the summary card. (6) **Storage.** `LessonShots` (`app/models/lesson_shots.rb`): `storage/lesson_shots/<sha256>.webp` (`BANCO_LESSON_SHOTS_DIR` overrides), written once per content, atomically. `bin/purge-lesson-shots [--days N] [--dry-run]` deletes the files named only by renders of a revision that no topic revision pins, that is not the latest of its lesson, and that are older than 30 days; a file that any kept render also names stays; the rows stay and a missing file shows as "immagine rimossa". (7) **Table.** `lesson_renders(lesson_revision_id, status, rules_version, harness_version, chrome_version, attempt, result_json, shots_json, created_at)`, append-only like every primary table. `status` is `passed`, `failed` or `error`; the spec's columns plus `status`, `rules_version` and `attempt` (the same shape as `item_validations`). `harness_version` is `Harness.lesson_version`: the host template, the host script and the `lesson2.render` numbers. `result_json` has `errors` (`code`, `card`, `viewport`, `message`, `where`), `cards`, `viewports`, `elapsed_seconds`, `exceptions`; `shots_json` lists `card`, `level`, `viewport`, `sha256`, `bytes`, `width`, `height`. (8) **Job.** `RenderLessonRevisionJob` on the `chrome` queue (one thread, ChromeRunner's lock) at priority 10 (item validation keeps 0: lower runs first); `LessonsController` of the API enqueues it after a stored lesson/2 revision, not on a dry run and not on a replay. A verdict made under the same `harness_version` is final; Chrome trouble appends an `error` row per attempt (3 attempts, 30 s apart per execution) and never a pass. A revision stored before R4 has no render: `bin/rails runner 'RenderLessonRevisionJob.perform_later(ID)'`. (9) **API and CLI.** `banco lesson status REV` gains `render` (status, errors, counts of shots and of files still there, times); `GET /api/v1/lesson-revisions/:revision/shots` lists the shots of the latest verdict and `.../shots/:sha` serves one image (a purged one is 404 "immagine rimossa"); `banco lesson shots REV --dir D` writes `card-NN_WIDTHxHEIGHT-theme.webp`; `lesson-review open` carries `render` and `shots_url` for a lesson/2. (10) **Teacher.** `GET /teacher/lesson-revisions/:id/shots` (a page of every picture by card, for the teacher and the guest, the operator's acceptance; the strip in the topic page is release 1.1) and `.../shots/:sha` (the image, 410 when purged). The topic page's box starts with the one line "Controllo grafico: nessun errore (35 immagini)" or the errors by card with a link that opens the box on that card (`lesson2_preview_controller.js#goto`). (11) **Gate.** `Approval::TopicGate.mechanical_reasons` adds, for a lesson/2 revision only, "the lesson revision has no render without errors" with three texts (not run, could not run, found N errors with the first codes and cards); the topic page groups them as the checklist line "Il controllo grafico della lezione non ha errori" and `Teacher::Wording` says them in Italian. The gate reads the latest row of the revision: a later `error` row does not hide a failed verdict, but a later pass clears it.
- **Where the spec was adjusted:** (a) `E-DIAGRAM-SMALL-TEXT` cannot come out of the data of a card in this renderer, because `layout` never draws a label under the base size (`label()` takes `max(px, fontPx)` and `fontPx` is at least 18); the check is a guard against CSS that shrinks a label, tested by injecting such a style in Chrome. The spec's fixture list (an over-long label, a too dense number line, a 1400 px table) gives `E-DIAGRAM-LAYOUT` for the first two (the layout's own error at 390 px, labels outside the figure at 1280) and `E-LESSON-OVERFLOW` for the third. (b) The spec's text-size rule covers "any text or label"; the check reads diagram labels and SVG text only, because the interface's own small buttons and kickers are legitimately under 18 px. (c) The render check found a real overflow in R2's page on its first run: the pager of "Prova tu" (`.try-nav`) did not wrap at 390 px and cut "Esercizio dopo"; `flex-wrap: wrap` fixes it. (d) Page-level errors with no card (a lesson that does not draw, a budget) show on the teacher's line as "Tutta la lezione". (e) The cover is looked at at every viewport but not shot: 11 core cards at three viewports and 2 extra cards at one are 35 shots, the spec's estimate; the teacher's line counts shots.
- **Known limit:** the shots are named by their content, so an unchanged card costs nothing only when Chrome paints the same pixels: the raster of one image in a run can differ by a sub-pixel antialiasing (seen once in about ten runs on a bottom-bar button), which costs one more file, not a wrong one; the test allows up to three.
- **Fixed after review (was: known issue found by looking at the shots):** the `≠` of the invented lesson (`a ≠ 0` in the case schema, and the points of the summary) is drawn as a missing-glyph box in the development machine's headless Chrome. The cause is real: the vendored Atkinson Hyperlegible woff2 files do not contain U+2260, and `lesson.css` sets the KaTeX relations (`.mrel`) to inherit the body font, so the glyph comes from the system fallback, which that Chrome does not have. A student's laptop has one, the server's banco-chrome may not. The render check does not detect a missing glyph; the shots show it. A fix belongs to R2 (let `.mrel` and `.mbin` fall back to the vendored KaTeX_Main, which has the symbols). Fixed in `lesson.css`: the KaTeX classes now use the stack `"Atkinson Hyperlegible", KaTeX_Main, Verdana, sans-serif`, so a glyph Atkinson lacks comes from KaTeX_Main, which the page already loads; `test/lib/lesson_css_test.rb` pins the stack. The render check still does not detect a missing glyph.
- **Measured:** the invented 11 core + 2 extra card lesson of `test/fixtures/lesson2/served/equations.json` renders in about 11 s on the development machine (three viewports, 35 shots); the 90 s of the pilot on the server is measured when the pilot is stored.
- **Why:** a card that overflows, a label drawn over another or a formula KaTeX refuses shows only when drawn; the author, the reviewer and the teacher must see it before the student does, and the reviewer needs the pictures.
- **Cost:** about 2.5 MB of WebP per revision, a job of up to 90 s below item validation; a lesson/2 topic cannot be approved without a passed render.
- **Number:** D-255 on the rl-r4 branch (D-254 is left to the R3 branch) label).
- **Status:** decided
- **Back-port:** none (D-249 stays as the design).

## D-256 · 2026-10-10 · rich lessons, the look of the pilot (E7): one slim bar, the balance in 2D, equations as member tiles, digits without a slash, the not-equal sign, no red or green in the equations' roles

- **Design ref:** spec A4 (blocks), A6 (roles), A7 (diagrams), A10 (the page), E7 (the prototype's mapping); D-246, D-253.
- **Design said:** the page of D-253 (a top bar with the counter, a toolbar, the thin positional bar), the balance of A7 as boxes and weights on two pans, the equations in KaTeX in the body font, colour roles by `\role{}` written by the author.
- **We do:** (1) **Chrome.** In a lesson the layout's trial notice, draft notice, student menu and "Torna all'argomento" stay in the page (the server renders them, the tests read them) but are hidden by `body.student:has(.l2-top)`; the bar reads them and folds them into one chip ("Prova", "Bozza", the full text as its title) and one "Menu" button that opens a dialog with the way back, the menu and the notices. The bar is one row: a mark, "Ripasso di matematica" over the lesson title, "Scheda N di M", the chip, and icon buttons for the map, the text and colours and the print (their words show on large screens, as a title everywhere and as a tooltip on focus), the thin positional bar under it. "Vedi tutte le schede" lives only in the settings dialog. The card starts at about 97 px on 1366x900; a test pins 140. (2) **Balance.** `balance.js` draws the prototype's balance as plain shapes: a beam on a stand with a base, pans (`bl-pan-left`, `bl-pan-right`) in the member colours, boxes as rounded purple squares with an "x" (always "x": the number tried was drawn in the box and showed as a slashed zero; it is now `x = N` beside the stepper), the units as brass bells with a "1". The beam and the pans are `group` shapes with a `move` (translate, rotate); `draw.js` keeps the last move of each key and lets a CSS transition run from it to the new one (no animation under reduced motion, a resize, or a change of width). New shape kinds: `ellipse`, `text` (SVG text, never under the base size), `group`. Above the drawing: the state's name ("Bilancia 1 di 3"), the equation as tiles, a status chip (in equilibrio / pende a sinistra / pende a destra); the try has large round buttons, `x = N`, both members and one line. (3) **Equations.** `lesson/eq.js` adds the roles to plain TeX: x, y, z as `unknown`, numbers as `known` (exponents and what the author wrapped in `\role` are left), and for a displayed equation (a `math` block, a paragraph that is only a formula, and, with `tiles`, the formulas with "=" in an example's problem and steps, a mistake, an exercise, a case) the two members as `left` and `right` tiles; `\to` chains tile each equation. Formulas in running text only get the colours. (4) **Cards.** The legend line is shown only on the card where a role first appears, and the map (side and dialog) lists them all; callouts have a big icon, a label and a tint; a procedure is a mnemonic of pills and numbered cards; an example has the problem, step cards with a verb tag, "Mostra il primo passo", "Mostra tutto" and "passo n di N"; a mistake is one card that turns on a touch; the cover is the title, the first sentence of `why_it` as one line, the large balance, the goals as three tiles, the start button, and the card list folded away; the summary has icon rows and the schema in the ink colour. (5) **Palette** (version stays 1: no lesson was approved on it): `known` is a dark ochre (`#5c3a00`), `left` a deep teal-blue, `right` a rust (`#7d3718` text, `#cc6a2a` mark); no role of the equations is red or green (`LessonPaletteTest`, and a system test on the drawn fills). (6) **Type.** The lesson's digits come from "Banco Digits", the digits of the vendored KaTeX_SansSerif (Atkinson Hyperlegible draws a slashed zero and has no feature to turn it off); "Banco Symbols" (`public/vendor/banco-symbols@1`, built by `bin/build-symbols-font` from KaTeX_Main's "=" and a slash) draws U+2260 in running text; KaTeX's own composed `\neq` keeps KaTeX's fonts (the stack of `.mrel` had sent its private-use glyph to Atkinson).
- **Why:** the lead compared the first pilot render with the prototype the operator liked: 400 px of chrome above the card, a red pan, a slashed zero for x, flat formulas and a legend on every card.
- **Cost:** one more vendored directory (two 2 KB fonts); the colours of two roles changed (a lesson stored before reads them from the palette, not from its data); the figure's SVG text is not an HTML label, so overlap detection does not read it.
- **Not done:** the 3D cover is release 1.1; the prototype's lab with move buttons is a different component (the try and the states of the balance are its place for now).
- **Status:** decided
- **Back-port:** none.

## D-257 · 2026-10-10 · rich lessons, round 2 of the pilot look: short names of cards, the lab beside the picture, cases as compact rows with one stepper, a centred schema, a bold not-equal sign

- **We do:** (1) A card heading may carry `short="Name"` (2 to 28 characters, quoted, no braces or `$`): body field `short_it`, served to the browser, used by the map and the Avanti button; without it the title up to its colon. The long title stays in the card heading only; the kicker above it no longer repeats "Scheda N di M" (the top bar says it). (2) A balance with controls (states or a try) is a two-column lab on a wide container: picture on the left, stepper, member tiles and verdict on the right; items shrink when a pan is crowded. (3) `cases` are compact rows (name, condition, text, a small balance); when several cases draw balances and one has a `try`, one stepper on top sets x in all of them (`api.setTry`). (4) Mistakes are a uniform two-column grid with a one-line intro and an icon on each group heading. (5) The summary points get an icon each (a keyword picks it, otherwise the next of a short list). (6) A flow that is a tree and fits the width is drawn centred with arrows and a dark first box; otherwise the indented layout. (7) `\neq` and `\ne` render as the character U+2260 from "Banco Symbols", rebuilt with two bars and a slash at the stroke of Atkinson (regular and bold); KaTeX's composed glyph is gone. (8) The cover has the Comincia button under the lead; the balance has soft shadows.
- **Why:** the lead's second comparison with the prototype: the three-cases card filled the screen, the lab was below the fold, titles wrapped to three lines in the map, the schema was a left-aligned stack, the not-equal sign was thin.
- **Cost:** one optional card field (schema, parser, projection); a keyword list in `summary.js` that only knows Italian words of the pilot's kind (the fallback is neutral); the font files changed (checksums).
- **Not done:** the 3D cover (1.1); a semantic icon per summary point chosen by the author.
- **Status:** decided
- **Back-port:** none.

## D-258 · 2026-10-10 · rich lessons, round 3 of the pilot look: the bar never overflows on a phone, the picture first, big equation tiles, quiet balance steps, compact mistakes

- **We do:** (1) The top bar keeps its buttons inside the screen: the counter shrinks and has a short form on a phone ("5 di 14", "Approf. 1 di 2"), the buttons and the chip do not shrink; the bottom bar drops the word "Avanti:" below 420 px. (2) A callout written before the first picture of a card is drawn after it (`visualFirst`), tinted blue (rule) or brass (tip) and compact; the legend chip sits at the end of the first card where a role appears, not under the title. (3) The steps of a balance are "Passo indietro" and "Passo avanti", small and outlined, so the one big "Avanti" is the bottom bar's; a crowded balance shrinks its items down to 0.55 so that the stage has little dead height. (4) The problem of a worked example ("Risolvi $...$.") is drawn as the big pair of member tiles with the lead word above; the parts of `equation_parts` are drawn at up to 1.9 times the body size. (5) Mistakes: the group is the tag of each card (no heading row, so no empty slots), the "Sbagliato" word and the hint are for the screen reader, the hint is an eye icon; "Non ho capito" is a quiet text button at the foot. (6) The "more" panel reads "Per saperne di più: Title". (7) In the summary the key word of a point is bold (`**..**` in the source) and in the primary colour.
- **Why:** the lead's review of the pilot against the prototype: the bar overflowed at 390 px on the appendix cards, the rule callout pushed the balance below the fold, two "Avanti" buttons competed, equations were small, mistakes left empty slots.
- **Cost:** `lesson.it.yml` has `card_short`, `extra_short`; the group headings of mistakes are no longer elements of their own (the test counts the tags).
- **Not done:** a slider for the three cases; key and no-entry icons (a new icon is a D entry and a vendored Lucide file); the 3D cover (1.1).
- **Status:** decided
- **Back-port:** none.

## D-259 · 2026-10-11 · rich lessons, round 4 of the pilot look: the exercise pager, the one-line answer, flip cards under headings, a short balance on a phone

- **We do:** (1) "Prova tu": one compact pager (previous, the number chips, next, on one row; the "Esercizio N di M" line stays for the screen reader only), the exercise first with no card around it, and the answer of an exercise is a line "x = [  ] [-] [/] Controlla" with the helper keys (a number gets "-" and ","); a `fraction` check without a mixed form is typed on one line in the lesson ("3", "-5/3", "5/2") and sent to the server as `{n, d}` (an integer is over 1), so the grading and its typical errors do not change; the stacked fraction boxes stay for mixed numbers and for the practice items. The sentence "metti 1 al denominatore" is gone from the four solve exercises of the pilot lesson; the page says "Le frazioni si scrivono con la barra: 5/2." under the line. (2) "Errori da evitare": the kinds are headings over their cards, every card says "Tocca per girare", the intro is one full-width line with only "Tocca una carta" bold. (3) A balance on a phone (up to 600 px): the stepper "- x = N +" sits above the drawing in one row, the drawing is at most 9.5 em tall, both members are one row, the steps buttons sit side by side; a chain of equations that starts with the equation the balance above it already shows loses that first line (`dropRepeatedStart`). (4) A line label of a graph keeps off the drawn lines (`labelNear` with `avoid`); the labels above or below an equation never let a connector cross another label (`stackLabels`); the options of an answer are full-width buttons without the numbered badge (the keys 1 to 5 still pick); an example shows its first step greyed before it is asked for.
- **Why:** the visual review of round 3 against the prototype.
- **Cost:** `lesson.it.yml` has `helper_keys`, `key_minus`, `key_bar`, `key_comma`, `fraction_line_hint`, `mistakes_tap`, `mistake_flip`; `mistakes_intro` has a `%{tap}` marker. The pilot lesson data lost four `answer_format_it` lines (re-import).
- **Status:** decided
- **Back-port:** none.

## D-260 · 2026-10-12 · the operator may record a teacher decision from the host console, never over HTTP

- **Design ref:** firm rule 2, D-08, D-059..D-062, D-074
- **Design said:** decisions are taken by the teacher in the browser (web listener only); no `/api/v1` route creates one and the CLI has no decision command.
- **Operator request (2026-10-12, verbatim):** "all approved proceed can you approve from here? If not implement the api then approve them".
- **We do:** `bin/rails banco:decide KIND=... TEACHER=<login> [SUBJECT=] [REVISION=] [REASON=] [PARAMS=json] [CONFIRM=1]` records a decision through `DecisionRecorder`, still the only writer, with every business guard of the kind (gates, latest-revision checks, reasons). The web-only guards (listener, edge proxy, CSRF, student device cookie) are replaced by: TEACHER is in `BANCO_TEACHER_USERS`, `BANCO_DECISIONS_ENABLED=1`, and the code runs only in a console process (`DecisionRecorder::Console` is not a request; no route, controller or job reaches it). The task is a dry run unless `CONFIRM=1` (the recorder runs in a rolled-back savepoint and prints the payload or the refusal reasons). Approving a graph or an entry test that is already the approved one is refused. Provenance: `teacher_login` = TEACHER, `remote_addr` and `groups` = `console`, `user_agent` = `banco:decide <os user>`, `request_path` = `rake banco:decide`, a fresh uuid as request id; the payload carries `via: "console"` and, for a kind without a reason, `console_reason`. The graph and entry test pages add "(da console)" next to the approval; `bin/reconcile-decisions` accepts the console group. The agent API token gains nothing: no route, no CLI command.
- **Why:** the lead refused an API route: the agent token is shared by the content agents, and a route that decides, even behind a flag, would let an agent decide for the teacher, which is what rule 2 prevents. A console command needs a shell on the host, which only the operator has, as with the reference import (D-074). The console guard is host-shell access (as D-074), and the web path has no "already approved" check while the console path does.
- **Cost:** a decision by console is as strong as a click: the operator must name the teacher and mean it; the ledger shows `console` so it can be told apart.
- **Attestation (2026-10-12, same day):** the operator read the lessons outside the app and said (verbatim) "Ok ho letto le lezioni di italiano e matematica tutte approvate" and then "approvale da qui"; `approve_topic` from the console was refused by `Approval::TopicGate` ("the topic review page of revision N was not opened"). `bin/rails banco:decide KIND=approve_topic ... ATTEST_IT="<the operator's own words>"` (`DecisionConsole attest_it:`) evaluates the gate with exactly one requirement waived: the page was opened (reason 5) and the confirmation that goes with it (reason 6, `confirm_seen`). Every other requirement holds and is tested to refuse: latest topic revision, topic in the latest course map, no stale pins, independent lesson review, lesson not sent back, render check, every pinned item through `Review::Gate`, and the reason for blocker or major findings. `ATTEST_IT` is accepted only on the console path and only for `approve_topic` (any other kind refuses it; the recorder refuses it from a non-console origin; the web controller does not permit it, so a POST carrying it is ignored and the gate still wants the page opened). The words are required, non-blank, at most 1000 characters. The payload records `attested: true`, `attest_it` and `waived: ["topic_review_page_not_opened"]`; no `teacher_viewed_topic`, `teacher_read_lesson` or `teacher_saw_exercise` event is written, so nothing pretends a page view. The topic page and the course path show "Approvato da console, senza aprire la pagina di revisione: «...»" for such an approval. The attestation is the operator's statement, not evidence the app can check: that is the cost, and why it is visible.
- **Attestation for approve_blueprint (2026-10-13, same mechanism):** the operator said (verbatim) "pronti per iniziare con andrea abilita tutti i test di ingresso". The entry tests could not be opened in the preview one question at a time, so `approve_blueprint` from the console now also takes `ATTEST_IT` (accepted for `approve_topic` and `approve_blueprint` only; any other kind refuses it, the recorder refuses it from a non-console origin, the web path is unchanged and ignores it). With the words, `Approval::BlueprintGate.check(waive_preview: true)` waives exactly two requirements: every "item revision N was not opened in the preview" reason, and "the test was not played to the end as the preview student, and not confirmed as seen in full". Everything else still refuses and is tested: the approved graph revision, guest skills, pinned items existing, `Review::Gate` of each item (blocker or major findings without the teacher's disposition, sent-back revisions), stale pins, multi-skill testlets, and the latest-revision check. The payload records `attested: true`, `attest_it` and `waived: ["items_not_opened_in_preview", "test_not_played_or_confirmed"]`; no `teacher_viewed_item` event and no preview run is written. The teacher's test page shows "Approvato da console, senza aprire le domande in anteprima: «...»" next to the approval. Same cost as above: the words are the operator's statement, visible in the ledger and on the page.
- **Status:** implemented
- **Back-port:** none.

## D-261 · 2026-10-13 · the warm-up is optional and always recallable; the release needs only consent and approvals

- **Design ref:** D-061 (release needs consent and the warm-up), D-240 (the warm-up before the release, the "Riscaldamento" menu item), D-217 (trial students), B-11
- **Design said:** `release_diagnosis` needs the consent, the warm-up completed and every subject approved; the warm-up page is open before the release only (for the official student) and Oggi offers it as the first step.
- **Operator request (2026-10-13, verbatim):** "facciamo in modo che il riscaldamento sia facoltativo e al massimo richiamabile".
- **We do:** supersedes the warm-up part of D-061 and the pre-release warm-up rule of D-240. `release_diagnosis` needs the consent, at least one subject and every subject with an approved graph and an approved entry test; no reason mentions the warm-up. The warm-up page and its endpoints are open to the official and the trial students, before and after the release, and can be done again (a new round after each `warmup_completed`; it never counts and writes no attempt in a run). No sitting, subject start or test depends on it. Oggi: before the release the block shows the line that the tests open when the teacher opens them and a secondary button for the optional warm-up (worded "rifarla" when done); after the release the subjects come first and the warm-up is one small line under them ("Vuoi provare i comandi prima? Riscaldamento, facoltativo"). The Test d'ingresso page links it after the release too. The menu is unchanged (the "Riscaldamento" item before the release while the warm-up is not done; "Test d'ingresso" after). The teacher's dashboard no longer lists the warm-up among what is missing to release; the state line reads "Prova dei comandi: fatta / non fatta (facoltativa)". `status` keeps `warmup_completed`.
- **Why:** the warm-up was a gate that the student had to pass before the teacher could open the tests; it only checks the controls and measures nothing.
- **Cost:** the teacher may open the diagnosis for a student who never tried the editor; the editor fallback to a text box is still written during a sitting when the editor fails.
- **Status:** implemented
- **Back-port:** none.

## D-262 · 2026-10-12 · firm rule 3 amended: agent-written free pages run only in browsers, sandboxed on pages.banco.scc.im; the teacher's approval covers content and behaviour tried, not code

- **Design ref:** firm rule 3; D-244 (F1: free pages yes, after release 1, firm rule 3 amended in its own D entry written and merged before any free-page work); SPEC B (free pages), B8, B10, B11, E4
- **Design said:** firm rule 3: "Agent-written code runs only in browsers (the server's Chrome at validation). Rails and the grader worker never execute it." Free pages (layer 3 of the rich lessons) put agent-written JavaScript in the student's and the teacher's browsers, which the old text read as forbidden.
- **We do:** the operator approved the amendment on 2026-10-09 (F1) and the origin `pages.banco.scc.im` (same site as the app, a separate origin). **New text of rule 3:** agent-written code runs only in browsers: the server's Chrome at validation and the render check, and approved free pages in the student's and the teacher's browsers, inside a sandboxed frame on the separate origin `pages.banco.scc.im`. Rails and the grader worker never execute it: Rails stores bytes, hashes them, scans them with a regex and serves them. **Sandbox (B3, B4, B10):** the frame has an opaque origin (no `allow-same-origin`), a CSP `sandbox` header, `connect-src 'none'`, no forms, no popups, no top navigation; cookies are stripped at the edge; the app answers `frame-ancestors 'none'` and `X-Frame-Options: DENY`.
