A page has nothing personal to send: its seed (one of eight), the theme, the text size and the student's interactions with the page itself; no name, no identity, no answers, no cookies. **Validation and review (B7, B8):** every page revision is validated in the server's Chrome on every seed (network log, budgets, a scripted session, visibility and resize) and reviewed by a session of the reviewer role that wrote no revision of the page and is of a model family different from every author, on 11 points and a plain diff against the previous revision; the author and the reviewer never read the course sources for a page. **What the teacher's approval covers:** `approve_topic` carries one confirmation per pinned page ("Ho provato ..."): the teacher approves what the page shows and teaches (content, look, behaviour he tried), **not its code**; he cannot audit JavaScript and is not asked to. The safety of the code rests on the sandbox and the CSP, the validation and the independent review; the operator, by approving F1, accepted that division. **Residuals accepted (B11):** the CSP does not cover WebRTC, so "no network" is not claimed (the scan bans the names, the kit stubs the constructors, the self-test records what each browser lets through; what holds is that the page has nothing personal to send); a branch on a long interaction count that the scripted session does not reach and the reviewer misses can still only draw inside its frame, and the teacher's send-back path removes it; a hostile loop could freeze a tab in a browser that keeps the frame in-process (Firefox, same site); self-navigation of the frame cannot be blocked by CSP and is caught by the scan and validation and killed by the watchdog. **Switch:** `BANCO_PAGES_ENABLED`. **Unchanged:** rules 1, 2, 4, 5 and 6; the components of the rich lessons stay data drawn by our code (agents write data, our templates draw it); a program in a lesson's `program` diagram is parsed in Ruby and run only in the server's Chrome (the wave 2 entry on render-time records).
- **Why:** the operator asked for anything a web page can do where the components cannot; the third layer needs this wording to exist, and the entry says in plain words what the teacher's click means.
- **Cost:** the free-page track (tables with triggers, the pages app and listener, the kit, the infrastructure) is built after this entry and not before; until then rule 3 means what it said for everything in the repository.
- **Status:** decided (the rule and its wording; no free-page code in this entry)
- **Back-port:** none.

## D-263 · 2026-10-12 · wave 2 of the rich lessons: the request, the 18 lessons, the batches W2-0 to W2-3, the lesson keys, the tracks, the first-look cut

- **Design ref:** D-244 to D-262; the nine subject designs; the plan of wave 2 (private working material, revision 2 with the critique answered)
- **Design said:** Release 1 gave two subjects (math, italian) six lessons at the level of the pilot. The other nine subjects have no lesson/2: no palette, no icons, no step verbs, and none of the pictures their topics need (a map, a climograph, a cell, a register, a document).
- **We do:** Operator, 2026-10-11: the math pilot is perfect; do the other subjects, at least two lessons each, see how each comes out and works, not the obvious, and where a subject needs something special make it. **Eighteen lessons** (two per subject), staged: the nine first lessons are the operator's first look at each subject, and a subject's second lesson is submitted after he has tried its first on the student's device. **Batches:** W2-0 (this entry: the contracts, one builder), W2-1 (the pieces of the nine first lessons), W2-2 (the second lessons'), W2-3 (3D styles, `calendar`, `chart` pyramid and scatter, `bar_model` fraction, `cartesian` sliders, `column_calc` repeated division, `scale` bytes, `rgb`, `sheet`, `cell_formula`, `trace`, `display.diagram` in practice items, the release 1.1 leftovers). **Names:** 29 diagram types (28 new and `bar_model`), extensions of `flow`, `sentence`, `cartesian` and `number_line`, five blocks (`source`, `reveal`, `oral`, `dialogue`, `image`), six check components, seven check options, ten domain libraries, fifteen data tables. **Lesson keys** are slugs, never "lesson 1" or "lesson 2" (the designs number theirs differently): `lezione.english.future-time-clauses` and `ripasso.english.irregular-verbs-passive`, `lezione.spanish.pronoun-pairs` and `ripasso.spanish.present-stem-change`, `ponte.history.republic-to-empire` and `lezione.history.augustus-principate`, `ripasso.geography.climates-biomes` and `lezione.geography.brazil-amazon`, `lezione.law_economics.parliament-lawmaking` and `ripasso.law_economics.contract-obligation`, `ripasso.business.invoice-total` and `lezione.business.payment-instruments`, `lezione.biology.nucleic-acids` and `ponte.biology.cell-basics`, `ponte.chemistry.symbols-formulas` and `lezione.chemistry.states-heating-curve`, `lezione.computer_science.twos-complement` and `ponte.computer_science.flowchart-variables-conditions-loops`. **Tracks** T1 core and checks, T2 text and voice, T3 words and languages, T4a time, T4b graphs, T5 maps, T6 charts, T7 science, T8 documents and blocks, T9 computing, T10 3D, T11 free pages, T12 practice display; at most six builder sessions at a time. Agents push branches; the lead lands them. **First-look cut:** if `map` is the last missing piece of `republic-to-empire` or `climates-biomes`, the lesson is submitted with the designers' release 1 fallbacks on its map cards, the operator previews it, and the map revision follows; the topic goes to the teacher only with the map. **The audience:** the student studies on a Mac or an iPad with Safari (D-266): features are checked against Safari, and Chrome is the render check's browser. **W2-0 delivers** the contracts: D-260 first, then the component contract v2, the schemas (W2-1 final, W2-2 drafts marked `x-banco-draft`, W2-3 names reserved), the registry, palette v2, the icon lists and step verbs, the error codes (registry version 20), the caps (rules version 9), the data-table schemas, the library signatures with vector skeletons, the stub modules, the gallery skeletons, the subject briefs and these entries. No migration in W2-0 and W2-1: select, tiles, ordering and `oral` answers are `check_answered` events, speech preferences are `student_preference` app events, `program` records live in `lesson_renders.result_json`; `lesson_assets` (W2-2) and the free-page tables come later with triggers and `bin/check-structure`.
- **Number:** D-263 (the plan's W2-D01 label).
- **Why:** Two lessons per subject let the operator see how each subject looks and works before the rest is written; freezing the shared files once, in one place, lets ten tracks build without touching each other.
- **Cost:** Large: about 85 pieces proposed became 29 types, 5 blocks and 6 checks (eleven names merged after the critique); each piece is a schema, Ruby checks, a browser module, vectors both ways, a gallery card, a look gate and an entry. The staging delays the second lessons until the operator has looked at the first.
- **Status:** decided (the contracts of W2-0; the pieces they name are built by their tracks, each with its own entry)
- **Back-port:** none.

## D-264 · 2026-10-12 · palette v2: roles scoped by subject, same_as, home palettes, the nine subject setups, the mixed-palette test, per-subject sprites

- **Design ref:** D-246 (palette, carriers, icons), D-256; spec A6
- **Design said:** One CSS custom property per role name, the first definition of a name wins, `bin/build-palette` reads math and italian only, `icons.yml` has two subject lists and one sprite.
- **We do:** `lesson_palette.yml` version 2 has the eleven subjects. **Scoping:** variables are `--r-SUBJECT-ROLE-(fg|mark|tint)`, `common` is `--r-common-*`; the classes (`.role-x`, `.mk-x`, `.st-x`, `.fl-x`, `.tn-x`, `.card-tone-x`) read generic `--role-x-*` variables that each `[data-palette="SUBJECT"]` element maps to its own subject's, so the nearest palette ancestor decides (a custom property is inherited from the nearest element that sets it; two subjects may use `right` or `base` for different things, and a role may be position in one subject and an icon in another). The lesson's root carries `data-palette` = its subject; a figure of a type with `x-banco-home-palette` (`balance`, `equation_parts` math; `cell`, `strand` biology; `formula`, `molecule`, `particles`, `phase_changes` chemistry; `register`, `column_calc` computer science) carries its home subject's. **`same_as: SUBJECT.ROLE`** makes a role take another subject's colours, icon and shape (english `subject`, `verb`, `object`, `agent`, `time` and spanish `verb`, `od` are the Italian roles, history `cause` is Italian `cause`); `label_it` and `question_it` may differ. **`centre_role`** (italian predicate, english and spanish verb) for `sentence layout: centre`. **`embeds`**: computer science draws math's `unknown`, `known`, `left`, `right` (the balance of the flowchart lesson) and biology draws chemistry's `coefficient` and `subscript` (sugars). **Roles** (eight at most per subject, `same_as` copies included): english `auxiliary`, `main`, `participle`; spanish `oi`, `stem`, `ending`, `stress`, `trap`; history `rome`, `other`, `senate`, `princeps`, `effect`, `date`, `source`; geography `temperature`, `precipitation`, `arid`, `hot`, `temperate`, `cold`, `place`, `flow`; law_economics `right`, `duty`, `people`, `legislative`, `executive`, `judicial`, `guarantee`, `norm`; business `creditor`, `debtor`, `bank`, `third`, `base`, `tax`, `outside`, `discount`; biology `phosphate`, `sugar`, `base`, `pair_at`, `pair_cg`, `prokaryote`, `eukaryote`, `plant`; chemistry `coefficient`, `subscript`, `group`, `solid`, `liquid`, `gas`, `heat_in`, `heat_out`; computer science `variable`, `condition`, `weight`, `sign`, `carry`, `reference`, `locked`, `output` (the designer's `code` is dropped: `[[code:...]]` is a span). The reserved span kinds `en es it la code g` are never role names; role names may use underscores (the markup grammar, both parsers and the schemas accept `[a-z]+([_-][a-z]+)*`). The colours were found by a search that keeps text 7:1, marks 3:1 and the colour-vision distance (12 between two roles that rely on colour alone, 6 when one has an icon; the best pair of every subject is at least 1.5 times the threshold), and the accent bands are pale tints of distinct hues. **Marker shapes** gain `pentagon` (the sugar). **Step verbs** for the nine subjects are the designers' (`step_tags`); each icon is in the subject's list or the structural list. **Icons:** `icons.yml` version 2 has a list per subject (at most 30), 123 Lucide files are vendored beside the 69 (same release 1.54.0, ISC), and `bin/build-icons` builds `banco-sprite.svg` (structural and ui) plus `banco-sprite-SUBJECT.svg`; `palette.js` maps every icon to its sprite and `icon()` and the diagram `icon` shape follow it. New ui icons: `listen`, `listen-stop`, `slower`, `glossary`. **The palette test** runs per subject on the resolved roles and on every mix a page can show (a subject with the `embeds` of its home palettes), plus `same_as` validity.
- **Number:** D-264 (the plan's W2-D02 label).
- **Why:** Wave 2 would otherwise recolour law's `right` with math's and business's `base` with biology's; the same meaning keeping the same colour across subjects is the point of the colour roles.
- **Cost:** Larger generated files (`lesson_roles.css` about 50 KB, `palette.js` about 27 KB, 12 sprites of at most 11 KB each loaded on demand); a role added later needs the search again.
- **Status:** decided (the contracts of W2-0; the pieces they name are built by their tracks, each with its own entry)
- **Back-port:** none.

## D-265 · 2026-10-12 · availability registry lesson_types.yml, lazy types and modulepreload, the reserved dry run, per-type files, stubs and galleries

- **Design ref:** D-245 (`RELEASE`/`BUILT` of the directives), D-247, D-252, D-253
- **Design said:** A block of a later release is refused by an earlier parser from two constants in `directives.rb`; the browser imports every diagram type at once (66 KB gzip).
- **We do:** `config/banco/lesson_types.yml` lists every diagram type, block, check component and check option with `status` (`available`, `reserved`, `draft`), `schema` (`final`, `draft`, `none`), `batch`, `track`, `family`, `module` and the views, layouts, kinds and options that are held back. `Lessons::Types` reads it; `Directives.build` refuses what is not available (`E-LESSON-BLOCK`, "is not available yet") down to a layout (`flow layout: line`), a view (`bar_model view: fraction`), a kind (`document kind: contract`) or a check option (`listen`, `verify`); with `allow_reserved:` a reserved or draft name passes for the dry run, which validates it against its frozen or draft schema and reports `W-TYPE-RESERVED` or `W-TYPE-DRAFT` (the header and the CLI flag are T1's); a lesson with such a use can never be stored, rendered or reach `awaiting_teacher`. `bin/build-lesson-types` generates `lesson/diagrams/registry.js` (the available types imported at once, the others behind lazy loaders with `load` and `preload`, `STATUS`, `HOME_PALETTE`, `FAMILY`, `HELD_BACK`), `lesson/checks/registry.js` and `lesson/voices.js` (CI checks them like `bin/build-palette --check`). The page head will carry a `modulepreload` for each type the lesson's body uses (T1). **Schemas:** `diagram.json` holds the 26 new types with a schema (`x-banco-release` is the batch, `x-banco-draft` marks the W2-2 ones; `calendar`, `rgb` and `sheet` are names only), `flow` is both a schema and a diagram (`layout: line`; `walk` is a draft), `sentence` takes `text_it`, `text_en` or `text_es`; `lesson.json` gains the blocks `source`, `reveal`, `oral`, `dialogue`, `image`, the checks `select`, `tiles`, `ordering`, `amount_words`, the check options and the front matter `glossary`, `teaches_en`, `teaches_es`. `bin/build-diagram-schema` now writes the release 1 schema and one `lesson/diagram_schemas/TYPE.js` per new type, so a lesson loads only the schemas of its types. **Per-type files:** `lesson/diagrams/FAMILY/TYPE.js` (the families `graph time maps chart science computing words docs`), `lib/lessons/diagrams/TYPE.rb` (stubs that `extend Lessons::Diagrams::Contract`), vectors `test/fixtures/diagrams/types/TYPE.json`, `app/assets/stylesheets/lesson/FAMILY.css`, `config/locales/lesson_FAMILY.it.yml` and the gallery skeleton `test/fixtures/lesson2/gallery/FAMILY.md`. **Caps:** `lesson2.types` in `validation_rules.yml` (rules version 9) holds the per-type numbers and `lesson2.apparatus_words` 250, `closed_original_words` 240, `card_source_only_visual_max` 3, `one_per_card`, the target-language limits and the budgets; `Lessons::Blocks` counts `source`, `dialogue`, `oral`, `image` and a `reveal` with options as visuals and `Lesson2Checks` enforces one of each per card and at most three cards whose only visual is a `source`. **Error codes** (registry version 20): `E-LESSON-DATA`, `E-LESSON-VERIFY`, `E-CHECK-ANSWER-IN-ALT`, `W-CHECK-ANSWER-IN-DIAGRAM`, `E-CHECK-ANSWER-BY-SIMULATION`, `E-DIAGRAM-REACHABLE-CAP`, `E-SELECT-MARKED`, `E-DIAGRAM-TARGET`, `W-TYPE-RESERVED`, `W-TYPE-DRAFT`, `E-PROGRAM-BOUND`, `E-LESSON-APPARATUS-WORDS`, `E-CHEM-SYMBOL`, `W-ES-TILDE`, `E-LESSON-LANG`, `W-LANG-LEVEL`; the bad fixture of each is described under `pending` in the manifest until its track writes it. **Briefs:** `briefs/lesson-SUBJECT.md` for the nine subjects (roles, verbs, icons, pieces with their status, the designers' rules); the main `lesson` brief points to them.
- **Number:** D-265 (the plan's W2-D03 label).
- **Why:** A type is built by a track over days; until then its name must be held without being usable, its schema must be known to the tracks that depend on it, and the bundle must not grow by the types a lesson does not use.
- **Cost:** One more file to keep (the registry) and the generators; every track's last step is a one-line change of `status`.
- **Status:** decided (the contracts of W2-0; the pieces they name are built by their tracks, each with its own entry)
- **Back-port:** none.

## D-266 · 2026-10-12 · text layer for the languages: spans, target-language keys (the rule 6 reading), code spans, glossary, mhchem, budgets; the operator's answers of 2026-10-12

- **Design ref:** Firm rules 1 and 6; D-110, D-112; plan sections 1.8, 1.11, 1.12 and 9
- **Design said:** English text shown to the student sat under `_it` keys with a lint exemption (D-112); there was no span for a foreign word, no glossary, no code span.
- **We do:** **The operator's answers of 2026-10-12.** Q1: the student studies on a **Mac or an iPad with Safari**, so "Ascolta" uses the Apple voices of that device and the voice gate is tried on it (D-267). Q2: **yes** to licensed photos as proposed (Wikimedia Commons: public domain, CC0, CC BY, CC BY-SA, 3.0 or 4.0; author and licence shown; at most 300 KB and at most 2 per lesson; `alt_it` and a text equivalent; the reviewer opens the licence page). Q3: **yes to both readings** (below). **Rule 6 reading:** rule 6 says keys that hold Italian text end in `_it`; the English and Spanish that the language lessons teach sit in keys ending in that language's code (`text_en`, `form_es`, `pieces_en`, `cells_es`, `base_en`), the interface and every explanation stay Italian, and `parts_it`, `gloss_it` and `meaning_it` hold the Italian meanings of foreign pieces. The language of a figure is read from its keys; one figure holds at most one target language beside Italian (`E-LESSON-LANG`). `sentence` and `tiles` accept exactly one of `text_it`, `text_en`, `text_es`. **Spans** `[[en:...]]`, `[[es:...]]` in any `_it` markup (`<span lang>`, the target ink, a small speaker button when an accepted voice exists); in english and spanish lessons a role span's text is target language by default and an Italian role span says so (`[[time|it:...]]`); the Italian lint skips them and the target-language set applies (12 words per sentence, 8 for a timeline tense mark, `W-LANG-LEVEL` against the first 3000 words, the lesson's glossary and `teaches_en`/`teaches_es`). **Code spans** `[[code:...]]`: literal, at most 40 characters, `textContent`, read with symbol names. **Glossary:** front matter `glossary` (at most 12 terms), inline `[[g:term]]` and the card's terms listed under the card. **mhchem:** `\ce{}` and `\pu{}` from the vendored KaTeX 0.19.0, chemistry and biology only; `E-CHEM-SYMBOL` checks every symbol against `chem/elements`. **Budgets:** 250 words of apparatus open by default and 240 words of originals closed by default on top of the 500 prose words (`E-LESSON-APPARATUS-WORDS`). The schema side and the markup role grammar are done in W2-0; the span parser, the lint split, the glossary and mhchem are T2's. **Browser support:** current Safari on macOS and iPadOS and Chrome (the render check); a piece that depends on a newer feature says so in its entry.
- **Number:** D-266 (the plan's W2-D04 label).
- **Why:** The language lessons teach foreign text; the suffix names the language of the text, which is what rule 6 already does for Italian.
- **Cost:** Authors write two kinds of keys; the lint has to tell the languages apart.
- **Status:** decided (the contracts of W2-0; the pieces they name are built by their tracks, each with its own entry)
- **Back-port:** none.

## D-267 · 2026-10-12 · "Ascolta": the device's voice, the voice gate, speech from the visible state (the rule 1 reading)

- **Design ref:** Firm rule 1; spec A10, D-244 (release 1.1); the operator's design "Alta leggibilità e ascolto"
- **Design said:** "Ascolta" was a release 1.1 item: the device reads approved text aloud.
- **We do:** The rule reads "no chat and no model in the student's path"; device speech synthesis reads fixed text that a reviewer and the teacher approved, generates nothing, takes nothing from the student, needs no network and no server, and is a rendering of the page like a font. Confirmed by the operator on 2026-10-12 (D-266). Five limits: **local voices only** (`voice.localService === true`; a network voice is never used), **accepted voices only** (`config/banco/voices.yml`, the names the operator heard on the student's device, changed by an entry; empty until then, so no speaker is shown and the lessons work by reading), **no speech recognition**, **no recording** (the `oral` rehearsal records nothing and the card says so), **nothing generated at run time**. Speech records no event; the speed and the switch are `student_preference` app events. The preference among accepted voices is en-GB then other English, es-ES then other Spanish, it-IT; rates are 1.0, "Più lento" 0.8 (English 0.75, Spanish 0.7). `speechOf(card)` walks the rendered card and reads only what is visible (not `hidden`, not `aria-hidden`, not in a closed `details`, not an unflipped back, an unopened gloss or a withheld follow-up); `describe` and `speak` take `ctx.state` and `ctx.revealed`, so a value not yet on screen is never read (L10). "Ascolta" never autoplays and stops on card change, Escape, focus leaving the card and another speaker. A `listen` check always has its text behind "Mostra il testo" and an answer given with the text shown is recorded as such (`text_shown: true` in `check_answered`). **Safari:** speech must start from a user gesture (it always does), `getVoices()` is asynchronous (`voiceschanged`), and the voice list differs between macOS and iPadOS: the voice gate is therefore tried on the student's own device. The server-side audio of a local TTS stays a later option, only if a language has no acceptable device voice. W2-0 ships `lesson/speech.js` with `voiceFor`, `rateFor` and the gate, `voices.yml`, and the frozen signatures of `speechOf`, `speak` and `stopAll` (T2).
- **Number:** D-267 (the plan's W2-D05 label).
- **Why:** The language lessons are built on hearing, and the student's reading difficulties make a voice a support, not a luxury.
- **Cost:** A visit with the student's device to listen to the voices; golden files of what is read for each family's gallery cards.
- **Status:** decided (the contracts of W2-0; the pieces they name are built by their tracks, each with its own entry)
- **Back-port:** none.

## D-268 · 2026-10-12 · checks of wave 2: select with pick, tiles, ordering, verify, profile, bits, contractions, thousands, how-to lines, teacher views

- **Design ref:** D-248, D-254; plan sections 1.10 and 2.11
- **Design said:** Six check components graded by the server; the browser serves a whitelist and shuffles ids.
- **We do:** **Components:** `select` (tap zones of the check's own figure, which is served in `mode: select` with targets `t1..tN` in reading order, all neutral; `pick: one` makes any one member of `answer` right, `many` the exact set; the response is the sorted `tN`, mapped back through the same `targets()` order and graded like `span_select`), `tiles`, `ordering` (graded as sequences, served shuffled by Rekey), and the W2-2 draft `amount_words`; `cell_formula` and `trace` are W2-3 names. **Options:** `listen: {text_en | text_es}` on `choice`, `matching`, `span_select`; `verify: {fn, args}` (truth at authoring time: Ruby calls the registered function, `E-LESSON-VERIFY`; always dropped from the served body); `profile` (`binary` with `width` and `leading_zeros`; `chem_formula` is a draft); `input: bits` (eight switches with their weights); `contractions: en`; `thousands: true` on `number`; `reachable_ok_it` (one Italian sentence saying why a figure's reachable values do not give the answer away). Step blanks accept `select` and `amount_words` too. Every component prints our fixed one-line how-to on its first use in a lesson (from `config/locales/lesson_checks.it.yml`, T1) and "Come si risponde" gains an entry per component. The teacher sees a `select` answer by the targets' names, never by `tN`. W2-0 puts the schemas, the whitelist rows and the registry in place; the plumbing is T1's.
- **Number:** D-268 (the plan's W2-D06 label).
- **Why:** A check must be able to ask about a drawing (where is the nucleus), a built sentence and an order without giving the answer away.
- **Cost:** Each component and option needs graders, serving, the teacher's view and a system test.
- **Status:** decided (the contracts of W2-0; the pieces they name are built by their tracks, each with its own entry)
- **Back-port:** none.

## D-269 · 2026-10-12 · leak rules L1 to L10 for the wave 2 pieces, the whitelist and the sentinel test

- **Design ref:** D-248, D-254; plan section 1.4
- **Design said:** The whitelist and the served body keep answers out of the page; the pilot's review 8 found a check answered by looking at its figure.
- **We do:** L1 every new piece has served and dropped columns in `test/fixtures/lesson2/whitelist.json` (version 2, one row per component, block and diagram type; `provisional` for the W2-2 drafts; the always-dropped list: `answer`, `accept`, `errors`, `explain_it`, `verify`, `reachable_ok_it`, every `x-banco-solution` and `x-banco-withheld` field); L2 a hidden value is served as null and a module never displays one; in student mode it computes only the outputs of declared controls; L3 a select figure's candidates are in one neutral style (`E-SELECT-MARKED`, `E-CHECK-ANSWER-IN-ALT`); L4 a text answer that a figure of the card prints in any state is `W-CHECK-ANSWER-IN-DIAGRAM`; L5 an answer a control can reach is the error `E-CHECK-ANSWER-BY-SIMULATION` (a reachable set over 500 is `E-DIAGRAM-REACHABLE-CAP`; the way past is `reachable_ok_it`); L6 follow-ups that answer a graded check (example steps after a blank, `explain_it`, the `oral` model answer) come only from the check endpoint; L7 figures inside `try` are static; L8 ungraded reveals are served but counted as printed; L9 a check may ask a fact a data table holds only if no figure on the card prints it; L10 speech and `describe` are built from the visible state. The sentinel property test (A2) draws `ANS-<hex>` sentinels in every dropped, hidden, withheld and L8 field and asserts that none reaches `StudentBody.for(...)`, `describe()`, `speak()` or the card's speech before its reveal (and that L8 ones do after it); it is each track's, run on its vectors. The tests of W2-0 check that the whitelist rows equal the schemas.
- **Number:** D-269 (the plan's W2-D07 label).
- **Why:** The pilot's best property is that a drawing cannot lie; the same must hold for a map, a register and an invoice, and no answer may travel to the page or the voice before it is due.
- **Cost:** Every piece pays for a vector with hidden values, a sentinel pass and a print test.
- **Status:** decided (the contracts of W2-0; the pieces they name are built by their tracks, each with its own entry)
- **Back-port:** none.

## D-270 · 2026-10-12 · vetted data tables: config/banco/data, schemas, second table, reference texts

- **Design ref:** D-074 (reference texts), firm rule 5; plan section 1.9
- **Design said:** A lesson's facts are the author's, checked by the reviewer from memory.
- **We do:** Facts of the world that a lesson shows (symbols, melting points, climate normals, sizes, irregular verbs, Spanish forms, place names, the gazetteer of the ancient Mediterranean) live in `config/banco/data/DOMAIN/NAME.yml`, each value with its source, a JSON Schema beside it, a unit test for internal consistency and a second table typed separately by another session and compared by the test; a model other than the author's reviews it; it changes only by an entry. The author names a row. `bin/build-lesson-data` validates each table and compiles it into `app/javascript/lesson/data/DOMAIN-NAME.js` (generated, at most 20 KB gzip each, loaded by the card that uses it); `Lessons::VettedData` reads them (`E-LESSON-DATA`). The 15 schemas are in W2-0: `chem/elements` (118), `chem/substances`, `chem/molecules`, `chem/terms` (seven changes of state), `bio/cell_parts`, `bio/sizes`, `geo/stations` (about 25), `geo/names`, `geo/countries`, `history/places` (about 60 places and 40 regions), `english/verbs` (about 120), `english/contractions`, `spanish/verbs` (every verb a lesson shows, six forms each), `computer_science/program_vb`, `network/kinds`. The tables are content (phase C0). Prose that is quoted verbatim (the Costituzione artt. 55-96 and 134-139, the codice civile articles of the contract lesson) stays reference text imported by the operator, one command each; the `source` block checks quotations with `E-QUOTE-REF`.
- **Number:** D-270 (the plan's W2-D08 label).
- **Why:** In geography, history and chemistry the risk is a wrong fact, not a wrong sum; a fact typed once, double-checked and drawn by our code cannot be mistyped on a card.
- **Cost:** Content work before the lessons that use it; a change of a value is an entry.
- **Status:** decided (the contracts of W2-0; the pieces they name are built by their tracks, each with its own entry)
- **Back-port:** none.

## D-271 · 2026-10-12 · render-time records and the program diagram: Rails never runs an agent's program

- **Design ref:** Firm rule 3 as amended by D-262; D-255; plan sections 1.2, 1.12 and 2.9
- **Design said:** The flowchart design ran the student's or the agent's program in Ruby (caps of 200 executed blocks and 12 trace rows).
- **We do:** `program` is the one wave 2 type with loops. **Ruby parses and never runs it:** `Lessons::Diagrams::Program` and `Lessons::ProgramGrammar` check the grammar, that every name is assigned or read before use, that every `read` has an input, and the static caps (12 statements, depth 2, 6 variables, values within +-10^6). **Our interpreter (`lesson/lib/program.js`) runs it only in the server's Chrome at the render check** through the optional `recordAtRender(data) -> { records, findings }` of the module contract: it runs the default inputs and every `try` value and stores per run the trace, the outputs, the final memory and the turns in `lesson_renders.result_json.records`; failures are render findings (`E-PROGRAM-BOUND` for the run-time caps, termination unless `endless`, no division by 0; `E-LESSON-VERIFY` for `verify: {fn: program.output | program.final | program.turns}`; `E-CHECK-ANSWER-BY-SIMULATION` computed from the records). **The student's page replays the records:** `StudentBody` merges the records of the revision's latest passing render into the served `program`; "Esegui un blocco", "Esegui tutto", "Ricomincia", the try chips and the `predict` taps step through the recorded trace, so the experience is the same with inputs from the declared chips. A revision without a passing render cannot be approved (D-255), and the teacher's preview of such a revision shows the static flowchart and "Esecuzione non ancora registrata". The Visual Basic listing is generated from the structure by our code, in Ruby and JS (a translation of data, not a run). Spreadsheet formulas (`sheet`, `cell_formula`, W2-3) are expressions without loops, evaluated like `cartesian.eq`. No migration: records are in `result_json`.
- **Number:** D-271 (the plan's W2-D09 label).
- **Why:** Rule 3 says agent-written code never runs on the server; a program written as data in a closed language is still the agent's, so the only place it runs is a browser.
- **Cost:** The render check gains a recording step (its 90 s budget is re-measured on the heaviest lesson) and `StudentBody` a merge.
- **Status:** decided (the contracts of W2-0; the pieces they name are built by their tracks, each with its own entry)
- **Back-port:** none.

## D-272 · 2026-10-12 · wave 2, track T5 on day one: the map bases from sourced open data (`bin/build-maps`, `banco-maps@1`), the gazetteer tables, the ancient Mediterranean built from Natural Earth and Pleiades

- **Design ref:** `prep/rich-lessons/WAVE2-COMPONENTS.md` 1.9 (`geo/names`, `geo/countries`, `history/places`), 2.3 (`map` and its bases), 5.1 (T5 starts on day one); the answers of 2026-10-12 (a Mac or iPad with Safari, licensed photos yes, `_en`/`_es` keys yes).
- **We do:** (1) `bin/build-maps` makes `public/vendor/banco-maps@1/<base>.js` for eleven bases: `world`, `europe`, `africa`, `asia`, `north_america`, `south_america`, `oceania`, `arctic`, `antarctic`, `italy` (the twenty regions) and `mediterraneo_antico`. It reads only files committed in git (`config/banco/data/geo/source/`, trimmed from Natural Earth v5.1.2 and the World Bank, each with the upstream address and checksum in `sources.yml`), so the build is offline and byte for byte deterministic; `bin/build-maps --fetch` refreshes the sources and the two generated tables from the network, `--check` is the test that the directory equals the build, `--verify-pleiades DUMP` compares `history/places` with a Pleiades CSV dump. (2) A base is a module with areas (path, label anchor, box), groups (the continents, Italy as its regions), oceans, lakes, rivers, cities, the graticule and the projection (type, scale, translation, so the browser can place a point). Equal Earth for the world and the continents (the viewBox is the largest upright rectangle inside the window, so no corner is empty), Lambert azimuthal equal-area for the poles, Mercator for `mediterraneo_antico` (a Mediterranean in Equal Earth leaves slanted edges; a straight-meridian base is what an atlas page of Rome looks like). Each base is at most 60 KB gzipped (the build tries coarser tolerances until it is). (3) Tables, each with a JSON schema beside it and tests: `geo/names` (id to `name_it`, `name_en`, `name_es`, with the source; the Natural Earth Italian label unless `names_overrides.yml` has the school exonym and the reason: San Paolo, Città del Capo, Rio delle Amazzoni, Reno, Eufrate), `geo/countries` (area from the World Bank WDI, FAO, 2021, and population, 2023, each with year and source; no number without a source, so Taiwan and Kosovo have no area), `history/places` (69 places, each with its Pleiades id, title, coordinates and the licence), `history/places_expected` (a second table of where each place is, typed apart; the test compares the two to a quarter of a degree, half or one for battlefields and lines), `history/regions` (35 regions composed from Natural Earth units, each with a line on what it misses). (4) Licences: Natural Earth is public domain; Pleiades is CC BY 3.0 (the attribution is in `LICENSE`, `PROVENANCE.md` and, when the card exists, on the card); the World Bank data is CC BY 4.0. (5) The **Ancient World Mapping Center's data is not used**: its licence is the ODbL (share-alike: a database derived from it must be offered under the same licence) and its province polygons carry no names, so naming them would be drawing them by hand. The regions are therefore approximations from whole modern countries, whole Greek and Turkish provinces, the regions of Italy, or a country cut by a box; the base is `"approximate": true` and the template must print "Confini approssimativi". The coast is today's coast.
- **Why:** the plan makes `mediterraneo_antico` the highest wrong-fact risk, so every region and place has a source, a second table and a review; Natural Earth and Pleiades are the two open sources with a licence that lets a public repository carry derived data.
- **Cost:** about 1.5 MB of trimmed sources and 0.4 MB of tables in git; about 130 KB gzipped of bases (served only to a card with a map). The regions of the ancient base are rough: Numidia and Mauretania are cut by boxes, the Anatolian regions follow today's provinces, Gallia has no Narbonensis. The lead decides before a lesson depends on a region whether the AWMC shapes (with an ODbL notice) are wanted instead; the pictures of the base need a second model's review and the teacher's look in the topic review of `republic-to-empire`.
- **Not done:** the `map` component, the select targets, the layers (arrows, circles, compare, inset, slider), `mercator: true` on the modern bases, the Italian names of the lakes (Natural Earth's lake labels lack "Lago": lakes are drawn unnamed), a second session typing `geo/names` apart from Natural Earth's labels, the review of the base pictures by another model.
- **Fixes after the contracts (T5 on W2-0):** (1) **Ids resolve per base.** `sicilia` is in `geo/names` (the Italian region) and in `history/regions` (the Roman province); a base now carries `reads`, the table each collection (`areas`, `groups`, `places`, `lines`, `oceans`) is read from (`italy` reads `geo/names`; `mediterraneo_antico` reads areas in `history/regions`, places in `history/places`, rivers in `geo/names`), and a test proves every id resolves in exactly its declared table and is unique within the base; the clash `geo/names` and `history/regions` is exactly `sicilia` and a new one fails the test until this entry names it. (2) **The base's `projection.type` is the authority**: `equal_earth`, `lambert_azimuthal` (with `pole`: `north` or `south`, replacing `azimuthal_north` and `azimuthal_south`) or `mercator`; the JS twin `app/javascript/lesson/lib/map_projection.js` supports all three and `projection_vectors.json` (version 2) holds the points of every base and of the three types with fixed parameters, the two poles included. (3) **`history/places` and `history/regions` are two tables on purpose**: places are points with a Pleiades source, regions are recipes (the modern units that make a shape, with a note on what they miss) with no Pleiades id. Dates live in one place: the optional `since` year of a region (negative = a.C., no year 0) with its `since_source`, in `history/regions` version 2; no other key carries a date, and a place gets one only by a schema change. The T5 shapes of `geo/names`, `geo/countries` and `history/places` are their version 2 (the contract's shapes were never filled by data); `history/regions` and `history/places_expected` are the two tables T5 adds beside the contract's fifteen. (4) **A base carries no `name*` or `label*` key** on areas, groups, places, lines, water or oceans: names come from the server after the answer in select mode (D-268, leak rules D-269); a test checks every base.
- **Status:** decided
- **Back-port:** none.

## D-273 · 2026-10-12 · wave 2, track T1 (core): tiles, ordering and select are built, verify, profile, thousands and the truth rules L3 to L5, how-to lines, teacher views by name, the preload of lazy types, sentence neutral; contractions waits for its table

- **Design ref:** `prep/rich-lessons/WAVE2-COMPONENTS.md` 1.3, 1.4 (L3 to L5, L9), 1.10 (`verify:`), 2.6 (`sentence` neutral), 2.11 (checks), 5.2 and 5.3 (T1, W2-1 column); D-264, D-265, D-268, D-269.
- **We do:** (1) **Palette v2, the nine subject setups, the mixed-palette test and the reserved and draft dry run were already built by W2-0** (D-264, D-265; `bin/build-palette --check`, `bin/build-icons --check`, `test/lib/lesson_palette_test.rb`, `test/integration/lesson2_api_test.rb`, the CLI test); T1 only verified them, and wrote the two bad fixtures of the dry run (`bad/type-reserved.md`, `bad/type-draft.md`, run with `allow_reserved`, a field of the manifest) and the one of `E-LESSON-VERIFY`. (2) **`tiles`, `ordering`, `select` are `available`.** Ruby: `Lessons::Checks.grade` grades a sequence (`answer`, `accept`, a coded `errors[]` sequence; `ordering` wants every item, `tiles` may be shorter and is then wrong, not unreadable) and a select (`pick: one`, any one member of `answer` and exactly one tap; `pick: many`, exactly the set); tiles and items are shown shuffled under `e1..eN` by the ordering re-key (never the key, its reverse or the stored listing first); a select's response is a list of `tN`, mapped back by `Lessons::SelectTargets` through the type's Ruby `targets(data, set)` (the same reading order as the type's JS `targets()`). `Blocks::Check` checks the shapes (ids, answer, distractors, one language per tile, a select's set and answers against the type's targets). `StudentBody` serves `tiles`, `items` and, for a select, the type's own `served(data, mode: :select)` projection, never the answer. (3) **The browser:** `lesson/checks/tiles.js` (a line built from a bank; a tap in, a tap out, left and right move a tile, "Svuota"; a used tile stays as an empty outline so the bank does not jump; `buildTiles` is the input `oral` (T8) reuses), `ordering.js` (every item in the list, Su and Giù buttons, Alt with the arrows), `select.js` with `draw.js` (`mode: select`: one HTML button over each shape the layout marked `target: tN`, one tab stop, arrows to the nearest zone, Home and End, a live line "Selezionate: n", every zone the same dashed outline, a chosen one solid with a check mark, never colour alone; a plain list of toggles stands in if the figure draws no target), models in `sequence_model.js` and `select_model.js` (pure, node tests), `lesson/checks/howto.js` (the one fixed line on the **first use in the order of the cards**, and a closed "Come si risponde" with its example under every use), `config/locales/lesson_checks.it.yml`, `app/assets/stylesheets/lesson/checks.css` (forced colors, reduced motion and print: a select prints its zones numbered and "Scrivi i numeri: ____", P3), and the render check's `E-DIAGRAM-TARGET` (a target under 24 x 24 px). `sitting` help gains `tiles` and `select` lines in `it.yml`. (4) **Lazy types and components are loaded before the page draws** (`lesson/preload.js`, called by the three entry points): W2-0 built `load` and `preload` in the registries but nothing called them, so no reserved type could ever have drawn; the checks registry gains `preload` and `moduleFor`, `describe(data, ctx)` takes the subject. (5) **A latent fault fixed on the server:** the browser sends the `raw()` of an input, a JSON **text** (`["e2","e1"]`), for `fraction`, `matching` and `span_select` as it does for the new components, and `Lessons::Checks` read only structured data (the integration tests sent a hash), so those answers were "unparseable" in a real browser; `Checks.structured` now reads a string that is JSON for a hash or a list, for the components that take data (the existing system tests, which send text, stay as they are). (6) **Options:** `thousands: true` (`Grading::Spec#thousands`, `Numbers.parse`: a dot that groups exactly three digits before the decimal comma is a separator, 1.115,00 is 1115; a dot decimal and spaces still refuse), `profile` (the lesson check passes the `binary` profile of `Grading::Closed::Text` through), `verify` (`Lessons::Verify`: a registry; the figure types' `verify_functions`; the libraries by their frozen `SIGNATURES` and a `pick` argument for a hash result; `Lib.mutants` for the coded wrong answers; `E-LESSON-VERIFY`; a function whose library is not built reports "not built yet" and never passes silently; `program.*` is the render check's), `reachable_ok_it`. **`contractions: en` is built but stays `reserved`**: `Grading::Closed::Contractions` expands the table's short forms on both sides (whole words and suffixes such as `'ll`, `n't`; forms marked `ambiguous`, `'s` and `'d`, are never expanded) and is tested on an invented table of the shape of the schema, but the vetted `english/contractions` table is not written (T3's data, which needs its second table and a review), and without it the option would grade as if it were off; a test holds the option back until `config/banco/data/english/contractions.yml` exists. (7) **The truth rules:** `Lessons::Blocks::Truth` (L3 `E-CHECK-ANSWER-IN-ALT`, `E-SELECT-MARKED`; L4 `W-CHECK-ANSWER-IN-DIAGRAM`; L5 `E-CHECK-ANSWER-BY-SIMULATION` and `E-DIAGRAM-REACHABLE-CAP`) read the figure types through the contract's hooks and **two optional ones**, which are additions and break nothing: Ruby `target_names(data, set) -> {id => name}` and `select_signatures(data, set) -> {id => style}` (the drawn style of each candidate; they must all be equal), and a JS `name_it` on a `targets()` entry (what the teacher reads). A type without a hook is skipped, never guessed. (8) **Teacher views:** the notes beside a check read tiles as the built sentence, an ordering as its items joined by arrows, a select by the targets' `name_it` (the id when a target has none), never by `e1` or `tN` (a system test). `oral` (T8) uses `sequenceText`. (9) **`sentence` neutral:** `text_it`, `text_en` or `text_es` for the sentence and each part (one language, the parts in the sentence's language), a label of the target language carries `lang`, `layout: centre` centres on the subject's `centre_role`, `describe(data, ctx)` reads the lesson subject's palette; six vectors both ways (`sentence-neutral-*`).
- **Why:** the pilot's rule that a drawing cannot lie, and that an answer never reaches the page before it is due, has to hold for the new components before an author uses them; the contract's plumbing is T1's so that eight other tracks need not agree on it again.
- **Cost (as written by T1; `network` of T4b landed in the integration, so the first select figure exists and `E-CHECK-ANSWER-IN-ALT` has its fixture `bad/select-alt-names-answer.md`, while `E-SELECT-MARKED` and `E-DIAGRAM-TARGET` wait for a figure whose candidates a lesson can style or shrink):** `select` is `available` but no figure type offers targets yet: until the first one does (`network`, T4b, is the first), a select check is refused with "does not offer select targets yet", and the three bad fixtures that need a select figure (`E-CHECK-ANSWER-IN-ALT`, `E-SELECT-MARKED`, `E-DIAGRAM-TARGET`) wait for `diagram:network` (their `needs` in the manifest). The select look gate was done on a probe figure of eight equal zones in a system test, not on a real type. The teacher's view of `oral` answers waits for T8's block (the helpers are in place). `W-CHECK-ANSWER-IN-DIAGRAM`'s fixture waits for `register` (T9).
- **Status:** decided
- **Back-port:** none.

## D-274 · 2026-10-12 · wave 2, track T9: the grid engine behind grid/api.js

- **Design ref:** WAVE2 plan 2.5 ("one grid engine, owned by T9, consumed by T3 and T7 through `grid/api.js`, published first"); D-265 (the frozen signatures)
- **Design said:** `grid`, `cellBox`, `outline`, `stackForPhone`, `scrollFrame` and `cellTargets` are frozen names that throw `NotBuilt`; `hide` and `tap` are cell attributes; a hidden cell's value is never in the grid (L10).
- **We do:** The six functions are built, with the signatures of W2-0 unchanged, in `lesson/diagrams/grid/engine.js`; `grid/api.js` keeps the names, `SIGNATURES`, `CELL_ATTRIBUTES` and `TAP_KINDS` and forwards. **A grid is geometry only**: edges, sizes, `headerRows`, `headerCols` and the sparse list of cells that carry an attribute, each with an `id` ("r2c3", 0-based) that a popover or a reveal is keyed by. It never holds a cell's text, so a hidden cell's value cannot be in it. `outline(grid, cells, {kind})` traces the boundary of the union of the cells as directed edges, so holes come out as their own loop; `"frame"` is the plain rectilinear path, `"boot"` is inset by 3 px with rounded corners. `stackForPhone(grid, width)` opens a grid that is wider than its room below 600 px into one section per data row (`title_it` "Riga N", which the type replaces with its own words); a grid that fits, or any width from 600 px, is one section. `scrollFrame` covers the grid and says whether the first column stays. `cellTargets(grid, set)` takes a list of `{row, col}`, `"cells"` (everything but the headers) or `"all"` and gives the targets in reading order, all with the same neutral words ("Riga 2, colonna 3": the place, never the content, L3). Helpers for the types that use the engine (`readingOrder`, `fitSize`, `cellAt`, `isHidden`, `GridError`) are in `engine.js`, not in the frozen file. Bad arguments throw a `GridError` (a programmer error: the types validate their data first). Tests: `lesson/test/grid.test.mjs`.
- **Number:** D-274.
- **Why:** T3 (`paradigm`, `word_parts`) and T7 (`periodic_table`) must not each invent a grid; publishing the geometry first lets them start.
- **Cost:** `grid/api.js` is no longer a stub; `contract.test.mjs` no longer expects `NotBuilt` from it.
- **Status:** decided
- **Back-port:** none.

## D-275 · 2026-10-12 · wave 2, track T9: Lessons::Bits, register (row and ring), column_calc, the switches of input: bits, and the L4 and L5 checks

- **Design ref:** WAVE2 plan 2.5 (`register`, `column_calc`), 2.9, 2.11 (`input: bits`), 1.4 (L4, L5), 1.10 (Bits); D-252 (the pattern); D-265 (the registry); D-269 (the leak rules)
- **Design said:** Each piece is a schema, Ruby checks, a browser module, vectors both ways, a gallery card, a look gate and an entry; `register` is one type with two views, `column_calc` computes carries, borrows and partial products, `input: bits` is eight switches with their weights.
- **We do:** **`Lessons::Bits`** (Ruby) and `lesson/lib/bits.js` (JS) read, write (two's complement included), add, subtract and multiply in columns and divide repeatedly, in bases 2 to 16, exact (BigInt in JS), index 0 the leftmost column, with `test/fixtures/lesson2/bits.json` run by both (a refused call is `{"error": "argument"}`). **`register`**: `view: row` draws every digit in its own cell (a bit is at least 24 px; sixteen bits break into two rows of eight on a phone), the weights over them (staggered over two lines, or written as powers, when a number is wider than its cell), the first weight negative and in the role `sign` in two's complement, groups, the hex or octal digit under each group, role markers, a readout and the sum of the weights, all computed; `toggle: true` makes each bit a switch (a native button, `role=switch`, laid over its cell) and `goals` the lab's "Prova a fare ..." with a local "Sì". `view: ring` draws the 8 or 16 codes on a circle, the unsigned value outside and the signed one inside, a seam for each reading, a pointer with its stepper (-1 and +1 round the circle), highlights, and moves drawn as arcs along the ring with the landing code computed; the codes are read off the pointer and a legend, not written round the circle (they would not fit a phone at the student's size), and a number that would touch another is left out. **`column_calc`** draws an addition (the carry over the next column, the carry out of the register falling out to the left, dashed, in the role `carry`), a subtraction (the digits a borrow changes, chains across zeros drawn at once and struck through) or a multiplication (one partial product per digit of the multiplier, shifted, the overflow outside); `reveal: columns` shows the work one column (one product) at a time with a stepper; the columns never get narrower than a digit plus 6 px, so sixteen bits on a phone are `E-DIAGRAM-LAYOUT` instead of digits touching. **Controls**: draw.js now builds what `controls()` declares (`lesson/diagrams/controls.js`): a toggle with a box in the scene is a button over the drawing, a stepper sits in the strip; the values are one object `{id: value}` passed to `layout` and `describe` as `ctx.controls`, reset when the state changes, and a polite live line says what changed (`scene.live`). A declared control may carry `initial`, `less_it` and `more_it` beyond the contract's fields. `describe(data, ctx)` and `printed(data, state)` take the state and the controls; `registry.describe` forwards `opts`. **Ruby**: `Lessons::Diagrams::Register` and `ColumnCalc` (`state`, `served`, `targets`, `printed`, `reachable`, `verify_functions` with `bits.read`, `bits.write` and `bits.add`), the same checks in the same order as the JS modules (the vectors of `test/fixtures/diagrams/types/{register,column_calc}.json` hold the first finding, the printed value tokens, the select targets and the reachable count for both). `printed` is the set of value tokens: the digits (bare, grouped with a narrow no-break space and with a plain space), the weights, group digits, readouts, sums and the values the step sentences say; every number `describe` says is one of those or a structural count (tested). **L4 and L5 are built**, in `Lessons::Blocks::Truth` (T1's module, which the integration kept as the one implementation: T9 had a twin, `Lessons::Leaks`, removed) called from `Validation::Lesson2Checks` for every card: `W-CHECK-ANSWER-IN-DIAGRAM` when a text-answer check asks a value a figure of the same card prints in any state, `E-CHECK-ANSWER-BY-SIMULATION` when it asks a value an interactive figure can be made to show (a register with `toggle`, a ring with `step`) unless `reachable_ok_it` says why not, `E-DIAGRAM-REACHABLE-CAP` when a figure can show more than 500 values on a card with a check; a type whose module is not built answers nothing. The bad fixture of L4 moved from `pending` to `bad` (`check-answer-printed-by-register.md`). **`input: bits`**: on a `normalized_text` check with `profile: {name: binary, width: N}` the answer is written with N switches in groups of four (`lesson/checks/bits_input.js`, served as `input: bits` and `input_width`, the profile staying server-side); the response is the string of N bits and is graded like a typed one. Ruby refuses the check unless the answer is exactly N bits and so is every `errors[].answer`; **when an error under test is `padding_missing` the check keeps the typed line** (`Lessons::Checks.bits_switches?`), because switches always give the whole width. **No weights are drawn on the switches**: the option does not say whether the first bit is a sign, and positive weights would contradict the sign weight the lesson teaches. **Page plumbing**: a page links `stylesheets/lesson/FAMILY.css` for the families its diagrams (and the `input: bits` check) use (`lesson_family_stylesheets`). The gallery `gallery/computing.md` shows every built piece and passes the render check at every viewport; the look gate was done on shots at 1366 and 390 px, cream and dark.
- **Number:** D-275.
- **Why:** The twos-complement lesson of computer science needs position, width and the carry that falls out to be drawn by us and never written by the author, and a register the student can change is the best way to see why a leading 1 is negative.
- **Cost:** `input: bits` needs T1's `profile`, which landed with the integration (w2-int), so a stored lesson can use it; the gallery may still be parsed with `allow_reserved` for cards that use other held-back pieces. The generated registry now imports `register` and `column_calc` eagerly. `op: repeated_division` of `column_calc` stays reserved (W2-3) though `Bits.repeated_division` is built with its vectors.
- **Status:** decided
- **Back-port:** none.

## D-276 · 2026-10-12 · wave 2, track T5: `map`, `insolation` and `cross_section` available (D-252 pattern), select targets, the bases cropped whole, Europe and Italy in Mercator

- **We do:** the three types of the maps family are `available` (W2-1). Ruby: `Lessons::Diagrams::{Map,Insolation,CrossSection}` (checks, `served`, `targets`, `printed`, `reachable`, words) with `Maps::Base` (reads a base: units per detail, ids resolved per base, compass phrase, reading order) and `GeoFormat`; JS twins `lesson/diagrams/maps/{map,insolation,cross_section,geo}.js`; vectors `test/fixtures/diagrams/types/{map,insolation,cross_section}.json` run both ways (`maps_types_test.rb`, `maps.test.mjs`: semantic first finding, layout at 320 to 1280 px and 18 to 26 px, describe, printed, reachable, targets and neutral phrases); gallery `gallery/maps.md` and `test/system/maps_gallery_test.rb`.
- **Map, built now:** the modern bases and `mediterraneo_antico`, `detail`, graticule, highlight with a pattern as well as a colour (auto pattern by order of the roles), bands, places, points (labels), lines (base line, meridian, parallel), routes, `candidates`, `states`, the year `slider` with `regions_since` (a year state when from equals to; its - and + jump to the next year a region appears), "Ovest", "Nord" and "Est" in a row under the map, the legend list, "Confini approssimativi", at most 8 text labels else numbered callouts (a crowded callout goes in a row under the map). **Held back for W2-2 and refused with E-LESSON-DIAGRAM:** `arrows`, `points[].value`, `compare`, `inset`, `mercator` on a base not built in Mercator. No coordinates on a historical base (points, bands, meridians, parallels, graticule other than greenwich are refused there).
- **Select (L3):** `targets(data, set)` for areas, places, bands, lines, points in reading order (north to south in rows of one viewBox unit, west to east, id); stored ids: gazetteer id, `meridian:LON`, `parallel:LAT`, `lat:FROM:TO`, `pt:LAT:LON`, belts `alt:FROM:TO`; keys `t1..tN`; `neutral_it` a compass phrase ("a nord-ovest"; "in alto a sinistra" on the polar bases). `served(data, mode: :select, set:)` and `ctx.set` carry the check's set (T1 passes them): the figure is the base alone, the targets in one style, no label, role, pattern, state or name table (the names are never loaded in select mode); the DOM holds `data-target` keys and "zona 3 di 12, a nord-ovest". Default `areas` are the units at least 45 viewBox units wide and high; `candidates` lifts that (E-DIAGRAM-TARGET from the render check). A belt gets the neutral label "fascia" in the served select figure (the schema asks for one).
- **Insolation and cross_section:** the spread is 1/cos(latitude - subsolar) with one decimal, subsolar within 23,5, at most 85 degrees from the Sun; a movable beam (-80 to 80 by 10) starts at the nearest free step to 0. The section's exaggeration is the largest nice number that keeps the drawing half as high as wide, always printed ("altezze esagerate 20 volte"); the temperature is base - per_km * altitude / 1000, exact; the stepper reads each 500 m (1000 above 4000 m) and the top; belts are numbered at the right with a legend list that is also the print table.
- **Shared code changed (the lead merges with T1):** `draw.js` and the new `scene_extras.js` implement the Scene additions of D-265 (group `scale`, `pattern`, `target` with a roving tab stop and arrow keys, `controls()` as stepper and slider with - and +, `scene.legend`, `printViews`, `star` and `ring` markers, `prepare`, `mode` and `set` to layout); `describe(data, ctx)` takes the visible state; the generated registry imports only the core types at once and every wave 2 type lazily even when available (`bin/build-lesson-types`); `preloadTypes(body)` loads them before the first card; `lesson_family_stylesheets` links `lesson/FAMILY.css` in the three pages.
- **Bases corrected:** the inner-rectangle crop of D-272 cut South America and Africa (the widest parallel lay outside it): the viewBox is now the window's bounding box (`crop: false`); `europe` and `italy` are Mercator, so that their window is a rectangle and no slanted cut crosses the Balkans. Known limit: the continent groups Europe and Asia both draw Russia whole. Texts of the maps are in the modules, as the words of the core types (layout is pure and run in node); `lesson_maps.it.yml` stays empty.
- **Status:** decided
- **Back-port:** none.

## D-277 · 2026-10-12 · wave 2, track T5 review fixes: select figures are drawn from opaque select plates, small targets get padded hit shapes, callouts on a phone

Review of D-276 found that a select figure loaded the full base module, which carries every gazetteer id beside its geometry (`rome` at its
coordinates, `AUT` with its shape): a student with devtools could read which shape is which. Decided:

- `bin/build-maps` also writes `public/vendor/banco-maps@1/select/<base>.js`, the same geometry with opaque keys (`a14` area, `g3` group,
  `p20` place, `l2` line) in place of every id, no `reads`, no `oceans`, plate order by key. The keys are drawn at random once and kept in
  `lib/maps/select_keys.json` (never under `public/`; a kept id keeps its key, a new id takes a free number; `bin/build-maps --check` compares it).
- `Map.served(data, mode: :select)` returns `candidates`, `places[].id` and `lines[].id` as keys; the page loads only the plate for a select
  figure (`G.prepare(name, names: false)`), never the base or the name tables. The reading-order tie of a target is its key, on both sides.
  The Ruby, node and system tests scan the served figure, the plate and the scene for every id of the base.
- A select target smaller than 24 CSS px (a small area, a thin belt) gets an invisible padded hit shape (`dg-hitpad`, `data-hit-for`) that
  forwards the click to the target. Two chosen `candidates` (or two belts) whose pads would share a centre are `E-DIAGRAM-TARGET`, raised by
  the layout; the default targets of an `areas` set, which the author does not choose, may overlap (the later shape wins).
- On a frame narrower than 420 px a figure with two or more labels uses numbered callouts placed beside the mark with a leader, so that text
  does not cover the map; the compass row keeps "Est" inside the frame. Select shapes have a stronger fill and outline.
- Known limits: the europe and asia continent groups both draw Russia whole (D-272); the slider was built in W2-1 (the plan has it in W2-2).
- **Status:** decided
- **Back-port:** none.

## D-278 · 2026-10-12 · wave 2, track T8, first half: the docs family (the shared flip, `reveal`, `oral`, `source` legal, `document` with the invoice and `Lessons::Money`)

- **Design ref:** `prep/rich-lessons/WAVE2-COMPONENTS.md` 1.10 (Money), 2.7 (`source`, `document`), 2.10 (`reveal`, `oral`), 5.2 (T8), 1.8 (apparatus words); D-252 (the pattern of a piece), D-259 (the mistake flip card), D-265 (the registry), D-268, D-269.
- **Design said:** T8 builds, for W2-1, `source` (legal half), `reveal` with the shared flip (the mistake moves onto it), `oral`, and the `document` frame with `invoice` and Money; the other kinds, the historical half, `image`, Dates, NumWords and `amount_words` are W2-2.
- **We do:** (1) **`Lessons::Money`** (Ruby, `lesson/lib/money.js` twin, `test/fixtures/lesson2/money.json`): exact euros (Rational, BigInt), half-up cents, VAT per rate, the invoice rows (gross, discounts, net, the seller's costs, imponibile, VAT, documented costs, interest, total) and the closed list of nine typical errors (`taxable_base_on_gross`, `vat_on_gross_added_to_net`, `documented_costs_taxed`, `undocumented_costs_untaxed`, `undocumented_costs_omitted`, `successive_discounts_added`, `two_rates_single_rate`, `two_rates_combined`, `vat_added_as_amount`). The invoice rules: successive discounts each on what is left and rounded to the cent; own costs inside the imponibile, documented costs added after the VAT; with two VAT rates an own cost is refused (it has no rate); interest on the net goods, added after the documented costs (whether it enters the imponibile is an open book convention and is not assumed). The vectors were computed by hand from the business brief (2.319,20; 1.000,40; 3.300,70 and its four errors). (2) **`document`** (frame and `kind: invoice`, `view: sheet | cascade`; `lib/lessons/diagrams/document.rb`, `lesson/diagrams/docs/document.js`): the rows are computed by Money from the data, never written; `hide` draws an empty dashed box with "?" and `describe()`, `printed()` and the labels never read the value (L10); `error` draws the invoice as that mistake computes it, titled "Fattura con un errore"; `mark: [base]` is the dashed fence. A cascade cannot hide a row (its bars would show the value); every euro amount in `alt_it` or `caption_it` must be a computed row or an amount of the data and never a hidden row's (`E-LESSON-ALT`); an error that changes nothing is refused. The JS and Ruby checks agree on code and path (`test/fixtures/diagrams/types/document.json`). Below 560 px the sheet opens into zone cards (the goods lines stack). Select targets `zones` and `rows` are `shapes[].target` in mode `select`; `Document.targets` and `targets()` return the same keys in the same order. `draw.js` gains the `ring` and `star` marker shapes. (3) **`lesson/blocks/flip.js`**: the one flip mechanism; `mistake` is rebuilt on it with the same markup and classes, `reveal` uses it as a card (plain) and with a separate button (the crossroads). (4) **`reveal`**: a flip card, or the crossroads (pick a road, see what comes of it, turn to what really happened; the real road marked with a word and an icon; our fixed line that the other roads are guesses); ungraded, nothing stored; the back is not in the document flow until opened (L10); open in print, safe mode and the teacher's view. (5) **`oral`**: the outline is graded by the check endpoint as an ordering (`Lessons::Oral.check`, `Checks.rekey` for `ordering`, ids e1..eN shuffled by Rekey); `model_it` is withheld until the outline is right or after the second try and rides on the reply (`model_it`), never in the served body; the teacher's preview grades with the seed "preview" and shows the model from the full body. The outline uses T1's `ordering` component when it is `available` (the frozen `render(check, ctx, hooks)`), and a small list with "Sposta su" and "Sposta giù" until then; no microphone, nothing recorded; the fixed line "Facoltativo. Nessuno ti ascolta e non registriamo niente." and a self-check that is not stored. (6) **`source`, `kind: legal`**: the plain version first behind a switch ("In parole semplici" / "Testo della legge"), commi numbered in the margin, marks with their role and icon, "Leggi con me"; every part is an exact substring of the imported reference text (`E-QUOTE-REF`, whitespace squished), a plain version on every part of a core card, at most 60 words per part, historical fields refused. (7) **The apparatus budget** `E-LESSON-APPARATUS-WORDS` (250 words open by default on core cards, 240 words of originals closed) is checked in `Validation::Lesson2Checks` from `Lessons::Blocks.apparatus_words` and `closed_original_words`; the branches of the other families (dialogue lines, mirror rows, glossary, document blocks) are theirs to add there. (8) **Plumbing every family needs**: `LessonPagesHelper#lesson_family_stylesheets` links `lesson/FAMILY.css` on the student's page, the teacher's box and the render host only when the lesson uses a type of that family; the family texts `config/locales/lesson_FAMILY.it.yml` reach the page as `t.FAMILY` (`lesson2_texts`). (9) The registry marks `document`, `source`, `reveal` and `oral` `available` (the draft kinds stay held back by their views); `test/lib/lesson_types_test.rb` and `contract.test.mjs` no longer assume that no piece is available or that every library throws `NotBuilt`.
- **Why:** the first business and law lessons (`invoice-total`, `parliament-lawmaking`) need the invoice and the legal source; the history lesson needs the crossroads and the oral. Money is shared with the practice generators later.
- **Cost:** `draw.js` and `lesson.css`-adjacent behaviour changed only by two marker shapes; the mistake card now goes through `flip.js` (same DOM, one more class `flip`). The interest convention and the "outside the imponibile" rule are the book-convention answers of business.md and will change by a new entry if the teacher's book says otherwise.
- **Not done:** Dates, NumWords, `amount_words`, the draft kinds of `document`, the historical `source`, `image` and `lesson_assets` (W2-2); the `verify` plumbing and the select check (T1) and the listen button on a model answer (T2: "Ascolta" reads the visible card); the mini outline beside the zone cards of a phone (the invoice's rows already stack).
- **Status:** implemented.
- **Back-port:** none.

## D-279 · 2026-10-12 · graphs and processes (T4b): the graph router, network, chain and the line layout of flow are available

- **Design ref:** WAVE2-COMPONENTS 2.1, 1.2 (contract v2), 1.4 (L1 to L10), D-252 pattern, D-265, D-269, D-270.
- **Design said:** one layout engine for node-and-arrow figures; `network`, `chain` and `flow layout: line` final in W2-1.
- **We do:** `lesson/diagrams/graph/router.js` (`place`, `route`, `flip`, `moveList`, signatures as frozen); `network` (pair, row, triangle, hub, fan, grid; notes, badges, holds, `everyone`, kind chips, hide per state), `chain` (line, fan, ring; "Togli una causa" with the fixed sentence; `show` states), `flow` line (stations, one second lane, returns as arcs, a token that jumps); Ruby twins `Lessons::Diagrams::{Network,Chain,Flow}` with checks, `served` (also the neutral select form), `targets`, `printed` and the descriptions; the table `network/kinds` (second table `test/fixtures/lesson2/network_kinds_expected.json`); vectors `types/network.json`, `types/chain.json`, `diagrams/flow_line.json` run by Ruby and the browser, with the printed strings and targets Ruby computed; gallery `gallery/graph.md` rendered in Chrome with no finding; `controls.js` builds the chips a type declares; draw.js passes `controls` and `mode` to layout and `{state, controls}` to describe, shows a note on a node, fades in the shapes a state adds, and has a polite live line.
- **Choices to confirm:** (1) nodes are written in reading order, so a chain link goes to the next node (or into the fan's event): that makes the layout fixed and the checks short. (2) A fan's links into the event use one word, printed once. (3) A station label is at most 4 words (the cap file says 2 to 4; the plan's own example has a one-word station). (4) The phone shows stacked nodes and a numbered list of moves (`Da A a B: ...`); a crowded wide figure takes numbers on its arrows, and if even those touch it is drawn as on a phone. (5) `states[0]` is the first state drawn; the top-level `token` is where the token was before it (a state's `via` starts there).
- **Why:** a figure is the same for every student and in print; the reading list keeps arrows readable for a student who reads with difficulty.
- **Cost:** the registry tests that named `network` as the held-back example now hold a piece back for the length of a test (`test/support/reserved_piece.rb`).
- **Status:** decided; the select mode is covered by figure tests until the `select` check (T1) can show it in a lesson.
- **Back-port:** none.

## D-280 · 2026-10-12 · charts (T6, W2-1): the axis engine, `climograph` with the vetted stations, `bar_model` parts and percent, `seats` with sliders, the leak rules L4, L5 and L7 wired

- **Design ref:** `prep/rich-lessons/WAVE2-COMPONENTS.md` 2.4 (charts and quantities), 1.1 (truth by construction), 1.4 (L2, L4, L5, L7), 1.9 (`geo/stations`); D-252, D-253, D-265, D-269, D-270.
- **We do:** (1) **The axis engine** `lesson/diagrams/chart/axis.js` on its frozen signatures: `linear` picks the smallest 1-2-5 step whose labels fit (so a tick is dropped, never a text shrunk), `fromZero` puts the baseline in the domain, the domain grows to whole steps; `log` ticks on powers of ten and drops every other decade when the labels would touch; `readCursor` steps by grid steps (Home and End, a label for the live line); `legend` gives each series its own pattern; `valueTable` is the table of P2. Optional keys the signatures leave room for: `orient` ("y": labels one above the other) and `nice` (keep the domain). `chart/format.js` writes exact numbers the Italian way (`1.860,5`, a true minus) and the author's way (`1860,5`), half up, with a Ruby twin `Lessons::Diagrams::ChartSupport`. (2) **`climograph`**: bars for the rain, a line for the temperature, on the Bagnouls-Gaussen scale (mm = 2 x degrees, zeros aligned); **above 100 mm the scale is smaller, in a marked band (Walter and Lieth)**, because the strict 2:1 scale would need 384 degrees for a monsoon month of 768 mm; the band says so in the legend. Arid months (P <= 2T, so never a month under zero), annual total, mean, warmest and coldest month and the range are computed in `Lessons::Diagrams::Climograph.stats` and `chart/climate.js` (shared vectors `test/fixtures/lesson2/climate.json`, exact fractions); the arid months are hatched between the bar and the line. One scale at a time: the axis of a layer that is not shown is not drawn, so a state that shows only the rain has only the mm axis. The read cursor is a stepper "Nessuno, Gennaio ... Dicembre" with its - and + buttons; it reads only the shown layers into a live line. "Vedi i numeri" opens the table (printed always, only the shown layers) and the source. **`station:` is `geo/stations.ID`** (the frozen `data_ref`; the plan wrote `brasilia` for short): the server resolves it (`Climograph.served`: the numbers, `place_it` "Brasília (Brasile)", `lat`, `alt_m`, `source_it`), so the page never loads the table; an unknown station is `E-LESSON-DATA`. Select mode (`mode: "select"`): twelve identical neutral month columns `t1..t12`, no hatch, no computed line. (3) **`geo/stations`** (`config/banco/data/geo/stations.yml`): 21 stations, WMO normals 1991-2020 as archived by NOAA NCEI (Winnipeg: Environment and Climate Change Canada), values with the decimal comma exactly as published; Roma Ciampino is left out (three months of rain missing in the primary). Names are the Italian exonyms of the school books. **The second table** `geo/stations_expected` is a summary of an independent computation (Meteostat's 1991-2020 normals; our own mean of NOAA GSOD for Roma Fiumicino): the annual mean, the annual total, the extremes, the arid months. The monthly numbers of the second source are **not copied** because Meteostat is CC BY-NC 4.0 and the repository is public; `test/lib/stations_test.rb` derives the same from the first table and compares (0,5 degrees, widened with a stated reason where a service's daily mean is defined differently, at most 2; total within max(20 mm, 10 %); arid months equal except the ones named as borderline). `bin/build-lesson-data` compiles both. (4) **`bar_model`**: `parts` (bars of parts on one scale, one total; a hidden part is the total less the parts that show, its value is served as `null` and drawn "?") and `percent` (a bar with euro above and percent below on one scale, the 100 % and each mark a tick; `anchor` finds the 100 % exactly; `chain` draws a new line per step, to scale; euro half up to the cent). **Exactness and hiding:** `values` (the value of each mark, `null` when hidden) and `chain_values` are computed by `BarModel.percent_values` (Ruby) and its JS twin and served beside the fields; `hide[]` (the percents whose value is hidden) is served, because it holds positions, not values; `base` is withheld when the 100 % is hidden; a hidden step hides every value after it. `fraction` stays reserved. (5) **`seats`**: hemicycle (concentric rows, seats per row proportional to the radius, groups as wedges in reading order) or grid (10 or 20 columns); numero legale, maggioranza dei presenti (a tie fails), assoluta, due terzi, tre quinti in integers (`seats.json`, reasoned by hand); a full dot says yes, a ring says no, a small faint dot says absent, spread evenly (positions mean nothing, only the counts are true); the readout lines are the live line. `try` makes two sliders with - and + (native range, the arrow keys); `reachable()` lists every number the readout can print inside the ranges. **YAML reads a bare `yes:` as the boolean true**, so `Directives.yaml` turns a key that came out as `true` into `yes` (no field of ours is called on, true or no). (6) **The leak rules, wired for every available wave 2 type:** `Lessons::Diagrams.answer_leaks` and `Lesson2Checks#answer_leaks` give `W-CHECK-ANSWER-IN-DIAGRAM` (L4: a check's answer equals a number the figure prints in some state), `E-CHECK-ANSWER-BY-SIMULATION` (L5: it equals a number a control can make the readout show; `reachable_ok_it` is the way past) and `E-DIAGRAM-REACHABLE-CAP` (more than 500 values on a card with a check); `static_figure` is L7 (a figure in an exercise of the try card has no `read`, `try`, `toggle`, `controls` or `run`). Three bad fixtures (`bad/diagram-climograph-unknown-station.md`, `bad/check-answer-by-simulation.md`, `bad/diagram-reachable-cap.md`) moved from `pending`. (7) **The renderer:** `draw.js` builds the controls a type declares (`diagrams/controls.js`: slider, stepper, toggle, chips; a label on a line of its own, then the buttons and the value, so it fits a phone), draws `shapes[].pattern` from a fixed `<defs>` per figure (hatch, dots, cross, grid), shows `scene.values` as "Vedi i numeri" (opened for print) and `scene.live` in a visually hidden polite region that speaks only after the student has acted; `registry.describe(data, ctx)` and `makeContext` carry `state`, `controls`, `mode` and `revealed`; `StudentBody.diagram` asks the type for its own `served` (the generic projection otherwise). The family stylesheet (`lesson/chart.css`) is linked by `lesson_family_stylesheets` in the student's page, the teacher's box and the render host, and the family's texts (`lesson_chart.it.yml`, keys `chart_*`) join the page's texts. (8) Tests: `chart_axis`, `chart_types` (every vector at 320, 390, 768, 1280 and 18, 20, 26 px, in every state, both ways), `test/lib/lessons/chart_types_test.rb` (semantic, printed, reachable, served, the sentinel property for hidden values), `test/lib/stations_test.rb`, `test/system/lesson_chart_gallery_test.rb` (the gallery `gallery/chart.md` at 390 and 1366 with shots, the cursor, the sliders and the keyboard, forced colours, print).
- **Why:** a chart cannot lie when our code draws it from a vetted table or from exact numbers; the three types are what `climates-biomes`, `invoice-total` and `parliament-lawmaking` need, and the leak rules had no code before a type had controls.
- **Cost:** a lesson with a climograph loads about 10 KB gzip of chart code (axis, climograph, format, schema; the controls module and the shared renderer additions are 1.5 KB gzip more), a bar_model about 9.5 KB, seats about 5.5 KB; nothing else loads them. The stations table is 9.8 KB raw, 2.6 KB gzip (the page never loads it: the server resolves a station). Seats have no non-colour carrier for groups except position and the legend (the wedges are contiguous); a role colour or the tones `dgs-g0..g3` carry the groups.
- **Not done:** `modulepreload` for the types of a lesson (T1's page-head work); the select plumbing that turns `shapes[].target` into focusable hit areas and the select endpoint (T1: the types return their targets and draw neutral columns); the speech segments of the three types (the default `describe` is read); `chart` and `scale` (W2-2); the review of the stations table by a model of another family; the teacher's rendering of `mode: "teacher"` solutions (a hidden part is `?` for the teacher too, until the teacher's strip shows solutions).
- **Status:** decided; the three pieces are `available` in `lesson_types.yml`
- **Back-port:** none.

## D-281 · 2026-10-12 · wave 2 integration (w2-int): where the six parallel tracks overlapped, one implementation was kept

- **Design ref:** `prep/rich-lessons/WAVE2-COMPONENTS.md` 1.2 (the component contract), 1.4 (L3 to L5), 5 (the tracks); D-265, D-273 to D-280.
- **Design said:** the tracks T1, T9, T5b, T8, T4b and T6 build on W2-0's contract in parallel; the integrator merges them.
- **We do:** the branches were merged in the order T1, T9, T5b, T8, T4b, T6. The D numbers of the tracks were renumbered in that order (T1 D-273; T9 D-274, D-275; T5b D-272, D-276, D-277; T8 D-278; T4b D-279; T6 D-280; the citations in each track's own files follow). Four things had been built twice and were reduced to one: (1) **L4 and L5**: `Lessons::Blocks::Truth` (T1) is the one implementation; T9's `Lessons::Leaks` and T6's `Lessons::Diagrams.answer_leaks` are removed, their tests run on Truth (`test/lib/lessons/leaks_test.rb`); Truth compares answers without spaces and with the true minus sign, calls a type's `printed(data, state_index)` as every type implements it, and ignores a figure whose own data is wrong (its own findings say so). A leak finding sits on the answer line of the check.
