## D-292 · 2026-10-13 · wave 2 final fixes: seats.threshold, chem.count without a pick, bare atoms in molecule, span_select in English or Spanish, sentence neutral available, a served example never has one state, no empty details on a failed figure

- **Design ref:** WAVE2-COMPONENTS 1.10 (`verify`), 2.4 (`seats`), 2.5 (`molecule`), 2.6 (`word_parts`), 2.11 (`span_select`), 1.11 (target-language keys); D-268, D-273, D-285, D-291; the final review of the nine drafts.
- **Design said:** `seats.threshold` is a `verify` function of W2-1; `'2 O'` draws two unbound atoms; `sentence` and `tiles` accept `text_it | text_en | text_es`; an example's diagram states match its steps one to one.
- **We do:** (1) `Lessons::Diagrams::Seats.verify_functions` registers `seats.threshold {threshold, seats, present?}` and gives the integer the readout prints (`legal_number`, `present_majority`, `absolute_majority`, `two_thirds`, `three_fifths`). (2) `chem.count` reads `element` as well as `pick`, and without either it answers the number of all atoms (a check answers a number, not a map). (3) `molecule` and `formula show: molecules` draw a bare atom of a nonmetal, halogen or noble gas that the library has no row for (`O`, `2 O`: one atom, no bonds, named as the element, from `chem/elements`); a metal or a metalloid is never a lone atom, so `Zn` stays `E-LESSON-DATA` (Ruby `ScienceSupport.atom_row`, browser `science/common.js` `atomRow`; vectors `molecule-lone-nonmetal-atoms` and `molecule-lone-metal-atom-not-drawn`). (4) `span_select` takes `text_it`, `text_en` or `text_es` for the sentence and its spans (one language, spans are exact pieces, `E-LESSON-CHECK` and `E-LESSON-LANG`); the page draws the English or Spanish text with its `lang`, the schema (`lesson.json`), the whitelist and `StudentBody` follow; the English draft needed it and the plan listed only `sentence` and `tiles`. (5) The `sentence` views `text_en` and `text_es` are `available` in `lesson_types.yml`: T1 built them in D-273 and the registry still held them back. (6) `word_parts` allows 20 letters in a word (was 16): `desossiribonucleico` has 19 and is the word of the lesson; the cap in `validation_rules.yml` and `diagrams/words/texts.js` change together (rules version 9 is still the wave's). (7) `StudentBody.example` cut a figure's states at the blank step, and one state or none is below the schema's `minItems: 2`: the browser refused the figure (`E-LESSON-DIAGRAM /states too few items`, a blank figure); with one state left that state becomes the figure, with none the figure is its base. (8) `draw.js` made the box "Vedi i numeri" without `hidden`, and a figure that failed returned before hiding it: Chrome wrote its own English "Details" beside "Descrizione"; the box starts hidden. The description of a figure is the base size (it was 0.8 of it). (9) System tests: a failed figure has no `details` without a summary, and the last block of a card ends above the fixed bar when the page is scrolled to the end, at 390 and 1366 px (the reviewer's shots only looked covered: they clip at the viewport).
- **Deviations and choices:** the arguments of `seats.threshold` were not frozen; the shape above is the one the law draft used. `chem.count` with no element answering a total is the draft's own reading (its `STATUS.md`). A bare atom is not offered for metals on purpose (a metal is a patch).
- **Not changed, for the content and data agents:** the drafts must follow the frozen schemas for `strand` (the `backbone` set has one target per side, not one per nucleotide), `formula` (target ids are `f1p4`, not `f1.p4`), `climograph` (`station: geo/stations.mumbai`), `cross_section` (`stepper` is a boolean), `insolation` bands (no `id`), `chain` (a fan link goes to the next node or into the event), `map` (arrows are W2-2), `cascade` (no hidden rows: its bars would show the value), `word_parts` (states keep the number of words); `bits.add` answers in the base of its inputs (the draft answers in decimal); the glossary term of the computer science draft has a digit. Data not written: `nola` in `history/places` (Pleiades id and second table), `english/contractions` (its second table and review), the imported `costituzione-artt-55-96` and `costituzione-artt-134-139` texts (operator import, D-074).
- **Why:** the final review found these as software faults (a function not registered, a map returned for a number, a figure refused by its own schema, a label in the wrong language) and the drafts could not be corrected until they were gone.
- **Cost:** none for the student; the Spanish and English drafts can now be written in their language.
- **Status:** decided
- **Back-port:** none.

## D-293 · 2026-10-13 · render check of wave 2: a figure measured while hidden is never cached, the print views are not judged, the plate words are measured as drawn, the rendering waits no longer than needed

- **Design ref:** D-249, D-255 (the render check), D-276, D-277 (maps and callouts), the chart axis engine (climograph)
- **Found:** the production render of the history and geography drafts failed on every map and climograph. Cause one: `makeMeasure` (draw.js) cached `0 x 0` for every text it measured while the figure sat in a hidden card (the cards view shows one card; a map loads its base asynchronously and draws once at the fallback width 320). Layouts built on those zeros put "Est" at the right edge with width 0 (so the bold word ran out of the box), stacked callouts and labels, and gave the climograph's tick engine a pitch test against zero-width labels (every tick kept: the smear at 390 px). Cause two: the print views (`.dg-print`, hidden on screen) hold `.dg-label`s with no box; the check read them as "outside the figure" and "overlapping". Cause three: the stacked table's visually hidden `thead` cells were reported as overflowing a 30 px box. Cause four: the `chain` fan-in word ("solo prima") was measured in regular weight and drawn in bold.
- **We do:** the measure never caches or trusts a zero box (`degenerate`), and the figure draws again when it shows (the resize observer also fires on `degenerate`); the render host judges only labels with a box, skips a clipped table head, waits at most 120 ms for the two animation frames (a throttled page no longer stalls a card) and 90 ms for the redraw debounce; `measure(text, px, maxW, cls)` takes the label's classes, used by `plateLabel` and the chain words, and a plate label is kept inside the figure. Tests: `lesson/test/render_fit.test.mjs` (every map vector at 320 to 1366 px, light and the 20 and 26 px sizes: labels inside, no overlap, the map scales to its box; every climograph vector: no overlap, tick labels few enough for the height), `test/validation/lesson_render_runner_test.rb` (the maps and chart galleries in Chrome: no layout error, no timeout, under half the revision budget).
- **Not changed:** the print check of a summary card whose schema is a 12 node decision tree (`flow` line layout, about 940 px tall at A4 width) still takes two pages; that is the drafts' content, to be shortened or split by the author. The seats gallery card (two steppers side by side) overflows at 390 px; not touched.
- **Status:** decided
- **Back-port:** none.

## D-294 · 2026-10-15 · entry diagnosis: no daily cap; dependencies and each run's sitting budgets stay

- **Design ref:** B-12, Q11, the operator's days decision, `docs/rules/diagnosis-1.md` section 6
- **Found:** the official student did not see all the entry tests: the daily caps (`DAILY_MAX_SUBJECTS` = 2, `DAILY_MAX_MINUTES` = 75) turned every further subject into "Domani".
- **Operator (2026-10-15):** asked whether to lift or raise the cap, answered "Togli il limite giornaliero".
- **We do:** both caps are removed (constants, `DailyPlan`, `Availability`). Every subject whose dependencies are met (`depends_on_subjects`: the first sitting of each dependency is closed) is startable, whatever was done today. A subject waiting on a dependency says why ("Dopo la prima seduta di Matematica"); the "Domani" state is gone. Unchanged: the sitting budgets (30 and 25 minutes, the short-answer reserve, the automatic second sitting from the next calendar day). The list proposes the sittings in progress and the first subject to begin.
- **Rules version:** `diagnosis/1` does not change. The caps never entered the engine, the grading or the derivation, only which subject the list lets the student open, so no run, event or result changes meaning and existing runs stay valid.
- **Status:** decided
- **Back-port:** none.

## D-295 · 2026-10-15 · number and fraction answers: a letter and "=" or one pair of parentheses are read, and an unreadable answer says what to write

- **Design ref:** E-03, `Grading::Closed::Numbers`, `Grading::Closed::Fractions`
- **Found:** on a number item of the entry test, the student's answers were refused as unreadable nine times in one minute, and the student typed an arbitrary number to get past. Invalid inputs keep no text, so the typed forms are unknown, but the grader refused reasonable ones (`n = -2`, `(-2)`) with the generic "Non riesco a leggere la risposta".
- **We do:** a number (and each fraction box) may carry one leading Latin letter and "=" (`n = -2`, `x=3`, `N = 2,5`) and one pair of parentheses around the whole value (`(-2)`, `( 2,5 )`, `n = (-2)`); they are stripped before the usual reading, so `normalized` and the typical-error matching see the bare value. Not read, as before: a second letter (`n = m = 2`), the letter after the value (`2 = n`), nested or unbalanced parentheses, a slash in a number box. The browser sends the text as typed and does not pre-validate, so only the server changed. Two new invalid codes with their own text: `unreadable_number` ("Scrivi solo il numero, per esempio −3 oppure 2,5.") and `unreadable_fraction` ("Scrivi la frazione, per esempio −3/4."), replacing `unparseable` for those two components only; `invalid_input` (and `practice_invalid_input`) keep recording the code and never the typed text. Empty answers, `use_comma`, `thousands_separator` and every other verdict are unchanged.
- **Rules version:** none changes: `grader_version` of a grading is the git sha, which moves with this commit. No earlier verdict changes: only answers that were invalid become gradable.
- **Status:** decided
- **Back-port:** none.

## D-296 · 2026-10-16 · the direction of an accent (grave or acute) never makes an answer wrong

- **Design ref:** E-03, `Grading::Closed::Text`, `Grading::Closed` (choice), `Validation::InstanceChecks`
- **Operator (2026-10-16):** from now on we do not distinguish much between è and é. An Italian keyboard has à è é ì ò ù and no á í ó ú, and the real exams are handwritten, where the direction of the mark cannot be told apart. This holds in every subject, Spanish included.
- **We do:** in `normalized_text`, an answer that equals an accepted answer once grave and acute are made one mark (NFD, U+0300 to U+0301, NFC, on both sides) is `correct`, whatever the item's `accent_policy`; `normalized` stays the student's normalized answer, and a declared error value that equals the key up to direction can no longer be hit. In `choice`, an option whose text equals the key option's text up to the same folding (after the text normalization) is `correct`; the grader reads the texts from the instance display, so the diagnosis item `italian-spelling-accent-choice` now takes the grave `perchè` for `perché`. Lesson checks and practice use these graders and needed no change; the browser never compares text for a verdict. Unchanged: a missing accent (`perche`, `e` for `è`: `it_accents`, `es_accents`), an apostrophe for an accent (`it_apostrophe_accent`), an accent on the wrong vowel or syllable, and the letters ñ and ü. Mechanical validation gains `E-ACCENT-DIRECTION` for new item revisions: a choice instance with two options equal up to direction, or a declared error value equal to the key up to direction. The authors' briefs carry one line saying so. What the lessons teach (the Spanish tilde is always acute) does not change.
- **Rules version:** none changes: `grader_version` of a grading is the git sha, which moves with this commit. Stored gradings are not regraded: the ledger is append-only and the rule holds from now on. Stored item revisions are not re-validated; the grader rule covers them.
- **Status:** decided
- **Back-port:** none.

## D-297 · 2026-10-16 · a repeated item shows the instance least alike the ones already served; instances of one item must not look alike

- **Design ref:** B-02 (sequencing), `Diagnosis::Candidates`, `Diagnosis::Engine.choose`, A-06 (`W-INSTANCES-ALIKE`)
- **Problem:** the student found the history and law questions "all look the same": in one run the engine served the same matching item again for the deciding answer, and the second instance shared most of its left rows with the first.
- **We do (engine):** when the item the engine is about to serve was already served in this run, it serves the instance of that item with the least text in common with the instances of it already served (`Diagnosis::Overlap.least_alike`). `Plan::Instance#texts` carries `{strong:, weak:}`, filled by `Diagnosis::InstanceTexts` in the loader from the instance display with `Grading::Closed::Text.normalize` (the engine stays free of ActiveRecord). Strong: the stem, a testlet's passage, the options, the ordering elements, the matching left rows (sub items included). Weak: the right column of a matching (categories repeat by nature), minus any text also strong. Measure: `alike(a, b) = 2 * |strong(a) & strong(b)| + |weak(a) & weak(b)|`, summed over the served instances of the item; the lowest sum wins and ties keep the seeded order, so a run with no repeat, or with no texts in the plan (simulations), chooses exactly as before. The choice of the item and the skill is unchanged: only which instance of the chosen item.
- **We do (validation):** `W-INSTANCES-ALIKE` (warning, `ruby` stage, static and generated items): two instances of one item share more than `pool.alike_share` (0.5, of the larger side) of the matching left rows, the ordering elements, or the choice options under the same stem, after the same normalization. Stored revisions are not re-validated. The two item briefs carry one line: instances of one item must look different to the student.
- **Rules version:** `diagnosis/1` and `engine/1` do not change: no constant of the rules changed, and a run replays from its logged `item_served` events (the fold reads which instance was served, never why), so past runs derive the same states; only live choices made after the deploy differ, and only in a repeat. `validation_rules.yml` stays at version 9 (as for the supports of D-216 and `E-ACCENT-DIRECTION` of D-296: a new check on content, a bump would flag every pinned revision as validated under older rules); `error_codes.yml` goes to version 22 for the new code.
- **Status:** decided
- **Back-port:** none.

## D-298 · 2026-10-16 · sitting feedback: the refused text is kept for the teacher, a pause after a refusal and the answer format at the second one, a pause suggested after two subjects in a day, a finished subject shows as finished

- **Design ref:** D-295, D-294, `Diagnosis::AnswerRecorder`, `Practice::AnswerRecorder`, `Diagnosis::Availability`, `sitting_controller.js`
- **Found:** on the entry test the student's number answers were refused as unreadable 23 times in two minutes on one item, often 3 or 4 in the same second, as if Enter were pressed again and again on the send button; the student then typed another number to get past. The event kept only the code, so the teacher could not see what was typed. The same morning the student did five subjects in a row (about 80 minutes) and paused the sixth after one answer. The list showed "In pausa" for a subject whose frontier was empty (for instance right after the teacher confirmed a short-answer grade): opening it only closed the run.
- **We do:**
  1. The app events `invalid_input` and `practice_invalid_input` now carry `text`, the typed text cut to 200 characters, for every invalid code (an empty answer writes no event). This replaces D-295's "never the typed text". The teacher reads it where the answers are read: the report (`Diagnosis::Report` with `with_answers: true`, section "Tentativi non letti" with the answer finally accepted) and the practice trail (under the answer of the try, in order, deduplicated with a count). The agent's report (`with_answers: false`, `/api/v1`) has no `refused_tries` key and never carries the text, exactly like the answers (operator Q8). `payload_json` joins the filtered log names so the text is not written to the request log (D-069).
  2. After an invalid answer the send button and "Non lo so" are inert for 1.5 seconds (`items/refusals.js`, used by the sitting and the practice page), the focus stays in the box, and when the same item is refused a second time its `answer_format_it` (if any) is shown above the box with the message in a polite live region (`items/refusal_notice.js`), and stays for that item. Grading does not change.
  3. When the student has worked on two or more subjects today (a sitting started today, Rome date; `Diagnosis::Pause`), the list and the end-of-subject screen show one line: "Hai già fatto due prove oggi: fai una pausa prima della prossima. Puoi riprendere quando vuoi." A suggestion only: no limit, no button taken away (D-294).
  4. A run whose engine's next action is `close_run` (`Conductor#finished?`) counts as completed in the student's list (label "Fatto") and in `Diagnosis::Report#status`, like a run held for pending answers. The list and the report only read; the close row is written when the student opens the run or its end screen, as before (the end screen now writes it instead of sending the student back to the sitting page).
- **Rules version:** none changes.
- **Status:** decided
- **Back-port:** none.

## D-299 · 2026-10-16 · content search (S1): one derived lexical index, three doors, nothing of the student's searches kept

- **Design ref:** firm rules 1, 2, 4 and 5; D-217 (roles and trial students), D-218 (references on the teacher's pages), D-236 (the student's course pages), D-298 (the refused text), `Course::Catalog`, `Course::StudentView`, `Items::Part`, `Lessons::StudentBody`
- **Asked:** a way to find things in the content: the student looks for a lesson, a word or an exercise; the teacher for anything, including what the student wrote; the agents (the content agents and the lead's sessions) for what exists before they write a duplicate, and for the article of a reference text to cite.
- **Operator decisions (2026-10-16):**
  1. One content search with three doors: the student, the teacher (and guests, read-only), the agents (`banco search`).
  2. A semantic ranking is wanted, for the teacher and the agents only. The student's search never touches a model (firm rule 1): lexical only, enforced in code and by a test. S1 builds the lexical engine and leaves the places where S2 plugs the semantic one in; the semantic part (embedding client, vectors, hybrid ranking, "Simili", `--like`) is the next entry.
  3. The student finds lessons (down to the card), glossary terms, topics and all the exercises of the courses open to them, done or not. Never entry-test (diagnosis) items, answer keys, solutions, hints, error catalogues, drafts or anything of a course not open to them, nor anything of another student.
  4. The student's searches are not recorded: no app event, no table, the words filtered from the request log, nothing shown to the teacher.
  5. The teacher searches the student's answers too (teacher role only: not guests, never the agents). Answers are searched lexically only.
- **We do:**
  1. **A derived index, outside the ledger.** A third SQLite database `search` (`config/database.yml`; production file `$BANCO_DATA_DIR/production_search.sqlite3`; `storage/{development,test}_search.sqlite3`), `database_tasks: false`, its schema in code (`Search::Schema`, version in `PRAGMA user_version`): no Rails migration, no append-only trigger, no table or column of the primary database changes (`bin/check-structure` is unaffected, firm rule 4 untouched). It is disposable: deleting the file and running `bin/rails banco:search:rebuild` gives the same rows (`Search::Index.replace_group` writes only what changed, so two builds are equal). The backup script (`traefik/banco/backup.sh` copies every `production*.sqlite3`) need not copy it; it is rebuilt in seconds.
  2. **Documents.** One row per unit (`Search::Doc`, `Search::Builders::*`, groups `lessons topics skills items references syllabus findings answers`): `lesson_card` (a banco.lesson/2 card through `Lessons::StudentBody`, so only the whitelist the student is served; a banco.lesson/1 section), `glossary_term` (with the card that marks it), `topic`, `course`, `skill`, `item`, `item_instance` (an entry-test instance), `practice_item` (an instance as `Items::Part` serves it), `reference_article` (per `Art. N`, else per paragraphs), `syllabus_line`, `finding`, `student_answer`. The index holds the latest revision of each object and the revisions a student may be shown (the approved topic revisions and what they pin). No document holds an answer key, a solution, a final answer or the error values. Each kind has one fixed audience: `student`, `staff` or `teacher` (`student_answer` only).
  3. **Lexical engine.** SQLite FTS5 (`unicode61 remove_diacritics 2`, so è and e are equal, like D-296) over title, body and a column of Snowball stems; a contentless trigram table for typos. The stemmer is the `ruby-stemmer` gem (libstemmer's own Snowball code for Italian, Spanish and English; a document carries Italian and the language its subject teaches, a query is stemmed in the three; deterministic, vectors in `test/models/search/text_test.rb`, no hand-made rules: "frazionaria" does not find "frazioni" because the stems differ). Steps: an exact key first (`math.powers-properties`); every word of the question (stop words dropped from a long question, the last word as a prefix); any word when that finds fewer than three; the words corrected by edit distance against the words of the documents the door can see (found through the trigram table) when that still finds few. Ranking: bm25 with the title weighted, plus a bonus for a title that holds the words, then `Search::Ranker` (the one place where lists become an order).
  4. **Visibility is decided at query time, never stored.** `Search::Scope::Student` asks `Course::StudentView` which lesson, topic and item revisions this student's catalog shows (official: approved topics of a released course; trial student: the latest map, drafts included, D-217; the teacher's preview and readers: nothing) and filters the documents to those revisions, to the student kinds and to the audience `student`; a practice item must also be an item of kind `practice_item` in the primary database. Withdrawing a release closes the door at once, with no new index. `Scope::Staff` (teacher, guests) and `Scope::Agent` show the latest revision of each object, every status; only the teacher's scope may include `student_answer`, for one student (`?student=KEY`, the official one by default). The agents' scope has no such kind: asking for it is `E-NOT-FOUND`.
  5. **Three doors.** `GET /search` (the student: grouped by kind, a snippet with the matched words, a link to the lesson at its card `#scheda-N`, the glossary definition inline, an exercise to the topic's practice page and never past the practice selector; "Cerca" in the student menu, not in a sitting, not in the preview); `GET /teacher/search` (teacher and guests: filters, `RefsHelper#ref_for` for skill and item keys, links to the existing pages, a tab for the student's answers for the teacher only); `GET /api/v1/search` and `banco search QUERY [--subject S] [--kind K] [--status S] [--limit N] [--json]`, answer `{query, semantic, indexed, results: [{kind, subject, key, revision_id, status, title, snippet, score, ref}]}` (`semantic` is false in S1, and will be false whenever the embedding service is not set up or does not answer). One line in the authoring briefs and the review briefs: search before writing, cite a reference found with `--kind reference_article`.
  6. **The student's words are not kept.** `q` joins the filtered parameter names (`[FILTERED]` in the request log), the search statements run under the name `SCHEMA` so that the log subscriber does not print them at any log level, the page is `no-store` with `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, and the controller writes no app event, row or cache entry. The web proxy's own access log is outside Rails: it may hold the query string of `/search`.
  7. **Freshness.** `Searchable` (a line in the models whose rows change what is found: item, lesson, topic, course, graph and blueprint revisions, validations, findings, reference texts, programme lines, attempts, the visibility decisions, the refused-text events) enqueues `SearchIndexJob` for the groups it touches (`Search::Indexer::TOUCHES`), 20 seconds later so that a burst is one build; it never fails the write and is off in the tests (`config.x.search.index_on_write`). A nightly full rebuild (`config/recurring.yml`) repairs a missed update. The first build after a deploy is `bin/rails banco:search:rebuild`; until then the doors say the index is not ready.
  8. **The firm rules.** 1: the student's door has no dependency on any embedding client and `Scope::Student#semantic?` is false (a test makes the engine's semantic hook raise and the student's search still works). 2: no decision anywhere in the search. 3: no agent code runs in Rails. 4: the ledger is untouched, the index is a separate derived file. 5: content stays in Rails revisions, the index is derived. 6: names English, texts Italian (`config/locales/search.it.yml`, `teacher.search.*`).
- **S2 plugs in at:** `Search::Scope#semantic?` (true for `Staff` and `Agent` when the embedding service is set up), `Search::Engine#semantic_list` (the semantic candidates), `Search::Ranker.fuse` (reciprocal rank fusion with k = 60 between the key hits and the rest), the `semantic` member of the engine result and of the API answer, and a vectors table in the search database (`Search::Schema`, version bump). Not in S1: the embedding client, vectors, hybrid ranking, "Simili", `--like`.
- **Why:** one index serves three doors with different eyes; making visibility a question asked of the pages' own code at the moment of the search means the index can never be a second, stale source of permissions.
- **Cost:** the `ruby-stemmer` gem (a small native extension, built in the Docker build stage like `bootsnap`); a third database file to keep out of the backups or ignore; a full rebuild reads the primary database (seconds at this size).
- **Rules version:** none changes.
- **Status:** decided
- **Back-port:** none.

## D-300 · 2026-10-16 · content search (S2): embeddings, hybrid ranking and "Simili" for the teacher and the agents; the student's door stays model-free

- **Design ref:** D-299 (the plug-in points S1 left), firm rules 1 and 4; D-217, D-218.
- **Asked:** the semantic part of D-299: find what means the same with other words, and find the near-duplicates of an item or a lesson card before a reviewer or an author lets them in.
- **We do:**
  1. **The embedding service.** `Search::Embedder` (resolver) with `Embedder::Http` and `Embedder::Stub`. `BANCO_EMBED_URL` (production `http://banco-embed:80`: Hugging Face text-embeddings-inference, model `BAAI/bge-m3`, 1024 dimensions, normalized, internal network only) is the whole configuration: `POST /embed {"inputs": [..]}` answers one vector per input, no query/passage prefixes, the server truncates long inputs. A request carries at most 8 inputs (`Embedder::Http::BATCH`; the server's own cap is 8 inputs and 4096 tokens), a passage is cut at 2,000 characters before sending. Timeouts: 3 s for a question, 60 s for a batch of passages; no retries in the request path. `BANCO_EMBED_MODEL` names the model recorded with the vectors, `BANCO_EMBED_MIN_SIMILARITY` (default 0.5 for bge-m3) is the cosine under which a neighbour is not listed. **The stub** (`config.x.search.embedder = :stub`, set by `BANCO_EMBED_STUB=1` for development and CI) is chosen by configuration, never by the presence of a network: hashed words (Snowball stem of each), 1024 dimensions, near-duplicates near; the tests give it a synonym table to show a paraphrase.
  2. **When the service is unset or down, nothing fails.** The search is the lexical one, `semantic: false` in the API answer, one log line without the question (`search: the embedding service did not answer ...`); after a failure the engine leaves the service alone for 30 s, so a hung service costs one timeout. The doors never show an error for it.
  3. **Vectors.** Table `search_vectors` in the search database (`Search::Schema` version 2: a bump drops and recreates, the index is disposable): `doc_id`, the document's `digest`, `model`, `dim`, `vec` (float32 blob) and `coarse` (128 floats, see 5). One per content document; never a `student_answer`, never a document of the teacher's audience (`Vectors::ELIGIBLE_KINDS`, `eligible_sql`), so no text a student typed goes to the model. A vector is current when its digest equals the document's and its model and dimension are the embedder's: a changed document loses its vector when `Index` rewrites it, a model or dimension change makes every vector stale, and the next build embeds them again. **Embedding happens in the index job and the rebuild task, never in a request** (`Indexer.embed!` after `reindex`; `SearchIndexJob` stops embedding after 20 minutes and the next run goes on). The rebuild builds the lexical index first and survives a service that is down: the vectors are left for the next run. `bin/rails banco:search:status` says how many documents have a current vector, the model and the dimension. The first full embedding of about 9,600 documents is 1,200 requests of 8: an estimate of 30 to 60 minutes on the production CPU (a question takes about 0.17 s; a batch of passages several times that); later runs embed only what changed.
  4. **Hybrid ranking, for `Scope::Staff` (not its answers tab) and `Scope::Agent` only.** `semantic?` is true there when an embedder is configured, false for `Scope::Student` (stated in the class itself) and false for the teacher's answers tab (no student text is ever a question to the model). `Ranker.fuse`: the exact key hits first, then reciprocal rank fusion (k = 60) of the lexical list and the cosine list (the 50 nearest documents of the scope, at least `min_similarity`). The question is embedded in a thread at the start of the search, beside the lexical queries. Without a service, or before any vector exists, the answer is the lexical one with `semantic: false`.
  5. **Cosine without a library.** Brute force in Ruby over the documents the scope may see (the same SQL clause as the lexical list): 9,600 x 1,024 floats is about a second, too slow, so each vector also has a coarse form of 128 floats (signed sums of the dimensions, a fixed sparse random projection, normalized); the question is compared with the coarse forms of the scope's documents, the best 200 go to the exact comparison. Measured with the stub on 9,600 documents of 1,024 dimensions: 220 to 290 ms for the whole hybrid query on a busy development machine, the cosine pass being the larger share; with the real model add the 0.17 s of the question's embedding (overlapped with the lexical queries, which take 30 ms). No sqlite-vec: it would be a native extension to vendor for a corpus this size.
  6. **"Simili".** `Engine#like(ref)`: the nearest neighbours of an object from its stored vector (no call to the service), the object itself left out. `ref` is a key or an address `kind:KEY#anchor` as `Links.address` writes it. By default neighbours are of the same family (questions with questions: `item`, `item_instance`, `practice_item`; cards with glossary terms), `--kind` overrides; other documents with the same key (the other instances of an item) are kept and labelled (`same_object: true` in the API, "stessa cosa, altra versione" on the page): that is how a reviewer sees instances that are alike. `GET /api/v1/search?like=...` and `banco search --like REF` (the contract command `search` gains `--like`; the answer adds `like:` and, when the object has no vector, `semantic: false`, no results and a `note`; the service not set up is `E-NOT-FOUND` on field `like`). The teacher's page `GET /teacher/search?like=...`, and a "Simili" button on the item cards (skill screen) and, in the lesson box, a list for the lesson and each card; the buttons exist only when an embedder is configured. The student's door has no such thing.
  7. **The notice for a typo.** When the hits come only from the typo fallback, the student's page and the teacher's say so: "Non ho trovato «costituzione». Forse cercavi «sostituzione»?", the corrected words being links that run the search (the teacher's keep the filters). `Engine::Result#corrections` and `#only_corrected?`.
  8. **The firm rules.** 1: the student's door has no dependency on the embedding client: `Scope::Student#semantic?` is false, `Engine` asks for a vector only when the scope says so, and two tests pin it (the search works with every method of the client raising; with `BANCO_EMBED_URL` set and `Net::HTTP.start` and `.new` trapped, the student's searches make no HTTP call while the agents' search does, which shows the trap is armed). The agents never get answers: `Scope::Agent` has no such kind, no answer has a vector, a test searches the answers' sentinel words through the semantic API and finds nothing. 4: the vectors are in the derived file. 6: names English, texts Italian.
  9. **Briefs.** `diagnosis-item`, `lesson` and `review` gain one line: `banco search --like KEY` on what you wrote, to find near-duplicates.
- **Production:** `BANCO_EMBED_URL=http://banco-embed:80` on the banco container; after the deploy run `bin/rails banco:search:rebuild` (the schema is version 2, so the file is recreated and every vector is built) and check `banco:search:status`. The backup need not copy the search file (D-299).
- **Why:** one engine, a second list fused in the one place that orders results; the model sits behind a client that can be absent, so the search never depends on it; the student's door is protected by a missing code path and by tests, not by a promise.
- **Cost:** the first embedding is slow; about 40 MB of vectors in the derived file (9,600 x (4 KB + 0.5 KB)); a hybrid query is the lexical one plus a cosine pass of 100 to 250 ms.
- **Rules version:** none changes.
- **Status:** decided
- **Back-port:** none.

## D-301 · 2026-10-16 · a matching with all pairs right but one counts as right, with a note

- **Design ref:** X-03 (evidence), E-03 (`Grading::Closed`, matching), A8.2 (practice outcomes), A9 (lesson checks)
- **Operator (2026-10-16):** a matching answer with all pairs right but one counts as right, with a note for the teacher. From now on; stored gradings are not regraded.
- **Found:** the matching component was all-or-nothing (`right_pairs == key.size`, else wrong or a typical error). In one run of the entry test, ten matchings were counted wrong and six of them had five of six or three of four pairs right; the skill picture came out worse than what the student knows.
- **We do (grader):** `Grading::Closed` matching gives the new verdict `nearly_correct` when the answer is not correct, hits no declared error (a declared error permutation keeps precedence and stays `typical_error`), the key has at least 3 pairs (`NEARLY_CORRECT_MIN_PAIRS`) and exactly one pair is wrong. So 3 of 4, 5 of 6 and 2 of 3 are `nearly_correct`; 2 of 4 and 4 of 6 stay `wrong`; a key of 2 pairs never. `normalized` carries `off_pair` (`left`, `given`, `key`, canonical ids). It is not `near_miss`: `NEAR_MISS = :pending` (a one-letter typo goes to the teacher) is untouched. Registered in `Grading::VERDICTS` and in `verdicts:` of `config/banco/error_codes.yml` (version 23). In a testlet, a sub item that is `nearly_correct` counts as right for the unit (all right is correct) and, in a mixture, as the other certain verdicts do (the unit goes to the teacher as undetermined).
- **We do (diagnosis):** `Diagnosis::Rules::V1::EVIDENCE["nearly_correct"] = :C` with the observation `one_pair_off` in `OBSERVATIONS`; the fold records an observation `nearly_correct` about the skill; `Diagnosis::Report` (with answers) lists the attempts as `nearly_correct` and the report page shows «Quasi tutto giusto» with the pair; the student's end screen sorts it with the right answers and shows `Grading::PairNote` under the answer.
- **We do (practice and lessons):** practice: `Practice::Outcome` reads `nearly_correct` as a credit key, so the try is `correct` (or `correct_aided`) and the serve state machine needs no new row; the feedback is «Corretto.» plus the note «Giusto, tranne una coppia: «A» va con «B», non con «C».» (`Grading::PairNote`, which reads the texts of the instance display). Lesson checks: the check is `right`, the reply carries the same line as `message_it` and the browser shows it under «Giusto».
- **Rules version:** none changes. `EVIDENCE` gains a key for a verdict no stored grading carries, so no outcome of any past run changes its evidence: a run pinned at `diagnosis/1` derives the same states before and after (as for D-295 and D-296, where the grader changed and the version did not). `practice/1` is likewise unchanged for every stored try. Stored gradings are not regraded: the ledger is append-only and the rule holds from now on.
- **Status:** decided
- **Back-port:** none.

## D-302 · 2026-10-16 · the law and economics entry test may be choice only, with ten of fifteen skills measured

- **Design ref:** `briefs/blueprint.md` rule 3 (discursive subjects: closed items, one reading testlet, exactly one short answer), A-06 (`E-POOL-REDO`, `descent_low_guess`), the blueprint schema (at most ten entries).
- **Operator (2026-10-16):** the student did not like the law entry test (30 questions in one sitting, many matchings, typed article numbers and dates); the operator asked for a multiple-choice test that is not heavy, to be taken again from the start. Asked that only ten of the fifteen skills can then be measured, the operator answered that ten are enough.
- **We do:** a new revision of the law and economics blueprint with choice items only (four options each, the wrong ones being catalogued typical errors), no reading testlet and no short answer, one sitting of about 20 minutes (about 12 to 17 questions for a typical profile in `banco diagnosis simulate`). Ten skills are entries, each with `choice_only_reason_it`; the five skills a choice-only descent cannot reach under `descent_low_guess` (legal capacity, the legal relationship and goods, the distinctions of law, legal versus social norms, the characters of a norm) are declared not measured in `not_measured_it` and are learned in the course. Rule 3 of the blueprint brief stays the default for every other discursive subject; this entry is the operator's exception for law and economics. The run in progress on the previous revision is voided by the teacher once the new revision is approved, and the student takes the new test.
- **Rules version:** none changes (`diagnosis/1`, validation rules version 9): no rule or threshold changed; a blueprint revision uses the existing schema.
- **Status:** decided
- **Back-port:** none.

## D-303 · 2026-10-16 · embedding throughput: a capped input, and a rebuild that survives a slow batch

- **Design ref:** D-300 (items 1 and 3).
- **Seen:** the first full embedding in production crawled (30 to 60 documents a minute on 4 CPU cores); batches of 8 sometimes passed the 60 s timeout, the rebuild stopped at the first one, and the service went on computing the abandoned batch, so a retry at once timed out again. bge-m3 takes 8,192 tokens an input, so a long document cost far more than it adds to a semantic match.
- **We do:**
  1. **A cap.** `Embedder::Http#embed_documents` cuts each text (title, then the start of the body) to `BANCO_EMBED_MAX_CHARS` characters (default 1,500, between 50 and 2,000), on a word boundary. A question is never cut. The cap is recorded in the vector's `model` column (`BAAI/bge-m3 cap1500`), so a change of the cap makes every vector stale exactly as a change of model does. The stub keeps its behaviour.
  2. **A slow batch does not stop the rebuild.** In `banco:search:rebuild` (not in the request path, not in `SearchIndexJob`, which keeps its stop on the first failure and its 20 minutes), a failed or timed-out batch waits `BANCO_EMBED_RETRY_WAIT` seconds (default 60, so the service drains the abandoned work), is retried up to `BANCO_EMBED_RETRIES` times (default 3), then skipped alone; the summary says how many batches (and documents) were skipped, and the next run embeds them. The task's document timeout is `BANCO_EMBED_DOCUMENT_TIMEOUT` (default 180 s); elsewhere it stays 60 s.
  3. **Progress.** Every `BANCO_EMBED_PROGRESS_EVERY` batches (default 10) one line: `vectors: 1200 of 9700, 41/min, eta 3h05`.
- **Cost:** the first rebuild after the deploy re-embeds every vector (the recorded model name changed).
- **Rules version:** none changes.
- **Status:** decided
- **Back-port:** none.

## D-304 · 2026-10-16 · comments anywhere (C1): the student comments on any page, the teacher answers; the clock stops in a sitting; no agent reads them

- **Design ref:** firm rules 1, 2, 4 and 5; D-08 (decisions' guards), D-217 (roles), D-218 (references on teacher pages), D-236 ("Ho una domanda"), D-260 (the console path), D-298.
- **Operator (2026-10-16):** (1) the student can comment on anything, on every student page (Oggi, lessons, practice, the entry test, search, settings, the warm-up, the end screens): pick the element or select a sentence, choose a quick reason, optionally write; the teacher manages the comments from the panel or, through the lead, from the console with the operator's words. (2) In the entry test it is allowed and the clock stops while the box is open; a comment never changes a grade or the engine's path. (3) Guests do not see a comment's text or a reply, they may see counts. (4) The teacher's replies show in "I miei commenti" and in Oggi, with a badge in the student menu. (5) "Ho una domanda" stays as it is and the teacher's inbox shows both kinds together.
- **We do (C1):**
  1. **Two append-only tables** (migration `20261016100001_create_comments`, triggers like every primary table, `db/structure.sql` updated, `bin/check-structure` green). `comments`: student, `client_comment_id` (unique, the page's outbox id), `trial`, `reason` (`not_understood`, `error`, `not_working`, `like`, `other`), optional `text_it` (1..500), `page_path`, `page_kind`, `anchor`, `selected_text` (up to 300), and the ids the server derived: subject, topic revision, lesson revision, card, practice serve, diagnosis run, served event, item instance, item revision, blueprint revision; viewport size, theme and text size (for "Non funziona"); no screenshot. `comment_events`: `reply`, `read`, `resolved`, `reopened`, `sent_back` (reserved for C2) by the teacher, `reply_seen` by the student; origin `web`, `console` or `student`, actor, request id. The state (inviato, letto, risposto, chiuso) is derived, never stored (`Comment#state`).
  2. **Anchors.** `data-comment-anchor="name"` or `name:value` on the components: lesson/2 cover (`cover`), card (`card:N`), block (`block:N`, nested blocks under their parent), item (`item`, `prompt`, `passage`, `quote`, `table`, `figure`, `answer`, `option:N`, `row:N`, `part:N` for the sub items of a testlet), the sitting's question (`question`) and "Come si risponde" (`help`), practice (`exercise`, `hints`, `feedback`, `solution`), Oggi sections, the menu (`menu`) and the settings controls (`setting:theme|size|voices`); an element without one is named by its nearest ancestor's id (`id:entry-test`). The page builds the path top-down, `card:3/block:2/option:1` (at most eight segments, up to 200 characters, `Comments::Intake::ANCHOR_FORMAT`). The ids come from `data-comment-lesson-revision-id`, `data-comment-serve-id` and `data-comment-served-event-id` on the element or an ancestor (the item on screen for a whole-page comment). **The server believes none of it** (`Comments::Intake`): the path must be a student page (`Comments::Pages`), the topic must be visible to this student, a lesson revision must be the one the topic pins and the card must exist in it, a practice serve must be this student's on a skill of the topic, a served event must be an `item_served` of a run of this student and of the run in the path; the revisions, instance and blueprint are derived from those, never taken from the browser; an id the page does not accept is refused. A refused comment is `{"status":"invalid"}` (final, the outbox drops it) and writes nothing.
  3. **The student's UI** on every student page: the "Commenta" control (the menu; in a sitting also beside "Come si risponde"; in a lesson/2 the lesson's own bar, which hides the menu), the comment mode (outlined elements, a tap picks one, or "Tutta la pagina", or a list for keyboard and screen reader; selected words are offered with the comment), a native modal box with the five reasons and 500 characters, "Invia" and "Annulla" (`comment_controller.js`; pure parts and their node tests in `items/comment_anchor.js`). A comment goes to a local outbox (`banco.coutbox.`) first and is sent when the network allows. The teacher's preview has no comment control and no route. "I miei commenti" (`/comments`): the student's own comments with state, replies and "Nuova"; showing a reply writes `reply_seen`. The badge is in the menu, one line in Oggi ("Il docente ti ha risposto").
  4. **The clock stop.** Opening the box in a sitting posts `comment_opened`, closing it `comment_closed`, to the run's events address (same door as `paused` and `hidden`; `Conductor.record` writes them only on change). `Diagnosis::Fold` keeps them in their own list `comment_stops`, and `State#excluded_intervals` is `pauses + hiddens + comment_stops`: the union is subtracted by `TimeAccount.overlap_seconds`, so an overlap with a hidden tab or a pause is counted once, and the abandon clock does not run either. An interval left open (a closed tab) ends at the next `sitting_started` or `item_served`, like the others, and the box's script closes it on load. Grading, the engine's choices, the cap and every rule are untouched (rules version `diagnosis/1` does not change). Properties (`PROP_RUNS=300`): with comment boxes of any length anywhere in an item, the run is exactly that of a student with no comments whose clock did not run in the box.
  5. **Privacy.** A reply is written only by `Comments::Responder`, the teacher's side: the guards are the decisions' own (`DecisionRecorder.refusal`: `BANCO_DECISIONS_ENABLED`, the web listener, a peer of the edge proxy, `BANCO_TEACHER_USERS` and the teacher group, a valid CSRF token, not the student's computer) or the console origin; never a guest, a student, the preview or the API. No `/api/v1` route, controller or CLI command names a comment, and a test walks the routes and calls every parameterless API read with an agent token looking for a comment's words. A guest's `/teacher/comments` shows the counts only. A student sees only their own comments (a trial student's are marked `trial`, and shown to the teacher so); the preview writes none. A comment writes no attempt, no serve, no event of a run (but the clock pair), no decision: a test counts every other table around it.
  6. **The teacher's page** `/teacher/comments` (menu "Commenti"): new, read, answered, closed, filters (state, reason, kind of place, subject, official or trial, comment or question), each comment with the place (page kind, subject, card title and block type read from the frozen lesson revision, `RefsHelper#ref_for` for the skill and the item, link to the teacher's own page), the words, the selected words, the device and the history; actions Rispondi, Segna letto, Chiudi, Riapri (POST, `Teacher::CommentsController`). The older "Ho una domanda" rows are listed with them, read-only.
  7. **Console.** `bin/rails banco:comments:list|show|reply|resolve|reopen|read` (`Comments::Console`, like D-260): reading needs no flag; writing is a dry run unless `CONFIRM=1`, needs `TEACHER=<login of BANCO_TEACHER_USERS>` and `BANCO_DECISIONS_ENABLED=1`, `TEXT_IT` (the operator's words, the teacher's reply) or `REASON_IT`, and is recorded with origin `console` (shown as "(da console)"). No route reaches it.
- **C2 will add:** "Rimanda all'autore" (the existing `send_back_item` / `send_back_lesson` decisions, prefilled with the place, the teacher's own text, the decision linking the comment id; the only thing that ever reaches an author), the Cruscotto tile (with the questions), the teacher's lexical search over comments, the frozen preview of what the student saw (`items/frozen_slot.js`, the lesson card) on each comment, polish after the operator tries C1.
- **Cost:** a student page has one more partial and one more script; the menu has one more item.
- **Rules version:** none changes.
- **Status:** decided
- **Back-port:** none.

## D-305 · 2026-10-16 · the look of comments (C1 polish): one «Commenta» pill with its own icon, a banner, a bottom sheet with five reason chips, a fading confirmation, calmer lists

- **Design ref:** D-304 (every behaviour, rule and test of it stands), D-246 (icons), B-11 (readability: short words, big targets, no alarm colours).
- **Operator (2026-10-16):** "Commenta" works but the interface must be more usable and more beautiful; the student has reading difficulties.
- **We do (a design pass, no change of behaviour, rule or data):**
  1. **The control**: a filled pill with the speech bubble and the word «Commenta» (new ui icon `comment`; the pin is no longer used for it), at the right end of the student menu on every page (full width on a phone, so it never overflows 390 px at the largest text), in the lesson's own bar as the same icon, and in a sitting also beside "Come si risponde" as an outlined pill so it is not mistaken for «Invia».
  2. **The comment mode**: a banner "Tocca la parte di cui vuoi parlare" with «Tutta la pagina», «Scegli da un elenco» (the keyboard and screen reader way) and «Annulla»; every commentable part has a faint dotted outline, the part under the pointer (the innermost) a solid one with a light tint; Esc leaves the mode.
  3. **The box**: a bottom sheet on a phone (up to 640 px), a card placed next to the chosen part on a wide screen (below it, above it, or centred when the part is tall); the place is echoed as a name ("Scheda 3 · Blocco 2", from the anchor path, `describeAnchor`) with a two-line excerpt of its words, and the part stays outlined behind the box; the five reasons are large chips (a real radio, an icon and a hue per reason, a thicker border and a filled dot when chosen, so colour is never the only sign); the text is optional with a placeholder and a counter; «Invia» (icon, primary) and «Annulla»; in a sitting a line "Il tempo del test è fermo." with a clock.
  4. **The confirmation**: a pill "Inviato al docente" (or "Salvato. Lo mando quando torna la rete.") at the bottom of the page, it is the live region, and fades after 3.5 s; with reduced motion nothing slides or fades gradually.
  5. **«I miei commenti»**: a card per comment (the place's icon on the subject colour, place in words, date, the state as a pill with an icon: Inviato, Letto, Risposto, Chiuso, the reason as a pill with its icon, the student's words, the teacher's reply as a bubble, a green outline and "Nuova" for an unread reply, a friendly empty state).
  6. **The teacher's page**: tabs with counts (Tutti, Nuovi, Letti, Risposti, Chiusi, Domande), filters as chips (reason, subject, official or trial, "Dove" folded; "Togli i filtri"), each comment a card (the place with `ref_for`, the words, the history as a thread, an inline reply box, the actions). The URL filters are the same (`state`, `reason`, `kind`, `subject`, `who`, `type`); a guest still sees the counts only.
  7. **Icons**: ui icons `comment`, `reason-not-understood|error|not-working|like|other`, `send`, `whole-page`, `pick`, `teacher-reply`, `clock-paused` (Lucide 1.54.0 `message-circle`, `circle-help`, `triangle-alert`, `wrench`, `heart`, `ellipsis`, `send`, `app-window`, `mouse-pointer-click`, `message-square`, `clock`; five new files vendored), `bin/build-icons` and `bin/build-palette` regenerated. Styles in `app/assets/stylesheets/comments.css` (the three themes, the three text sizes, the focus rings, 2.75 rem targets).
- **Cost:** one stylesheet; the sprite grows by ten symbols.
- **Status:** decided
- **Back-port:** none.

## D-306 · 2026-10-16 · the interface redesign, slices 1 and 2: one design system for the whole site, in the lessons' style

- **Design ref:** B-11 (readability: 20 px, 7:1, no alarm colours), D-240 (the student's menu), D-246 and D-264 (palette roles and icons), D-304 (comments), the interface audit and proposal of 2026-10-16.
- **Operator (2026-10-16):** the style of the lesson/2 pages is the reference and is extended to every page, the teacher's too (more sober); build directly, slice by slice, with before and after screenshots; after the base, the student pages and the teacher pages are redone in parallel.
- **We do (slices 1 and 2):**
  1. **Tokens in one place** (the top of `application.css`, next to the two themes): a spacing scale (`--space-1..8`), a type scale (`--text-s` to `--text-display`, nothing under 0.9 rem), radii, two shadows, the border, the tap size (`--tap` 2.75 rem, `--tap-small` 2.25 rem, both at least 44 px), the focus ring, motion (`--dur-1`, `--dur-2`, both 0 under `prefers-reduced-motion`) and five tones built from the lessons' palette roles (`--tone-info|success|nearly|error|hint`, never red and green for right and wrong). The lessons keep their own em scale inside `.l2`.
  2. **Components** in `components.css`, helpers in `UiHelper`, documented in `docs/ui.md`: button (primary, secondary, text, danger, small, block; a row with equal heights), card, tag, state pill, list row clickable as a whole, notice with icon, dialog (a bottom sheet at 600 px or less), form fields and styled radios and checkboxes, page header, table wrapper (scrolls inside; a stacked mode), disclosure, empty and loading states, meter and dots, designed error pages. Six icons are added to the `ui` list of `icons.yml` (back, alert, empty, loading, locked, not-found), four of them new Lucide files of the vendored version.
  3. **The unused `light` theme is removed** (it was never offered; `ReadabilityTest` now expects cream and dark only). A stored `light` would fall back to cream.
  4. **Quick wins:** link-buttons centred with equal heights (one `.button` rule for `a` and `button`); the overflows at 390 px (number field with a unit, search box, `.cards` minimum, the teacher's tables inside `.table-wrap`); targets of 44 px (`summary`, menu, breadcrumb and step links, reference links and "i", labels around radios and checkboxes, selects and inputs, "Non ho capito"); the end screen draws only the non-empty groups and says "non è un voto" first; a guest sees no "Prova come S" and no orphan "Rimanda all'agente"; the report's sittings show "2 nov 2026, 09:00"; 403 and 404 (and the static 400, 404, 422 and 500) are designed Italian pages with the same text for everyone; the settings radios are choice cards in the app's colours; the maths keyboard's tab colours follow the theme.
- **Cost:** the old `.banner` and `.badge` shapes are replaced by the notice and the tag; pages that used the square outline now have rounded cards. A page that wants a new look uses the components; nothing else changes behaviour, routes, privacy or texts beyond the few above.
- **Rules version:** none changes.
- **Status:** decided
- **Back-port:** none.

## D-308 · 2026-10-17 · the interface redesign, slices 6 to 8: the teacher's pages as tools

- **Design ref:** D-306 (tokens and components), D-241, D-242, D-243 (the teacher's path, dashboard and menu), D-218 (refs), D-305 (comments look, kept as it is).
- **Operator (2026-10-16):** the lessons' style for the whole site, more sober on the teacher's side; the teacher's pages become tools, not long documents.

The "Torna a..." paragraphs of the subject pages are gone (three ways back became one); flash messages are notices with an icon.

## D-309 · 2026-10-17 · the teacher enters as a student: the whole student's site under /teacher/preview, two views, a reset by a new preview student

- **Design ref:** D-217 (trial students), D-240 (the student's menu), D-304 (comments), D-306 and D-307 (the interface), firm rules 1, 2 and 4.
- **Operator (2026-10-17):** a way for the teacher to enter as a trial student, not only for the tests but for the lessons too.
- **We do:**
  1. **Who acts.** Identity stays the teacher's (`EdgeTrust`). The pages of the course (Oggi, Materie, a subject, a topic, the lesson, practice, search, settings), the warm-up, the preferences and the entry test run as the student's own controllers under `/teacher/preview/...`: the route default `preview: true` (`ActingStudent#preview?`, from `path_parameters` only, never a parameter) makes the acting student the teacher's **preview student** (a `students` row of kind `preview`). Links and script addresses go through `spath` (`student_root`: `/teacher/preview` or nothing); a test fails if a preview page links to the student's own addresses. A guest, a student, a trial student or nobody get 403 on every preview address.
  2. **Two views** (`Course::Catalog.for(student, view:)`, `Course::StudentView.new(student, view:)`, `Search::Scope::Student.for(student, view:)`): «Come lo vede S» (`official`, the default: released courses, approved topics) and «Con le bozze» (`drafts`: the latest map and topics, flagged «Bozza»). The view is kept in the teacher's session (`POST /teacher/preview/view`, CSRF; the back address is accepted only if it is a preview address), never in the address. The Oggi «Ora» card carries the draft tag too.
  3. **Banner** (`shared/_preview_banner`, on every preview page): «Stai provando come studente · Vista: …», «Passa a: …», «Ricomincia da capo» (a `<details>` that asks first) and «Esci dalla prova» (to `/teacher`). The menu "Prova come studente" opens `/teacher/preview` (Oggi); the entry test list is `/teacher/preview/test`, reached from Oggi and the menu. No «Commenta» (bar or lesson), no «Non ho capito» (`urls.questions` is left out of the lesson's addresses), no logout item.
  4. **Progress** is recorded on the preview student, append-only (lesson events, practice serves, tries, hints, solutions, preferences, warm-up, entry test runs in the context `teacher_preview`). The seeds of its practice come from its own entry-test runs, as for a trial student.
  5. **Reset** = a new preview student (`Student.reset_preview!`, key `preview.N`; the first is `preview`). No UPDATE and no DELETE: the old rows stay, the loaders read the latest preview student, the triggers are unchanged. `preview.N` can never be a login's key (`Student::KEY_FORMAT` has no dot), so no student can act as one. `Approval::BlueprintGate#previewed?` reads the runs of every preview student: a reset does not take back that the teacher played the test.
  6. **Isolation.** The preview student is of kind `preview`; everything that reads students reads kind `student` (`Student.real`, the Cruscotto, `ViewedStudent`, the reports, `Search::Builders::Answers`, the API controllers, the comments inbox, the teacher's lesson progress line). No comment, no question and no decision come from a preview page: there is no route (`/teacher/preview/comments`, `/questions` and every decision are 404), and `/comments`, `/questions` stay the students' (403 for the teacher). `LessonsController` seeds the shuffle by the acting student's key, so what the page shows and what the check grades agree after a reset.
- **Tests:** `test/integration/teacher_as_student_test.rb` (the walk, the views, who may enter, nothing on S or a trial student, nothing in reports, Cruscotto, comments, search answers and the API, no decision or comment, the reset), `test/system/teacher_preview_test.rb` (Chrome: Oggi to a graded try in both views, the reset; `BANCO_SHOT_DIR` takes screenshots). Changed: `student_menu_test`, `search_student_door_test`, `student_pages_test`, `guest_read_only_test` (the preview has a menu now; the test list moved to `/teacher/preview/test`).
- **Cost:** the preview student's practice and lesson rows grow the ledger a little; the view is per session, so two tabs share it.
- **Rules version:** none changes.
- **Status:** decided
- **Back-port:** none.

## D-310 · 2026-10-18 · lesson/2 renderer polish after the wave 3 authors' reports: markup drawn wherever it is written, a mirror and an ordering that fit a phone, a typed answer on its formula's line, neutral tiles, quoted math

- **Design ref:** D-253 (the lesson/2 renderer), D-249 and D-255 (the render check), D-266 and D-282 (spans and the text layer), D-273 (tiles, ordering), D-280 (`bar_model`), D-284 (`mirror`), A1 (the `math` block), A9 (checks).
- **Reported (the authors of wave 3, 2026-10-17):** at 390 px a `table` printed its header markup raw in the stacked rows (`[[es:hablar]]: hablo`) and wrapped its caption into a column one or two words wide; `cases` titles printed markup raw; a `mirror` piece with an icon role overflowed its box and the render check did not say so; `bar_model` part and total labels and the header cells of a `schema table` printed `$...$` raw; a `math` block written in YAML quotes kept them and KaTeX failed; the options of a lesson `choice` did not draw their markup; an `ordering` with long sentences was wider than the phone; the fixed words of `tiles` («La tua frase», «Le parole») read oddly when the tiles are facts; a `number` check with text before and after the box put the hint line between the formula and the box.
- **We do:**
  1. **Markup is drawn wherever it is written.** A stacked table cell starts with its column's name as a real element drawn from the header cell with its markup (`.cell-label`, `aria-hidden`: the head says it to a screen reader and to «Ascolta»), shown only under 600 px; the CSS `attr(data-label)` is gone. The `table` block and the `table` figure share one `tableNode` (`lesson/blocks/table.js`). Titles: `cases` (the block's and each case's), `callout`, `procedure`, `more`, `dialogue`, `source`, a mistakes group, and the card's own title (its heading, the map and «Avanti»; the parser already accepted `$...$` in a heading); the live region says the title in plain words. `bar_model`'s part, total and mark labels keep their markup (they went through `plain()`; the bar's own label never did); the descriptions stay plain. The options of a lesson `choice` (card checks, example blanks, Prova tu) are drawn by the lesson's inline renderer through a hook of `items/choice.js` (`ctx.inline`); items keep their own markup, bold and formulas, the same as their prompts. Matching chips, span chips and Italian tiles use the same inline markup. A title drawn inside a flex head (a case's head beside its icon, a mistakes group's heading) is one span (`.case-title`, `.mistakes-group-title`), so its words, a formula and a word of another language wrap as one line of text, not as one column per piece.
  2. **Inside a control, no control.** `insideControl(ctx)` (`lesson/text.js`): an option, a chip, a tile, a title inside a button and a stacked label draw the same markup with no speaker button, no glossary bubble and no link (a button inside a `<label>` would take the tap meant for the option). Names for screen readers (an ordering's Su and Giù, a tile, a dialogue's and a source's region) and live regions are plain text, read by `plainText` (`lesson/text.js`): the page's own markup reader with the markup taken away, so bold, a role span with a hyphen or `|it` and a link lose their marks too (`plain()` of the diagrams kept them). A mistake card names its group for the screen reader inside its button in the same plain words: printed as written, a `group_it` holding a span failed the render check of the whole lesson.
  3. **One short word in another language never breaks** (`.lang-word`, up to 24 characters, no space): «-emos» no longer splits after its hyphen.
  4. **Table caption.** Under 600 px the caption is a full-width line above the rows (a caption in a table that is no longer a table shrank to its longest word).
  5. **Mirror on a phone.** In the two-column list, a piece whose word is wider than the room beside its role icon draws the icon above the word, and the word has the box's whole width; a word wider than its column first gets a little more room (the space of the link down to 28 px, the boxes' side padding down to 4 px: the gallery's «constipado» touched its box at 390 px and now fits beside its pair); a word wider still (a large text size) puts each pair one piece under the other, with a short upright link, its mark and its word. The render check's node-border rule now reads the mirror's texts too (it read only the node texts of the graph family).
  6. **Ordering.** Under a list width of 30em (a phone, a large text size: a container query on the component), the place and the text share the first row and Su and Giù sit under the text on the right, so a long sentence has nearly the whole width; long words break inside the item rather than overflow. The interaction is unchanged: the buttons and Alt with the arrows (the component never had dragging).
  7. **Tiles' fixed words are neutral**: «La tua risposta», «Le tessere», «Tocca le tessere qui sotto.», the how-to line and «Come si risponde» to match. A check with the new optional field `builds: sentence` (schema `check_tiles`, served by `Lessons::StudentBody`, whitelist version unchanged) keeps «La tua frase», «Le parole» and the sentence how-to. We chose a field over free texts: no words for the author to write and lint, one meaning.
  8. **A typed answer with text before or after the box** (a card check or an example blank; not the one-line answers of Prova tu): the box's hint («Scrivi il numero...») moves above the line, still the box's label, and the box takes its own width, so the formula, the box and the rest read as one line where it fits. «Ascolta» now reads the hint before the formula (the docs golden is rewritten for it).
  9. **Quoted math: stripped, not refused.** A one-line `math` body written in quotes, `'...'` or `"..."`, loses the one matching pair around it in `Lessons::Directives.math`; what is inside is kept as written (no YAML escape is read: a backslash stays a backslash, `''` stays two primes); empty quotes are refused as an empty formula. We chose this over a new error code: the author's intent is never in doubt, every other block body is YAML where quotes are the habit, and KaTeX cannot draw a quote at the edge of a formula anyway. `lines:` bodies were already YAML. A quoted body that holds the same quote inside is refused with `E-LESSON-BLOCK` (`'f''(x)'` is YAML for f'(x); showing f''(x) would be a different formula): write the formula without quotes.
  10. **The render check says when markup reaches the page as text**: `E-LESSON-RENDER` "markup printed as text" for a span (`[[es:...]]`, `[[role:...]]`) or a formula between dollars with a TeX character (a backslash, `^`, `_`, a brace) in any text node of the card outside KaTeX and code (`lesson/raw_markup.js`). Money in an English sentence ("$5 and $6") and `\$` are not markup. The host script changed, so `Harness.lesson_version` changes: the next render of a revision is a new verdict. A text node the inline reader made (`parsedText` in `lesson/raw_markup.js`) is never flagged, so literal dollars (`\$A_1 oppure \$B`) do not fail; `raw_markup.js` is part of the harness `lesson_version` hash, so a change to the detector gives fresh verdicts. The exemption covers only the formula test: a span the parser left as text (an empty or malformed one, a reserved name, a nested one) in a parsed node is still found. When rows stack, the row header (first column) also carries its column's name (`.cell-label`), unless the corner header is empty.
- **Tests:** galleries `test/fixtures/lesson2/gallery/polish-spanish.md` and `polish-math.md` (one card per report), drawn by `test/validation/lesson_polish_gallery_test.rb` (Chrome at the viewports of `lesson2.render`, no finding; with the renderer of main they fail with the new findings, the ordering overflow and the KaTeX error), `test/system/lesson_polish_system_test.rb` (the student's page at 390 and 1280: column names, caption width, titles, options without controls inside, the ordering fits and moves by button and key, the tiles' words, the hint above the formula and the box on one line, formulas in labels, headers and quoted math; a long case title and a mistakes group that mix words with a Spanish word or a formula: one title span in the head, its pieces on one line a space apart, the group said in plain words), `app/javascript/lesson/test/polish6.test.mjs` (the raw-markup reader, short titles, `insideControl`, `plainText`, the tiles' words, bar labels, the mirror's two narrow layouts), vectors `mirror-icon-role-long-word` and `bar_model-parts-formula-labels`, `test/lib/lessons/parser2_test.rb` (quotes). Changed: `served/checks.json` (its first tiles check builds a sentence, so the how-to line the system test reads is the sentence one), the speech golden `docs.json` (order of the hint and the box), the whitelist (`builds`).
- **Not in this round** (also in the authors' list): a card with one text block and one figure shows the figure first on a phone; the render check draws only the first exercise of Prova tu; `exact_check.py` reads no lesson/2 file; the biology figures `cell`, `scale`, `nested` are drafts; `banco findings list` lists only item findings. The teacher's server-drawn pages still print card titles as written.
- **Cost:** a lesson that printed raw markup still passed its render check; from now it fails it with a clear line (the authors' notes show they had written plain text in those places). Lessons whose options, titles or labels hold markup look different, as their text does.
- **With D-311 (one mirror layout):** `words/mirror.js` has one helper, `placement`, for where a piece's icon goes (above the text when the box wraps and a word is wider than the room beside the icon); the text keeps D-311's class `dg-nodetext` and the keys `KEY:t` and `KEY:icon` that the render check reads; D-310's `stackedPairs` stays for a word wider than a whole column. `test/validation/lesson_render_states_test.rb` now crosses a box with a 40-letter word (the old test's word fits since D-310).
- **Rules version:** none changes (the schema gains one optional field).
- **Status:** decided
- **Back-port:** `briefs/lesson.md` (quotes in `math`, markup in options and titles, `builds: sentence`), `docs/validation.md` (the two render check rows).

## D-311 · 2026-10-18 · the render check draws every state a card can reach: every exercise of «Prova tu», the closed parts opened, the oral's form; a box's text and icon inside its box

- **Design ref:** D-249, D-255, D-293 (the render check), D-253 (the pager of «Prova tu»), D-284 (`mirror`), D-278 (`oral`), D-283 (the `listen` option), D-266 (the glossary).
- **Found (the wave 3 authors, 2026-10-17):** the render check drew only the first exercise of «Prova tu». The pager shows one exercise at a time (`.exercise:not(.is-current)` is `display: none` in the cards view), so exercises 2 to 8 (tiles, orderings, figures) were never drawn at 390 px and their overflow was never caught; a figure of a hidden exercise was stepped through its states at width 0 (a wait per state, nothing measured). A `mirror` piece with an icon role («lavamos» with the verb's lightning) ran out of its box at 390 px and passed. Looking for the same kind of gap: the text of a listening check stays behind «Mostra il testo» (`hidden`) and was never measured; the glossary bubbles are closed; the `oral` was drawn as print draws it (the outline as a list), never as the student answers it (the ordering form). What sits behind a reveal, a flip (`mistake`) and «Vuoi saperne di più?» was already drawn and measured (`config.expand` opens them, as in print); Chrome lays out a closed `<details>`' content when it is asked for its size, so a «Descrizione» or the guide of a source was measured too, though no picture showed it open.
- **We do:**
  1. **The states of a card** (`lesson/render_host.js`): `inspect(n, state)`, and `inspect(n)` (the card as drawn) answers the card's further states: `exN` for each exercise of «Prova tu» after the first (the host taps its number chip; the exercise's figures are drawn at the width they now have and stepped through their own states), `open` (every closed part of the card opened at once: each closed `<details>` not hidden on purpose, such as «Descrizione», «Vedi i numeri», «Come si risponde», the guide of a source and the cover's two; «Mostra il testo» of a listening check) and `exN-open` (the same inside exercise N). Each state is measured with the checks of the card (overflow at the page and inside the card; the figure findings), at the same viewports. Each inspect first undoes what the previous state changed. The card as drawn no longer steps the figures of hidden exercises.
  2. **The glossary bubbles** are opened one at a time in the opened states. A bubble opens over the text under its word (`position: absolute`), so it is wider than its paragraph by design (the generic test said «p is 792 px wide in a 778 px box» for a word near the end of a line); what is checked is that it stays inside its card and the window and that nothing in it is wider than the bubble.
  3. **Overflow:** every innermost element wider than its box is reported (up to four for a state, each with its own text), not only the first, so a state that adds an overflow of its own is not hidden behind the card's. The same-sized findings are kept apart by their text (the dedup key is code, message and place), and the culprits inside the state's own exercise come before those of the rest of the card when the four are taken.
  4. **A box's text inside its box:** the check that a node's text clears its box's border finds the box by key (a label `K:t` or `K:label` is the text of the shape `K`), so a word that runs far out of its box is no longer missed because its centre left the box; the box's icon (`K:icon`) must sit inside the box and off the text. The `mirror` pieces' text is `dg-nodetext`: before, only a piece that crossed the figure's edge or another label was caught, and an Italian piece runs into the gap of its link. **The mirror's layout:** in the narrow list (under 520 px) a piece whose word is wider than the room beside its icon puts the icon above the word (a word cannot wrap, and a wrapped measure is never wider than its room, so the box was drawn too small: «lavamos», «vediamo» at 390 px). A word wider than the whole box is still an error, the author's to fix.
  5. **The oral** is drawn in the render check with the student's form (the outline in the ordering component), not the printed list (`ctx.renderCheck`); `lesson/preload.js` loads the ordering component for a lesson with an oral, so the student's page draws the form at once too.
  6. **Runner** (`Validation::LessonRenderRunner`): each state has its own 5 s and its own `timings` row (`state`); the revision keeps its 90 s. An error carries `state` (none for the card as drawn); one that a further state repeats (the same code, message and place) stays the first state's. The opened states of a viewport are looked at after its last picture: opening a part can make a short page (1280 x 800) scrollable for a moment, and Chrome then painted the fixed bars (their backdrop blur) of the following pictures a little differently from one run to the next, so a second render of an unchanged revision stored five to ten new files (`lesson_render_runner_test` allows three).
  7. **Pictures:** the card as drawn, as before; another exercise at the first viewport the card is drawn at (390 cream, the phone); any further state at a viewport where it found something new, so that what was found can be seen. The opened states are otherwise measured, not pictured. A shot carries `state`; `GET /api/v1/lesson-revisions/:revision/shots` passes it; `banco lesson shots` writes `card-NN-STATE_WIDTHxHEIGHT-theme.webp` (the card's own name is unchanged); the teacher's pictures page puts a card's states after the card, captioned «Esercizio 2 · 390 px, chiaro» or «Con le parti chiuse aperte · …». `bin/purge-lesson-shots` removes them with the card's (a state's picture is one more entry of `shots_json`).
- **Not drawn, on purpose:** the solutions («Mostra la soluzione»), a check's feedback and the oral's model answer: they come from the server and are answers, and the host has the student's projection only (no answer in a picture, D-255). The closed face of a flip is its open face without the back and with the fixed hint «Tocca per girare»: nothing on it is not drawn already.
- **Measured** (development machine, the shared headless Chrome 1243 while other agents' tests ran, so a revision's wall time wanders by up to 40 % from run to run; three runs before and three after, alternated; the states' own seconds are their `timings` rows; three viewports):

  | lesson | cards, exercises of «Prova tu» | the states' own time | the revision, quietest run, before → after | shots before → after | KB before → after |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | `test/fixtures/lesson2/served/equations.json` | 13, 3 | 1.5 to 1.7 s | 14.6 → 16.5 s | 35 → 37 | 2,165 → 2,207 |
  | `test/fixtures/lesson2/demo.md` | 12, 4 | 1.7 to 2.2 s | 12.8 → 14.4 s | 32 → 35 | 1,994 → 2,054 |
  | `test/fixtures/lesson2/gallery/docs-lesson.md` | 10, 4 and an oral | 1.5 to 2.0 s | 10.0 → 11.9 s | 30 → 33 | 1,730 → 1,820 |
  | a history draft of wave 3 | 14, 8 | 3.5 to 4.1 s | 16.3 → 20.9 s | 42 → 49 | 2,768 → 2,996 |
  | a biology draft of wave 3 | 13, 8 | 3.2 to 4.8 s | 16.4 → 20.1 s | 39 → 46 | 3,047 → 3,328 |
  | a Spanish draft of wave 3 | 13, 8 | 3.1 to 4.5 s | 16.2 → 20.5 s | 39 → 46 | 2,843 → 3,035 |

  About 10 to 25 % more per revision; the slowest run of any of them took 34 s, the budget is 90 s; the slowest single card or state took 1.3 s, the limit is 5 s. An opened state costs about 45 ms (one round trip to the page); another exercise about 0.07 s to measure at each viewport and 0.1 s to picture at 390. One more picture per further exercise, 30 to 40 KB each.
- **Rules version:** none changes (no number moved). `Harness.lesson_version` moves with the host script, so a lesson/2 revision is drawn again the next time its job runs.
