- **Tests:** `test/validation/lesson_render_states_test.rb` (Chrome: exercises 2 and 3 caught at 390 px and pictured, a clean exercise pictured once; a reveal, a mistake and a «more» measured as drawn; the guide of a source; a listening text caught only with the card open; a glossary bubble near the edge of its card is not an overflow; a mirror piece that crosses its box inside the figure is caught, the same roles on short words pass; the oral's form), `lesson_render_runner_test` (the equations shots: the card's plus exercises 2 and 3 at 390; a second render still stores almost no new file), `lesson/test/words_types.test.mjs` (the icon above a word too wide to sit beside it), `checks_t1.test.mjs` (the oral preloads the ordering component), `test/integration/lesson_render_test.rb` (the state in the API, the teacher's captions and their order, the purge), `cli/cmd_course_test.go` (the file name).
- **Status:** decided
- **Back-port:** none.

## D-312 · 2026-10-18 · `cell` and `nested` available (T7, T4b, W2-2): the labelled cell from the vetted table bio/cell_parts, boxes inside boxes; `scale` waits for bio/sizes

- **Design ref:** WAVE2-COMPONENTS 2.8 (`cell`), 2.1 (`nested`), 2.4 (`scale`), 1.9 (vetted tables), 1.4 (L3, L4, L8), 2.14 (the per-type matrix); the biology design 2.1, 2.3, 2.5 and its cards; D-262 to D-271 (the W2-0 contracts), D-275 (controls and select scenes), D-288 (`strand`). The authors' report of 2026-10-17: the cell lesson (`ponte.biology.cell-basics`, cards 3, 4, 7, 8) had to use concept maps because `cell`, `scale` and `nested` were drafts.
- **Design said:** `cell` draws one or two cells of fixed shapes, colours and places, the same in every lesson, with the parts each kind may have from `bio/cell_parts`; it refuses a part the kind does not have and requires the four shared parts; labels all, tap or none, notes on a tap, highlight, paths, the water of the vacuole, "Solo le differenze", `true_scale`; select set `parts`, neutral. `nested` is boxes inside boxes ("is made of") with an inside box and a focus; select set `levels`. `scale` is a powers-of-ten ruler with a true-size panel on the vetted sizes `bio/sizes`. All three were W2-2 drafts, frozen at their family's first look.
- **We do:**
  1. **The table** `config/banco/data/bio/cell_parts.yml` (schema of W2-0): kinds `bacterium`, `animal`, `plant` with the parts the figure may draw for each (OpenStax Biology 2e, 4.2, 4.3 and 4.5 Table 4.1, CC BY 4.0), the Italian names (Treccani "nucleoide", it.wikipedia "Organulo", "Procarioti"), a one-line job from the Function column said in plain Italian, and a fill and an outline per theme (graphics, not palette roles; every outline 3:1 or more against the surface, the cytoplasm and its own fill). The second table `bio/cell_parts_expected` (its own schema) is the Italian route: per kind and part `always`, `some` or `never` with a quoted source, and the stem of each name; `test/lib/cell_parts_data_test.rb` holds an `always` part in the kind and a `never` part out of it, the four shared parts in every kind, the colours, and `science.css` equal to the table. `dna` is a part no kind lists: it is drawn inside the nucleoid or the nucleus.
  2. **`cell`** (`lesson/diagrams/science/cell.js`, `Lessons::Diagrams::Cell`, `available`): each kind is a fixed drawing in fractions of its width (a capsule with wall, membrane, a tangled nucleoid, dots, a wavy tail; a wobbly animal cell with a double-ringed nucleus, chromatin and nucleolus, folded mitochondria, reticulum sacs round the nucleus, a Golgi stack, vesicles; a plant cell with a wall band, chloroplasts with stacks round a large vacuole). Every part has a fixed zone (its tap target, its number and the end of its leader), at least 0.115 of the width from any other, so zones never touch at 240 px. `labels: all` puts the names in two columns with leader lines when they fit, else a number on each part and one key under the figure, the same number for the same part in both cells; `tap` names a part only when tapped (the figure's `hits`: name, then the job or the author's note); `none` names nothing and the description says shapes ("un groviglio di filo", "tanti puntini"). `highlight` (and `dna`) lights parts with a halo and a thicker outline and dims the rest of the figure, never colour alone; `paths` are dashed arrows between two parts of one cell, their label beside the bulge and off every zone and leader, else under the figure; `fill: {vacuole: low}` shrinks the vacuole and the whole protoplast inside the wall (plasmolysis). Two cells whose parts differ offer the chips "Solo le differenze" (`controls()`; none with `labels: none`), which light what one has and the other has not and say it in the live line. The DNA of a eukaryotic cell gets its own label inside the nucleus when any state names `dna`, in every state, so the numbers never change. Select mode: a line drawing in one neutral style, no part name in a class, a key or a label, one zone per part in the table's order (`c1.wall`, `c1.membrane`... then `c2.`); `target_names` is the name without its bracket ("DNA" for the nucleoid), `select_signatures` reads the served select projection (which drops labels, highlight, paths, fill, notes and states), and Ruby's checks are the browser's, in the same order (vectors `test/fixtures/diagrams/types/cell.json`, 43 cases).
  3. **Held back, with a reason:** `true_scale: true` is a draft view in the registry (it needs the real sizes of `bio/sizes`) and a finding; `kind: red_blood` and `omit_shared` are refused (the red blood cell has two parts, and the table's schema asks at least three per kind; a `more` says it).
  4. **`nested`** (`lesson/diagrams/graph/nested.js`, `Lessons::Diagrams::Nested`, `available`): the outermost level is the whole figure, each level a box inside the next with its name and its example (beside the name when both fit on one line, else under it), neutral tints alternating by depth, the inside box dashed in the innermost; on a phone the same boxes with smaller margins, which reads as an indented outline with frames (the design's phone layout, kept as boxes so the picture is the same at every width). `focus` gives one level a thick outline, a tint and its name underlined. Select set `levels`, outermost first: the names are not drawn, the examples are, no focus and no inside box; so the stem asks for a level by its name or by an example the figure does not show, never by the example printed in the answer's box (that tests the reading: the brief says it and the gallery's check asks "Tocca il riquadro dell'organo" over the examples; no finding catches it yet, the reviewer does). Checks: ids unique, names at most 6 words and all different, the inside's name at most 6 words, a focus that names a level (vectors `nested.json`, 14 cases).
  5. **The look gate:** the gallery `test/fixtures/lesson2/gallery/science-biology.md` (twelve cards: the two cells with Avanti, the comparison, the animal cell with the RNA's arrow, names on a tap, the vacuole, the tail, two select checks over the parts of one cell, an example with a linked pair of cells whose blank asks the kind of the second (the design's "Foglia o guancia?"), a select over the parts of two cells, the levels, a select over the levels), the render check at every viewport (`test/validation/biology_gallery_test.rb`), the page in Chrome (`test/system/biology_figures_test.rb`, with the shots at 390 and 1280 px, cream and dark), the node tests `lesson/test/cell_nested.test.mjs` and the Ruby `test/content/cell_nested_types_test.rb`. The registry test now lets a W2-2 type be available once its look gate froze its schema (`x-banco-draft` gone from `cell` and `nested`). The briefs `lesson` and `lesson-biology` teach both. The tests that used `cell` as their example of a draft (the reserved dry run, `bad/type-draft.md`) now use `scale`. One more gallery render check made `test/validation/lesson_render_timing_test.rb` fail in CI on its wall clock, which also counts the wait for the shared Chrome lock while other workers' render checks hold it: its budget is now the runner's own `elapsed_seconds` (the clock that starts once the lock is held), the wall clock stays in the message.
  6. **Met on the way, in the shared renderer:** (a) a select check's figure got the chips of its type (`draw.js` built them in every mode): the select projection of `cell` drops `labels`, so a select over two cells that differ showed "Solo le differenze"; a figure in mode `select` now has no chips, as it already had no value controls. (b) A cell's `label_it` is what its description and its tap buttons say for it (the kind only without a label), so an example can ask which kind a cell is without the text alternative answering. (c) The follow-up of R3 (D-254, its choice 3): the reply to an example's blank carried the drawing's states from the blank on, which the page never used, so a linked figure stopped at the step before the blank. The reply now carries `diagram`, the served figure cut at the next blank as the page's was cut at this one (and `states` is cut there too: it ran to the end, past a later blank), and `lesson/blocks/example.js` hands it to the figure (`replaceData` of `draw.js`); a figure that had no state left before the blank gets its states then (`test/integration/lesson_events_test.rb`, the gallery's example in Chrome).
  7. **`scale` is not built.** Its facts are the vetted table `bio/sizes`, which is not in the repository: the data author's draft has open disagreements (the size of a prokaryote, of a eukaryote, a source error) and still needs its second table by another session and a review by another model family (1.9); the draft schema has no `source_it` for the inline objects the design allows, and `pictograms` is not described. Building the ruler before its numbers would let a lesson type sizes from memory, which the brief forbids. Until the table lands, a size is a sentence from the vetted reference or a `bar_model`.
  8. **The review round (2026-10-19), before landing.** (a) *A `nested` select figure named its answer in the page source.* Its projection dropped focus, inside and states but kept every level's author id and `label_it`; the body is a `<script>` in the page, so the card's check served `{"id":"organ","label_it":"organo"}`. `Nested.served(mode: :select)` now serves each level as `{id: "l1".., label_it: "·", example_it}` (stored order, numbered in reading order: `l1` is the outermost, the target `t1`), as `chain`, `network` and `timeline` already did; the browser skips its "two levels with one name" check in select mode only. Grading is unchanged (`SelectTargets.id_map` reads the stored check). `test/content/cell_nested_types_test.rb` now holds, for every select case of both types, that no string of the served figure is a stored id or a target's name; the vector `nested-select-served` is that projection, drawn in select mode (`select_layout`); the system test reads the check's figure out of `#lesson-body`. (b) *The wall's and the membrane's targets could not be told apart.* Both were squares on bands 8 to 10 px apart, so each covered both, and the neutral drawing put the membrane on the wall's inner outline. A select figure now draws the wall's band 5 or 6 px out from the membrane (two lines with a clear gap), the wall's target on the top edge from that gap outwards (the figure keeps room above it), the membrane's on the bottom edge from the gap inwards; a plant cell's cytoplasm target moves into the room left of the vacuole (at its usual place, between the vacuole and the membrane, it hugged the membrane like the membrane's own); a ribosome's dot under another part's target is left out (with a dot in it, the membrane's target looked like the ribosomes'); every target is drawn as large as its button on the page (28 px at least, `draw.js` grows smaller ones), and the cell's buttons get a ring of the surface so the nucleoid's reads over the tangle (whose line is lighter in a select figure). The vectors say which pairs keep apart (`select_apart`, a new case `cell-select-two-walls`); the node test samples the drawn paths at every width and text size, and the system test hit-tests every pixel of the two buttons in Chrome (`isPointInStroke`, `isPointInFill`). The lesson's own drawing (labels `all`, `tap`) is unchanged. (c) *On a phone `labels: tap` had nowhere visible to tap.* Each part had one transparent button at its zone (an outline on hover only), so five of six chloroplasts, most of the wall and the membrane did nothing. Every shape of a part now forwards its tap to that part's button (`shapes[].hitFor`, wired in `draw.js` for any type's `hits`), with invisible pads along the thin parts (a strip inside the membrane, outside the wall, along the tail, a ring round each ribosome and vesicle, the sectors of the reticulum and the Golgi); the buttons stay the keyboard's and the screen reader's way in. The system test taps, at 390 px, a chloroplast far from the chloroplasts' button and the top of the wall far from the wall's.
- **Choices to confirm:** (1) The animal and plant cells show the typical organelles only (no lysosomes, centrosome, peroxisomes, cytoskeleton, nucleolus as a part); a plant flagellum (gametes) is refused. (2) `vacuole` is the plant's large central vacuole; an animal cell's small sacs are `vesicles`. (3) The bacterium's DNA region is called "DNA (nucleoide)". (4) The comparison button appears on any two cells whose parts differ, not only when the author asks.
- **Number:** D-312.
- **Why:** three graph skills and seven graph errors are about which cell has what; one drawing that refuses a false cell, learnt once, becomes the map of every later lesson (membrane, respiration, photosynthesis, mitosis, protein synthesis). Boxes inside boxes are the only picture of "is made of".
- **Cost:** the second table is a separate extraction by the same session, not a second session: a model of another family still has to review both tables (as D-285); the job lines are ours and the teacher's book may word them differently; no `true_scale`, no red blood cell, no `scale` yet. A select figure of a cell differs from the lesson's in a few pixels (the band apart from the membrane, a dot or two fewer); its targets go in the table's order (`t1` is the wall of a walled cell), which is also the keyboard's first stop, because the server has no geometry to sort them by place; a `nested` example that contains a level's name ("tessuto muscolare del cuore") names that box in a select figure, which the brief forbids and no finding catches yet.
- **Rules version:** none changes.
- **Status:** decided
- **Back-port:** none.
## D-313 · 2026-10-18 · lesson-review findings are first-class for the agents: an id, the list, the author's answer

- **Design ref:** D-220 (the author answers findings), A5 and A6.1 (lesson review, approve_topic), D-222 (the third reviewer), firm rules 2 and 4.
- **Design said:** a lesson review keeps its findings inline (`lesson_reviews.findings_json`). `banco findings list` showed only the findings of items and `banco findings respond` answered only those (`review_findings` ids). A lesson finding had no id in the CLI, so the author could not answer a blocker or major one: a new revision was the only answer. Several authors hit this in wave 3 (2026-10-17).
- **We do:**
  1. **Id.** The review row is append-only, so its list of findings never changes: the n-th finding (from 1) of lesson review R is `L<R>-<n>` (`LessonFindings`), for every review already stored and every new one. No item finding id (a bare number) can look like it. No table of findings is added and no row is rewritten.
  2. **List.** `GET /api/v1/subjects/:subject/findings` gives the rows of the items first (now with `kind: "item"`), then those of the lesson reviews: `finding_id`, `kind: "lesson"`, `lesson`, `review_id`, `revision_id`, `seq`, `current` (the newest revision of the lesson), `pinned` (the latest topic revision pins it), `severity`, `card` and `block` (lesson/2) or `section` and `exercise` (lesson/1), `quote`, `problem_it`, `fix_it`, `decision` (`sent_back` when the teacher sent the revision back, `topic_approved` when the topic's latest approval pins it) and the latest `response`. Blocker and major only; `all=1` adds the minor ones. `open=1` keeps the rows with no decision, no response, on the current or the pinned revision (the item rows keep their D-220 rule). New filters: `kind=item|lesson`, `lesson=KEY` (that lesson's findings only), `topic=KEY` (the topic's lesson and the items its latest revision pins). An unknown kind, lesson or topic is `E-NOT-FOUND`. CLI: `banco findings list [--subject S] [--kind item|lesson] [--lesson KEY | --topic KEY] [--open] [--all]`; with `--lesson` or `--topic` the subject is the key's middle part.
  3. **Answer.** `POST /api/v1/findings/L<R>-<n>/responses` (the same route; its constraint takes either form) with `{response: {stance, revision_id?, note_it}}`: `lesson_right` (no revision; the note is a short proof) or `fixed` (`revision_id`: a later revision of the same lesson). The rules of D-220: an author-role session of this token, not the session that wrote the review, holding no other role on the lesson (`LessonSessions`, `E-SESSION-NOT-INDEPENDENT`); `note_it` 1 to 700 characters through the readability lint (`E-READ`); `--dry-run` stores nothing; `item_right` is refused with a message that names the two lesson stances. New append-only table `lesson_finding_responses` (`lesson_review_id`, `finding_n` 1 to 30, `agent_session_id`, `stance`, `lesson_revision_id` required exactly when `fixed`, `note_it`, `created_at`, the two triggers). CLI: `banco findings respond L12-3 --file response.json`. A lesson finding has no third reviewer: `banco findings assess L12-3` is a usage error, the route also takes the L id and answers a JSON 422 `E-NOT-FOUND` saying so, and the arbiter brief lists `--kind item`. With `topic=KEY&open=1` the item revisions the topic's latest revision pins count as pinned even when a newer revision of the item exists. The list hint names the `lesson` and `lesson-v1` briefs, and `lesson-v1` carries the two answer shapes inline.
  4. **Where the agents see the ids.** `banco lesson-review submit` answers each finding with its `id`; `banco lesson open` and `banco lesson status` give every review's findings with `id` and `response`.
  5. **The teacher.** On the topic page (`Teacher::TopicReview#lesson_findings`, `teacher/topics/_lesson_finding`): in step 1 each review has a line "Rilievi: N, gravi: M. Risposte dell'autore ai gravi: K." with a link to the findings; the lesson/2 box has a list by card (a link opens the box on the card, one reads the finding, and for a blocker or major whether the author answered; a minor one expects no answer and says nothing of it); step 3 shows each finding with where it is ("Scheda 3: title · blocco 2", "Copertina", or the section and exercise), the quote, problem and fix, and "Risposta dell'agente autore:" with "Secondo l'autore la lezione è giusta." or "L'autore l'ha corretta nella revisione N." and the note; a blocker or major without an answer says "L'autore non ha ancora risposto." The guest reads the same and writes nothing.
  6. **Nothing decides.** A response is not a decision and changes no gate: `Approval::TopicGate` still asks for the teacher's reason when the latest review has a blocker or major finding, and the teacher still approves the topic or sends the lesson back in the browser. No route or command was added that decides (firm rule 2). The rows hold content only; no student data is read or shown.
- **Tests:** `test/integration/lesson_findings_api_test.rb` (ids, rows, filters, open, the answer and its rules, the decision field, no student data), `test/integration/lesson_findings_teacher_test.rb` (lesson/2 box and findings step), `test/integration/teacher_course_pages_test.rb` (lesson/1 place and a `fixed` answer), `test/integration/course_api_test.rb` (submit, respond, lesson open and status), `test/models/lesson_finding_response_test.rb`, `cli/cmd_findings_test.go`; contract examples `findings-list.lesson-rows`, `findings-respond.lesson-created`.
- **Cost:** the id depends on the order of the findings in the review document, which is fixed once stored. The item rows of `findings list` gain `kind`; the old row members are unchanged.
- **Rules version:** none changes.
- **Status:** decided
- **Back-port:** none.

## D-314 · 2026-10-18 · a matching one pair off is not nearly correct with a right column of two options or one option for every row; W-MATCHING-JUDGE-ROWS for new items

- **Design ref:** D-301 (`nearly_correct`), D-092 and D-093 (classifications, two categories from 6 rows), E-03 (`Grading::Closed`, matching), A-06 (validation warnings), A8.2 (practice outcomes), A9 (lesson checks).
- **Found (English review, 2026-10-17):** in a right/wrong "judge" matching (two options on the right, six or more rows), an instance with a single odd row was `nearly_correct` when the student gave the same option to every row: five of six right with no knowledge at all. The same hole is open in any classification whose key has one odd row (three of four with one category for every row).
- **Operator (2026-10-17):** fix the rule: `nearly_correct` does not apply when the right column has only two options, nor when the answer maps every left row to the same right option. Not retroactive.
- **We do (grader):** `Grading::Closed` matching gives `nearly_correct` only when, besides the D-301 conditions (not correct, no declared error hit, a key of at least `NEARLY_CORRECT_MIN_PAIRS` = 3 pairs, exactly one pair off), the right column has at least `NEARLY_CORRECT_MIN_RIGHT` = 3 options (the instance display's right column; a spec without one counts the distinct right ids of the key) and the answer uses at least two different right options. Otherwise the answer is `wrong`, as before D-301. So a judge is all or nothing; a classification of three or more categories keeps «one row off» unless the answer gives one category to every row; a one-to-one matching (n+1 right options) is unchanged. A declared error keeps precedence (`typical_error`). The ids are mapped (`id_map`) before the count, so a shuffled instance is judged on its canonical answer. The verdict is decided in one place: practice (`Practice::AnswerRecorder` through `Grading.grade`), lesson checks (`Lessons::Checks.closed`), testlet sub items and the warm-up all call `Grading::Closed`, so they follow without a change of their own. Shared vectors: five new matching cases in `test/fixtures/grading/vectors.json` (judge with one label for every row, judge five of six, classification with one label for every row, classification one row off, a two-label key without a display).
- **We do (validation):** `W-MATCHING-JUDGE-ROWS` (warning, `ruby` stage, `Validation::InstanceChecks#judge_rows`, static and generated instances, testlet sub items included): a matching instance with exactly two right options whose key has fewer than `JUDGE_MIN_ROWS` = 2 rows of one of them. The field is the option (`.../display/right/N`), the detail the row count. A warning only: it does not block approval; stored revisions are not re-validated. The two item briefs (`diagnosis-item`, `practice-item`) carry the content rule: a judge has at least 2 rows of each category in every instance.
- **Not changed:** stored gradings are not regraded (the ledger is append-only; a `nearly_correct` already recorded keeps its evidence C, its practice credit and its note); `Grading::PairNote`, the observation `one_pair_off`, the report and the end screen read the stored verdict as before; lesson checks get no new validation code (the grader rule covers them).
- **Rules version:** none changes, as for D-301. `diagnosis/1` and `practice/1` derive every stored outcome from the stored verdict, which no deploy changes; only gradings made after the deploy differ, and only on judges and one-label answers. `validation_rules.yml` stays at version 9 (a new check on content, as for D-296 and D-297: a bump would flag every pinned revision as validated under older rules); `error_codes.yml` goes to version 24 for the new code and the narrowed meaning of `nearly_correct`.
- **Status:** decided
- **Back-port:** none.

## D-315 · 2026-10-18 · content search: a new document gets its vector within minutes, lessons and cards are objects of "Simili"; the preview banner is one row at every width

- **Design ref:** D-299 (item 7, freshness), D-300 (items 3 and 6), D-303 (item 2), D-309 (item 3, the banner); firm rules 1, 4 and 6.
- **Seen (wave 3, 2026-10-17):** authors and reviewers ran `banco search --like` on items and lessons submitted hours earlier and got «no vectors yet for this object», sometimes `E-NOT-FOUND` (the lexical index did not have them either); «lessons are not addressable as --like documents». The production log of 2026-10-17 and 18: 330 `SearchIndexJob` runs in a day, one per write (11 for the same groups within 23 s after one burst of decisions); jobs waited 3 to 53 minutes in the queue; at 12:22 three jobs started together and each embedded the same pending documents for 4 to 5 minutes, holding the three threads of the default queue (the grading's too), and two questions' embeddings timed out meanwhile.
- **Causes:** (1) every index job embedded inline after its rebuild, for up to 20 minutes, so the jobs of a burst embedded the same documents side by side and blocked the queue, the lexical rebuild of the next change included; (2) the pending documents went oldest first, so a new revision (the highest ids) came last; (3) a vector was dropped whenever its document's digest changed, and the digest covers the status: every review step re-embedded a whole item or lesson, and a new revision re-embedded its unchanged instances and cards; (4) nothing went on after a job's 20 minutes but the next write or the nightly rebuild; (5) `like` knew only document kinds: `lesson:KEY` is none, and a card was only `lesson_card:KEY#scheda-N`.
- **We do:**
  1. **The index job is lexical only.** `SearchIndexJob` rebuilds its groups and enqueues `SearchEmbedJob` when a document waits for a vector. A burst is one rebuild: `Indexer.reindex` records when each group's read of the primary database began (`read_GROUP` in `search_meta`), and a job skips a group whose last read began after the job was enqueued (`Searchable` enqueues after the commit, so that read holds the write). A job run by hand always rebuilds.
  2. **`SearchEmbedJob`**: the newest documents first (`Vectors.pending` by id, descending), at most 160 documents or 120 seconds a run (the deadline is checked before each batch of 8), then, while some wait, it enqueues itself again. A service that is down is asked again 10 minutes later, 3 times at most, then the next change or the nightly rebuild tries. A run that took documents and embedded none, the service answering, does not go round again. Queue `search`, polled after `default` by the same worker (`config/queue.yml`: `queues: [ default, search ]`), so the grading never waits behind it. Never in a request.
  3. **One embedder at a time** (`Search::Lease`): a row of `search_meta` (`embed_lease`, "EXPIRES TOKEN") taken by one upsert that replaces only a lapsed lease, renewed before each request to the service (for as long as one request at its timeout, the retry wait and 60 s), given back at the end. A job that finds it held returns at once; the holder looks for new work after giving it back, so nothing written meanwhile is left behind; a holder that died leaves it for that long at most. The rebuild task takes it too (waiting up to `BANCO_EMBED_LEASE_WAIT`, 600 s, for a job's run) and hands what it leaves to the job; `banco:search:status` says when an embedder is at work.
  4. **A vector goes with its text.** `Index.replace_group` keeps the vector of a rewritten row whose text for the model (`Vectors.text_of`: title and body) is unchanged, a change of status, and gives a new row the vector of a row of the same object (same key and group) with the same text, the unchanged instances and cards of a new revision; the donors' vectors are read before the group is rewritten. The counts gain `reused`. Neither the digest nor the schema changes (version 2): the deploy re-embeds nothing.
  5. **Lessons in "Simili".** `Engine#like` takes `lesson:KEY`: the lesson is its cards in the revision the scope sees, the cover first; a document's score is its cosine with the nearest card (`Semantic.nearest_any`, one pass), `Hit#near` (API `near:`) says which card, and every document of the lesson (cards and glossary terms) is left out. A card is `lesson_card:KEY#N` or `lesson:KEY#N` as well as `lesson_card:KEY#scheda-N`. When some or all of the object's documents have no vector yet (`Result#members`, `#missing`) the API adds `waiting:` (how many documents of the index wait) and a `note`, the teacher's page says how many texts are queued, and a lesson with some cards embedded answers with those. Stored vectors only: no call to the model. The lesson box's «Simili alla lezione» links `lesson:KEY`; the CLI help, the briefs `lesson`, `lesson-review`, `review` and `diagnosis-item`, and the contract example `search.like-lesson.json` follow.
  6. **The preview banner (D-309) on a phone.** At 390 px its three actions wrapped into about 280 px. Now one row at every width, in the form that fits. The banner is a size container (`container: preview-banner / inline-size`) and its forms follow its own width in em, so the student's text size (`data-size`, 20, 24 or 28 px) moves the steps with the words; each step is the measured width of the form above it at the normal size plus a little: from 63em (1,260 px) «Stai provando come studente · Vista: …» and the three actions in one aligned row (66 px at 1280); from 50.5em (1,010 px) «In prova · …» and the same three actions (66 px at 1024 and 1180); below, «In prova» over the view, «Opzioni» (a `<details>` whose panel, over the page and the top bar, shows «Passa a: …» and «Ricomincia da capo» with their icons; `:has` on the open disclosure) and «Esci» (56 px at 390, 641, 768, 844×390 and 900); under 17.5em (350 px) «Opzioni» and «Esci» are their icons (`more-options`, `close`) and the view may break (56 px at 320). The status never shrinks under its longest phrase (each is `nowrap`; it breaks between them), and a row that still has no room puts the actions on a second row (`flex-wrap`), never off the screen. Every control's accessible name is the whole action (`aria-label`). Two ui icon aliases of icons already vendored, `view-switch` (`arrow-left-right`) and `more-options` (`ellipsis`); sprite and palette rebuilt. Review (2026-10-18): a first version chose its form with one `max-width: 40rem` media query and let the status shrink (`min-width: 0`), so between 641 and about 1,240 px the status went one word a line and the banner grew to 379 px (283 px at 844×390, with a sideways scroll at 641 to 700); the three forms and the floor above replace it. Measured in Chrome from 300 to 1,800 px, both views, the three text sizes: one row everywhere at the normal size, from 310 px at 24 px and from 360 px at 28 px (the narrowest of those break the view or wrap the row, never the screen's width).
- **Supersedes:** D-300 item 3 where it says the index job embeds for 20 minutes and the next run goes on, and D-303 item 2 where it speaks of `SearchIndexJob`'s stop on the first failure: items 1 to 3 here.
- **The firm rules.** 1: the student's door is untouched (`Scope::Student#semantic?` is false; nothing is embedded in a request; "Simili" reads stored vectors). 4: the index is the derived file; no table of the primary database changes. 6: names English, texts Italian.
- **Tests:** `test/jobs/search_embed_job_test.rb` (a bounded run, newest first, it goes on, work written meanwhile, the lease, a lapsed lease, the service down, no loop, the deadline, the queue order), `test/jobs/search_index_job_test.rb` (lexical only, the burst), `test/models/search/lease_test.rb`, `test/models/search/semantic_test.rb` (a status change keeps the vectors, a new revision takes them, a donor whose own text changed, newest first, `lesson:KEY`, card numbers, partly embedded, no model asked), `test/integration/search_api_test.rb` and `search_teacher_door_test.rb` (lessons over the API and on the page), `test/system/teacher_preview_test.rb` (the form, one row and nothing wider than the screen at 1280×900, 1180×820, 1024×768, 900×600, 844×390, 768×1024, 641×900, 390×844 and 320×568 in both views; the reset's question on the screen at 1024; the panel at 390; screenshots with `BANCO_SHOT_DIR`).
- **Cost:** one more key in `search_meta`; while a backlog lasts a short job every few seconds on the `search` queue; "Simili" of a whole lesson compares the scope's cards with each of its cards: 300 to 440 ms with the stub on 9,600 documents of which 1,800 cards (one card: about 40 ms).

## D-316 · 2026-10-19 · the true model of a session (a correction line, independence read with it) and no second opinion

- **Design ref:** A-08, Q8-bis, D-070 (a blind solver and a reviewer on another MODEL than every author), D-222 and D-239 (the third reviewer), D-260 (console decisions), firm rules 2 and 4.
- **Background:** the independence rule (`config/banco/providers.yml`) wants the blind solver and the reviewer of an item on another model than every author of it. A session declares its model (`banco session new --model`) and nobody can prove it. On 2026-10-18 a lead workflow ran its solver and reviewer agents on claude-opus-5-5 (no model was set on them) while its prompt told them to declare claude-sonnet-5-5: ten sessions declared a false model (agent sessions 772, 773, 775, 776, 783, 784, 816, 817, 819, 820), which filed the blind solves and reviews of Spanish, Italian and law topics (59 item reviews, 59 blind solves and 11 lesson reviews). Those reviews were not independent of the Opus authors. Separately, the arbiter's second opinion (D-222) had to run on claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 but the lead's agents can only run claude-haiku-5-5: second-opinion sessions since 2026-10-08 declared 4.5 while running 5.5 (no gate reads the second opinion). Every batch-2 topic was then re-reviewed by true Sonnet sessions (ids from 833).
- **Operator (2026-10-19):** two decisions. «Riga di correzione» (the ledger stays append-only, so a correction is a new row) and «Togli il secondo parere» (the arbiter's second opinion is dropped).
- **We do:**
  1. **The correction line.** A primary table `agent_session_corrections` (agent_session_id, model, reason, origin columns like the console decisions: os_user, groups `console`, remote_addr `console`, user_agent, request_path, a unique request_id, created_at) with the append-only triggers. `AgentSession#model` is the TRUE model: the model of the latest correction, else the declared one; `declared_model` stays readable. Every reader of a session's model uses `model` (Providers, FindingAssessment, ReviewFinding, the teacher's pages, the API serializers).
  2. **Independence at read time.** `Providers.independent?(session, authors)` (no author on the same true model) and `Providers.counting(rows, thing)`. A blind solve or a review (item, lesson, page) by a session on the same true model as an author of what it reviewed counts for no gate: `Review::Gate` (so `Approval::BlueprintGate`, `SubjectStage` and `Teacher::TestReview`), `Approval::TopicGate`, `Course::TopicStage`, `Course::Status`, `Pages::Validations.gate_reason` read `counting_reviews` and `counting_blind_solves`. The teacher's pages mark such a row «non indipendente» and show the model as «modello (dichiarato: X, corretto dall'operatore: motivo)». Its findings stay (they are observations) and stay listed. The write-time refusals stay (they now read true models).
  3. **The arbiter.** `different_model_from_raiser` is derived at read time too: an assessment by a session whose true model equals the true model of the session that raised the finding does not count (`FindingAssessment#counts?`); a minor finding it had closed goes back to the teacher.
  4. **The console task** `bin/rails banco:correct_session SESSION=772,773 MODEL=claude-opus-5-5 REASON="..." [CONFIRM=1]` (`AgentSessionCorrector`) is the operator's only way to write a correction: no HTTP route, no API, no CLI command, so no agent corrects a session, not even its own. A dry run (the default) runs the recording in a savepoint and prints, per session, the role, the declared and the current true model and the new model, then the reviews and solves that stop counting, the gates that close (items, topics, blueprints) and the minor outcomes that reopen. CONFIRM=1 records one row per session. A correction to the model a session already has (true) is refused.
  5. **No second opinion.** `providers.yml` allows only claude-opus-5-5 for the arbiter (`second_opinion_model` removed). `FindingOpinion` takes its state from the one counting opinion (none, clear, unclear); «Segui il parere» on a blocker or major follows a clear opinion. Past second opinions stay in the ledger and show as history («Secondo parere, non più richiesto (D-316)»); they never change a state. The API refuses an arbiter session on any other model (`E-PROVIDER-NOT-ALLOWED`). `briefs/arbiter.md` is version 2.
  6. **Not done here:** the sessions 772 to 820 are not corrected by this change; the operator runs the task (dry run first). No gate, rule version or threshold changes.
- **Tests:** `test/integration/agent_session_correction_test.rb` (the table and its triggers, the readers, each gate, the page says «non indipendente», other sessions untouched, the dry run, CONFIRM, the refusals, no route), `test/models/finding_opinion_test.rb`, `finding_assessment_test.rb`, `test/integration/third_reviewer_pages_test.rb`, `findings_api_test.rb`, `teacher_course_pages_test.rb`, `test/models/append_only_test.rb`.
- **Cost:** a gate reads the sessions of the item's authors each time (a few small queries per revision).
- **Rules version:** none changes.
- **Status:** decided
- **Back-port:** none.

## D-317 · 2026-10-21 · the entry test accepts every non-empty answer; a dot decimal and a trailing % are read; `banco:answers:pending`

- **Design ref:** firm rules 1, 2 and 4; D-295 and D-298 (refused answers and their text), D-222/D-260 (console), `Diagnosis::AnswerRecorder`, `Grading::Closed::Numbers`, `Teacher::Corrections`, rules `diagnosis/1`.
- **Found (operator, 2026-10-21):** in the entry test S lost a lot of time to refused answers. On a power item S typed 0.03125, was refused three times («usa la virgola»), deleted the dot and sent 003125. On a root item S tried for ten minutes to write words in the math field («non c'è valore per a», «nessun valore», «manca»): 37 refusals, then two comments «non funziona». On a fraction item S typed −29 over 3x five times (letters in a fraction are refused), spent an hour and left the item. On a percentage question S typed 45%, «45percento», 45x100. On the results page S pressed «Penso che la mia risposta fosse giusta» on five answers, two of which were already right: the page does not say which answers were right.
- **Operator decision:** «Risultati più chiari, Avviso nel campo di math, Accetta il %, anche accettiamo tutto poi lo controlliamo da qui». This entry does «Accetta il %» and «accettiamo tutto, poi lo controlliamo da qui»; «Risultati più chiari» and «Avviso nel campo di math» are separate work.
- **We do:**
  1. **Every non-empty answer is accepted in the diagnosis sitting** (the official student, trial students and the teacher's preview alike: one recorder). An answer the grader calls invalid is recorded as an attempt like any other: `raw` as typed and one `attempt_gradings` row with the verdict `undetermined`, `error_codes` = `["invalid_answer", <the grader's invalid code>]` (the marker first, as `Grading::Recorder.grade_attempt` already wrote it for a retry that turns out invalid; the code second, so the teacher's page and the console say why; `form_violations` stays empty). `Grading::Recorder::INVALID_ANSWER_CODE` is the marker. The `invalid_input` app event is still written, with the code and the text (D-298). Still refused: an empty answer, an answer over the size limit (20 000 bytes) and the grader's codes `empty` and `incomplete` (no part written; a refusal for nothing answered, not for a form). The browser shows «Risposta salvata. La guarderà il docente.» (`sitting.unreadable_saved`, sent as `message_it` of a `recorded` reply) and goes on to the next question after the usual pause. As no sitting refusal of this kind exists any more, `items/refusals.js` (cooldown, format line) no longer blocks the sitting; it stays for the refusals that remain (oversize, and the practice page).
  2. **The engine: nothing changes, so no rules version change.** The claim was checked: `Diagnosis::Rules::V1::EVIDENCE["undetermined"]` is `:pending` already (the table is untouched). `Diagnosis::State::Answer#pending_reason` says `verdict_pending`; the run holds (`Conductor#holding?`, reason `pending_answers`) like on a short answer or a worker that did not answer, the end-of-subject screen waits for the teacher's word, `Diagnosis::Summary` and the report show the pending state they always showed, and a teacher's `resolve_attempt` (`correct`, `wrong`, `dont_know`) counts it as a certain outcome and lets the run close. `test/integration/accepted_answers_test.rb` follows a whole run from the unreadable answer to the closed run.
  3. **The teacher's corrections page** (`Teacher::Corrections`, section «Verdetti incerti») already listed every attempt whose evidence is pending, with the item, the key, what S typed and the three resolve buttons. For these answers the line «Il correttore ha detto:» now reads «Risposta non leggibile dal programma» with the grader's message in brackets (`Verdict#unreadable`, `#unreadable_note`, `teacher.corrections.unreadable`), not «non so dire».
  4. **Two slips are read everywhere** (`Grading::Closed::Numbers`, so diagnosis, practice and the lesson checks): a dot used as a decimal separator when it cannot group thousands (0.03125, 5865.2, 12.5, 0.250) is read as the decimal comma; `1.250` and `12.345` (a dot every three digits, so possibly thousands) stay refused as ambiguous (`thousands_separator`), as before; the item's `allow_dot` and the check's `thousands` option keep their meaning. A trailing `%` or `percento` (any case, with or without a space) is dropped: 45% is 45, 45percento is 45; a lone `%` or a `%` in the middle stays unreadable. The code `use_comma` is no longer produced (it stays in the registry and the messages for the rows already written). Shared vectors `test/fixtures/grading/vectors.json` (`number-dot-*`, `number-percent*`); the client does not parse numbers, so no node twin is needed. Practice and lesson checks keep refusing what is still unreadable (their feedback is immediate), with these two slips accepted.
  5. **«Da qui».** `bin/rails banco:answers:pending [STUDENT=student] [SUBJECT=key]` (`lib/tasks/answers.rake`, `Teacher::PendingAnswers`), read-only: the answers waiting for the teacher (undetermined and short answers) with the attempt id, run, subject, item key, the instance's stem, the key, what S typed and the `banco:decide KIND=resolve_attempt` line to paste. No route, no API, no CLI command: the agents never read a student's answers (a test checks it).
- **Done with it:** the results page («Risultati più chiari»: which answers were right) and the warning in the math field («Avviso nel campo di math») are D-318, landed together with this entry.
- **Tests:** `test/integration/accepted_answers_test.rb`, `test/system/accepted_answers_system_test.rb` (Chrome; screenshots), `test/grading/vectors_test.rb` with the new vectors, `test/lib/lessons/checks_test.rb`, `test/models/practice/answer_recorder_test.rb`, `test/integration/sitting_feedback_test.rb`, `student_pages_test.rb`.
- **Cost:** a held run waits for the teacher's click on every unreadable answer (that is the intent: «poi lo controlliamo da qui»); a student who types nonsense on every item holds the run until the teacher resolves each.
- **Rules version:** none changes (`undetermined` was `:pending`; the grading rows only carry more error codes).
- **Status:** decided
- **Back-port:** none.

## D-318 · 2026-10-21 · results that say right or wrong, and a hint in the math field for typed words

- **Design ref:** B-11 (the end screen), E-04 (the expression field), D-298 (refused answers), D-306 and D-307 (house components), firm rule 1 (no model in the student's path).
- **Background:** in the entry test S lost much time to refused answers: on an exponent item 0.03125 refused three times and then sent as 003125; on a root item ten minutes writing words in the math field (37 refusals, two comments «non funziona»); on a fraction item −29 over 3x five times; on a percentage 45%, «45percento», 45x100. On the results page S pressed «Penso che la mia risposta fosse giusta» on five answers, two of which were already right, because the page did not say which answers were right.
- **Operator (2026-10-21):** «Risultati più chiari, Avviso nel campo di math, Accetta il %, anche accettiamo tutto poi lo controlliamo da qui».
- **We do:**
  1. **Results say how it went.** Each solution card carries a pill with an icon and the word: «Giusta» (correct), «Quasi giusta» (nearly_correct, with its existing note), «Da rivedere» (wrong, typical_error, wrong_form_skill), «Non lo sapevi» (dont_know), «La guarda il docente» (everything the machine does not settle: short_answer, undetermined, near_miss, wrong_form_declared and the like). `Diagnosis::Summary::Solution#outcome` makes the five words from the verdict. The order is unchanged (not right first). The teacher's preview shows the same page.
  2. **The flag only where it helps.** «Penso che la mia risposta fosse giusta» shows only on «Da rivedere» (`Solution#flaggable?`). Not on right, nearly right, «Non lo sapevi» (S said so) or pending cards (the teacher looks at them anyway).
  3. **A hint in the math field.** `items/expression_words.js` decides from the field's LaTeX whether words were typed: `\operatorname`, `\text`, `\mathrm` and the like are flattened and a run of three or more letters that is not a known function name (sin, cos, log, mcm...) nor made only of the item's own letters (those in the `$..$` of its texts) counts. `items/expression.js` then shows, under the field and without blocking anything, «Qui va solo l'espressione, senza parole: la lettera resta nella risposta, per esempio 24a³. Se pensi che non si possa fare, premi «Non lo so».» (a fixed example, never the item's answer; `items.expression_words_hint`). It goes when the words go. The sitting and the practice page share the template.
  4. **Done with it:** accepting «%» and «accepting everything and checking it from the teacher's page» are D-317 (grading), landed together with this entry.
- **Tests:** `test/javascript/items/expression_words.test.mjs`, `test/integration/student_pages_test.rb` (each verdict's label, the flag only on a wrong one), `test/system/results_and_hints_test.rb` (the results at 390 px, the hint in the sitting).
- **Cost:** none on the server; the hint runs on each keystroke in the field (a few regular expressions).
- **Rules version:** none changes.
- **Status:** decided
- **Back-port:** none.

## D-319 · 2026-10-24 · a tap on a map zone selects it (the `select` check over a map)

- **Design ref:** wave-2 T1 (D-273, the `select` check), T5 (D-276, the maps family), D-312 (select targets of the cell).
- **Background:** on the teacher's pages, in the history lesson `ponte.history.republic-to-empire` (revision 82), the check «In quale zona sta Cartagine? Tocca la zona sulla carta.» (`::: check select`, map `mediterraneo_antico`, `targets: areas`, `candidates` of four zones) could not be answered by touching the map: the operator had to use the list. The author had already moved from `targets: places` to `targets: areas` after review 41 (the places were not drawn).
- **Cause:** `draw.js` named a select target (`data-target="tN"`) only on the shapes it adds at the top of the figure. A map draws its zones inside a scaled group (`dg-mapgroup`), so the four zones were drawn but carried no target: `selectTargets()` found none, called `onNoTargets` and the page showed only its fallback list («zona 1 di 4, al centro»), the «list alternative». The places (circles outside the group) and the pads were top-level and worked, which is why the cell and the probe figures never showed it. Even with the name, the buttons took their box from `getBBox()`, which is in the group's own units (a map's 1000-wide viewBox), not in stage pixels, and a zone's bounding box would have covered its neighbours. Same on every page that draws a lesson/2 check (the student's lesson, the teacher's box on the topic page, `/teacher/preview`): one renderer.
- **We do:**
  1. `shapeNode` names the target on the shape at any depth (`app/javascript/lesson/diagrams/draw.js`).
  2. The boxes of the buttons are read with `getBoundingClientRect()` against the stage, so they follow a group's transform.
  3. A target inside a group (an irregular zone) is tapped on the shape itself: its click, and the click on its invisible pad (a small zone), press its button. The button of such a shape stays the keyboard's and the screen reader's way in (`dg-target-shape`: no pointer events, no dashed box, a focus ring). A chosen zone takes `is-selected` (`maps.css`, with a forced-colours rule). A top-level target (a place, a band, a line) keeps its button as the tap target.
  4. The list alternative is unchanged (it is still shown when a figure draws no target, and in safe mode).
- **`targets: places`:** the server already serves the set the check names (`StudentBody.select_figure` passes `set:`), so the review-41 bug is not present in this tree; a system test now taps places over `mediterraneo_antico` (cartagine, roma, atene, alessandria) and grades them. Authors may use `targets: places`.
- **Polish (review, 2026-10-24):** in print, a zone's button number is hidden (the drawn `.dg-tnum` stays) and a chosen zone or line prints like an unchosen one (numbered targets, none chosen: P3); on the keyboard the ring is drawn on the zone itself (`is-focus` on the target shape, `var(--focus)`, `Highlight` in forced colours) and not round the zone's bounding box. Bands and lines over a modern map (`europe`) are tapped and graded by the same test.
- **Tests:** `test/system/map_select_system_test.rb` (Chrome: the student's lesson, `/teacher/preview` and the teacher's box, at 390 px with touch events and 1280 px with the mouse; every target of an `areas` check with candidates and of a `places` check is tapped at a point the page really hits (`elementFromPoint`), a pick selects only itself, a wrong and a right answer are graded), fixture `test/fixtures/lesson2/map_select.md`. Screenshots before and after in `~/tmp/ui-shots/map-select-fix/`.
- **Cost:** none on the server; no rules version changes; lessons with `targets: areas` need no edit.
- **Status:** decided
- **Back-port:** none.

## D-320 · 2026-10-29 · the blind solver and the reviewer see the figures of an item

- **Design ref:** A-05 (the blind solve and the expert review), M6 (D-133, D-169: they see the item as the student does).
- **Background:** found in the chemistry wave (2026-10-29). An item whose instances show a figure (a heating curve, a graph to read: an SVG asset of the item) reached the blind solver as the figure's relative asset name and its `alt_it` only, and the solve brief said to work from what is displayed. The solvers answered «Non lo so» on every instance (36 automatic major findings on three items); the reviewer could only check the keys against the stored data points.
- **We do:**
  1. `Review::Figures` finds the figures of the displays the agent reads (the item's prompt, an instance's own, a testlet sub item's) and gives each distinct asset one file, `figure-1.png`, `figure-2.png`, ... in order of first appearance, with the instances that show it. `Review::FigureImage` draws the SVG in the server's Chrome (the one door, `ChromeRunner`, under its lock) as an `<img>` of a data URL, 1000 px wide on white, and keeps the pixels as a PNG; cached in `storage/item_figures/<sha256 of the SVG>.png` (`BANCO_ITEM_FIGURES_DIR`).
  2. `GET /api/v1/revisions/:revision/solve` and `/review` carry `figures` (`name`, `alt_it`, `instances`, `width`, `height`, `sha256`, `png_base64`; `[]` when no instance shows a figure; `missing: true` for an asset the revision does not hold). In the solver's display a figure is only `{alt_it, file}` (no asset name); the reviewer's keeps its own members and gains `file`. Chrome that cannot draw answers 503 `E-CHROME-UNAVAILABLE` and nothing is opened: an agent that never saw the picture would only guess.
  3. `banco solve open REV` and `banco review open REV` write the files in `banco-figures/REV/` (`--dir DIR`), print `figures` with each file's `path` instead of the picture, and `figures_dir`; an answer with no figure is printed as it came. Stdlib only; the names are checked (`figure-N.png`).
  4. Briefs: `solve` version 2 (look at every figure file before answering; never `dont_know` for a missing or unreadable figure, stop and report it) and `review` version 3 (look at every figure file and check the drawing against the key; a missing figure is a finding).
  5. **Review round (2026-10-29), on D-321.** The figure is resolved through `Items::Figures` (same digest, same refusal rules) and drawn from the stored copy the student's `<img>` gets; a figure the student would get no picture for (refused, absent, digest without a stored file) is `missing: true`, never a drawing; a figure with neither asset nor digest is its alt text only. All uncached figures of one open are drawn in one Chrome session (lock wait 60 s, drawing budget 60 s, the CLI's timeout is 300 s); a busy Chrome is 409 `E-CHROME-BUSY`, no Chrome 503, both with retry advice. Cached PNGs are checked (signature, IHDR, IEND) and redrawn when bad; cache dir 0700, files 0600. The CLI clears stale `figure-*.png` in the folder and removes a symlink instead of following it, writes 0600 in a 0700 folder, and when a figure is missing prints the item with a `warnings` line and exits 3 with `E-FIGURE-MISSING`.
- **Still nothing a student does not see:** the PNG is what Chrome paints. The SVG's `<title>`, `<desc>`, metadata, comments, `data-*` attributes and any value that is not drawn cannot be in it, and the SVG text itself is never sent; the PNG holds only image chunks (the test lists them). The solver still gets no key, solution, hints or stored data.
- **Cost:** a Chrome run on the first open of a figure (cached by content afterwards); a response with the figures inline (about 15 to 60 KB of base64 per figure).
- **Status:** decided
- **Back-port:** none.
## D-321 · 2026-10-29 · an item's figure reaches the student: the digest and the stored copy are made when the item is drawn

- **Design ref:** X-02, A-03; completes D-049 (4).
- **Design said:** D-049 left the seam: «M5 stores the figure's digest in the display's figure.sha256 and the file under its digest (or tells us the shape it uses)». It never happened: an instance display carries `"figure": {"asset": "assets/h1-01.svg", "alt_it": "..."}`, the SVG lives in the revision's `files_json`, and nothing wrote a digest or a file under `storage/item_assets/`. `Items::Part#figure` gave an `<img>` only with a `sha256`, so the student saw the alt text only (found 2026-10-29; 13 production revisions have assets, none pinned yet).
- **We do:** (1) The ledger rows are not rewritten (append-only): the figure is resolved at read time. `Items::Part` takes the item revision (`revision:`); for a figure with an `asset` it reads that file from the revision's `files_json`, computes its sha256 and makes sure `<sha256>.svg` exists in the item assets directory (`Items::Figures`, written once, to a temporary file renamed into place), and tells the browser `src: /assets/items/<sha256>.svg`. An explicit `sha256` on a display is still honoured and then nothing is written. Every path that draws an item for a person goes through `Items::Part`: the sitting, the teacher's preview, the item cards and all-questions page (`Teacher::StoredPresentation`, `ItemPlaysController`, both through `Diagnosis::ItemPresenter`, testlet sub items included, which read the same revision files) and the practice pages (`PracticeController`). The warm-up has no figures. The search index builds its text without a revision (it only needs the alt text) and writes nothing. (2) Safety: the SVG is agent-written and is shown only as an `<img>` (no script runs there) from `ItemAssetsController` with `nosniff` and `default-src 'none'; style-src 'unsafe-inline'; sandbox`. In addition a copy is stored only when it passes `Validation::ItemChecks.svg_problem` (the validation's own check: script, on* handlers, foreignObject, outside href, url() and @import) and a stricter pass in `Items::Figures` (DOCTYPE and entities, `javascript:` `vbscript:` `data:` addresses, iframe, embed, object, media, canvas, animate, set, handlers, an href to anything but `#id` on use, image, a, feImage, link; more than 512 KB; not an SVG). A dirty SVG is refused, not cleaned (a cleaned copy would be a figure nobody approved): no file is written and the student sees the alt text, as before. (3) The picture: `img.figure` is `max-width: 100%`, `max-height: min(26rem, 60vh)`, centred, on the white background; the `alt_it` is the image's alt (a figure that cannot be shown stays a paragraph with that text). Checked in Chrome at 390 and 1280 px (the sitting and the practice page).
- **Why:** The figure is part of what the question asks; without it the student cannot answer. Resolving at read time keeps the ledger append-only and needs no migration of the 13 revisions.
- **Hardening (review):** a disk that cannot be written (read-only, full, bad path) is logged and the figure falls back to its alt text, never a 500; the `data:`/`javascript:` test looks at attribute values only, so a label «Data: 5» keeps its picture; an explicit `sha256` is honoured only when its file exists, else the asset is used.
- **Cost:** An item draw reads the revision's `files_json` when it shows a figure (one JSON parse) and stats one file; the directory fills with one SVG per distinct figure (small, never deleted). The sibling branch `solver-figures` adds D-320 for the blind solver's side.
- **Status:** implemented
- **Back-port:** X-02, A-03 (the digest is made by the app at draw time, not stored by M5).
- **Tests:** `test/models/items/figures_test.rb` (digest, written once, explicit sha, no figure, missing asset, dirty SVGs), `test/integration/item_figures_test.rb` (practice and sitting payloads, the image served), `test/system/item_figures_system_test.rb` (Chrome at 390 and 1280 px; shots in `~/tmp/ui-shots/item-figures/`).

## D-324 · 2026-11-08 · topics outside the programme («Fuori programma»), acronyms in parentheses, links to topics of computer_science and law_economics

- **Design ref:** A2.1 (kinds of a lesson), A2.2 (the course map), A2.3 (the topic pool), A8.8 (Oggi), A9 (the student's course pages), A10 (the teacher's course page); A-06 (readability).
- **Design said:** Three kinds of topic, all of them part of the course: `ripasso`, `ponte`, `lezione`; a course skill is taught in the current year's programme (`seconda-2025-26`). Every topic is suggested by Oggi and counted. ALL-CAPS words of 3 or more letters are E-READ unless in `caps_allowlist`. A lesson link target is lowercase letters, digits, dots and hyphens.
- **Operator (2026-11-08):** on the items the official programme marks as already done that the previous school's programme does not have: «vorrei che queste fossero fuori dal programma ma ugualmente gestite in banco e segnate come esterne al programma (possiamo modificare banco e aggiungere funzionalità se necessario). Sono cose che lo studente ha voluto fare e devono comunque essere un minimo gestite da esercizi facoltativi e integrazioni se necessario.» On acronyms: «accettiamo anche le sigle da [lo studente] e nel testo mettiamo le sigle tra le () quando la sigla è importante» (the student's name replaced: no person in git).
- **We do:** (1) A fourth kind, `extra` (key `extra.<subject>.<slug>`) everywhere a topic key is matched: `Lesson::KINDS` and the `lessons_kind` constraint (migration `AddExtraLessonKind`, a table rebuild as in D-222), the routes, the API and teacher controllers, `Comments::Pages`, `Lessons::Parser|Parser2`, the schemas `course`, `lesson` (kind and scope `extra`) and `topic`, the CLI's `lessonKeyRe`. (2) The official programme is the syllabus source `ufficiale-2026-27` (`course.extra_source`), imported by the operator with `bin/rails banco:syllabus:import SOURCE=ufficiale-2026-27 FILE=-`. A course skill cites `taught_in` on `seconda-2025-26` or on it (citations checked the same way); a skill whose only `taught_in` refs are on it is held only by an extra topic (`E-COURSE-EXTRA-SKILL`, also in the contract of `course submit`); an extra topic may hold graph skills no other topic holds. An extra lesson has `scope: extra` and a `taught_in` ref on the official programme, no seconda ref (`E-LESSON-REFS`). (3) `E-TOPIC-POOL` of an extra topic asks per skill 10 distinct instances, 6 hard to guess, one level 1 item (`practice.extra_topic_*`); lesson review, item reviews, blind solves and `approve_topic` are unchanged. (4) The student: Materia lists the extra topics after the programme's under «Fuori programma (facoltativo)», each with a «Fuori programma» badge (also on the topic page); Oggi never suggests nor resumes them, the counts of Materie and Materia leave them out, their skills are never named «senza argomento», a programme topic's «Prima conviene fare» never points to one. Their practice runs when the student opens the topic and is graded and recorded like any other. (5) The teacher: the course path has its own section «Fuori programma» (numbered apart), the topic page shows the badge and one line on what the kind means; approval and release are those of any topic. (6) Readability: an ALL-CAPS word that stands alone inside parentheses passes («prodotto interno lordo (PIL)», «(UNESCO)»); outside parentheses the allowlist rule is unchanged; ISO, RAW, LED, GPS, UTC, GIS, UNESCO join `caps_allowlist`. The rule has one implementation (`Validation::Readability.caps`), used by items, lessons, maps and pages; no JS twin. (7) Student answers: no grader change; the practice-item and lesson briefs say that a typed answer whose words have a common acronym accepts both (the key and the instance's `accept`). `Grading::Closed::Text.normalize` already folds case unless `case_sensitive: true`, so «pil» and «PIL» are the same answer; a dotted «P.I.L.» is another string. (8) A lesson link `argomento:` accepts `_` (subject keys `computer_science`, `law_economics`) in `Lessons::Markup::LINK_TARGET` and in `items/markup_parser.js`, and so `extra.` keys (the topic must still be in the map, `E-LESSON-LINK`). (9) `validation_rules.yml` version 10 (the readability rule and the allowlist change a check). (10) An item's source on the official programme is a programme line of kind `seconda_line` with `ref: "ufficiale-2026-27:N"`: no new kind and no schema change, because `ItemChecks.sources` already checks any `SOURCE:N` ref of a line kind (line exists, citable, exact fragment, `E-SOURCE`) and `Review::ItemText#programme_lines` already shows it to the reviewer; the practice-item brief now says so (authors had fallen back to `inferred`).
- **Why:** The operator's words: these topics are outside the programme but the student wants them, so they are managed (lesson, a few optional exercises, the teacher's approval) and marked as external; nothing about them may become a duty in Oggi or a count. Acronyms in parentheses after the words are how a textbook introduces them.
- **Cost:** One migration (a rebuild of `lessons`, ids kept, triggers reinstalled, foreign keys checked). The CLI must be rebuilt (`lessonKeyRe`, and the contract lists the new code). Version 10 is informational for what passed under 9: `ItemRevision#status` is the latest validation's verdict whatever its rules version, `Approval::TopicGate` and `Review::Gate` read that status only, `ValidateItemRevisionJob` re-validates only an explicit resubmission (D-154), and `older_rules` (topics, lessons, the blueprint's `W-` warning) is a line, never a blocker. An identical lesson resubmitted under 10 is a new revision, not a replay.
- **Status:** implemented
- **Back-port:** A2.1 (kind `extra`), A2.2 (`course.extra_source`), A2.3 (pool of an extra topic), A8.8 and A9 (Oggi and Materia leave them out of suggestions and counts), A-06 (acronyms in parentheses).
- **Tests:** `test/integration/extra_topics_test.rb` (map, lesson and topic validation accepted and refused over the API; Materia's section and badge; Oggi never suggests an extra topic; the teacher's course path and topic page), `test/validation/course_codes_test.rb` (`E-COURSE-EXTRA-SKILL`), `test/validation/readability_test.rb` (an acronym in parentheses, a bare one, the new allowlist), `test/fixtures/markup/v2.json` (a link to `lezione.computer_science.*` and `extra.law_economics.*`).

## D-325 · 2026-11-14 · the course starts from every finished entry test, closed or not; a request reads each run once

- **Design ref:** A8.6 (the seed from the entry diagnosis), B-11 and D-298 (the list says «Fatto» for a run that has nothing left to ask), A9 (the student's pages).
- **Design said:** The seed comes from the student's latest non-voided closed run in the subject (`Practice::Seeder`). The list of tests (`Diagnosis::Availability`) already calls a run «completed» when it is closed or, with no item open, held for pending answers or with the engine's next move «close the run» (D-298).
- **Observed (a copy of production, 2026-11-14):** S had finished the entry test of six subjects (Spanish, history, geography, business, computer science, chemistry): the engine's next move was `close_run`, only the `run_closed` row was missing, because that row is written when S opens the run again. The list said «Fatto»; the course ignored the six results (S's Materie page said «26 da vedere» for geography after the test). Student pages also took 3.5 to 9 seconds (about 14,800 queries for Oggi): every subject loaded the plan of every run of S again, and each plan loaded its items one by one.
- **We do:** (1) `Diagnosis::Conductor#completed?` is the one definition of «this run asks nothing more of S» (closed; or no open item and the engine holds for pending answers or wants to close). `Diagnosis::Availability`, `Diagnosis::Report#status` and `Practice::Seeder` all call it, so the list and the seeds cannot drift. (2) The seeder uses the latest non-voided run that is completed in that sense; the derivation is the same engine over the same log, so a finished run seeds exactly what it seeds once the close row is written (a test writes the row and compares). A skill still pending (an answer waiting for the teacher) is not seeded, as before. No row is written to close the run. (3) Reads: `Diagnosis::Reads` (`CurrentAttributes`, emptied at the end of every request, job and test) keeps what a request has already read: the plan, the events and the skill rows of each run, the instances of a blueprint revision, the other subjects' graphs. It is dropped as soon as the largest id of any table the loaders read changes (runs, events, attempts, gradings, decisions, retry exhaustions, validations, skill graphs; one query), so a write is seen at once. (4) `PlanLoader` loads the pinned items and their instances in bulk (two queries), the texts of an instance for the overlap rule are worked out only when two instances of an item are compared, `EventLoader` reads the voided runs and the exhausted retries once, `Conductor#state` is folded again only when the log changed, and the list derives a run once.
- **Why:** S did six tests and the course ignored them: S would redo work already shown, and the page would say «da vedere» for skills the test had already settled. The page of a student with reading difficulties must also open at once. The engine stays pure (`lib/diagnosis` has no database); no rule, no state and no text changes, so rules version stays 10.
- **Cost:** One extra read of a few maximum ids per question to the ledger (answered by the query cache inside a request). Reads of a run are shared inside one request, so code that changes a run's rows must do it through ActiveRecord (it always did: the tables are append-only). A seed made from a finished run carries the time of the run's last event.
- **Status:** implemented
- **Back-port:** A8.6 and `docs/rules/practice-1.md` section 6 (which run seeds practice).
- **Tests:** `test/models/practice/loader_test.rb` (`PracticeSeederFinishedRunTest`: a finished run with no close row seeds, and seeds what the closed run seeds; a voided one seeds nothing), `test/models/diagnosis/reads_test.rb` (the memo is dropped when a row is added), and the existing seeder tests.

## D-326 · 2026-11-14 · Materie, Materia and Oggi show what S has done, what is missing, what is mandatory and what is optional

- **Design ref:** A9 (the student's course pages), A8.8 (Oggi), D-307 (Materie cards), D-324 (topics «Fuori programma»).
- **Design said:** The Materie card showed a bar and chips of skill states («5 dimostrate», «6 da riprendere», «12 da vedere») over the programme topics' skills; Materia listed the programme under «Gli argomenti» and the extra topics under «Fuori programma (facoltativo)» with a status per topic; Oggi had the entry test and the suggestions only.
- **Operator (2026-11-14):** S starts the exercises now and must see at a glance, without confusion, what S has done, what is still missing, what is mandatory (the programme) and what is optional (`extra`), including the optional work already done. S has reading difficulties: short Italian sentences, one idea per line, no jargon.
- **We do:** (1) `Course::StudentView#progress(sv)` and `#overall_progress` count topics, once per request, from the statuses the view already computes: `Tally(total, done, in_progress)` with `missing` and `percent` (floor, so a bar never says 100 with one topic missing), for the programme and for the extra topics apart. Done is `Practice::Today.done?`, in progress is started and not done, missing is not done. The skill `counts` are removed with their helper `subject_progress` and the partial `_progress`. (2) Materie and the top of Materia show the same three lines (`course/_summary`): «Obbligatori: X fatti su Y» with a bar, «Facoltativi: N fatti su M» only when the subject has extra topics (also when N is 0: the same shape on every card is easier to read than a second wording), and «Test d'ingresso: fatto | da finire | da fare» from `Diagnosis::Availability` for the acting student, the same rows Oggi reads (`CourseController#entry_test_for`; `fatto` includes a run that only waits to be closed, as Oggi says; no line when the tests are not open or the subject has none); on Materia the line also links to the results. (3) Materia's sections are «Obbligatori · programma» and «Facoltativi · fuori programma», each with its «N fatti su M»; «Tutti» / «Solo quello che manca» are two links (`?show=missing`, `aria-current`, no script) that hide the done topics of both sections, keep the counts and keep each topic's number; a section with nothing left says «Qui non manca niente. Bravo.». (4) A topic row has three looks: done has a check in its pill, a filled number and a teal side; in progress a pencil and a blue side; to do a dashed number and a plain side; «Da riprendere» stays a tag. (5) Oggi gets «Il tuo percorso» under the entry test: «Argomenti obbligatori fatti: X su Y» across all subjects with a bar, «Facoltativi fatti: N» (when there are extra topics) and «Vedi le materie»; Oggi still suggests only the programme. (6) The skill counts are not kept on Materia: «abilità» is a word S has no use for there, and the per-skill states stay on the topic and practice pages. The teacher's preview runs the same controllers and shows the same.
- **Why:** A skill count answered a question S did not ask; S asks «quanti argomenti mi mancano e quali sono obbligatori». Counting topics with the rule that already draws «Fatto» on each row makes the numbers on the card and the rows agree.
- **Cost:** `entry_test_for` runs `Diagnosis::Availability.for` on Materie and Materia too (Oggi already did): one pass per request. Nothing is written; no migration.
- **Status:** implemented
- **Back-port:** A9 (Materie, Materia, Oggi), A8.8 (Oggi's card), docs/ui.md (the subject card).
- **Tests:** `test/integration/course_pages_test.rb` (counts and labels on Materie, Materia in both filter states, Oggi, and the preview; the world `build_progress_world` in `test/support/student_course_world.rb`), `test/integration/extra_topics_test.rb`.

## D-327 · 2026-11-14 · the public API: api.banco.scc.im, the token roles bot_read and teacher with an expiry, teacher decisions and comment actions over the API (changes firm rule 2 and D-304's comment rule)

- **Design ref:** firm rule 2 (decisions are the teacher's, in the browser), D-05 (agent tokens), D-08 (the decisions' guards), D-222 and D-239 (the exceptions to rule 2 for minor findings), D-260 (the console path, never over HTTP), D-304 (comments; «no /api/v1 route reads a comment»), D-317 (the pending answers, console only).
- **Design said:** No `/api/v1` route creates a decision and the CLI has no decision command; the operator alone records a decision from the host console (D-260). No `/api/v1` route and no CLI command reads or answers a comment (D-304); the pending answers are the operator's console list (D-317). The API listener is internal, reached by the content agents.
- **Operator (2026-11-14):** the bot that drives banco can run the `banco` CLI but cannot use SSH, so the API is published on a new host, `api.banco.scc.im`, and the operator accepts the risk knowingly: (1) the bot may record teacher decisions through the API with a dedicated teacher token; (2) the API may show S's answers and S's comments; (3) protection is HTTPS on the new host, Bearer tokens with an expiry and a dedicated role for the bot, a read-only role, rate limiting at the edge and an audit trail of every decision and every comment action; no IP allowlist.
- **We do:**
  1. **Roles and expiry.** `ApiToken::ROLES` gains `bot_read` (any GET, never a write: every other method is 403 `E-AUTH`, reason `read_only_token`) and `teacher` (the reads of `bot_read`, plus decisions and comment actions as the login stored on the token; never content: any other write is 403 `teacher_token_no_content`). Neither opens a session. The content roles (`agent_claude`, `agent_omp`, `ci`) keep what they had and read none of the teacher's views (403 `token_role` on decisions, comments and pending answers). The migration `AddPublicApiTokens` adds `api_tokens.expires_at` and `teacher_login` (a check: a teacher token has a login), rebuilds `api_tokens` and `comment_events` for their CHECK constraints (the origin `api`), and reinstalls the append-only triggers. An expired or revoked token is refused like a wrong one (401 `E-AUTH`); the teacher login must be in `BANCO_TEACHER_USERS` at every use (403 `teacher_not_listed`: removing a teacher from the list cuts the token). `banco:token:issue` gains `EXPIRES_DAYS` (default 90, at least 1: no token is issued without an expiry) and `TEACHER=<login>` (required for role teacher); `banco:token:list` shows public id, role, label, teacher, expiry and state, never a secret.
  2. **Reads without a session.** A session only attributes writes, so a `bot_read` or `teacher` token reads without one the commands that need a session for the content agents: `work open --role verifier`, `review open`, `solve open`, `lesson-review open`, `page-review open`, `submissions --pending`, and it sees every opinion of the third reviewer.
  3. **Decisions.** `POST /api/v1/decisions {kind, params, reason_it, attest_it, confirm}` (a teacher token only) goes through `DecisionConsole`, so through `DecisionRecorder` and every gate of the kind (`BANCO_DECISIONS_ENABLED`, a teacher of `BANCO_TEACHER_USERS`, the business guards), with the origin `DecisionRecorder::Api` (login from the token; groups `api`; the address the edge proxy saw; payload `via: "api"` and the token's public id; the reason of a kind that takes none is `api_reason`). Without `confirm: true` it is a dry run, exactly like the console's: the recorder runs in a savepoint that is rolled back and the answer is the payload. `attest_it` is accepted from the console and from a teacher token over the API only: the operator decided that the bot may approve, knowing that a leaked or misled teacher token can approve a topic or a test nobody opened (the words are recorded and shown on the teacher's pages; `BANCO_DECISIONS_ENABLED=0` stops every API decision at once). `GET /api/v1/decisions?since=ID` lists the recorded decisions (kind, subject, payload, via, teacher, token, created_at) for audit, to `bot_read` and `teacher`. `banco decide KIND [--params JSON|--params-file F] [--reason T] [--attest T] [--confirm]`, `banco decisions [--since ID]`. Refusals: `E-TEACHER-REFUSED` (403: flag off, teacher not listed), `E-DECISION-INVALID` (422, the gate's reasons), `E-NOT-FOUND`.
  4. **Comments.** `GET /api/v1/comments[?state=open|all|sent|read|answered|closed]` and `GET /api/v1/comments/:id` (text, anchor, place, state, events) to `bot_read` and `teacher`; `POST /api/v1/comments/:id/reply|resolve|reopen|read {text_it | reason_it, confirm}` to a teacher token, through `Comments::Console` and `Comments::Responder`, a dry run unless `confirm: true`, recorded as the teacher with origin `api` (the event's payload names the token), shown on the teacher's page as «(da API)». `banco comments list|show|reply|resolve|reopen|read`. **This supersedes D-304 where it says that no `/api/v1` route reads a comment and that the agents never read one**: the content agents' tokens still read none; the student's words reach only the tokens of these two roles. The student still writes comments only in the browser; no route creates one. Refusal: `E-COMMENT-INVALID` (422).
  5. **Pending answers.** `GET /api/v1/answers/pending[?subject=KEY][&student=KEY]` (`Teacher::PendingAnswers`, the rows of `bin/rails banco:answers:pending` plus the decision that settles each one), `banco answers pending`; `bot_read` and `teacher`.
  6. **Docs and edge.** `docs/api.md` is the bot's manual. The rate limit (Traefik: average 10 requests per second, burst 30, per client IP), the TLS host and the router are the operator's, outside this repository.
