  7. **Hardening before opening the host (the security review, 2026-11-14).** Through the edge proxy (the request's peer is `BANCO_EDGE_PROXY`) only `bot_read` and `teacher` tokens are served (`403 E-AUTH`, reason `not_public_role` for a content token; the local agents keep `127.0.0.1:3100`); no token is issued without an expiry (`EXPIRES_DAYS` at least 1; a model validation makes `expires_at` mandatory for the public roles; there is no database CHECK for it: a CHECK added in the migration did not appear in the rebuilt table, so none is claimed); each public host belongs to one listener (`Banco::Hosts::ListenerHosts`: `api.banco.scc.im`, or `BANCO_API_HOST`, only on the API, `banco.scc.im` never on it); Puma refuses a body over 10 MB; the health check of a reader or the edge runs no browser probe and shows no exception text; an API approval of a graph or a test needs an explicit `revision_id`; the API records the kinds of `DecisionRecorder::Api::KINDS`, which leave out `record_consent` and `release_diagnosis`; the API origin keeps the request's id and the caller's User-Agent; every answer is `Cache-Control: no-store` and the contract digest goes to a good token only; the teacher views and the student's progress are for `bot_read` and `teacher` only; the CLI refuses `http://` for a host that is not loopback (`E-URL`) and names the edge's 429.
- **Why:** The bot has no shell on the host, and the operator wants it to do what the operator does from the console (D-260, D-304, D-317) without SSH. The risk is taken knowingly; the design keeps the rest of rule 2 in force: the same recorder and gates, a flag that switches every decision off at once, a login list that cuts a token at once, tokens that expire, a read-only role for what only reads, and an append-only trail where every row says `api` and the token.
- **Cost:** One migration (two rebuilds, triggers reinstalled, foreign keys checked). The CLI and the contract grow by nine commands. `Decision#api?`, `Decision#via`, `SubjectStage.approval_origin` (replaces `approved_from_console?`) and the pages' «(da API)». The guard tests of rule 2 and D-304 (`TestNoCommandApproves`, `test/lib/contract_test.rb`, `decision_console_test.rb`, `comments_test.rb`) now name the exception. Firm rule 2 in `AGENTS.md` carries it.
- **Status:** implemented in the code; nothing is exposed until the operator publishes the host and the rate limit.
- **Back-port:** AGENTS.md firm rule 2 and the layout; D-260 and D-304 (this entry supersedes their «never over HTTP» and «no API reads a comment» for the teacher and `bot_read` tokens).
- **Tests:** `test/integration/public_api_roles_test.rb` (roles, expiry, revocation, the teacher list, the token tasks), `public_api_decisions_test.rb` (dry run, confirm, the flag, the gates, the list), `public_api_attestation_test.rb`, `public_api_comments_test.rb` (reads, the four actions, pending answers), `cli/cmd_teacher_test.go`.

## D-328 · 2026-11-14 · the teacher's pages and the student's progress over the API (read-only)

- **Design ref:** C-04 (the teacher's pages), A9 and A10 (the student's and the teacher's course pages), D-063..D-068, D-241, D-304, D-327.
- **Design said:** The API is the content agents' door: it writes drafts and reads what they need to work (`banco status`, `banco findings list`, `banco practice progress`); the teacher's screens are HTML on the web listener, behind the edge proxy. Nothing told an agent what the teacher sees.
- **Operator (2026-11-14):** the bot that drives banco through the public API (D-327) must see what the teacher sees in the browser, and what the student sees, without a browser and without SSH.
- **We do:** (1) Five read-only endpoints on the API listener, answered to the tokens that read (`bot_read`, `teacher`; a content agent's token is 403 `token_role`: the pages hold the third reviewer's opinions and the student's progress): `GET /api/v1/teacher/home` (`?student=KEY`), `GET /api/v1/teacher/subjects/:key/course` (`?only=ready`), `GET /api/v1/teacher/subjects/:key/topics/:topic` (`?lesson=full` adds the lesson's text), `GET /api/v1/teacher/subjects/:key/test`, `GET /api/v1/students/:key/progress`. (2) They are the pages' own read models turned into hashes, with no query of their own: `Teacher::ApiView` over `Teacher::Dashboard|Home`, `CourseReview`, `TopicReview`, `TestReview` and `ItemCard`; `Course::StudentProgress` over `Course::StudentView` (`subjects`, `programme_topics`, `extra_topics`, `status`, `progress`, `overall_progress`, `state`; D-326's tallies, the same facts Materie and Materia show: per subject the programme and the extra topics as `total`, `done`, `in_progress`, `missing`, `percent`, and `overall`) and `Diagnosis::Availability` (the entry test state). The Italian texts the page words (badges, what is missing, the gate's reasons, the waiting lines) come as `_it` members beside the English reason or the key. (3) A read here writes nothing: the topic page records `teacher_viewed_topic`, the exercises `teacher_saw_exercise`, and the approval gate asks for them; the API never records either, so reading through it can never stand in for the teacher opening the page (the attestation, D-260, is the waiver: from the console, and, by the operator's decision in D-327, from a teacher token over the API, with the risk named there). (4) The CLI: `banco teacher home|course|topic|test`, `banco progress [--student KEY]`; each has its row in `contract/commands.json`. (5) `bin/build-cli-dist` cross-compiles the CLI for linux, darwin and windows on amd64 and arm64 into `dist/` (git-ignored) with `SHA256SUMS`, the version stamped from git (`-X main.version`, `<base>+<commit>`, `.dirty` with uncommitted changes in `cli/` or `contract/`). `BANCO_URL` accepts `https://host`, a bare `host` (https; a loopback address without a scheme is http) and a trailing slash; anything else is `E-URL`. The CLI explains a refused token (a wrong, an expired and a revoked token all answer 401 `E-AUTH`) and a read-only token that writes (403 `E-AUTH`, reason `read_only_token`). (6) The manual of the bot is `docs/api.md`, «Teacher views».
- **Why:** A bot that cannot open a browser needs the same facts the teacher reads before it can advise or, with the teacher token (D-327), decide; building them on the pages' read models keeps the two in step: a change of what a page says changes the API with it, and the tests compare the two for the same world.
- **What the API never does here:** it does not open the topic page for the teacher, does not record that anything was read, and shows no student's name: students are named by key only.
- **Cost:** The topic and test endpoints do the work of the page (the samples of every exercise, the engine's two traces for the test); the home runs the dashboard's queries. The edge limits the rate (docs/api.md).
- **Status:** implemented
- **Back-port:** C-04 (the teacher's pages also as JSON), A9/A10 (the student's progress as JSON).
- **Tests:** `test/integration/teacher_views_api_test.rb` (each endpoint compared with the page for the same world; both reading roles get the same answer and the content roles are refused; no token is refused; a read records no event), `test/integration/student_progress_api_test.rb` (compared with Materia and the diagnosis list), `cli/cmd_teacher_test.go` (paths, usage errors, `BANCO_URL`, the refused-token messages).

## D-329 · 2026-11-14 · the `code` block: a whole program to copy and try on the Mac

- **Design ref:** A4 (the blocks of a card), WAVE2 1.8 (word counts and apparatus), D-290 (a block of release 2: `page`), D-310 (markup wherever it is written), the VB conventions of `STATUS-wave9.md`.
- **Design said:** A lesson/2 card holds no whole program: code is a short inline `[[code:..]]` span, a table cell, or the listing of the draft `program` diagram, which our code would generate.
- **Operator (2026-11-14):** the VB lessons must carry instructions to try every program on the Mac. S (15, reading difficulties) reads short Italian sentences, one idea per line.
- **We do:** (1) A block `code` (batch r2, core: no family stylesheet): `{lang, text, title_it?, input_it?, output?, note_it?}`. `lang` is `vb` and nothing else. `text` is the program (a YAML `|` block: newlines and indentation kept, four spaces, no tab, at most 60 lines of 90 characters). `input_it` is what S types, in order (at most 12 lines of 40). `output` is the screen at the end of the run (at most 30 lines of 90, no tab). `title_it` and `note_it` are markup. The numbers are `lesson2.types.code` in `validation_rules.yml`; new keys only, so the rules version stays 10 (as D-216's optional checks). (2) The schema `b_code` keeps the sizes and `lang` loose (strings, 20 000 characters) so that each limit has its own code, registered as `E-LESSON-CODE-LANG`, `E-LESSON-CODE-SIZE` (empty, too many lines, a line too wide, too many typed lines) and `E-LESSON-CODE-TAB`; error registry version 26; `Lessons::Blocks::Code` checks them, each with the line of its field. Bad fixtures `bad/code-lang.md`, `bad/code-size.md`, `bad/code-tab.md`. (3) **What the word cap counts:** `Lessons::Blocks.prose` lists, per type, the strings that count as the prose S reads to learn: the 500 words of core prose (`E-LESSON-WORDS`), the 90 of a core card (`E-CARD-WORDS`), the depth budget (`E-LESSON-EXTRA-WORDS`) and, through `apparatus_words`, the 250 open by default. A `code` block has no branch in any of them: its program, typed lines, output, title and note are never counted. Its `title_it` and `note_it` are markup fields, so the language lint (`E-READ`, banned phrases) still reads them. The program, the typed lines and the output are plain characters: never markup (`$"{x}"` and `[[` are safe). It is not a visual (`E-CARD-NO-VISUAL` still wants a diagram on an idea card), not a check, not in a `more` block. (4) It is served whole (`StudentBody::BLOCKS`, `whitelist.json`): it holds no answer; the brief tells the author never to put the answer of a check of the same card in `output`. (5) The browser: `lesson/blocks/code.js`. A `<pre><code>` with `white-space: pre` and `overflow-x: auto`, a region with a name and `tabindex=0` so a keyboard can scroll it, `translate="no"`; a long line scrolls inside the box at 390 px and never wraps (print wraps). «Copia» writes `block.text` to `navigator.clipboard`, exactly, and shows «Copiato» for 2,5 s on the button and in a polite live line; if the clipboard is refused the program is selected and the line says «premi Cmd e C». «Scrivi:» lists what S types, each line as a key, then «Dopo ogni riga premi Invio.»; «Sullo schermo vedi:» shows the output in a dashed box. The monospaced font is the Mac's (`ui-monospace`, `SF Mono`, `Menlo`). (6) **Highlighting:** none. The palette of computer science already has its eight roles, so there is no keyword colour; the box is plain, which also suits S. (7) **Speech:** «Ascolta» says «un programma di N righe» and never reads a listing (`data-speech-text`; the typed lines and the output are `data-nospeech`). (8) The render check draws it like any block, one state per card; `overflowFindings` skips `.code-box` and `.code-screen` (a box that scrolls on purpose) and still reports a page wider than the window. Gallery `test/fixtures/lesson2/gallery/code.md` (a 90-character line, an empty line, deep indentation).
- **Why:** S must be able to run every program of the school's programme at home, on a Mac, one step at a time; a listing inside a text paragraph or a table cannot be copied without its indentation, and a program is not prose: counting it in the word cap would punish the lessons that carry the most code.
- **Cost:** one more block to draw and to keep in step with `lesson.css`, the schema, the whitelist, the brief and the gallery; the `title_it` and `note_it` of a code block are prose that escapes the word counts (at most 80 and 200 characters, and `E-READ`); no new dependency.
- **Not done:** other languages (`lang` is `vb`; a second one is a registry change and a D entry), syntax colours, line numbers, a code block inside `more`, running a program in the page (Rule 3 of AGENTS.md stands: agent-written code runs only in browsers' sandboxes, and a lesson program is for S's own Terminal).
- **Status:** implemented
- **Back-port:** A4 (the blocks), docs/lessons-wave2.md (section «The `code` block»), docs/validation.md (overflow), briefs `lesson` and `lesson-computer-science`.
- **Tests:** `test/lib/lessons/code_test.rb`, `app/javascript/lesson/test/code.test.mjs`, `test/validation/code_gallery_test.rb` (render check), `test/system/lesson_code_block_test.rb` (390 px, copy), the manifest, whitelist and registry tests.

## D-330 · 2026-11-14 · a public token renews itself on use; the bot learns what changed and updates its CLI over the API

- **Design ref:** D-05 (agent tokens), D-327 (the public API, its token roles and their expiry; the security review), D-328 (the release build `bin/build-cli-dist`), firm rule 4 (the ledger is append-only).
- **Design said:** D-327: every public token expires (`EXPIRES_DAYS`, 90 by default, at least 1; no token without an expiry), and the security review made the expiry mandatory for `bot_read` and `teacher`: an expired token is refused like a wrong one and the bot asks the operator for a new one. The CLI refuses a server of another contract (`E-CONTRACT`, «rebuild the CLI»); the release build is copied to the bot's machine by hand (D-328); nothing tells the bot what changed in the software.
- **Operator (2026-11-14):** «il token api si autoaggiorni e non scada» while the bot uses it; and the API must tell the bot what changed in the software, so that the bot can update itself on its own.
- **We do:**
  1. **Renewal on use.** A new append-only table `api_token_renewals` (`api_token_id`, `expires_at`, `created_at`; the UPDATE and DELETE triggers; a check that a renewal lies in the future of its row). A token's effective expiry is the latest of its own `expires_at` and its renewals' (`ApiToken#effective_expires_at`); every reader uses it: `Banco::TokenAuth` (through `ApiToken.lookup`), `ApiToken#expired?`, `banco:token:list`, `GET /api/v1/token`. A `bot_read` or `teacher` token whose request passed authentication and the scope checks of `Api::BaseController` (the edge's roles, the teacher list, the method) records a renewal, even if the action then answers 404 or 422, when less than its lifetime minus one day is left (half its lifetime for a one-day token, which would otherwise never renew): new expiry = now + the lifetime, the lifetime being its original `expires_at - created_at` in whole days, at least 1 (`ApiToken#renew_on_use!`). So at most about one row a day; a token used at least once per lifetime never expires, and an idle one still dies. An expired token is never renewed (no resurrection), nor a revoked one, nor a content role's (`agent_claude`, `agent_omp`, `ci` keep the expiry they were issued with), nor a request refused by those checks. A renewal that fails (a database error) is logged and the request goes on. Two concurrent requests may both write a row: the later expiry wins, harmless. `api_tokens` itself is never updated.
  2. **`GET /api/v1/token`** (any token role): `{public_id, role, teacher, label, created_at, expires_at (effective), renews_on_use, lifetime_days, revoked: false}`, never the secret; `banco token`.
  3. **What changed.** `GET /api/v1/updates[?since=D-NNN]` (any token role): `{server: {commit (BANCO_GIT_SHA), built_at}, contract_digest (the X-Banco-Contract digest), cli: {version, files: [{name, os, arch, sha256, size}]}, docs: [{name, sha256}] for bot and api, changes: the rows of this index after since, oldest first}` (`Updates`). The CLI build is read from the image's `dist/SHA256SUMS` and `dist/build.json` (an empty list and null version where there is none, as in development). `GET /api/v1/docs/:name` serves `bot` (`docs/bot.md`) and `api` (`docs/api.md`) only, as `{name, sha256, text}`. `GET /api/v1/cli/:file` streams a binary named in `dist/SHA256SUMS` (the allowlist; no path is built from the request) with its sha256 in `X-Banco-Sha256`; anything else is 404. All `Cache-Control: no-store`; through the edge, as every route, only `bot_read` and `teacher`.
  4. **The CLI updates itself.** `banco self-update [--check]` compares its version and embedded contract digest with `/updates` (equal or not: commits are not ordered), refuses a listed size over 100 MB before downloading, streams the build for its `GOOS`/`GOARCH` into a temporary file beside its executable (read to at most the listed size plus one byte) checking size and sha256 as it writes (`E-SELF-UPDATE`, nothing replaced, when they differ), gives the file the old program's mode and renames it over itself; on Windows it stages `banco.new.exe` and reports `staged: true, updated: false`; `--check` only reports. `banco changes [--since D-NNN]` and `banco docs show bot|api`. These three and `banco token` work when the CLI's contract differs from the server's (exempt from the `E-CONTRACT` refusal); `E-CONTRACT`'s `next` is now `banco self-update`. The HTTPS rule is unchanged (no `http://` off loopback), and no request of the CLI follows a redirect (Go would forward `Authorization` to the same host on another scheme or port).
  5. **The image carries the build.** A Dockerfile stage `cli` from the official golang image (`GO_VERSION` 1.27.4, the Go of `go.mod`) copies `go.mod`, `cli/`, `contract/` and `bin/build-cli-dist` and builds the six binaries, `SHA256SUMS` and `build.json`, the version stamped from `ARG GIT_SHA` (the stage has no `.git`; `bin/build-cli-dist` takes `GIT_SHA`; the production build passes `--build-arg GIT_SHA=$(git rev-parse HEAD)`); the final image has it at `/rails/dist`, owned by root and read-only, so the app user cannot rewrite a binary or `SHA256SUMS`, and `/api/v1/cli/:file` serves only a regular file inside `dist/`, never a symlink. `.dockerignore` lets `cli/` into the context (the Rails build stage removes it) and the three docs the API reads (`docs/bot.md`, `docs/api.md`, `docs/decisions.md`), and keeps a local `dist/` out.
  6. **Docs.** `docs/api.md` «Staying current» (the renewal, the four routes, the loop: at start `banco self-update --check`; on `E-CONTRACT` or a new commit `banco self-update`, then `banco changes --since <last seen>` and `banco docs show bot` again); `docs/bot.md` «Staying current» and its rule 7.
- **Why:** A bot that runs for months should not stop because a date passed while it was working, nor because the server moved on: the operator wants it to keep going without a hand on its machine. The renewal keeps the expiry's point (an abandoned token still dies within its lifetime) and costs one row a day; serving the image's own build keeps the CLI and the server of one commit together, and the decisions index is already the one list of what changed.
- **Cost:** One migration and table, one more query per API request (the latest renewal), a row a day per token in use. Four routes, four commands (the contract digest changes once). The image build gains a Go stage (the CLI's tests run in it) and six stripped binaries in `/rails/dist`.
- **Risk (named):** a leaked public token never expires while it is used: whoever holds it keeps it alive by using it. The answer is revocation: `bin/rails banco:token:revoke ID=<public id>` (or, for a teacher token, removing the login from `BANCO_TEACHER_USERS`); renewal stops for a revoked token and for an idle one. The binaries are served over the same HTTPS host and checked against the sha256 list that the same server sends: this protects against a broken download, not against a compromised server.
- **Not done:** no signature of the binaries beyond the sha256 list; no automatic restart of the bot after an update; no renewal for the content roles; no limit on the total life of a token in use (the operator chose «non scada»).
- **Status:** implemented; production gets it at the next image build and deploy (the operator's).
- **Back-port:** D-327 (a public token's expiry is now a lifetime without use), D-328 (the release build is in the image and the CLI updates itself), `AGENTS.md` (layout line).
- **Tests:** `test/integration/public_api_updates_test.rb` (renewal once a day to now + lifetime, the one-day token, content roles, expired, revoked and refused requests, a failing renewal, append-only renewals, `banco:token:list`; `/token`; `/updates` with and without a build and `since`; the `/docs` and `/cli` allowlists, symlinks, directories and traversal attempts; the edge), `test/models/append_only_test.rb` (the new table, through `test/support/ledger_rows.rb`), `test/lib/toolchain_test.rb` (the Go stage, `dist/` root-owned), `cli/cmd_update_test.go` (atomic replace keeping the mode, sha mismatch refused with nothing replaced, a download read to at most size + 1, the 100 MB cap, `--check`, the Windows staging, the exemption from `E-CONTRACT`, redirects never followed, usage errors, the HTTPS rule), `cli/main_test.go` (`E-CONTRACT`'s `next`).

## D-331 · 2026-11-15 · a narrow lesson table keeps its grid on a phone

- **Design ref:** D-310 (a table's rows stack under 600 px, each cell with its column's name), A8 (the `table` figure), `render_host.js` (`E-LESSON-OVERFLOW`).
- **Design said:** every lesson/2 table stacks its rows into separate boxes under 600 px.
- **We do:** `tableNode` (`blocks/table.js`) estimates a table's width with the pure `keepsGrid`: each column's longest cell, header included, as plain text without its markup (`plainText`: a language span or a role as its words, a formula as its text, bold as its words), at 9 px a character plus 26 px of padding and border a cell. A table of at most 5 columns and at most 280 px (the lesson's box is about 295 px at a 390 px viewport) gets the class `dg-keep` beside `dg-table`; `lesson.css` stacks only `.dg-table:not(.dg-keep)`, so a kept table keeps its head and hides its cell labels on a phone. A wider table still stacks, with D-310's cell labels; a misestimated one that overflows its box is still caught by the render check's `E-LESSON-OVERFLOW`.
- **Why:** a reviewer flagged a biology lesson as a major: a Punnett square, a 2×2 truth table or a short conjugation table read as stacked boxes is unreadable, since the grid itself is what the student reads.
- **Cost:** a width estimate that is not a measurement (a font change can move a table across the line); the render check is the net.
- **Status:** implemented
- **Back-port:** D-310 (only a table wider than a phone stacks).
- **Tests:** `app/javascript/lesson/test/table_keep.test.mjs` (a Punnett square, two columns of Spanish forms and a 3×3 table of numbers kept; four columns of sentences and six columns of digits stacked; `[[en:chemist's]]` counted as 9 characters).

## D-332 · 2026-11-15 · view links: a temporary URL opens the teacher's pages read-only, without login

- **Design ref:** firm rule 2 (decisions are the teacher's), D-217 (the guest role reads and writes nothing), D-327 (the public API, `bot_read` is GET-only), D-328 (the teacher's pages over the API), D-330 (a token's ledger rows are append-only), firm rule 4 (the ledger is append-only), `Banco::EdgeTrust`, `Banco::Listeners`.
- **Design said:** D-217: the teacher's pages are read by the teacher and, read-only, by a guest, both identified by the edge's login (`Remote-User`, `Remote-Groups`, trusted only from the edge proxy on the web listener). The bot reads the same facts over the API as JSON (D-328), but the user who works with the bot has no way to look at a page without a login. `bot_read` never writes (D-327).
- **Operator (2026-11-15):** a way, over the CLI and the API, to generate temporary URLs so that the bot and the user who uses it can browse the site and see what they want without logging in or any other step.
- **We do:**
  1. **A bearer URL for the guest, nothing wider.** A view link opens the teacher's pages (every teacher GET) as the **guest** role of D-217: it reads, it writes nothing, it never previews and never decides; never the teacher identity, never the student's pages, never `/teacher/preview`. `Identity#guest?` is true for it and `teacher?` and `student?` never are, so every page that already hides a form, «Esci» and a button from a guest does it for a view session.
  2. **A separate listener, so `Remote-*` is never read there (fail closed).** A fifth Puma listener `view` (`VIEW_PORT`, default 3400, never `PORT`; `Banco::Listeners`, `ListenerSwitch` sends it to Rails, `ListenerTag`). On it `EdgeTrust` never reads `Remote-User` or `Remote-Groups`: a Traefik misconfiguration, a missing middleware or a forged header can never turn into teacher access. Identity there comes only from an encrypted cookie (`banco_view`, host-only, `httponly`, `secure` in production, `same_site: :lax`, expiring with the link) set when a link is redeemed, and **re-checked against the ledger on every request**: `ViewLinks.active(id)` (not revoked, `expires_at` in the future, flag on). The listener answers only GET and HEAD (any other method is 403 with the designed `shared/error` page) and only to requests whose TCP peer is the edge proxy (`Banco::EdgeProxy`; anything else is 404). `edge_trusted?` stays web-only. The teacher's GET routes (the pages, `page-posters/:sha`, `assets/items/:sha256.svg`, `teacher/lesson-revisions/:id/full.json`) sit under a constraint for `web` or `view` (`Banco::ListenerConstraint` takes several names); every POST, every student route and `/teacher/preview` stay web-only.
  3. **The URL is the credential.** `POST /api/v1/view-links {path, minutes}` returns `<BANCO_VIEW_URL>/v?view_token=<token>`; the token is `SecureRandom.urlsafe_base64(32)` and only its SHA-256 is stored (`token_digest`), so the URL is shown once and a lost one is replaced, never recovered. `path` (default `/teacher`) must be a teacher path (`ViewLinks::PATH_FORMAT`, at most 300 characters, never `/teacher/preview`) and is **only the landing page, not a scope**; `minutes` is an integer from 5 to 1440 (default 60). At most 20 active links per API token. `GET /v` (`ViewLinksController#redeem`) sets the cookie, answers 303 to the link's path with `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` and `Cache-Control: no-store`, and appends a redemption row; a `HEAD` on `/v` redeems nothing (link unfurlers), a `GET` does; an unknown, expired, revoked or disabled link is the same 410 with a designed page («Il link è scaduto o non è valido. Chiedi un link nuovo.»), so a caller cannot tell them apart. `view_token` is filtered from the log (`filter_parameter_logging`). A link may be redeemed any number of times until it expires (a second device, the user pasting it again).
  4. **The ledger is append-only (firm rule 4).** Three tables with the UPDATE and DELETE triggers (`Banco::AppendOnly.install`): `view_links` (`api_token_id`, `token_digest` unique, `path`, `expires_at`, `created_at`; check `expires_at > created_at`), `view_link_redemptions` (one row per redemption, no address: the peer is the proxy) and `view_link_revocations` (one per link). The state is derived: active = not revoked, not expired, flag on, **and the minting token still valid**. `POST /api/v1/view-links/:id/revoke` appends the revocation (idempotent) and ends the session of every browser holding that link on its next request. A link dies with the token that minted it: revoking the token, its effective expiry (D-330), or removing a `teacher` token's teacher from `BANCO_TEACHER_USERS` ends its links and their open sessions at the next request. `GET /api/v1/view-links` lists the token's newest 100 links.
  5. **The kill switch.** The feature needs `BANCO_VIEW_LINKS_ENABLED=1` and `BANCO_VIEW_URL` (an https origin; http only in test and development; never the web host `banco.scc.im`: that turns the feature off). Otherwise creation answers `E-VIEW-DISABLED` (503) and the view listener answers 404 to everything: **turning the flag off ends every open view session at once**, since each request re-reads it.
  6. **The `bot_read` exception: `reader_grants`.** `bot_read` is GET-only (D-327). `Api::BaseController` gains the class attribute `reader_grants` (default false); `Api::V1::ViewLinksController` sets it, so `bot_read` and `teacher` may POST there. The write only grants reading, never wider than what the token reads through the API anyway (D-328 reads the same pages as JSON), and decides nothing. It is not a dry run: creation is immediate (there is nothing to confirm). The content roles stay 403 (`token_role`), and the token renews on use as for any other request (D-330).
  7. **The host.** There is no DNS name for it yet: Traefik routes the non-`/api/` paths of `api.banco.scc.im` to the view listener with two routers: `banco-view` (`Host(api.banco.scc.im) && !PathPrefix(/api/)`: the `Remote-*` headers stripped, a rate limit sized for page loads, `sec-headers`, no Authelia) and `banco-view-redeem` (`Host(api.banco.scc.im) && Path(/v)`) with access logs off (`observability.accesslogs=false`), so the token in the query never reaches Traefik's access log; Rails filters `view_token` in its own log. Static files (`/assets`, `/vendor`) were already answered on that host by every listener: nothing new is public. `BANCO_VIEW_URL` is the one place that names the host, so a dedicated name moves it with one setting; `Banco::Hosts` lets the API host on `:view` too and refuses the web host `banco.scc.im` there (the API host is still never on `:web`).
  8. **What a view session cannot do.** POST anything (403, whatever the page); open `/teacher/preview` or any student page (403 without a session, and the routes are web-only); record a decision or a comment action, or reply to a comment; write an event: a view session records nothing but its redemption row (no `teacher_viewed_topic`, no `teacher_saw_exercise`, no minutes), so the approval gate's «page opened» and «exercises seen» stay the teacher's.
  9. **Docs and tools.** `docs/api.md` «View links», `docs/bot.md` «Giving the user a link», `AGENTS.md`. CLI `banco view-link new [--path P] [--minutes N]`, `list`, `revoke ID` (`cli/cmd_view_link.go`; not a dry-run command: no `--confirm`); error codes `E-VIEW-DISABLED`, `E-VIEW-PATH`, `E-VIEW-LIMIT` in `config/banco/error_codes.yml`.
- **Why firm rule 2 holds:** a view link never decides. It grants the guest role (D-217), which has no form and no decision route; the decisions' doors are still the teacher in the browser behind the login (web listener), the console (D-260) and a `teacher` token over the API (D-327). The new listener answers GET and HEAD only and its identity can never be the teacher's, so no path through it can reach a recorder. That is why the text of rule 2 is unchanged.
- **Why:** The user of the bot wants to look at the teacher's pages, with their layout and figures, which the JSON of D-328 does not give, and without a login. A bearer link for the guest costs the operator nothing at the edge (no new identity provider), reads nothing that a `bot_read` token does not read, and dies by itself (a TTL of at most a day), by a revocation row, or by the flag. Keeping it on its own listener means that the only code path that trusts a header is still the web listener, and the link can never carry more than the guest.
- **Cost:** Three tables, one migration, a listener and its port (the unit file and the Traefik router are the operator's); the teacher's GET routes move under a shared constraint; one class attribute on `Api::BaseController`; three commands (the contract digest changes once); one more query per page on the view listener (the link). The view host shares `api.banco.scc.im` until a DNS name exists.
- **Risk (named):** a link is a bearer, and **`path` is only where the user lands, not a scope**: whoever holds the URL opens the whole read-only teacher site, every page a guest reads, including the corrections and reports with the student's typed answers, the student's progress and the reviewers' opinions, until the link expires, is revoked, or its token dies. The answer is the short TTL (5 to 1440 minutes, 60 by default), the limit of 20 active links per token, the one-way digest in the database, `no-referrer` and `no-store`, the log filter on `view_token` (and no Traefik access log on the redeem route), revocation (`banco view-link revoke ID`), the death of a link with its token, and the flag. The cookie is host-only (no `domain:`), so it never reaches another host. A chat app that unfurls the URL with a GET redeems it and may show the page title in its preview. The bot sends a link only to the user who asked, never to a group or a third party.
- **Not done:** no scope narrower than the whole teacher site (`path` is a landing page); no link to a student's page or to the preview; no write over a view session; no per-redemption address (the peer is Traefik); no listing of the url (the raw token is not stored); no separate DNS name yet.
- **Status:** implemented and live since 2026-11-15 (359f38c): Traefik routers `banco-view` and `banco-view-redeem`, `VIEW_PORT=3400`, `BANCO_VIEW_URL=https://api.banco.scc.im`, `BANCO_VIEW_LINKS_ENABLED=1`. The redeem router carries its own headers middleware (`referrerPolicy=no-referrer`, HSTS, nosniff) instead of `sec-headers`, whose `strict-origin-when-cross-origin` replaced the app's `no-referrer` on the redirect that carries the token (seen in the first smoke).
- **Back-port:** D-327 (`bot_read` may POST where a controller sets `reader_grants`), D-217 (a view link identity is a guest), `AGENTS.md` (ports and layout line). Firm rule 2: unchanged.
- **Tests:** `test/integration/view_links_api_test.rb` (the three endpoints, the roles, the errors, the limit, `reader_grants`, the append-only rows), `test/integration/view_listener_test.rb` (redeem and the cookie, expiry, revocation and the flag ending a session, GET/HEAD only, the peer, `Remote-*` ignored, no preview or student page, no event recorded, the log filter), `test/models/view_links_test.rb` (`ViewLinks`: the path rule, the minutes, the digest, the limit, `redeem`, `active`, `revoke!`), `test/models/append_only_test.rb` (the three tables, through `test/support/ledger_rows.rb`), `cli/cmd_view_link_test.go`.

## D-333 · 2026-11-15 · the bot's commands: a decision's text, next, digest, revoke --all; the public reads need no token

- **Design ref:** D-327 (the public API and its token roles), D-328 (the teacher's pages and the progress over the API), D-330 (`banco changes`, `docs show`, `self-update`, `token`; the decisions index as the list of what changed), D-332 (view links), firm rule 2 (decisions are the teacher's).
- **Design said:** D-330: `banco changes` lists the index rows of `docs/decisions.md` (number, date, title, status) and nothing more; `/updates`, `/docs/:name` and `/cli/:file` need any token of the two public roles, so a machine with no token cannot even start `banco self-update`. D-328: the bot reads the teacher's pages and the progress one request at a time; no command says what the student should do next. D-332: a link is revoked one by one. `banco token` shows the expiry and says nothing when it is near.
- **Operator (2026-11-15):** the operator's bot asked for «un comando che mostra il testo intero di una decisione, perché `changes` dà solo il titolo; un `banco next` con il prossimo argomento per materia, minuti e abilità da recuperare; un `banco digest` con cruscotto, commenti, risposte in attesa e progressi in un colpo solo; un `view-link revoke --all`; rendere `changes`, `docs show` e `self-update --check` usabili senza token, visto che non mostrano dati dello studente; un avviso in `banco token` quando mancano meno di 7 giorni alla scadenza». It also found that `self-update` could not start on a machine with no token.
- **We do:**
  1. **A decision's whole text.** `GET /api/v1/updates/decisions/:number` (`D-332` or `332`) answers `{number, date, title, status, text}`: `text` is the section of `docs/decisions.md` from its `## D-NNN · …` heading up to the next `## D-` heading or the end of the file; an unknown number is `404 E-NOT-FOUND`, field `number`. `Updates` parses the same file as for the index; the parsed index, the sections and the docs' sha256 are memoized per file, keyed on its mtime and size (a new version of the file is parsed again), so a request costs a hash lookup. CLI: `banco changes show NUMBER` prints the JSON, `--text` only the markdown.
  2. **No token for what is public.** `GET /api/v1/updates`, `GET /api/v1/updates/decisions/:number`, `GET /api/v1/docs/:name` and `GET /api/v1/cli/:file` never read `Authorization`: they serve the public repository's own content (the decisions index and text, the two docs, the CLI binaries) and no student's data, and `X-Banco-Contract` is still sent. The answers are the same as before. `banco changes`, `changes show`, `docs show` and `self-update` (with and without `--check`) neither need nor send a token; every other command, and `GET /api/v1/token`, still needs one. This ends the case of D-330 where a machine with no token could not update its CLI.
  3. **`banco token` warns.** `GET /api/v1/token` gains `expires_in_days` (whole days from now to the effective expiry, D-330) and `expiring_soon` (true under 7 days). When `expiring_soon` is true the CLI also writes one line to stderr: `warning: this token expires in N days (YYYY-MM-DD); ask the operator for a new one`, or, for a token that renews on use, that using it renews it.
  4. **`banco view-link revoke --all`.** `POST /api/v1/view-links/revoke-all` appends a revocation for every **active** link of this token and answers `{revoked: [ids], count}` (`{"revoked": [], "count": 0}` when there is none); another token's links are never touched. It is a `reader_grants` write like the others (D-332): it only ends reading. `banco view-link revoke` takes exactly one of `ID` or `--all`.
  5. **`banco next [--student KEY] [--subject S]`.** `GET /api/v1/students/:key/next[?subject=S]`: for each subject (or the one asked) `next` (Oggi's own pick: the topic the student left, else the first of Oggi's ranked suggestions, with `topic`, `title_it`, `kind`, `minutes`, `term`, `why_it`; `null` for a subject whose course the teacher withdrew), `skills_to_recover` (`skill`, `label_it`, `taught_in`) and `done_it`. It is `Course::StudentNext` over the read models of the pages and adds **no rule**: it never proposes a topic outside the programme, and the skills are the ones the pages call «Da riprendere».
  6. **`banco digest [--student KEY]`.** `GET /api/v1/digest?student=KEY` (default `student`) answers in one request `{generated_at, home, progress, next, comments: {open, unread, latest}, answers_pending: {count, rows}, activity}`: `home`, `progress` and `next` are exactly the JSON of `teacher/home`, `students/KEY/progress` and `students/KEY/next`; `latest` and `rows` are up to 5 rows as `comments` and `answers/pending` list them; `activity` is the 15 latest rows of D-334's feed. It calls the builders of the existing endpoints: there is no second query logic.
  7. **Docs.** `docs/api.md` (the public routes, `changes show`, the token's warning, `revoke --all`, «Next and digest», «Who did what»), `docs/bot.md`, `AGENTS.md`. The contract (`contract/commands.json`) gains the new commands; its digest changes once.
- **Why:** The bot reads `changes` to learn what changed and then needs the decision itself, not its title; `next` and `digest` replace five or six requests that every session starts with, and the edge allows three in flight (`docs/bot.md` rule 5). The three public reads hold nothing the repository does not publish, and a bot that cannot update itself without a token cannot be given the token that fixes its CLI; the warning gives the operator a week to issue a new token before the bot stops. Nothing here decides: the new routes read, and the one write (`revoke-all`) only ends reading.
- **Cost:** Six routes and six commands (the contract digest changes once); `Updates` reads decision sections; one more builder shared by the digest and the endpoints it repeats. The public routes carry no authentication, so only the edge's rate limit stands in front of them.
- **Risk (named):** anyone who reaches `api.banco.scc.im` can read the server's commit, the contract digest, the decisions index and text, the two docs and the CLI build; this is the public repository's content and the commit is a fingerprint of the running version, no more. `next` and `digest` show a student's progress to a `bot_read` or `teacher` token, which already reads it (D-328).
- **Not done:** `banco token` and every other read still need a token; no new rule of the course (what comes next is what the student's pages already propose); no write other than `revoke-all`.
- **Status:** implemented.
- **Back-port:** D-330 (`/updates`, `/docs/:name` and `/cli/:file` no longer need a token; `/updates` gains the decision's text; `GET /api/v1/token` gains the expiry warning), D-332 (`revoke --all`), `docs/api.md`, `docs/bot.md`, `AGENTS.md` (layout line).
- **Tests:** `test/integration/public_api_updates_test.rb` (the public routes without and with a bad `Authorization`, the decision's text, an unknown number, `expires_in_days` and `expiring_soon`), `test/integration/view_links_api_test.rb` (`revoke-all`: this token's active links only, none, the roles), the tests of `next` and `digest`, `cli/*_test.go` (the tokenless commands send no `Authorization`, the stderr warning, `view-link revoke` ID or `--all`, `next`, `digest`, `activity`).

## D-334 · 2026-11-15 · several teachers and bots on the same students: who did what is recorded and shown to the others

- **Design ref:** firm rule 2 (decisions are the teacher's), firm rule 4 (the ledger is append-only), D-05 (agent tokens), D-08 (the decisions' guards), D-304 (comments), D-327 (the `teacher` token carries a login; decisions and comment actions over the API record their token), D-330 (a token's lifetime), D-332 (view links record their token).
- **Design said:** D-327: a `teacher` token acts as the login stored on it, and every write records its origin (web, console, api with the token's public id). Nothing put the records of the people together: a teacher saw her own work and had to ask the ledger, or the operator, what another teacher or another bot had done.
- **Operator (2026-11-15):** a second bot, run by another person (a second teacher, already on `BANCO_TEACHER_USERS`, her teacher token issued) works on the same students, and later three or four teachers and bots will. «Quello che fanno dovrebbe essere registrato con chi lo ha fatto e visibile all'altro.»
- **We do:**
  1. **One token per person and per bot.** Each teacher and each bot has its own `teacher` token (`bin/rails banco:token:issue ROLE=teacher TEACHER=<login> LABEL=…`): the role carries `teacher_login`, the label names the bot (for example `teacher2-bot-example`), and the token's `public_id` (the 8 characters after `bnc_`, not a secret) tells two tokens of one teacher apart. Tokens are never shared: a shared token would make two actors one. A `bot_read` token is named in the feed as `bot_read:<label>`.
  2. **Every write records who and how.** The ledger already says it, and nothing is rewritten: a decision has `teacher_login` and its `via` (`web`, `console`, `api`; an API decision names its token, D-327); a comment action has its actor, its origin (`web`, `console`, `api`, `student`) and, for the API, its token; a view link and its revocation name the token that made them (D-332). Where one of these facts is missing for an action, the gap is named under «Not done» below.
  3. **The activity feed.** The read model `Activity` (`Activity.recent(since:, actor:, limit:)`) joins those records into one list, newest first: `{at, actor: {login, via, token: {public_id, label} | null, os_user}, kind, summary_it, ref}` (`os_user` is the host account of a console row, from the decision's `user_agent` or the comment event's payload, `null` otherwise), with `kind` `decision`, `comment_reply`, `comment_resolve`, `comment_reopen`, `comment_read`, `view_link_created`, `view_link_revoked`. The summary is a short Italian line: never the student's text, never the text of a reply. It reads the ledger and writes nothing. Three doors: the API `GET /api/v1/activity[?since=ISO8601][&actor=LOGIN][&limit=N]` (`bot_read` and `teacher`) returning `{rows, actors}`; the CLI `banco activity [--since DATE|ISO] [--actor LOGIN] [--limit N]`; the teacher's page `/teacher/activity`, «Chi ha fatto che cosa» (read-only, Quando / Chi / Come / Che cosa; for teachers only: a guest and a view link get 403 and no menu entry, because the page names the teachers' logins and the bots' labels; the bots read the same rows over the API), linked from the teacher menu. The digest of D-333 carries the 15 latest rows.
  4. **The existing outputs name the actor.** `GET /api/v1/decisions` rows have `teacher`, `via` and `token`; the events of `GET /api/v1/comments/:id` have `actor`, `origin` and `token`; the digest and the feed repeat them.
  5. **Working together.** `docs/bot.md` «Working with other teachers and bots»: before acting on a comment or a decision another may have handled, read `banco activity` (or `banco digest`); a bot's actions show its token's label.
- **Why firm rule 2 holds:** each teacher decides as herself: a decision, a reply or a resolution is recorded under the login of the token that made it and under no other, and a bot never decides as a teacher whose token it does not hold. The feed only reads. Nothing new decides, and the guards, the flag `BANCO_DECISIONS_ENABLED` and `BANCO_TEACHER_USERS` are unchanged. That is why the text of rule 2 is unchanged.
- **Why:** With one teacher the ledger was her own diary; with several, two people can answer the same comment or approve the same topic without knowing. The facts were already in the ledger: what was missing was one place where they are put together, readable by the bot as JSON and by the teacher as a page.
- **Cost:** A read model, an endpoint, a command, a page and a menu entry; no table, no migration, no new row. The feed reads several tables per request (a window of at most 200 rows). The contract digest changes once (with D-333).
- **Risk (named):** the feed shows teachers what other teachers did, with their logins and their bots' labels; the page is for teachers only (a guest and a view link get 403), so a login is not shown to a bearer-URL reader, and the API feed needs a `bot_read` or `teacher` token. The summary holds no student text. Concurrent work is shown, not prevented: two teachers can still answer the same comment, and both replies are recorded and delivered.
- **Not done:** no lock, no «taken by» mark and no notice to the other teacher; no per-teacher filter of what a teacher sees; no change of an old row to add a missing fact. Nothing new is recorded unless the feed's slice finds a gap. Gaps found: a console comment action (`banco:comments:*`) recorded the teacher login but not the host OS user, while a console decision keeps it in its `user_agent` (`banco:decide <os_user>`). Now recorded: `Comments::Responder` writes `os_user` into the `payload_json` of a new console comment event (no migration, no old row touched), and the feed shows it as `actor.os_user` for console rows (a decision from its `user_agent`, a comment event from its payload; `null` for web and api rows and for old console comment events). No gap in the others: a view-link revocation always has a token (there is no console path that revokes a link), and `sent_back` events are the system's, not a teacher's action, so they are not in the feed.
- **Status:** implemented.
- **Back-port:** D-327 (several `teacher` tokens, one per person and bot), D-332 (a link's token appears in the feed), `docs/api.md` «Who did what», `docs/bot.md` «Working with other teachers and bots», `AGENTS.md` (layout line). Firm rule 2: unchanged.
- **Tests:** `test/models/activity_test.rb` (the sources, the order, the filter, the limit, no student text in a summary, read-only), `test/integration/activity_api_test.rb` (`GET /api/v1/activity`: the roles, `since`, `actor`, `limit`, a bad value), the controller test of `/teacher/activity` (the teacher reads it; a guest and a view link get 403 and no menu entry), `cli/*_test.go` (`banco activity`).

## D-335 · 2026-11-15 · student-facing fixes found by the wave 13 reviews

- **Design ref:** D-282 (the text layer: `\ce{}` and `\pu{}` through KaTeX's mhchem), D-310 (markup wherever it is written; the inline typed answer), the lesson/2 blocks `example`, `try` and `check` and the diagram types, the grading vectors (`test/fixtures/grading/vectors.json`), firm rule 4 (the ledger is append-only: a recorded grade is never rewritten).
- **Design said:** the worked example counted «passo N di M» over the steps the page served; a single `number` or `fraction` check of «Prova tu» with `input_before` kept its prompt for the screen reader only (`quietPrompt`); the palette gave `.st-ROLE` and `.mk-ROLE` only to a role with a mark colour; `items/markup.js` rendered a formula with KaTeX without mhchem; the expression grader's text mode read letters as variables; no check told a lesson's author that a hidden step gives a datum the student cannot know.
- **Operator (2026-11-15):** the wave 13 reviews, which look at the lessons and items as the student sees them, reported six things the student sees wrong. They are rendering and grading-input fixes; none changes a course rule.
- **We do:**
  1. **The example's counter.** `Lessons::StudentBody` sends `steps_total`, the example's whole number of steps (a count only: the steps after a blank stay unserved; `test/fixtures/lesson2/whitelist.json` lists the field), and `lesson/blocks/example.js` shows `max(steps_total, steps served)` as M. Before, «passo 1 di 2» grew as the student answered a blank step.
  2. **«Prova tu» shows its question.** A single number or fraction check with `input_before` hid its `prompt_it` (`sr-only`, the `quietPrompt` option of `lesson/blocks/check.js`, passed by `lesson/blocks/try.js`): the student saw «2p =» and no «perimetro». The prompt is always drawn; the text around the box only labels the box. `quietPrompt` is removed.
  3. **A tint-only role is drawn.** A role with only a tint (`highlight`) had no `.st-` or `.mk-` class, so a highlighted segment, line or point was invisible in every diagram type. `bin/build-palette` now emits `.st-ROLE` (a marker-pen stroke: the tint darkened toward the text colour, 8 px, round) and `.mk-ROLE` (tint fill, text-colour outline) for such a role (`lesson_roles.css`); `lesson/diagrams/cartesian.js` draws it as a wide tint band (`dg-halo`, `fl-ROLE`) under ink in the text colour (`lesson.css`: `.dg-halo`, `.dg-halo-dot`, `.dg-ink`).
  4. **Chemistry in items.** `\ce{}` and `\pu{}` in an item's formula showed as red errors in practice, the entry test and the teacher's item pages. `items/markup.js` loads KaTeX's mhchem on demand (`ensureChem()`) when a formula needs it, shows plain text for the moment (never an error) and redraws when it arrives; a draw that changed meanwhile is not overwritten.
  5. **The grader reads `pi`.** In the expression grader's text mode (the fallback box and the blind solves) the typed word `pi` was read as p·i. `grader/checker.mjs` maps the standalone word `pi` to `\pi`, as it does `rad` and `sqrt`: case-sensitive, never inside a longer word (`pipe`, `spin`) or after a backslash; `p*i` stays the variables p and i. New grading vectors cover it, and `hasTypedWords` still says «no» for these forms.
  6. **`W-BLANK-STEP-DATUM`.** A warning (`config/banco/error_codes.yml`, version 28): the `do_it` of an example's blank step is never shown before the answer, so a number or a cell reference that only that `do_it` gives («Scrivi 8 in B3.») is a datum the student cannot know. `Lessons::Blocks::Example.blank_data`, called per card by `Validation::Lesson2Checks`, compares the numbers and cell references of that `do_it` with everything visible before the question (the card's title and earlier blocks, the problem, the earlier steps, the step's own `why_it` and question); the blank's own answer, and what sits in a formula or a span, are exempt. The lesson brief (`briefs/lesson.md`) says so.
  7. **A render that only timed out is drawn once more.** Under load a lesson render failed on its 90 s limit and the author had to resubmit, which put another job behind the single Chrome. `Validation::LessonRenderRunner::Result#timeout_only?` says a failed render has no error but `E-LESSON-RENDER` with a message that starts `timeout:` (the budget of the revision, a card, or the print check); `Validation::LessonRenderCheck#call` then draws the revision once more, in the same job and under a fresh Chrome session (the lock is taken again, so a job queued meanwhile goes first), and records the second answer. The lesson_renders row says how many draws it took (`render_attempts` in `result_json`; the `attempt` column stays the job's execution number, which is about Chrome being unreachable) and the first failure is logged. A content error (overflow, layout, exception) is never drawn again.
  8. **`E-ACCEPT-IS-ERROR`.** An error (registry version 30): a `normalized_text` lesson/2 check (`Lessons::Blocks::Check.text`) or item instance (`Validation::InstanceChecks#accept_is_error`; the item's `accept` and the instance's) whose `accept` holds a text that is also one of its declared error values. The grader tries the key and `accept` before the errors, so the wrong answer was graded right and the error never fired (lesson revision 1151, exercise 6: «no salimos como llovía» in both). The two texts are compared as the grader reads them (`Grading::Closed::Text.same_answer?`: its normalisation, the direction of an accent, and the same contraction in an English check), not as written. The three briefs that teach `accept` say so (`briefs/lesson.md`, `diagnosis-item.md`, `practice-item.md`).
  9. **The `is-split` order is the rule.** A card whose blocks are exactly one `text` and one `diagram` or `schema` draws the figure first at every width (`cards.js`: the class `is-split`; `lesson.css`: `.card-body.is-split > .block-diagram { order: -1 }`), since the first renderer (D-258's picture first). The reviewers of wave 14 saw it as a bug (lessons 1040, 1079, cards 4 and 6); the approved lessons were reviewed as drawn, so it stays, and D-310's «not in this round: a card with one text block and one figure shows the figure first on a phone» is read as: already so, on every width. The brief says it now (`briefs/lesson.md`: write the text so that it reads after the picture), and a node test fixes it.
  10. **An ordered list keeps its first number.** A lesson text whose first line starts «N. » is an ordered list that begins at N: the markup v2 block of an `ol` has `start: N` when N is not 1 (`items/markup_parser.js`, mirrored by `Lessons::Markup.block_json`; the shared cases in `test/fixtures/markup/v2.json`), and `lesson/text.js` (and `items/markup.js` for v2 lists) draws `<ol start=N>`. A table whose cells read «1. Sillabe», «2. Sinalefe», «3. Parola finale», «4. Nome» is a one-item list in every cell and drew every cell as «1.» (lesson revision 1080, card 13, on a phone). The cells hold markup wherever it is written (D-310), so the cell stays a list; only the number is kept. Markup v1 (items) is unchanged: an item's list still counts from 1.
  11. **Figure files are per revision, and the printed checksum is the file's.** `banco solve open REV` and `banco review open REV` wrote `figure-N.png` straight into `--dir`, so two revisions opened into one folder overwrote each other's figures (and the clean-up of stale `figure-*.png` deleted the other's). The files now go to `DIR/REV/figure-N.png` (`--dir DIR` is the parent; the default `banco-figures` gives the same `banco-figures/REV/` as before); only that revision's folder is cleared; `figures_dir` and each figure's `path` are the real ones. The `sha256` the server sends is the digest of the *source SVG* (the key of the PNG cache, D-320), not of the PNG; the API and `Review::Figures` are unchanged, and the CLI prints `sha256` as the sha256 of the written PNG file (equal to `sha256sum FILE`) and keeps the server's value as `source_sha256`. Briefs say `DIR/REV/`.
  12. **The render shots wait for the icons.** The reviewers of lesson revisions 1167 (cards 1 and 2 and the finch diagram) and 1133 (card 1) saw empty squares for the card badges and the diagram icons in the 390 px shots, while the same cards at 1280 px showed them. It was timing in the render host, not a bug at narrow width (no rule under 600 px hides or zeroes an icon, and a student's phone fetches the sprite and draws the icon when it arrives): an icon is a `<use>` of an external sprite (`/vendor/lucide@1.54.0/banco-sprite-SUBJECT.svg#NAME`) that Chrome fetches when the icon is first drawn, and `Page.captureScreenshot` does not wait for it, so the first viewport (390 px) met the sprite cold and later ones found it cached. `lesson/render_host.js` now waits (`iconsDrawn()`, polling every 40 ms, at most 8 s) until every `<use>` on screen has a box, at the end of `ready` (every card is shown in the scroll view then, so every sprite is asked for at once) and at the start of each `inspect`; a symbol the sprite does not have never draws, so it is waited for once and then ignored. No new finding, no change to the student's page.
  13. **A «−» key on every number and fraction answer.** An iPhone «decimal» or «numeric» keyboard (`inputmode`) shows no minus sign, so a negative answer could not be typed in the entry test or in practice. `items/helper_keys.js` is now the one module of the helper keys of a typed answer (`helperKeys`, `insertAtCaret`, the keys `minusKey`, `commaKey`, `barKey`): `items/number.js` draws «−» and «,» after its box (scientific notation too: «−» for a negative exponent after `^`) and `items/fraction.js` draws one «−» that writes into the box that last had focus among the numerator and, in a mixed number, the whole (the numerator at first; never the denominator). A key is a `type=button` (never submits the form), a pointer press does not take the focus from the box (the phone keyboard stays up), it inserts `-` at the caret and gives the focus back, and it is reached by Tab. The names are the items' own texts (`items.helper_keys`, `key_minus`, `key_comma`, `key_bar` in `config/locales/it.yml`, moved from `lesson.it.yml`), so every page that draws items has them: the sitting, practice, the teacher's item play and preview, and «Prova tu». `lesson/blocks/check.js` no longer draws a second row for the same box: a number check's keys are the number template's, and the one-line fraction input draws the shared «−» and «/». `.helper-keys` and `.helper-key` moved from `lesson.css` to `components.css` (the lesson keeps its own sizes under `.l2`), so the item pages show the same keys at 390 px. In a check with text before or after the box (`.check-row.is-around`) the keys sit on the formula's line: the box there is `5em` (`4em` under 600 px), nowrap with its keys, and the phone keys are smaller (`2em`), because the keys widen the answer past what the row line holds and the box would otherwise drop under the formula (`lesson_polish_system_test.rb`, «a typed answer stays with its formula»).
  14. **A table of signs keeps its columns on a phone.** D-331's `keepsGrid` (`lesson/blocks/table.js`) stacked a table of more than 280 px estimated, so the sign table of a lesson («Fattore | x < −4 | −4 < x < 2 | x > 2», rows «x + 4 | − | + | +» …; math, lesson revision 1156, card 3, and a 3-column table of a CS pivot lesson) became one box per row and the columns that the text talks about («guarda la colonna») vanished. A table is **compact** when it has a row and every cell after a row's first is at most 3 characters of plain text (signs, digits, «0», «∄», «T»; markup does not count): it keeps its grid up to 7 columns whatever the estimate, since its width is the header's and the first column's, and those wrap. Every other table keeps D-331's rule (at most 5 columns, at most 280 px at 9 px a character and 26 px a cell, the 600 px breakpoint). A kept table of the `table` block sits in a box that scrolls sideways (`.block-table.dg-scroll`, `overflow-x: auto`, under 600 px), so the grid never widens the page; `render_host`'s E-LESSON-OVERFLOW skips that box (`.dg-scroll`, as it skips `.code-box`) and still reports the page wider than the window and every other box that overflows. `CHAR_PX` stays 9: measured in Chrome at 390 px (the lesson font at 19 px), text takes 8.1 to 9.2 px a character (a 40-character sentence 342.9 px, «hablasteis» 85.2 px, «quoziente» 82.4 px), the cell padding 26.6 px and the lesson's box 312 px; the signs «+» «−» are 11.5 px, which is why the compact rule is not an estimate.
  15. **Text on a solid fill keeps the fill's ink.** The first box of a flow is filled with the accent (`.dg-flow .dg-start`, ink `--primary-text`), and a word of another language is drawn in the same accent (`.l2 .lang`, D-282), so «Have you ever been to London?» written as `[[en:…]]` in that box was blue on blue (lesson revision 1178, card 1: invisible in the cream and dark themes and at 1280 px; plain Italian in the box was fine, because the box's rule sets the colour on the label and the span has its own). `lesson/text.css` now says that a `.lang` or `.role` span inside a filled box takes the box's ink and no tint of its own (`color: inherit; background: none; box-shadow: none`): the first box of a flow (`.dg-starttext`), a pressed chip (`.dg-chipbtn[aria-pressed="true"]`), a chosen category chip (`.chip-input:checked + .chip-label`) and a chosen span chip (`.span-chip[aria-pressed="true"]`), the figures whose fill is a solid colour and whose text is rich. The span keeps its weight, its `lang` attribute and the speaker. The rule is by pair (fill, ink), so it holds in every theme; the other filled shapes hold only numbers or no text (`.dg-numlabel`, `.dg-flow-here-station`, `.mk-ROLE` marks).
  16. **A map figure waits for its base.** On a busy machine a `map` (or another wave 2 type with assets) could draw before its base arrived and the render check saw an empty frame. `lesson/preload.js` now collects the page's figures with their mode (`usedBy` returns `figures`) and fetches every type's assets (`moduleFor(type).prepare`) together before the first card; `lesson/diagrams/draw.js` keeps a figure's `settled` promise (`assetsPending`), and `lesson/render_host.js` awaits every figure's `settled` before it answers `ready`. A base that does not load is left to the figure, which says so.
  17. **A long formula in an item scrolls inside its box.** A `\ce{}` equation of 300 to 550 px overflowed a card of the entry test, practice and the teacher's item pages at 390 px. In `application.css` an inline `.math` of item markup (the prompt, options, matching and ordering rows, the steps, `data-markup`, the v1 lesson body) is an `inline-block` with `max-width: 100%` and `overflow-x: auto`, and the flex items holding it may shrink (`min-width: 0`); the lesson renderer (`.l2`) keeps its own overflow rules.
  18. **`W-BLANK-STEP-DATUM` compares numbers by value.** The warning read «1.200» and «1200», «0,5» and «0.5», or an accepted form of the blank's answer as different numbers and warned on data the card did give. `Lessons::Blocks::Example.blank_data` now compares numbers by value (thousands dots, the decimal comma, the blank's accepted forms); `test/lib/lessons/blank_datum_test.rb` has the cases.
  19. **`W-MATH-LAST-NOTE`.** A `math` chain shows each line's note under it as the step to the next line, so the note of the last line is never shown. A warning (`config/banco/error_codes.yml`) when the last line of a `math` block has a note (`Lessons::Blocks::Simple`); the lesson brief says a note leads to the next line (`briefs/lesson.md`); `lesson/blocks/math.js` documents the rule; `test/lib/lessons/math_block_test.rb`.
  20. **`W-SOLUTION-STORED-ORDER`.** A warning (registry version 31): the options of a choice, the rows of a matching and the steps of an ordering are shuffled for every student (`Diagnosis::Rekey`, practice instances, `items/matching.js`), but authors wrote solutions, finals and hints that point at the stored order («Dall'alto: Linea, Colonna, …», «Nell'ordine delle righe: …», «la prima frase», «l'opzione b», or the ids `l1`, `r2`, `e3`), so the student read a list that did not match the screen (items 3705, 3860, 3686, 3669, 3840, 3664). `Validation::InstanceChecks#stored_order` reads each solution step, the final and the effective hints of an instance of a `choice`, `matching` or `ordering` component (also a sub-item of a testlet) and warns on (a) an id of that instance's options, rows or steps as a bare token (an id with a digit as written, case-sensitive and outside `$…$`; a lone letter only as «a)»), or (b) a place: «dall'alto», «dal basso», «nell'ordine delle righe/opzioni/frasi/risposte» or «dell'elenco», «prima|seconda|terza|quarta|quinta|penultima|ultima» followed by frase, opzione, riga, risposta or alternativa (not «… del testo/brano»), «opzione|risposta|alternativa|scelta|lettera» with a letter a to e, and «in alto», «in basso», «a sinistra», «a destra» within 25 characters of a word for a row of the list. «La prima guerra mondiale», «a destra della retta» and a solution that names the option's text are quiet. It is a warning, never an error; the message tells the author to name the option by its text. The practice and diagnosis item briefs say so.
  21. **Axis labels hang from their gridline.** On lesson/2 `cartesian` figures the x labels sat to the right of their gridlines (5 to 17 px at 390 px on revision 1150, card 4) and the last tick's label straddled the frame («4» outside the plot when the window ends at 4). Cause: `draw.js` drew a one-line label as a fixed box of `l.w + 2` px at `left = round(l.x)`, so a text wider than its measure (the font arriving after the first measure, a larger text size) overflowed to the right inside its `nowrap` box; and `cartesian.js` centred the last label on the plot's right edge (the `min(l.x, W − l.w)` clamp only kept it in the stage). Now `draw.js` places a one-line label by its anchor point, whatever its real width: `left` is the anchor (the box's left, centre or right as the label's anchor says) and the CSS `translate` property moves it by −50 % (middle) or −100 % (end), with `width: auto` (the `translate` property, not `transform`, because the move animation of a keyed label owns `transform`); a wrapped label keeps its measured box. `cartesian.js` nudges a tick label at an edge of the frame inside it (x labels between the frame's left and right, y labels between its top and bottom), and picks the first nice step, from the one the room allows, whose nudged labels stand clear of each other (a 3-digit label at the end of a narrow axis made the step 2 instead of 1). Every other figure type that draws a one-line label takes the same path; the diagram vectors and the node suite are unchanged.
  22. **A mark after a formula never starts a line.** On a phone a full stop, a comma or a «?» that follows an inline formula (KaTeX or `\ce{}`) wrapped onto a line of its own, because a line may break between the formula's box and the next text (lesson 1166 cards 1, 9 and 6, lesson 1200 exercises 2 and 3, lesson 1148 «Prova tu» 6). `items/formula_punct.js` (`glueFormulas`, pure) rewrites the inline nodes of a paragraph, list item or cell before they are drawn: a formula and the run of closing marks right after it (`. , ; : ! ? ) ] » ” ’ " ' …`, no space between), and the run of opening marks right before it (`( [ « “ ‘ „`), become one `{t: "nowrap"}` node, drawn as `<span class="nowrap">` by `lesson/text.js` and `items/markup.js`; a formula followed by a space or a word is untouched, and so is a formula alone in its block (a display). The parsed tree, `plainText`, `keepsGrid` and the text of the page are unchanged, and the voice says the same words (`speech.js` walks a span like any other and already takes a mark back to its word). A formula wider than the line keeps its own way of fitting: in a lesson (`lesson.css`) the KaTeX box inside the wrapper is an inline-block (one unit for the line breaker, so `nowrap` holds it with the mark) that still breaks between its parts when it is wider than the line, with `max-width: calc(100% - 3em)` so that the mark never pushes the page sideways, and a chain of equations (`.eq-chain`) still breaks between its pieces; in an item (`application.css`) the scrolling `.math` box keeps `overflow-x: auto` and gives up 3em of its width to the mark. Rendering only: it fixes every approved lesson and item at once. The glue is for prose only, never for text a diagram lays out: the first version also glued the labels of a figure, and the span changed the width a label was measured and wrapped at, so two lessons failed their render with `E-DIAGRAM-LAYOUT two labels overlap ($\Delta < 0$? and sì)` and `($b = c = 0$? and sì)` (a flow node ending in a formula and «?», next to its edge label). `renderInlineRich` now skips `glueFormulas` when `ctx.noGlue` is set (`unglued(ctx)` in `lesson/text.js`), and `lesson/diagrams/draw.js` (the measuring probe, the labels of both layers, the effect line) and `diagrams/controls.js` (the chips) draw with it; a caption, a table cell and a prompt stay glued.
  23. **The render's time goes to loading the page, not to the dark theme.** Lesson revisions 1201, 1203, 1223, 1244 and 1245 (spanish and english, with a hero figure, `[[es:..]]` spans and dialogue blocks) failed with `timeout: the render of the revision passed 90 s` at card 0 of `1280x800-dark` (or «the page did not answer» there), though every card of the first two viewports took under 1.7 s (2.5 to 5 s of `inspect` and 4 to 9 s of pictures per viewport in the stored `timings`, 10 to 15 s in all, against 90 s elapsed); revision 1259, the same lesson, passed in 34 s, and a failure also fell on `1280x800-cream` card 4 (1202) and on `1280x800-dark` card 10 of a maths lesson (1261): the dark theme was only the last viewport to meet the 90 s, and nothing in it hangs (rendered locally, and in a `chromedp/headless-shell:156` with the sidecar's flags and 768 MB, all three viewports pass in 20 s). The seconds went outside the cards, before the first card of each viewport: the host page was loaded three times, each in a browser context of its own (empty cache), and its `javascript_importmap_tags` also modulepreloaded the whole student importmap (the Stimulus controllers and the item templates): 176 requests per load to the harness listener, which shares the five Puma threads of the `banco` container with the API (`lesson-review` opens of 12 to 29 s and 31 910 queries each are in the API log of the container that followed; the log of the failing windows went with the container that ran them), so under a busy API each load waits in a queue, and the in-job retry of item 7 meets the same queue. Now: `Validation::LessonRenderRunner` draws the viewports in one browser context (the second and third load take every file from its HTTP cache: the page alone is asked for) and closes each viewport's page before the next; `harness/lesson_render.html.erb` writes the inline importmap and the entry module with no `modulepreload` (the page imports what it needs); `render_host.js` bounds everything `ready` waits for (the fonts, `preloadFor`, the figures' `settled`) to 24 s in all (`?ready_ms=` asks for less) and answers `waited more than 24 s for the fonts` (or the modules, the figures) instead of leaving the runner's 30 s to say «the page did not answer»; the result keeps `loads` (per viewport the seconds of the page's load, `open`, and of the host's readiness, `ready`) so that the seconds outside the cards are told apart the next time. The 90 s budget is unchanged. Not done: the harness listener still shares the Puma threads of the API; if `loads` shows a slow `open` again, it needs its own threads.
  24. **`W-MATH-SPACE-PUNCT`.** A warning (registry version 32): an inline formula whose TeX ends with a spacing command (`\;`, `\,`, `\:`, `\ `, `\quad`, `\qquad`) and is followed right after its closing `$` by a mark (`$C_3H_6\;$.`, or `\ce{C3H6}\;` before a full stop) shows a gap before the mark (lesson revision 1179). The renderer already keeps a mark glued to its formula (item 22), so the spacing only opens a gap: the author drops it. `Validation::FormulaSpace` finds them in a text; `Validation::Lesson2Checks` reads every markup field of a lesson/2 (the message names the line, the field the card and block) and `Validation::InstanceChecks#formula_space` reads the display, the solution and the hints of an item instance (the field names the instance). The lesson brief and the two item briefs say so. A warning only: approved content keeps validating.
  25. **`W-SENTENCE-COMMA-VARIANTS`.** A warning (registry version 32): `Grading::Closed::Text.normalize` strips only the marks at the end of a typed answer and keeps every comma and semicolon inside it, so a `normalized_text` key that is a sentence (it holds a space and ends in `.`, `!` or `?`) with a comma or a semicolon («No salimos, ya que llovía.», «Llueve; por lo tanto, nos quedamos.») marks the same sentence written without it, or with it elsewhere, wrong. `Validation::InstanceChecks#sentence_commas` warns when the key has one and no `accept` entry (the instance's or the item's), compared as the grader reads it, is the same sentence with fewer of them; the author adds the variant to `accept`. The grader is unchanged (a recorded grade is never rewritten, and a missing comma stays its own difference). The diagnosis and practice briefs say so.
  26. **No `W-SOLUTION-INTERNAL-ID`.** The internal ids of rows and options (`l1`, `r2`, `e3`, `o4`, item revision 3840) in a solution step or final were already caught, as whole words of the instance's own ids, by `W-SOLUTION-STORED-ORDER` (item 20: `stored_order_ids`, with its test «internal ids fire as bare tokens»); a second code would warn twice on the same text, so none was added.
  27. **The era of a year on a timeline.** A `timeline` printed «d.C.» after every year, also on a modern axis (lesson revision 1276, card 3: «1969 d.C.», «1977 d.C.»), and the widened labels touched at 390 px. `yearLabel` and `eventYearLabel` (`lesson/diagrams/time/years.js`, twin `Lessons::Diagrams::Timeline.year_label`) now take the axis: «a.C.» is always written; «d.C.» only when the axis has a year before Christ (its first year is negative), so a modern axis prints «1969». The ticks, the event plates, the description and the printed strings of a state all follow the same rule; the century names («I secolo d.C.») are unchanged.
  28. **A whole-number box does not talk about decimals.** The help line of a number box («Scrivi il numero. Per i decimali usa la virgola.») was shown on checks whose answer is a count (syllables, species). `Lessons::StudentBody` serves `integer: true` on a `number` check when its key and every accepted form are whole numbers (a fact about the key's kind, never the key; `test/fixtures/lesson2/whitelist.json` lists it as computed), and `items/number.js` then shows `items.number_integer_label` («Scrivi il numero intero.») instead. A decimal key, or an item (which never carries the field), keeps the old line.
  29. **The key of a formula draws a group's subscripts.** In the `formula` figure the key's sample of a bracket group read «(C2H4)» as plain text, while the formula above it lowers its subscripts (lesson revision 1179). `Chem.subscripted` (`lesson/lib/chem.js`) writes the group as lesson markup, `$(\mathrm{C}_{2}\mathrm{H}_{4})$`, and the key's sample uses it; its plain text is the formula as typed, so the layout's measure and the voice do not change.
  30. **A three-column table of short cells keeps its grid.** D-331's `keepsGrid` (`lesson/blocks/table.js`) stacked a table of more than 280 px estimated, though the card's box is 312 px at 390 px (D-335 item 14 measured it): a city, a shift and a number (8 rows, «Campobasso | mattina | 1250») became boxes. The limit is now 310 px; a table that does not fit still stacks (a 15-character city name, a long third header), and a kept grid that is wider than the box scrolls sideways (`.dg-scroll`).
  31. **A card title with a formula, on the teacher's topic page.** The place of a lesson finding («Scheda 7: Con $\Delta < 0$ non ci sono soluzioni reali · blocco 2») and the card links of the render box printed the title's TeX as text (seen on the formula lesson at 390 px). `teacher/topics/_lesson_finding` and `_lesson2_box` now put those texts in a `data-markup="inline"` span, which the page's `markup` controller already draws for hints, steps and keys.
  32. **The cover is pictured by the render check.** `Validation::LessonRenderRunner` looked at the cover (card 0, the lesson's hero figure) at every viewport but never shot it, so no reviewer saw the hero as the student has it on a phone: all 61 reviews of the last two content waves lacked it. `shoot?` no longer excepts card 0: the cover is pictured as drawn at every viewport it is drawn at (390 x 844 cream, 1280 x 800 cream and dark: the same bound as a core card, 3 files per lesson, stored by content); its further states follow the rule of the other cards (the first viewport of the core set for another exercise, anywhere for a new finding). The shot has `card: 0` and `level: "cover"`; `banco lesson shots` writes it as `card-00_390x844-cream.webp` (nothing in the API, the CLI, `LessonShots` or `bin/purge-lesson-shots` assumed cards start at 1: the API lists the stored order, the file name is `%02d`, the purge works by sha), and the teacher's shots page (`teacher/lesson_shots/index`) heads it «Copertina» (`teacher.render.cover`, alt `teacher.render.shots.alt_cover`) and, sorted by card number, shows it first. Renders already stored keep their shots without a cover; the next render of a revision has it.
  33. **A number item's box says nothing of decimals when the answer is whole.** Item 28 did it for the checks of a lesson; the items of the entry test and of practice still told every number box «Scrivi il numero. Per i decimali usa la virgola.» (a count of syllables, a size in bytes, a number of items). `Items::Part#call` takes the instance's `answer:` and `accept:` (the item's own `accept` plus the instance's, `Items::Part.accepted`) and serves `integer: true` on a `number` part (not a scientific one) when the key and every accepted form are whole numbers (`Items::Part.whole?`: digits with an optional minus, the ASCII hyphen or U+2212); `Diagnosis::ItemPresenter` (the sitting, the preview, the all-questions page, the item shots: one testlet sub item at a time, with its own key and accepted forms) and `PracticeController#item_part` pass them. A boolean about the key's kind, never the key (the leak scans of the payloads stay as they were); `items/number.js` already read it (`items.number_integer_label`, «Scrivi il numero intero.»). A decimal key, or an accepted form with a comma or a dot, keeps the old line. The grading is untouched: «7,0» is still read as 7.
  34. **A code span in an item.** `[[code:..]]` (the lesson reader's literal span, up to the first `]]`, 40 characters) is drawn in item text, options and table cells as it is in a lesson: `items/markup_parser.js` reads it when the text has no roles (`{t: "code", v}`), `items/markup.js` draws `<code class="code-span">`, and `application.css` gives `.code-span` the lesson's look (the body font on a calm tint, never monospace, `pre-wrap`). Before, it was printed as it was written.
