  35. **A table of an item breaks a word only when the word alone is wider than the room.** `.markup { overflow-wrap: anywhere }` reached the cells of `table.data` and let the browser shrink every column to one letter, so at 390 px a cell «CInt(Console.ReadLine())» broke as «CInt(Console.ReadLi / ne())», «quota \ 100» as «quota \ / 100» and the short header «N.» as «N / .» while the table had room to wrap at its spaces. `table.data th, td` now have `overflow-wrap: break-word; word-break: normal`: each column keeps the width of its longest word, the other cells wrap at their spaces, and a table whose longest words still do not fit the card scrolls sideways inside `.table-wrap` (as it was designed to; the item shots report it as «scrolls sideways»). No content is cut. **Soft break points for long tokens (the same day, after the redrawn 4244):** a program line is one word («CInt(Console.ReadLine())», «Console.WriteLine("Livello»), so with `break-word` alone its column grew past the card and half of each line hid behind the scroll, the caption with it, and for this student hidden code is worse than a break. `items/soft_breaks.js` (`softBreaks`, called by `items/prompt.js` on every `th` and `td`; `pieces` is the pure part) puts a `<wbr>` after «.», «(» and «,» and before «=» and «&» inside a word of more than 12 characters (a formula's own tree is left alone): an invisible break opportunity that the table's min-content width respects, so the line breaks at a dot («CInt(» / «Console.» / «ReadLine())»), never inside a name, and the table fits the card. The text, its copy and the screen reader's reading are unchanged (a `<wbr>` holds no character).
- **Not retroactive:** a grade already recorded is never rewritten (firm rule 4); the grader change applies to answers graded from now on. Items 1 to 4, 10, 14, 15, 21, 22 and 27 to 30 are rendering only: they fix every approved lesson and item at once, with no new revision and no new approval.
- **Why:** The reviewers read the pages as a student does. A counter that moves, a hidden question, an invisible highlight and a red `\ce` error are what a student with reading difficulties cannot get past; a typed `pi` marked wrong is an unfair grade; a blank step that needs a number nobody gave cannot be answered, and the author needed to be told.
- **Cost:** A field in the example's student body, a few stylesheet rules (the palette is regenerated), mhchem loaded on the first chemistry formula of an items page, one lookahead regex in the grader, a warning code (the registry version becomes 31 with `E-ACCEPT-IS-ERROR` and `W-SOLUTION-STORED-ORDER`); a render that timed out costs one more Chrome pass in the same job.
- **Risk (named):** the band under a highlighted line or point is a rendering choice that the render check's overflow rules do not measure; `W-BLANK-STEP-DATUM` is a heuristic over numbers and cell references and may warn on a datum that the card gives in another way (it is a warning, never an error).
- **Not done:** no re-grade of recorded answers; no warning for a datum that is not a number or a cell reference; no change to how a blank step is served.
- **Status:** implemented.
- **Back-port:** `briefs/lesson.md` (the blank step's `do_it`), D-282 (mhchem in items), D-310 (the inline typed answer shows its prompt).

## D-336 · 2026-11-15 · the shots of an item as the student sees it on a phone: one picture of every instance, on demand, for the reviewer and the blind solver

- **Design ref:** D-249, D-255, D-311 (the lesson render check and its shots: `RenderLessonRevisionJob`, `Validation::LessonRenderRunner`, `LessonShots`, `banco lesson shots`), D-320 and D-321 (the solver and the reviewer see an item's figures; `Review::Figures`, `Items::Figures`), D-335 (item 12: the render shots wait for the icons), A-05 (the blind solve and the expert review see the item as the student does), firm rules 3 and 4.
- **Design said:** a lesson had pictures of every card at 390 px for its reviewer (`banco lesson shots`); an item reached its reviewer and its blind solver as text (`review open`, `solve open`: the display, the key for the reviewer) and its figures as PNG files (D-320). Nobody looked at an item as the student's phone draws it.
- **Operator (2026-11-15):** in 61 topic reviews nobody could see an item instance at 390 px; the overflow and the markup bugs of the item pages were found late, by the student's side. The reviewers and the blind solvers must see each practice and diagnosis item instance as the student sees it, like the 390 px shots they already have for lessons.
- **We do:**
  1. **The render host** (`HarnessController#item`, `GET /h/:token/item-render.html?n=N&theme=cream|dark`, harness listener only, token kind `irev`, `app/views/harness/item_render.html.erb`, `app/javascript/items/render_host.js`). It draws instance N (the N-th stored instance of the revision in the order of their ids: the number the solver's and the reviewer's openings use) with the student's own page: the same CSS (`:app`, KaTeX), the same importmap and `renderItem` (`items/render.js`: one template per component, MathLive for an `expression`, KaTeX with mhchem on demand, the figure's `<img>`), inside the frame of the page the student meets the item in (a `practice_item`: the practice page's card with «Controlla», «Mostra un aiuto (1 di N)» when the item has hints and «Mostrami la soluzione»; any other kind: the sitting's card with «Come si risponde» closed and «Invia» / «Non lo so»), **unanswered**, in the cream theme (the student's default). What the browser is told is `Diagnosis::ItemPresenter`'s (`Items::ShotPresentation` builds it; `Items::Part`): never the key, the error values, the hints or the solution (the page and the DOM are scanned for them in `test/validation/item_render_runner_test.rb`). The CSP is the lesson host's (`default-src 'none'`, `connect-src 'none'`, the inline importmap and the two JSON blocks by hash). A figure's `<img src="/assets/items/<sha>.svg">` is served on the harness listener too (`HarnessController#item_asset`: content-addressed, the same bytes and headers as `ItemAssetsController`, no token because an `<img>` cannot carry one).
  2. **The order a student would see, from a fixed seed.** A choice's options, a matching's rows and an ordering's elements are shuffled as the sitting and the practice shuffle them (`Diagnosis::Conductor.rekey`, `Diagnosis::Rekey`) with the seed `item-shots|<revision id>|<instance number>`; the shot's metadata says the `seed` and the `shown_order` (the stored ids in the order drawn, per column; a testlet per sub item), so the number on an option (the picture's `1`, `2`, …) is `shown_order.options[n-1]`, the id the solver's `answers.json` uses. The shuffle avoids the key's own order for an ordering and a matching (`Rekey`), so the order reveals nothing but a permutation. A matching's right column is a closed `<select>`: its options are not open in the picture (a native menu is not drawn); their order is `shown_order.right`.
  3. **The runner** (`Validation::ItemRenderRunner`, `lib/validation/`, with `Validation::ItemRenderCheck` for the row, as the lesson's pair): one browser context under `ChromeRunner`'s lock, one page for the whole revision (the context's HTTP cache serves every load after the first), a viewport of `item_render.viewport` (390 x 844, cream, **device scale 1**: a picture is 390 CSS px wide and 390 px of file), the instances in order (`item_render.max_instances` 40; a longer pool is pictured to there and says so in `notes`), a budget of 150 s for the revision and 12 s for an instance. A shot is the **whole page**: the window is made as tall as the page for the picture (never under the phone's 844 px), so nothing is cut and the sticky action bar sits under the item as it does when the student has scrolled to the end; WebP quality 80. The host measures and the runner records per instance (all `E-ITEM-*` codes are **findings of the drawing, an aid, never a gate**): `E-ITEM-OVERFLOW` (the page wider than the window, something wider than its box, a long formula that scrolls sideways inside its box), `E-ITEM-RENDER` (an exception or a console error, a refused script or request, a KaTeX error, markup printed as text, a figure that did not draw, a timeout). A render that failed only on its time limits is drawn once more (`render_attempts`), like the lesson's. Chrome that cannot be reached is an `error` row, never a pass.
  4. **Storage and the ledger.** `item_renders` (migration `CreateItemRenders`, the UPDATE and DELETE triggers like the other tables; `item_revision_id`, `status` `queued|passed|failed|error`, `rules_version`, `harness_version` (`Validation::Harness.item_version`), `chrome_version`, `attempt`, `result_json` with the errors, notes, timings and instance counts, `shots_json` with each shot's `instance`, `seed`, `shown_order`, `viewport`, `width`, `height`, `scale`, `sha256`, `bytes`, `created_at`). One row per event: `queued` (a request that enqueued the job), then the verdict (`passed`, or `failed` when there are findings) or `error`; the latest row is the status. The pictures go to the lesson shots' store (`LessonShots`, `storage/lesson_shots/<sha256>.webp`, `BANCO_LESSON_SHOTS_DIR`): one store by content for both. `bin/purge-lesson-shots` (`LessonShots.purge`) now also reads `item_renders`: a file named only by shots of an item revision that no blueprint or topic revision pins, that is not the latest of its item and whose render is older than 30 days is deleted; a file a kept render also names stays; the rows stay.
  5. **On demand, not on every validation** (a Chrome load for every item would queue behind the validations). `POST /api/v1/item-revisions/:revision/shots` (`Items::ShotRequest`) appends a `queued` row and enqueues `RenderItemRevisionJob` (queue `chrome`, **priority 20**, below item validation and below the lesson render and the page validations, which gate approval) **once**: no second job while a `queued` row younger than `item_render.queued_stale_minutes` (30) stands with nothing after it (forced or not), nor when a render (a verdict) made by the current host exists, unless `force` (`?force=1`); an `error`, a lost job and a verdict made under another `Validation::Harness.item_version` (the host template and script, the student's `items/*.js` and stylesheets, the numbers) are asked again freely; the row and the check of the rows before it are one transaction. The job names its request (the `queued` row's id) and draws unless a verdict was appended since, so a forced request draws a revision that has a verdict again and two jobs for one revision draw once; its retries (Chrome busy or gone, three attempts) leave the `queued` row standing and the last appends the `error` row; any other crash appends an `error` row at once and raises, so a request never stays `queued` for the half hour. The token of the render is issued once the job holds Chrome. The host's script is pinned `preload: false` in the student importmap, so no student or teacher page preloads it. `GET /api/v1/item-revisions/:revision/shots` answers `{status: none|queued|passed|failed|error, render_id, errors, notes, instances, shots: [{instance, seed, shown_order, viewport, width, height, scale, sha256, bytes, available, path}], seed_note, next}` (the pictures of the latest verdict while a newer request is queued), and `GET .../shots/:sha` the WebP (404 «immagine rimossa» after the purge; a content address of another revision is no key). Token roles: every role reads (the content roles, `bot_read`, `teacher`); only the content roles request (`bot_read` is 403 `read_only_token`, `teacher` 403 `teacher_token_no_content`: the default of `Api::BaseController`); a dry run (`X-Banco-Dry-Run`) says what it would do and queues nothing; a revision with no instance is 422 `E-ITEM-NOT-PASSED`. Contract: `item shots` (`contract/commands.json`, example `contract/examples/item-shots.list.json`).
  6. **The CLI** (`cli/cmd_item_shots.go`). `banco item shots REV [--dir DIR] [--wait] [--force] [--timeout S]` reads the status and always asks for the render (the server alone knows whether a verdict is outdated, drawn under another `Harness.item_version`, and enqueues at most once; a token that cannot ask reads the verdict there is), and with `--wait` polls until it is (`BANCO_POLL_MS`, `--timeout` 300 s: `E-TIMEOUT`; an `error` row is `E-CHROME-UNAVAILABLE`, exit 6); it writes `DIR/REV/instance-NN_390x844.webp` (the default `DIR` is `banco-figures`, so one folder per revision holds the figures and the pictures; earlier `instance-*.webp` of that revision are cleared, another revision's are not) and prints, per file, the instance, its `seed` and `shown_order`, with the `errors` and `notes` of the render and `removed_by_purge` (`--force` draws again). `banco review open REV` and `banco solve open REV` now request the shots after the open (best effort: a token that cannot request, a revision with nothing to draw or a busy server never fail the open) and add `item_shots: {requested, enqueued, status, fetch, why}` to their answer, `fetch` being the command that brings the pictures; they never wait for them.
  7. **The briefs.** `solve` (version 3) tells the solver to look at the picture of an instance before it answers it and how to read `shown_order`; `review` (version 4) tells the reviewer to look at every picture first, to make a finding of an item that overflows, cuts a formula or hides its question on a phone, and to read `errors`. Neither may use a picture to find a key: there is none in it.
- **No gate change.** The shots are an aid: no `Review::Gate`, `Approval::TopicGate`, `Approval::BlueprintGate` or validation verdict reads `item_renders`; nothing records a decision; the rules version does not move (the `item_render` block of `validation_rules.yml` adds numbers nothing else reads; registry version 33 adds `E-ITEM-RENDER` and `E-ITEM-OVERFLOW`, described as aids).
- **Why:** the reviewer who sees only the text of an item cannot see that a long formula pushes the page off a phone, that a table is cut, that a matching's row is unreadable or that a figure did not draw; the blind solver is shown the instance as text, not as the student's page. The student's phone is where these show.
- **Cost:** a Chrome pass of a few seconds per revision, on request and behind validation; about 10 to 20 KB of WebP per instance in the shared store, purged with the rest.
- **Not drawn, on purpose:** the answered states (feedback, hints opened, the solution: they come from the server and are answers); a matching's open menu; the dark theme and a large text size (the first shots are the cream phone; `item-render.html?theme=dark` draws the dark one, the runner does not ask for it yet); the diagnosis' formula sheet and the sitting's help text opened.
- **Status:** implemented
- **Back-port:** none.
- **Tests:** `test/validation/item_render_runner_test.rb` (Chrome: an item revision of each of choice, number, fraction, matching, ordering, expression and a choice with a figure, every instance with a file 390 px wide of WebP, the seed and the shown order; no key, error value, hint or solution in the host's page nor in the DOM, in the practice and the sitting frames, and MathLive's field there; an overflowing instance and a figure that did not draw are reported; the cap), `test/integration/item_shots_api_test.rb` (roles, one job per request, force, stale and error, the list, the image, the purge, the append-only rows, the host page on the harness listener only, the figure's address), `test/models/items/shot_presentation_test.rb`, `test/models/brief_test.rb`, `cli/cmd_item_shots_test.go` and `cli/cmd_review_test.go`.

## D-337 · 2026-11-16 · practice the student can skip, leave half done, come back to and redo: the list of exercises, drafts, rules `practice/2`

- **Design ref:** D-235 (the practice engine, rules `practice/1`), D-236 (the student's practice page), D-309 (the teacher's preview), A-09 (the serve state machine and the selector).
- **Design said:** on a skill the student had one open serve at a time: the next exercise came only after an answer (or the 24 hours of abandonment), there was no way to skip one, what he had typed was lost with the page, and nothing listed the exercises of a topic or let him do one again on purpose.
- **Operator (2026-11-16):** «lo studente deve avere la possibilità di saltarli interamente o in parte, una sorta di salvataggio a metà esercizio, e di navigare tra gli esercizi tipo una sidebar con l'elenco che segna quelli fatti e da fare, e lo studente può rifare gli esercizi.»
- **We do:**
  1. **Rules `practice/2`** (`lib/practice/rules/v2.rb`, `docs/rules/practice-2.md`; `practice-1.md` stays as the record of version 1, `v1.rb` is gone and every reference moved). There is at most ONE open serve per (student, skill, pinned item), not per (student, skill). A serve is abandoned after 336 hours (14 days: an exercise left half done is kept two weeks) or when a newer serve of the same student on the same item exists (superseded). `Practice::Selector.next` takes `item:` (an item key: that exercise's open serve, else a new instance: the first unseen, else the oldest seen, reason `reseen`) and `advance:` («Avanti» and «Salta»: the next exercise, the open ones kept open); with neither it resumes the open serve touched most recently. A serve creation stays one transaction, so two tabs get one serve. Reasons and the `practice_serves` table do not change; the old rows are read with the new rule (states are derived).
  2. **Drafts.** `practice_drafts` (migration `CreatePracticeDrafts`, UPDATE and DELETE triggers like every primary table; `student_id`, `practice_serve_id`, `raw`, `source`, `created_at`). The latest row of a serve is its draft, a `raw` of "" clears it. `POST /practice/serves/:serve_id/draft {raw, source}` answers `saved`, `unchanged` (the text equals the draft now: no row), 422 `too_long` (more than 20 000 characters), 409 `closed` (the serve is closed or abandoned) and 404 for a serve that is not the student's own or not visible to him. The serve body (`POST /practice/serves`) gains `draft` (`{raw, source}`: the latest draft, only while it is newer than the serve's last try and not "") and `exercise` (`{skill, item, n}`: the item key and its 1-based place in the pin order). A draft is never graded and is not a try.
  3. **The list.** `GET /practice/exercises?topic=KEY` (`Practice::Exercises`, both in the student's pages and in the preview's) answers, for each skill of the topic, the items pinned on the topic revision the student sees, in pin order, each with `n`, a `title_it` (the first sentence of the item's prompt stem, at most 90 characters, lesson markup kept whole; never the key, never an instance's text), a `status` (`todo`, `done`, `tried`, `left`, `skipped`), the open serve's id and the counts of correct closes and of serves with a try. The status, in this order: `left` when the item's open serve has a try or a non-empty draft; `done` when a serve of it closed correct; `tried` when a closed or abandoned serve has a try or a shown solution; `skipped` when it has an open serve with nothing typed; else `todo` (so a redo with nothing typed does not hide a `done`; the open serve's id is given whenever there is one, and a click resumes it). The addresses are built with the acting student's base (`spath`), so the preview's stay in the preview.
  4. **The page** (`practice/show`, `practice_controller.js`, `items/practice_urls.js`, the templates' `draft()` and `restore()` and their `item-change` event): on a wide screen a sidebar with the list, on a phone a collapsible panel above the exercise («Esercizi: 2 fatti su 5»); an entry opens that exercise (its open serve with the typed answer put back, else a new instance); «Rifai» on a done or tried one gives a new instance; «Salta» saves the draft, keeps the serve open and opens the next exercise; the draft is saved after 1.5 s without typing and when he leaves (Salta, a click in the list, closing the page).
- **What does not change.** What counts toward «dimostrata» is the same: a correct answer without help on an instance not seen before counts; a skipped serve has no try and counts for nothing; a redo of an instance already seen is `reseen`, aided, and counts for nothing toward the demonstration. The thresholds and the skill states (`Practice::Fold`) are the same; the diagnosis and the lessons are untouched. Nothing in the list or the draft is a decision.
- **Why:** a student with reading difficulties who is stuck on one exercise must be able to leave it, do another and come back, without losing what he wrote and without the page forcing a try; and he must see what he has done and what is left, and be able to practise an exercise again before the exam.
- **Cost:** one append-only table; one more read of the serves per list request (per skill of the topic, at most three); a draft write per pause in typing (one row per change, `raw` at most 20 000 characters, nothing when the text is unchanged).
- **Not done:** no purge of old drafts (append-only); a skip does not close the serve nor count anywhere; the text sizes are another entry (D-338).
- **Status:** implemented.
- **Back-port:** D-235 (the selector's rule 4 and the serve's abandonment, now per item), D-236 (the practice page).
- **Tests:** `test/integration/practice_navigation_test.rb` (the draft's `saved`, `unchanged`, `too_long`, `closed` and 404 for another student's serve; a draft comes back in the serve body after a reload and not after a newer try; the list's statuses todo, skipped, left and done; «Rifai» on a done item gives a new serve; the preview writes only the preview student; the list holds no key and no instance's text), `test/lib/practice/rules_test.rb`, `test/lib/practice` and `test/models/practice` (the selector with `item:` and `advance:`, one open serve per item), `test/models/append_only_test.rb` (the new table), the node tests of the templates' drafts and of `practice_urls.js`, `test/system/practice_flow_test.rb` (the list, Salta, a click, Rifai, the draft restored).

## D-338 · 2026-11-16 · two smaller text sizes; a matching with an empty row says so and marks the row

- **Design ref:** B-11 and E-10 (the student's theme and text size, `Diagnosis::Preferences`), D-298 (a refused answer and its message), D-317 (what is still refused), D-337 (the practice page).
- **Operator (2026-11-16):** «in generale mettiamo un testo configurabile più piccolo, mettiamo small e smallest».
- **We do:**
  1. **Five text sizes.** `Diagnosis::Preferences::SIZES = %w[smallest small normal large larger]` (smallest first wherever they are listed): the root font is 16 px («Molto piccolo»), 18 px («Piccolo»), 20 px («Normale», the default), 24 px and 28 px; the lesson's own dialog says «Più piccolo», «Piccolo», «Normale», «Grande», «Più grande», and the teacher's lesson box has `.l2-box[data-size]` at 0.8 and 0.9 rem. Diagram labels keep their 18 px floor (`lesson/diagrams/common.js`). `test/lib/readability_test.rb`'s «at least 18 px» scan skips the two root rules: they are the student's own choice.
  2. **A matching with an empty row** (found in the student's first practice, 2026-11-16: four rows of five chosen, the first left empty, refused twice with «Scrivi una risposta prima di continuare.», then he asked the solution). `Grading::Closed#matching` answers `invalid("incomplete_rows")` when some rows are empty («Manca una risposta: scegli una risposta per ogni riga, poi controlla.»; every row empty stays `empty`); the code is in `STILL_REFUSED` (D-317: never an attempt) and in the registry's grader codes. The item handles gain `showMissing()` (matching: the empty rows get the class `missing` and their select `aria-invalid`, the first is focused; testlet: the parts left without an answer), called by the practice page and the sitting after a refusal; `student.css` draws a dashed warning border and «Manca».
  3. **The phone's action bar.** At 40rem or less the sticky bar of the practice page is three rows at most («Controlla», the hint, then «Mostrami la soluzione» and «Salta» side by side, both text buttons), and the page keeps the focused box above it (`scroll-padding-bottom: 15rem` on a page with a sticky exercise or sitting bar): at 390 px the box that took the focus sat under the bar (measured after the fix: the input at 389 to 445 px, the bar from 550 px).
- **Why:** a student with reading difficulties asked for less text on the screen as well as more; a refusal must say what is missing, or he cannot get past it.
- **Not retroactive:** recorded answers and refusals stay as they are.
- **Status:** implemented.
- **Tests:** `test/integration/preferences_test.rb` (the five sizes, their order and labels, kept on /settings and from the lesson), `test/lib/readability_test.rb`, `test/system/lesson2_teacher_box_test.rb`; `test/fixtures/grading/vectors.json` (`matching-first-row-empty-is-incomplete`, `matching-all-rows-empty`), `test/integration/accepted_answers_test.rb` (a partial matching in the entry test is refused with the new message and writes no attempt), `test/javascript/items/draft_restore.test.mjs` (`showMissing`), `test/system/practice_flow_test.rb` (the refusal and the marked row).

## D-339 · 2026-11-17 · whole sentences for a blank, repeated answers, plainer messages, «ci sei quasi», «Fai controllare»

- **Design ref:** D-296 (the text grader), D-298 (a refused answer), D-301 (a near answer earns a line), D-317 (what is still refused), D-337 (the practice page), D-304 (comments anywhere), D-309 (the teacher's preview writes no comment).
- **The student's case (2026-11-17):** in his English practice the exercises asked only the words in place of `___`. He wrote nine whole sentences, six of them right, and all nine were marked wrong with «Questa risposta non corrisponde a un errore che conosco»; he then pressed «Controlla» again with the same sentence each time.
- **Operator (2026-11-17):** accept a whole sentence written around the `___` blank; refuse a repeated identical answer; plainer messages; «ci sei quasi» for typos and for one missing word; and a smaller line under the message with a button «Fai controllare» that sends an answer the student believes right to the teacher.
- **We do:**
  1. **A whole sentence for a blank** (`Grading::Closed`, `Grading::Frame`). When the instance's stem holds exactly one `___`, the words he wrote between the frame's words are graded exactly as if he had typed only them (result observation `full_sentence`, `answer_part`; the stored `normalized` is the normalized part). The blank copied into the answer is refused as `blank_copied`; a long answer that repeats the frame without fitting it as `not_in_frame` (both never an attempt: `Diagnosis::AnswerRecorder::STILL_REFUSED`). A right whole sentence carries the note «Bastava scrivere solo le parole che mancano: …».
     The frame is the line with the blank, after the last `→`, without the instruction before the last «: » that comes ahead of the blank («Negativa con will: She ___ the test.» is «She ___ the test.»). Checked on his answers of 2026-11-17 with the deployed grader: «She will not pass the test.» was refused as `not_in_frame` because the three-word label «Negativa con will» stayed in the frame (the first rule dropped only one- or two-word labels); with this rule it is right.
  2. **The same answer twice** is refused, not a try, nothing stored (`Practice::AnswerRecorder`): the raw stripped and its spaces collapsed, a text answer as the grader normalizes it, compared with every try of the serve. The message offers «Fai controllare» only while a contest is allowed (`practice.same_answer`), else it only asks to change something (`practice.same_answer_plain`).
  3. **Plainer messages.** `practice.unrecognised` «Non è ancora giusta. Leggi l'aiuto e riprova.» and `unrecognised_no_hint` «Non è ancora giusta. Riprova.»; short sentences, neutral in gender.
  4. **«Ci sei quasi»** (`Grading::NearText.kind`, pure): a text answer that is plain `wrong` and one typo away from a right one (`near_typo`) or one whole word missing or added (`near_one_word`; a substitution such as «is» for «are» is a grammar error, not near) is the outcome `near_miss` (N; the near-miss rows of the state table: one retry, then closed with the solution). The loader derives it from the stored grading and the instance, so old tries are re-derived the same way.
  5. **«Fai controllare»** (`POST /practice/serves/:serve_id/contest`, `Practice::Contest`, table `practice_contests`, append-only, unique per attempt). Allowed on the latest try when its outcome is `unrecognised` or `form` and it is not contested yet, whether the serve is open or closed `wrong`. In one transaction: the contest row; a comment for the teacher through `Comments::Intake` (reason `error`, the practice page, anchored to the exercise's answer, the serve as its ref, text «La mia risposta, secondo me giusta: «…»» cut at 200); the solution event (`after_contest`) unless already sent. The try's outcome becomes `contested` (N: counts neither way), the serve is closed `contested` with actions `next`, `back`. Not allowed → 409 `not_contestable`; a second click answers the same and writes nothing; another student's serve is a 404. In the teacher's preview the contest is written for the preview student and no comment (D-309). The teacher answers in «I miei commenti».
  6. **The list says «Da riprovare»** (`Practice::Exercises`): an open serve with at least one try is `retry` (he answered once and can try again; the student's comment: «L'esercizio non è stato lasciato a metà, ma viene segnalato così»); an open serve with no try and a non-empty draft is `left` («Lasciato a metà»); an open serve with neither is `skipped`. Order: retry or left, done, tried, skipped, to do (an open serve with nothing typed on a done or tried exercise keeps done or tried).
  7. **Rules `practice/3`** (`docs/rules/practice-3.md`): numbers unchanged; `Outcome.call(near:)`, the outcome `contested`, the contest rows of the state table.
- **Why:** a student with reading difficulties was told his right answers were wrong and could not tell how to be heard; the engine must accept what the question asked for however it is written, and must say plainly what to do next.
- **Not retroactive:** past answers are not regraded (the ledger is append-only); a try already stored is read with the new rules wherever the grading row allows (a near answer is re-derived from the stored text), no row is changed.
- **Status:** implemented.
- **Tests:** `test/integration/practice_feedback_test.rb` (the contest for the student and the preview, the repeated answer, «ci sei quasi», the whole sentence, the new unrecognised text, the list's statuses), `test/models/practice/contest_test.rb`, `test/lib/grading/near_text_test.rb` and `test/fixtures/grading/` (the grader's), `test/models/append_only_test.rb` (the new table), `test/system/practice_flow_test.rb`.

## D-340 · 2026-11-17 · what is still needed to close a topic

- **Design ref:** D-339 (the practice page), D-337 (the list of exercises), rules `practice/3` section 5 (skill states, `docs/rules/practice-3.md`), D-307 (Oggi).
- **The student's words (2026-11-17):** «Continuano ad essere da riprendere anche se in realtà sono finiti» and «Se sono già stati fatti possono anche essere rimossi, no?». For the engine a topic is done when every skill is demonstrated (3 distinct exercises right without help, on 2 different days, 2 of them hard to guess); he thinks it is done when he has done the exercises.
- **We do:** tell him what is still needed, in short sentences and plain words, where he looks.
  1. **The rule, once.** Topic page, step 2, under the title: «Per chiudere l'argomento: in ogni abilità, 3 esercizi giusti senza aiuto, in 2 giorni diversi.» (`practice.close_rule`).
  2. **What is missing, per skill** (`Practice::Messages.missing`, `missing_it`; texts `practice.missing.*`), for every skill not yet demonstrated (in studio, not seen, to recover, to learn), on the topic page under the existing «perché» line and on the practice page's skill-status line (`#skill-missing`, redrawn after each answer: the payload's `skill.missing_it`). Examples: «Ti mancano 2 esercizi giusti senza aiuto.», «Ti manca un altro giorno: torna domani e fanne uno giusto senza aiuto.», «Ti manca un esercizio giusto senza aiuto di quelli da scrivere, abbinare o mettere in ordine.» (hard to guess is `Diagnosis::Rules::V1.low_guess?`: a written answer, an ordering or a matching of 4 rows or more; «più lungo» would be false for a short written answer). The count of exercises is the larger of the 3 in all and the 2 hard to guess still lacking; the second day is said only once one day is done. The fold's `why` of an `in_study` skill gains `low` (the hard-to-guess fingerprints so far, at most 2) to say it; the `why` line itself is unchanged. A skill demonstrated, consolidated or «da ripassare» (its own line already says what to do) shows no missing line.
  3. **Oggi.** The «Riprendi» card has one line for the topic (`today.close_line`, `Practice::Messages.close_line`): the exercises still to do in the skill nearest to done, else «Per chiuderlo: torna domani e rifai un esercizio senza aiuto.»; nothing when nothing is missing. No colour-only cue: the lines are text.
- **Rule unchanged:** the numbers and the fold of `practice/3` are the same (`low` is a report of what the fold already counted); a topic still closes only when every skill is demonstrated. Topics are not removed from Oggi by the student's wish: the page now says what closes them.
- **The matching line (same day):** above a matching that reuses its answers the page said «Scegli per ogni voce la risposta giusta. Una risposta può servire per più voci.»; on the English judge items, now labelled «scritta bene» / «con un errore», «giusta» brought back the word the labels avoid (reviews 4805-4811). It now reads «Per ogni voce scegli una risposta. La stessa risposta può servire per più voci.» (`matching_reuse_label`).
- **Why:** a student with reading difficulties saw «da riprendere» on a topic he believed finished and could not tell what was left; the page must say it in a sentence.
- **Status:** implemented.
- **Tests:** `test/integration/close_hint_test.rb` (a skill in study with 2 right on one day: the missing lines on the topic page, the practice page and Oggi; a demonstrated skill none; the topic line), `test/lib/practice/fold_test.rb` (`low` in the why).

## D-341 · 2026-11-17 · a skill is demonstrated on one day

- **Design ref:** D-235 and rules `practice/3` section 5 (`docs/rules/practice-3.md`, the two-days condition), D-340 (what is still needed to close a topic).
- **The operator's words (2026-11-17):** «mi sembra troppo aspettare 2gg, facciamo anche sullo stesso giorno».
- **We do:** a skill is demonstrated when the student has answered right without help 3 distinct exercises, 2 of them hard to guess (low guess), on one day or on several. Rules `practice/4` (`docs/rules/practice-4.md`, `lib/practice/rules/v4.rb`, `Practice::Rules::V4`): `DEMONSTRATE_DISTINCT_DAYS` is removed, with no replacement; every other constant is as in version 3. A change of any constant is a new rules version, so this has a D- entry.
  1. **The fold** (`Practice::Fold`): `in_study` gives `demonstrated` at the first try after which the unaided right tries cover 3 distinct fingerprints, 2 of them low guess. The why of `in_study` loses `d` (`{code: :in_study, n:, low:}`); the why of `demonstrated` loses `days`.
  2. **The texts** (`config/locales/course.it.yml`): `why.in_study` «Corrette senza aiuto: %{n} su 3.»; `why.demonstrated` «Dimostrata il %{date}: 3 esercizi giusti senza aiuto.»; `practice.close_rule` «Per chiudere l'argomento: in ogni abilità, 3 esercizi giusti senza aiuto, almeno 2 da scrivere, abbinare o mettere in ordine.» (the hard-to-guess part is named in the rule too: without it, 3 right choices would look enough).
  3. **D-340's day line goes:** `practice.missing.day` and `today.close_line.day` are removed with their code in `Practice::Messages` (`missing`, `missing_it`, `close_line`): only exercises are missing now.
- **What stays:** 3 right without help, 2 of them hard to guess; consolidation 14 days after the demonstration, on a fresh exercise right without help, which still checks that he remembers; `to_review` after a wrong try without help.
- **Not retroactive in the ledger:** no row is rewritten. The states are derived, so they are re-derived by the new rules at the next read: a skill with 3 right on one day and 2 hard to guess reads as demonstrated now. Serves already stored keep `rules_version` `practice/3`; nothing compares it with the current version, and new serves record `practice/4`.
- **Why:** waiting for a second day made the student come back to repeat exercises he had already done right; the consolidation 14 days later is the check that he remembers.
- **Status:** implemented.
- **Tests:** `test/lib/practice/fold_test.rb` (3 distinct right unaided with 2 low guess on the same day: demonstrated; with 1 low guess: still in study), `test/integration/close_hint_test.rb`, `test/models/practice/messages_test.rb`, `test/models/practice/answer_recorder_test.rb`, `test/lib/practice/rules_test.rb` (the drift test on `practice-4.md`).

## D-342 · 2026-11-17 · the student answers the teacher's reply (comment threads)

- **Design ref:** D-304 (comments anywhere, the events and the derived state), D-327 (the comments over the API), D-334 (who did what).
- **The operator's words (2026-11-17):** the student must be able to answer the teacher's replies to his comments, as a thread.
- **We do:** a comment becomes a conversation: his first text, the teacher's `reply` events and his new `student_reply` events, in id order (`Comment#thread`).
  1. **One new kind of event, `student_reply`** (migration `20261117110000_add_student_reply_comment_event`, rebuilt as in D-324 with the append-only triggers installed again and the foreign keys checked, `db/structure.sql` updated): origin `student`, actor the student's key, `text_it` 1..500 characters (`Comment::TEXT_MAX`). The CHECKs: `comment_events_kind` gains it; `comment_events_seen_by_student` is `(kind IN ('reply_seen','student_reply')) = (origin = 'student')`, so a student kind comes only from the student and the student writes no other kind; `comment_events_student_reply_text` asks for the text. No row is rewritten.
  2. **The state stays derived** (`Comment#state`): if the latest message of the thread is a `student_reply`, the comment needs the teacher again: `sent`, or `read` if a `read` follows it; a `student_reply` after a `resolved` reopens the comment the same way. Otherwise the state is as before. `unread_reply?` is still about the teacher's replies after the last `reply_seen`. The teacher's inbox counts and filters read the derived state, so such a comment is in «Nuovi» or «Letti»; `Comments::Responder` and `Comments::Console` (reply, resolve, reopen, read) are unchanged.
  3. **The student's door** (`Comments::StudentReply`, `POST /comments/:id/reply`, `CommentsController#reply`): the student's own comment only (another's is a 404), the student listener, CSRF, the teacher, a guest and the preview refused (403, or no route); only on a comment with at least one teacher reply; the text trimmed, 1..500 characters; idempotent on a hidden `client_reply_id` of the form (the event's `request_id`, one per student, like `client_comment_id`). A plain form post with a redirect back to `/comments#comment-ID` and a confirmation «Inviato: il docente lo vedrà.»; no outbox. A comment that is closed takes a follow-up too (it reopens).
  4. **The pages:** «I miei commenti» draws the thread in order, each message labelled «Hai scritto» or «Il docente ha risposto», and under a comment with a teacher reply the form «Rispondi» (500 characters, «Invia»); the teacher's `/teacher/comments` shows the follow-ups in the history of each comment («Lo studente ha risposto»); `bin/rails banco:comments:show` prints them; `GET /api/v1/comments` and `/:id` show them as events (`kind: student_reply`, `origin: student`, `text_it`, `created_at`), `docs/api.md` and `docs/bot.md` say so. The activity feed still leaves out the student's own events.
- **Not done:** no notice to the teacher beyond the state (the comment is «Nuovo» again, as for any comment); no follow-up before a teacher reply; no edit or delete of a follow-up (append-only); no new API route to write one (the student writes it on his page).
- **Why:** a reply from the teacher left the student with no way to say that he still did not understand, or to say thanks, except by writing a new comment out of context.
- **Status:** implemented.
- **Tests:** `test/models/comment_test.rb` (the CHECKs of the new kind, the state after a follow-up, after resolved and a follow-up, the thread, `unread_reply?`), `test/integration/comments_test.rb` (the student's post and its refusals, the thread on both pages, the teacher's actions on such a comment, the API row and the console).

## D-343 · 2026-11-17 · the subjects' names at the student's school; the settings gear

- **Design ref:** D-023 (every table append-only: `subjects` rejects UPDATE), D-307 (the student's shell and its icons), D-246 (the icon list `config/banco/icons.yml`).
- **The student's words (2026-11-17, passed on by the operator, who approved all three changes):** three subjects have other names at his school, [the school], where he takes the exam; the «Impostazioni» menu item shows a «T» instead of the classic gear; and the English lesson title «Numerabili e non numerabili: some, any, much, many e gli altri» is not appropriate.
- **We do:**
  1. **The names of the school's programme:** chemistry is «Scienze integrate – Chimica», biology «Scienze integrate – Biologia», geography «Geografia economica». The other eight keep their names.
  2. **Why a locale:** `subjects` is append-only (triggers block UPDATE and DELETE), so `subjects.name_it` stays the seed name of `db/seeds.rb` and cannot be corrected in place. The display names are texts in git, `config/locales/subjects.it.yml` (`it.subjects.display_name_it.<key>`, the key ends in `_it` because it holds Italian text); `Subject#name_it` returns the locale text when there is one, else the column. Every page, API reply and search text reads the name through the method: the pages, the teacher's views and menus, the course, progress, status and diagnosis payloads, the search builders; `SearchHelper#search_subject_name` no longer plucks the column. The lesson page's lower-case subject names (`lesson2.subject.*` in `config/locales/lesson.it.yml`, «Lezione di …») follow the same three names.
  3. **Long names wrap:** «Scienze integrate – Chimica» is longer than any old name. The subject lists (Oggi, Materie, the entry tests) let it wrap (`overflow-wrap`), the teacher's subject switcher is as wide as its longest name up to 20 rem or the screen, and the comments' subject filter chips grow in height; nothing is cut with an ellipsis.
  4. **The gear:** `nav-settings` points to the Lucide `settings` (the gear) instead of `type`; `settings.svg` is vendored under `public/vendor/lucide@1.54.0/icons/` (lucide-static 1.54.0) and the sprite is rebuilt with `bin/build-icons`. `text-settings` («Testo e colori», the text size and colour panel) stays on `type`.
- **Not done:** no data migration and no change of the seeds (they are the base names); the English lesson title is a content change, not made by this entry.
- **Why:** the student reads the names of his school on his exam programme, and a «T» for settings is not what he looks for; the ledger stays append-only.
- **Status:** implemented.
- **Tests:** `test/models/subject_test.rb` (the school's name for the three subjects, the column for the others, the search helper), `test/integration/course_pages_test.rb` (Materie, Materia and Oggi print the name of `Subject#name_it`), `test/integration/student_progress_api_test.rb` (the entry test of geography, on the page and over the API).

## D-344 · 2026-11-17 · Scienze motorie, the twelfth subject

- **Design ref:** D-023 (every table append-only: `subjects` accepts an insert), D-002 and D-298 (the entry test of all the subjects together), D-246 and D-264 (the palette and the icons by subject), D-324 (the official programme `ufficiale-2026-27`, `course.extra_source`), D-343 (the names of the subjects).
- **The student's words (2026-11-17, passed on by the operator):** «Manca scienze motorie dalla pagina». The ministerial order on the idoneità exams (DM 218/2025, art. 6, comma 1) has the candidate take all the subjects of the piano di studi, so the subject is part of what he prepares.
- **We do:**
  1. **The subject:** `physical_education`, «Scienze motorie», position 12 (after chemistry), theory and exercises only: the practical part (gym, tests, workouts) stays outside the app. The row comes from the migration `20261117120000_add_physical_education_subject` (an insert that does nothing when the key is there, as `subjects` is append-only: no update, no delete, and `down` refuses) and from `db/seeds.rb` (the same name and position); `db/structure.sql` gains only the migration version.
  2. **Every list of subjects names it:** the JSON schemas (`skill_graph`, `lesson`, `item`, `blueprint`, `topic`, `course`: the subject enums and the skill-key patterns), `config/banco/lesson_palette.yml` (accent `#f7d0c9` cream and `#4d2621` dark; the roles `cause`, `purpose`, `time` take the colours, icons and shapes of the italian ones with `same_as`; four step verbs), `config/banco/icons.yml` (the subject icon `subject-physical-education` is Lucide `dumbbell`, vendored from lucide-static 1.54.0 with its SHA256 line; a list of nine content icons), the sprites and `lesson_roles.css` / `palette.js` rebuilt with `bin/build-icons` and `bin/build-palette`, `StudentUiHelper::SUBJECT_ICONS`, `SearchHelper::SUBJECTS`, the lesson locale. No physics or chemistry diagram type applies to it and no foreign language (`Lessons::Lang`). `lib/pages_kit/1.0` is a released, locked kit and does not change.
  3. **No entry test:** `Subject::WITHOUT_ENTRY_TEST` (`physical_education`) and `Subject#entry_test?`, `Subject.with_entry_test`. It has no blueprint and never will: `Diagnosis::Availability` (the entry test list, Oggi's block) already lists only the subjects with a blueprint; the release of the diagnosis (`Teacher::Dashboard#release`, `DecisionRecorder#release_diagnosis`) and the report of all subjects (`Diagnosis::Report.call`) count only the subjects with an entry test, so it does not wait for a test it cannot have; `Diagnosis::Rules::V1::SUBJECTS` (rules `diagnosis/1`) stays at the eleven. The teacher's dashboard says «Nessun test d'ingresso.» in its test cell instead of «Da scrivere.», shows no diagnosis line for the student and no link to a test; the menu offers none; the test page says it has no entry test; `SubjectStage` is `approved` with the approved graph alone (no blueprint is needed), `awaiting_teacher` once the graph is in.
  4. **The official programme is its programme:** the seconda programme of the school has no section for it; the official one (`course.extra_source`, the section «Scienze motorie e sportive») does. `config/banco/validation_rules.yml` gains `course.official_programme_subjects: [physical_education]` (rules version 11, no number changes): for those subjects a `taught_in` ref on `ufficiale-2026-27` is the programme ref of a course skill (no `E-COURSE-EXTRA-SKILL`: `ripasso`, `ponte` and `lezione` topics may hold it, `Validation::CourseChecks.extra_only`), of a lesson (`taught_in` for a `lezione`, `needed_by` for a `ripasso` and a `ponte`, and a `ripasso` needs no ref on the previous year's programme, which has no line for it: `Validation::LessonChecks.refs`) and of a graph skill (`needed_by`, `Validation::GraphChecks.needed_by`); `TopicsController` lists the official lines the lesson cites; `Validation::Rules.programme_source(subject)` and `.official_programme_subject?` name the rule once. `GET /api/v1/subjects/physical_education/skill-graph/coverage` answers `E-NOT-FOUND` (no range of the previous year's programme to cover).
  5. **The authors' brief:** `briefs/lesson-physical-education.md` (theory only; short cards, lists and small tables, one idea per card; school-level health facts, no medical advice, no diet; the five topics: apparato locomotore, capacità motorie e allenamento, sport di squadra (pallavolo e pallacanestro), atletica leggera, salute e sport; practice items of choice, matching of 4 rows or more, ordering and short written answers so that a skill can be demonstrated); `briefs/skill-graph.md` and `briefs/course.md` say how the subject cites the official programme.
- **Not done:** no content (skill graph, course map, lessons and practice items are written later by the content agents through `banco`); no entry test, no blueprint; no teacher's graph map for the official lines (`Teacher::GraphMapContext` still reads the seconda `needed_by` lines only); no change to the student's pages (a subject without a released course is not listed).
- **Why:** the exam covers all the subjects of the piano di studi and the page had eleven; a twelfth subject with its own test would have blocked the release of the diagnosis and shown the teacher a test to write that does not exist.
- **Status:** implemented.
- **Tests:** `test/models/physical_education_subject_test.rb` (the seeds, the migration, no entry test, the schema enums and patterns, the palette, the icons, the accent), `test/integration/physical_education_pages_test.rb` (the teacher's dashboard and pages, the stage, the release count, the entry test list and the report), `test/validation/official_programme_test.rb` (course map, lessons and graph with the official programme; the same map for another subject is still `E-COURSE-EXTRA-SKILL`), and the subject lists of `prod_seeds_test`, `brief_test`, `lesson_palette_test`, `lesson_icons_test`.

## D-345 · 2026-11-17 · Educazione civica: a view in Materie over topics of other subjects

- **Design ref:** D-324 (extra topics: optional, apart, never suggested by Oggi), D-326 (progress in topics: mandatory and optional), D-309 (the preview under `/teacher/preview`, `spath`), D-343 (the subjects' names).
- **The student's words (2026-11-17, passed on by the operator):** «Manca educazione civica tra le materie».
- **Law:** L. 92/2019 makes Educazione civica a transversal teaching, not a subject with its own marks; the Linee guida of DM 183/2024 name three nuclei: Costituzione; Sviluppo economico e sostenibilità; Cittadinanza digitale.
- **Options:** A, a view that gathers topics that already exist; B, a thirteenth subject with its own content. The operator chose **A**: optional but visible, no content change.
- **We do:**
  1. **The list in git, `config/banco/civics.yml`:** the three nuclei (`key`, `title_it`, a one-line `intro_it`) and, in page order, the lesson keys of the topics each gathers (law_economics, geography, business, biology, computer_science, italian). A key is a lesson key of any kind; the file is the only place that says what belongs to a nucleus, and adding a topic is a line there.
  2. **The read model `Course::Civics`:** built only from `Course::StudentView` of the acting student (official, trial, or the preview with its view): each nucleus keeps the topics this student can see, a key he cannot see is skipped silently, a nucleus with none is not drawn. Each entry carries its `SubjectView`, its `TopicView` (kind programme or extra) and the status the subject page shows (`StudentView#status`). No query of its own on the ledger.
  3. **Materie:** after the subjects, a card «Educazione civica» marked «Facoltativo · in più materie», with a one-line explanation and «N argomenti», linking to the page. Not a subject: no progress lines, no bar; the topics keep counting once, in their own subject (D-326). Shown only when at least one topic is visible.
  4. **The page `GET /civics`** (and `/teacher/preview/civics`, route in the `course_pages` concern, `spath`): «Educazione civica», the intro «Non è una materia a sé: sono argomenti di altre materie. Sono facoltativi qui; quelli del programma li trovi anche nella loro materia.», one section per nucleus, the rows of the Materia (`course/_topic_row`, without the number: the chip and the name of the subject instead) linking to the existing topic page. 404 when this student sees no topic of the list; 403 for the teacher and a guest as on the other student pages. The menu stays as it is (Materie is current on this page).
  5. **Oggi:** unchanged. It never suggests, resumes or counts through this view.
- **Not done:** no content, no exercises, no mark or test of Educazione civica, nothing becomes mandatory; no new menu item; the nuclei have no progress of their own.
- **Why:** the student looked for Educazione civica among the subjects and did not find it; the topics are there, scattered. The law makes it transversal, so a view over them says the truth and adds no new burden.
- **Status:** implemented.
- **Tests:** `test/integration/civics_view_test.rb` (the card, the page by nucleus with subject and status, an invisible topic skipped, a draft only for the trial student, progress and Oggi unchanged, the preview path and its view, the refusals, and the keys of `civics.yml` well formed and unique).

## D-346 · 2026-11-17 · the teacher bot reads the student's practice attempts

- **Design ref:** D-327 (the public API: token roles, the teacher token), D-328 (the teacher's pages and the student's progress as JSON; per-skill counts only), D-304 (comments and their anchors), D-317 (every answer is accepted in the entry test; `undetermined`), D-337 (drafts), D-339 («Fai controllare», `contested`), D-254 (the lesson ledger, read only by `Lessons::Progress`), D-299 (search and its doors), firm rule 4 (append-only).
- **The operator's words (2026-11-17):** the teacher bot judges the student's practice, exercise by exercise (52 tries on 6 skills in the first practice, many comments reporting errors): is a wrong answer the student's error, a software or content error, or something else? It can verify the items (keys, error catalogues) but cannot see what the student answered, only per-skill counts, and an anchor `row:3` means the 3rd row of an order the bot cannot see. Later the same day: it must read the entry test's answers and the answers to the checks inside the lessons too.
- **We do (read-only, for a `teacher` token alone):**
  1. **The list:** `GET /api/v1/students/:student/attempts` (`banco attempts`), oldest first, one list over three kinds (`kind=practice|diagnosis|lesson`, default all). Filters `subject`, `topic`, `skill`, `item` (key), `since`, `until` (a date is its first or last moment, UTC), `outcome`, `serve`, `comment`; a kind that cannot hold a filter has no row for it. Pagination as the other lists: `limit` (default 100, at most 500), `total`, `more` and a cursor, `after`, which is the `ref` (`practice-12`, `diagnosis-7`, `lesson-31`) of the last row. A row: the id and `ref`, `at`, subject, topic, skill, item key and `revision_id`, the instance, the answer **exactly as given**, the outcome and the matched error code, and by kind: the serve, try number, hints shown before it, solution requested and seconds (practice); the run, sitting, evidence and `unreadable` (entry test); the card, block, exercise/step/part, try number and `right`/`wrong` (lesson check). An attempt on a superseded item revision is listed (`superseded`, `latest_revision_id`).
  2. **The outcome is the engine's, not a second opinion:** practice, `Practice::Instances.grade` (correct, correct_aided, typical_error, unrecognised, form, near_miss, undetermined, contested, and `not_a_try`/`ungraded` for a stored text that is no try); entry test, the stored latest `attempt_gradings` verdict with its `Grading::Evidence` class; lesson, the verdict `Lessons::CheckAnswer` stored. Nothing is regraded, nothing recomputed from a new rule.
  3. **The detail:** `GET /api/v1/students/:student/attempts/:ref` (`banco attempts show REF`). The exercise **as the student saw it**: the stored display re-keyed with the shown order the serve logged (practice: `practice_serves.shown_order_json` and `id_map_json`, replayed with `Diagnosis::Rekey.replay` through `Items::Part`, as `PracticeController` does; entry test: `item_served` through `Diagnosis::ItemPresenter`; lesson check: `Lessons::Checks.rekey` with the student's own seed, through `Lessons::CheckAnswer#located`), the shown order and the id map, the key and its words, the answer in words, the error catalogue and the matched codes, the stored gradings; for a practice try the hints (shown before this try), the events, the serve's tries, the draft (D-337) and the refused texts.
  4. **Anchors and comments:** the anchor `row:N` / `option:N` names the Nth of the **shown** column; `Attempts::Shown#anchor_row` resolves it through the shown order to the shown id, the stored id and the text, and says what the try did with it (an ordering: where the student put it and where the key has it; a matching: the pair given and the key's; a choice: chosen, is key). `comment=ID` on the list resolves a comment's refs to its answers (`practice_serve_id`, else `item_instance_id`; `served_event_id`; a lesson comment's card and block); `comment=ID` on the detail keeps that comment and its `anchor_row`.
  5. **Search:** `GET /api/v1/search?kind=student_answer[&student=KEY]` is open to a `teacher` token only (`Search::Scope::Agent.new(answers_for:)`, the teacher console's answers visibility: one student, lexical, never a model); `bot_read` and every other token keep `404 E-NOT-FOUND` for that kind; without that kind the search is the content search as before. A row gains `student`, `at` and `attempt` (the ref).
  6. **Where the code is:** `Api::V1::AttemptsController`, `Attempts::Log` (the three sources, the merge and the cursor), `Practice::AttemptLog`, `Attempts::DiagnosisLog`, `Attempts::LessonLog`, `Attempts::Shown`, `Attempts::InstanceBlock`, `Attempts::Comments`; the lesson ledger stays read only by `Lessons::Progress` (`check_index`, `check_tries`); `contract/commands.json` (`attempts`, `attempts show`, and `--student` on `search`) and `cli/cmd_attempts.go`.
- **Not done / must not change:** no write endpoint, no new decision kind, no change to the decision recorder, firm rule 2, grading, the outcomes or the practice rules (`practice/4`); nothing the student sees changes. A read records nothing (no event, no decision; the token's renewal is the one row any public token's request may write, D-330). `bot_read`, `ci` and the content agents are `403 E-AUTH` (`token_role`) on both routes. The student's answers are never in git, in a fixture from production, and nothing written here logs one; the tests use invented data. The voided revisions of `void_revision_attempts` are listed, not dropped: the log is the ledger. The teacher's preview and the warm-up are not the student's answers and are not listed. The lesson checks are not in the search index.
- **Why:** the teacher's judgement of «student's error or ours» needs the answer, the key in the same ids and the order the student saw; the counts cannot give it. One read model of the ledger keeps the bot's view and the teacher's pages from drifting, and a teacher-only door keeps a minor's words from the tokens that need none of them.
- **Status:** implemented.
- **Tests:** `test/integration/attempts_api_test.rb` (the three kinds with every field, the refusals of `bot_read`, `ci` and the content agents, the filters, the superseded revision, the comment filter and the anchor row, the detail of each kind, nothing recorded by a read), `test/integration/search_api_test.rb` (teacher against `bot_read` for `student_answer`), `cli/cmd_attempts_test.go`.

## D-347 · 2026-11-17 · icon sprites carry a version in their URL

- **Design ref:** D-246 and D-264 (the icon sprites, `bin/build-icons`), D-343 (the settings gear), D-335 (the render host waits for the sprites), D-307 (the student's shell and its icons).
- **The student's words (2026-11-17, passed on by the operator), about the gear of D-343:** «non è vero, o almeno non mi è arrivata la nuova versione»: «Impostazioni» still shows the «T».
- **Cause:** the sprites (`public/vendor/lucide@1.54.0/banco-sprite.svg` and `banco-sprite-SUBJECT.svg`) were named at fixed URLs, and production serves `public/` with `cache-control: public, max-age=1 year` (`config/environments/production.rb`). A browser that had loaded the sprite once never asked again, so D-343's rebuilt sprite (the gear) never reached it. The same would have happened to every later icon change.
- **We do:**
  1. **A version in the address:** every sprite URL ends `?v=` plus the first 12 hex digits of the SHA-256 of the file's bytes: `/vendor/lucide@1.54.0/banco-sprite.svg?v=438f981bb785#nav-settings`. The file is the same, the URL changes whenever its bytes change, so the browser fetches the new one and keeps the old cache for the unchanged ones. Nothing else about caching changes (the one-year header stays; `public/` is still served as it was).
  2. **The server's pages:** `Banco::Sprites` (`lib/banco/sprites.rb`, required at boot) computes the href of a sprite once per process from the file; `ui_icon`, `comment_icon` and `search_icon` use `Banco::Sprites.icon_href`, so every layout and page of the student and the teacher (and the render hosts, which draw with the same helpers) carries it.
  3. **The browser's code:** `bin/build-icons` also writes `app/javascript/lesson/sprites.js` (the digest of each sprite, the same 12 digits) and `bin/build-icons --check` covers it like the sprites and `SHA256SUMS`; `app/javascript/lesson/sprite.js` builds the address (`spriteUrl`), used by `lesson/dom.js` (`spriteHref`, the lesson renderer and its diagrams) and by `practice_controller.js`. No layout prints a version and no page needs to be told: the module is part of the importmap, so it is fingerprinted by Propshaft and changes with the sprites.
- **Not done:** no change to the cache header, to the sprites' content or to the icons; no rename of the files; a development server reads the digests once, so it needs a restart after `bin/build-icons`.
- **Why:** an icon that changes in git must change on the student's phone; a version in the URL is the boring answer that needs no cache purge and no change of the server's headers.
- **Status:** implemented.
- **Tests:** `test/integration/sprite_version_test.rb` (a student page's icons end with `?v=` and the digest of the current file; the digest follows the file's bytes, stubbed; every sprite's digest is the file's; `sprites.js` agrees with the files), `app/javascript/lesson/test/sprite_href.test.mjs` (the address builder: structural sprite, a subject's own, the fallback, a missing version is an error), `test/system/lesson2_page_test.rb` (the badge icons' href), `bin/build-icons --check`.

## D-348 · 2026-11-17 · clearer practice: the list's words, «esercizio simile», the pool that runs out, «Dal test: da ripassare»

- **Design ref:** D-337 and D-339 (the list of exercises and its statuses), D-235 and rules `practice/4` section 7 (serving), D-341 (how a rules version is made), D-340 (the lines that explain what is still missing), D-333 (the digest), D-328 (the progress endpoints).
- **The student's words (2026-11-17, passed on by the operator):** «Non passa all'esercizio seguente»; «non deve essere da riprovare in quanto quell'esercizio è ed era finito» (an exercise he had answered and closed with the solution was flagged as unfinished).
- **The operator's words (2026-11-17):** «dobbiamo stare attenti a non rifare sempre gli stessi esercizi: se non ce ne sono più disponibili va detto e salvato».
- **We do:**
  1. **The list's words** (`Practice::Exercises#status`, `config/locales/course.it.yml`): «Fatto» when a serve of the exercise closed correct; «Finito: con la soluzione» when a serve with a try or a shown solution closed or was abandoned without a right answer and a solution was shown; «Finito» for the same without a solution; «Da finire» for an open serve with a try or a typed draft (the two old states `retry` and `left` become `unfinished`); «Saltato» and «Da fare» as before. The codes are `done`, `finished_solution`, `finished`, `unfinished`, `skipped`, `todo` (`tried` is gone). «Rifai» shows on `done`, `finished` and `finished_solution`. The counters `done` and `tried` of an entry are unchanged.
  2. **The same exercise again, said on screen** (`Practice::Repeat`, the serve body's `reason_it`): the selector keeps the student on the current item until it has `ADVANCE_AFTER_CORRECT_UNAIDED` (2) right tries without help, and after a solution offers a similar instance, so he met the same kind of exercise three times and thought the app was stuck. When the served instance is of the same item as the previous serve of the skill, its reason is `next` or `after_solution`, and the item has fewer than that many such tries, `reason_it` is «Ti propongo un esercizio simile: per passare al prossimo ne servono 2 giusti.» (the number is the rules constant; it takes the place of «Prova un esercizio simile» after a solution). An exercise the student chose from the list or with «Rifai» never carries it. A reload of the page says it again for the same open serve, as it is computed, not stored.
  3. **No silent repeats when the pool runs out** (`Practice::Selector`, rules `practice/5`): when no instance of the skill's pinned items is unseen, the selector no longer picks a seen one on its own (the `reseen` fallback of the automatic choice is gone). `next` answers `Practice::Selector::EXHAUSTED`, `POST /practice/serves` answers `{type: "exhausted", message_it, note_it, skill}` and the page says «Hai visto tutti gli esercizi di questa abilità. Ne stiamo preparando altri.» and «Puoi rifare un esercizio dalla lista: non conta per dimostrare l'abilità.», with «Torna all'argomento». An open serve of the skill is still resumed first. Choosing an exercise (the list, «Rifai», `item`) keeps the old rule: its oldest instance, reason `reseen`, aided, not counted. The fact is recorded once per student, topic revision and skill in the new append-only table `practice_pool_exhaustions` (migration `20261117130000`, unique index on the three, `Banco::AppendOnly`; model `PracticePoolExhaustion.record!`), inside the serving transaction.
  4. **The teacher sees it:** a line per exhausted skill on the practice page of the subject (`Teacher::PracticeProgress`, `teacher.practice.pool_exhausted`, `data-pool-exhausted`); `pool_exhausted_at` (ISO time of the first exhaustion on any topic revision, `null` otherwise) on every skill of `GET /api/v1/subjects/:subject/practice/progress` (`Course::ProgressView`) and on every skill of `GET /api/v1/students/:key/progress`, which `GET /api/v1/digest` carries as its `progress` part (the digest lists skills, not practice items; no other part changes). The contract example `practice-progress.official.json` shows the field.
  5. **Rules `practice/5`** (as D-341 made `practice/4`): `lib/practice/rules/v5.rb` (`Practice::Rules::V5`, same constants as version 4), `docs/rules/practice-5.md` (section 7 rules 1, 8 and the new 10; `practice-4.md` stays as the record), every reference moved (`V4` to `V5`, `practice/4` to `practice/5`), the drift test `test/lib/practice/rules_test.rb`, the contract example's `rules_version`. The selection rule changed, so it is a new version: new serves record `practice/5`, stored serves keep their version, no state is re-derived differently (the fold and the numbers are untouched).
  6. **«Da riprendere» for the student** becomes «Dal test: da ripassare» (state `to_recover`, topic tag, Oggi's reason «Dal test è risultata da ripassare: …», the skill's why «Dal test d'ingresso: da ripassare.», Materia's «Dal test: da ripassare, ancora senza argomento: …», the entry test's results «Da ripassare»). The first tag of each kind on Oggi, Materia and the topic page carries one line (`recover_note_once`, `data-recover-note`): «Vuol dire che nel test d'ingresso questa parte non era sicura: si chiude con gli esercizi.» A topic whose skills are only `to_review` (a wrong answer after a demonstration, not the test) keeps «Da ripassare» with its own line («Vuol dire che l'avevi capita, ma di recente hai sbagliato: si chiude con gli esercizi.»): the test's name would be false there (`Practice::Today.recover_kind`). The teacher's own texts keep «Da riprendere» (`teacher.practice.without_topic`); the states shared with the teacher's pages (`states.to_recover`) read the new words there too.
- **Not done:** no new exercises (the pool is the authors' work: the row tells the teacher where it is missing); no change of the fold, the numbers, the grading or what counts to demonstrate; the «esercizio simile» line is not stored, so a reload after choosing the same item again from the list may say it (it cannot tell a chosen serve from a selected one).
- **Why:** a closed exercise is finished, whatever way it closed; the page must say why the same kind of exercise comes back; and running out of exercises must be said to the student and recorded for the teacher, not hidden by serving old ones.
- **Status:** implemented.
- **Tests:** `test/integration/practice_navigation_test.rb` (the statuses, «esercizio simile» only when the item repeats, exhaustion: no automatic serve, the message, one row, the list and «Rifai», the teacher's page), `test/models/practice/selector_test.rb` and `test/lib/practice/properties_test.rb` (no seen instance on its own, `reseen` on a chosen item, one row, a resumed open serve), `test/integration/course_api_test.rb` and `test/integration/digest_api_test.rb` (`pool_exhausted_at`), `test/integration/recover_wording_test.rb`, `test/lib/practice/today_test.rb`, `test/models/practice/messages_test.rb`, `test/lib/practice/rules_test.rb` (the drift test on `practice-5.md`), `test/models/append_only_test.rb` via `test/support/ledger_rows.rb`, `test/system/practice_flow_test.rb`.

## D-349 · 2026-11-17 · «I miei commenti» like a mailbox and a chat; the teacher's answer time

- **Design ref:** D-304 (comments anywhere), D-305 (their look), D-342 (the thread and the student's follow-up), D-304's derived state (`Comment#state`), `items/outbox.js` (the outbox that the comment box already uses).
- **The student's words (2026-11-17):** about «I miei commenti»: «non ha senso ed è poco pratico»; about the answers: «Non ricevo le risposte», «arrivano raramente e alcune dopo mesi». The model he knows is Gmail (the list) and WhatsApp (the conversation).
- **We do:**
  1. **The inbox** (`GET /comments`, `Comments::StudentInbox`): one row per comment, the newest activity first (the last message of the thread, so a follow-up or a reply brings it up); each row has the place's icon and title, a one-line preview of the LAST message with its author («Tu:» or «Docente:»; a first message without words shows its reason), the time («oggi 15:40», «ieri», «12 nov»), the state chip, and, when a teacher message is not seen yet (`Comment#unread_reply?`, unchanged), bold text and a dot. Tabs with counts: «Tutti», «Risposte nuove» (unseen teacher message), «In attesa» (state sent or read: the teacher has the move), «Chiusi» (a comment can be in two tabs); an empty state for each tab; an unknown `?tab=` is «Tutti». **Opening the list no longer marks anything seen.**
  2. **The conversation** (`GET /comments/:id`, another student's or an unknown id is a 404): the place at the top (its title, the selected words, a link «Vai a dove l'hai scritto» only when that page still exists for the student: today, settings, search, and subject, topic, lesson with its card, practice when the course shows it), the messages as bubbles (student right, teacher left), the time under each, a separator for each day («Oggi», «Ieri», «12 novembre»), the composer at the bottom. **Opening it records `reply_seen`** (a student's row, once per unseen reply), so the menu badge and the dot go away. Without a teacher reply there is no composer and the page says «In attesa della risposta del docente.» (the rule of D-342 is unchanged: a follow-up only after a reply; a closed comment takes one and reopens). The pages' address `/comments/:id` is a page of kind `comments` for the comment box.
  3. **Sending** (`comment_thread_controller.js`): the textarea grows; on a computer Enter sends and Shift+Enter is a new line, on a phone (`hover: none` and `pointer: coarse`) Enter is a new line and «Invia» sends; at most 500 characters. The message goes to a local outbox first (`banco.routbox.<comment id>.`, the same `items/outbox.js`; a prefix that does not start with the comment box's `banco.coutbox.`, so no page sends it to the wrong address), the bubble shows at once («Invio…»), then the server's answer makes it a sent bubble with its time; a network failure leaves the bubble with «Non inviato. Tocca per riprovare.» and the entry in the outbox (it goes out when the network is back, or on a tap, or when the conversation is opened again); a refusal of the server («invalid») gives the text back to the composer with the reason. The view scrolls to the newest. Without script the form posts as in D-342 and the page is drawn again with the confirmation.
  4. **The server**: `POST /comments/:id/reply` answers JSON when asked (`Accept: application/json`): `{status: "recorded", at}` (also for a repeat of the same `client_reply_id`), `{status: "invalid", error}` or `{status: "missing"}` with 404; the plain form is redirected to `/comments/:id` (it was `/comments#comment-ID`). Idempotent as before, everything append-only, the state derived as in D-342; no migration.
  5. **Layout**: a phone shows the list or the conversation (with a back arrow); from 1000 px (62.5rem) the list is on the left and the conversation on the right, in both pages. No new colour or icon; the sizes are in rem.
  6. **The answer time**: `config/banco/comments.yml` `reply_within_hours: 24` is the one place of the number (`Comments::ReplyWindow`). Both of the student's pages say «Il docente risponde entro un giorno.». The teacher's inbox says how long each waiting comment has waited («In attesa da 5 ore»: the student has the last word and it is not closed), marks those over the limit «In ritardo» and counts them at the top («In ritardo: N», also in the guest's counts: `Comments::Inbox.counts["late"]`). The dashboard's count is unchanged (new comments).
- **Not done:** no push or e-mail to the student when the teacher answers (he sees the badge and the dot); no live refresh of an open conversation; no read receipts for the teacher; no edit or delete of a message (append-only); no change to what a comment is or to how it is written (the «Commenta» box).
- **Why:** one long page with every thread and a form under each did not read like anything he knew; a reply was easy to miss and nothing told him when to expect one. The list says at once where something new is and what is waiting; the conversation is the one thing a phone user already knows how to use; the stated time makes a slow answer visible to him and to the teacher.
- **Status:** implemented.
- **Tests:** `test/integration/comments_test.rb` (the inbox's order, the preview and the time, the tabs and their counts, unseen only, the list marking nothing, the conversation marking `reply_seen`, the bubbles, the place link, the JSON reply and its refusals, the refusals for another student, the teacher, a guest, an unmapped login and the preview, the teacher's «In ritardo» and the one config), `test/system/comments_v2_test.rb` (inbox, conversation, Enter sends, Shift+Enter, the failure and the outbox, the phone with the back arrow), `test/system/comments_ui_test.rb`.

## D-350 · 2026-11-17 · the pages scale as a whole; one more size; a tighter desktop; Chiaro and Automatico

- **Design ref:** B-11 and E-10 (the student's theme and text size, `Diagnosis::Preferences`), D-306 (tokens and components, rem), D-307 (the student's shell), D-338 (the sizes «Molto piccolo» and «Piccolo»), D-337 (the practice page's container query, which keeps its share when the root changes).
- **The student's words (2026-11-17, passed on by the operator):** «La grafica e i testi sono troppo grandi»; «la grafica rimane troppo grande»; «molto grande e poco omogenea, su tutti i punti di tutte le pagine». He uses a desktop window about 1160 px wide, and also a phone.
- **What was wrong:** the root was 20 px at the default, so a desktop page was a phone page stretched (70 ch of 20 px text, cards with 1.5 rem of padding, one long column of cards); a smaller size moved the text and, in rem, most of the page, but the targets (`--tap`) fell under 44 px on a phone at the smallest size, a few lengths were px (the lesson's `max(2.4em, 44px)`, the lesson's grid paper), and the lists did not use the width.
- **We do:**
  1. **A size scales everything.** The size is the root font size and nothing else is a length in px (borders and hairlines aside; a test pins that `application.css` has no px width, height, padding, margin or gap above 1 px). The tokens (`--space-*`, `--text-*`, `--radius-*`, `--tap`) and all components are rem or em, so «Piccolo» makes the page smaller evenly. The lesson's paper grid is 1.3 rem. `test/system/preferences_test.rb` measures a button and a card at 14 px and at 28 px and finds a ratio of 2.
  2. **One more, smaller size.** `Diagnosis::Preferences::SIZES = %w[minimum smallest small normal large larger]`: «Minimo» is 14 px (the lesson dialog says «Minimo», the teacher's box 0.7 rem). Stored like the others (`student_preference`, latest counts); an unknown value is still ignored.
  3. **Touch keeps 44 px.** `@media (pointer: coarse)`: `--tap: max(2.75rem, 44px)`, `--tap-small: max(2.25rem, 44px)`; the lesson has a block of the same kind (buttons, icon buttons, try dots, helper keys, check options, inputs, summaries). With a mouse (`pointer: fine`) a target follows the size, so at 14 px it is 38 px: allowed.
  4. **A desktop is tighter by default.** From 1000 px of window width with `pointer: fine`, `student_scale.css` (loaded after `student.css`) redefines under `body.student` the spacing (×0.8), the headings (h1 1.6 rem, h2 1.3 rem), the radii and the targets, makes the page 52 rem wide and lays the lists of cards in a grid of at least 21 rem (17 rem for Materie): Oggi's suggestions, Materie, the topics of a subject, the entry-test rows, the two steps of a topic; the «Ora» card stays across. A phone, a tablet with a finger, a narrow window and the teacher's pages (`body.teacher`) are unchanged. The settings page puts its two cards side by side when there is room, at every width.
  5. **Themes.** `THEMES = %w[cream light dark auto]`. «Chiaro» is white (`#ffffff`) with neutral greys (text 17:1, muted 10:1, button 11:1, the same checks as the others in `readability_test.rb`); the lesson roles of `light` are the cream roles (`lesson_roles.css` has `:root` as the default), which have more contrast on white. «Automatico» follows `prefers-color-scheme`: a small script in the head of the student's layout (`shared/_theme_script`, with the CSP nonce) sets `data-theme` to `dark` or `cream` before the first paint and again when the device changes; `data-theme-choice` keeps the pick (`auto`). No stylesheet knows `auto`: every `[data-theme="dark"]` rule of the lessons, the graph and the comments keeps working. Light device gives **Crema**, not Chiaro: it is the student's reading default (a cream page is less glaring for him), and Chiaro stays a choice of its own.
